# BMW SERVICE

BMW recommends you have your maintenance and repair work performed by an authorized BMW center.

# MAINTAINING YOUR BMW VEHICLE

A well-maintained vehicle will help safeguard its operational performance, road-safety and its reliability. This is why it is important to follow and perform BMW’s recommended periodic vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks as indicated by your vehicle’s Maintenance Service Display, along with the other maintenance work described in this booklet.

A improper maintenance is not covered under the BMW New Vehicle Damage, including consequential damage, which results from lack of or Limited Warranty for Passenger Cars and Light Trucks.

# MAINTENANCE INTERVALS

Maintenance intervals on motor vehicles were conventionally based solely on a fixed time period or a specified amount of accumulated driving mileage.

However, operational and driving conditions have a major influence on your vehicle’s routine maintenance requirements; the distance traveled is only one of these significant factors. A vehicle used for short trips in the city with numerous cold starts, prolonged periods of idling, stop-and-go driving, and high engine speeds during acceleration may require more frequent maintenance intervals than a vehicle that is driven long distances at moderate engine speeds.

Your BMW vehicle uses sensors and algorithms together with the elapsed time and the driving distance/profile to monitor and evaluate your vehicle’s maintenance service needs. This information is then used to adapt dynamically the parameters used to forecast the applicable maintenance service task intervals.

# THE BMW MAINTENANCE SYSTEM

All BMW vehicles are equipped with an integrated BMW Maintenance System. This maintenance “reminder” system helps ensure that the vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks are performed at the forecasted intervals that apply to your vehicle.

The BMW Maintenance System display provides the vehicle operator access to the current status information for the following maintenance service tasks:

$\\triangleright$ Engine oil (date and miles)\*

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle check (date and miles)

$\\triangleright$ Front brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Rear brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid (date)

$\\triangleright$ 1200 Mile running-in service (date and miles) (Applicable to BMW M vehicles only)\*

For each specific maintenance service task, either the future date (month/ year), remaining miles or both are provided as noted above. The system monitors variable inputs to forecast the intervals and alert the driver when one or more specific maintenance tasks should be performed.

NOTE: For certain vehicles, the status of the front and rear brake pads will only be observable in the maintenance system’s display when there are approximately 2,000 miles or less remaining before a brake service will be required to be performed.

For information about the vehicle’s maintenance system displays, please refer to the Maintenance Service Display Overview section beginning on page 5.

The following “combine with Engine oil”\* maintenance service tasks may be identified as needing to be performed with a specific occurrence of the “Engine oil” service task (service counter number):

$\\triangleright$ Cabin Microfilter(s)

$\\triangleright$ Engine air filter(s)\*

$\\triangleright$ Spark plugs\*

$\\triangleright$ Final drive oil (Applicable M vehicles only)

\\* Does not apply to BEV

Although these items do not appear in the BMW Maintenance System’s display in the vehicle, these services should be performed when your vehicle’s engine oil is changed in accordance with the interval identified by your vehicle’s BMW Maintenance System.

For more information on your vehicle’s maintenance services requirements, procedures and intervals, please refer the Maintenance Service Summary section beginning on page 10.

The BMW Maintenance System also includes an option to set service reminders for the following state-specific mandatory vehicle inspections, including:

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle safety inspection; and/or $\\triangleright$ Emissions test

The corresponding interval data for these inspections can be inputted into the BMW Maintenance System by a service provider; they are not determined by the vehicle.

For your convenience, you may also wish to have your authorized BMW center perform the work necessary to fulfill these state inspection requirements in your area concurrent with the maintenance services specified above when possible.

Should you request more frequent maintenance service than is indicated by the BMW Maintenance System during the coverage period, the cost of these services will not be covered by the BMW Maintenance Program.

# SERVICE DATA — REMOTE CONTROL KEY

Maintenance service task status information for your BMW vehicle is continually updated and stored in your remote control key.

Your authorized BMW center can access this data and consult with you about applicable service procedures and tasks for your vehicle.

Therefore, always provide your service consultant with the most recent remote control key that was used to operate the vehicle when servicing your vehicle at a BMW center.

# VEHICLE STORAGE

Disconnecting the battery during periods of long-term vehicle storage will interrupt the calculation of time-dependent maintenance services.

In this situation, BMW recommends that you have all your time-based maintenance services, such as brake fluid, engine oil and cabin microfilter, brought up to the correct date by an authorized BMW center.

# ENGINE OIL

2025 model year vehicles with internal-combustion engines are factory-filled with:

Z BMW-approved fully synthetic oil for gasoline engines

Engine oil should be changed when the vehicle’s engine is at operating temperature.

If an engine oil service is being performed or you need to add engine oil between changes, please refer to the Owner’s Manual for the recommended engine oil for your BMW vehicle.

# LONG-TERM RATED FLUIDS AND OILS

The following systems and assemblies are factory-filled with long-term rated fluid and oil; fluid replacement is only necessary when repairs are being performed (unless otherwise noted):

$\\triangleright$ Engine cooling system (antifreeze/coolant) $\\triangleright$ Automatic (except for X1 and X2) and manual transmissions $\\triangleright$ All-wheel drive transfer cases (except when indicated by the vehicle)

# REGULAR CHECKS — VEHICLE OPERATOR

In addition to the maintenance service procedure information contained in this booklet, BMW recommends that you regularly check (when refueling, for example), and address when necessary, the following items:

$\\triangleright$ Washer fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Coolant level

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Tires — pressure, condition and wear

Please refer to the Owner’s Manual for additional information.

![2023 BMW 3 Series](https://dealerinspire-image-library-prod.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/images/oQNj43gWWpbDX49jH1rgvQGxo94MTLo8jKbCVaRn.jpg)

Your [BMW 3 Series](https://www.bmwtigard.com/new-vehicles/3-series/) is a finely-crafted piece of machinery, but it will still require routine service from time to time. Keeping up with the BMW 3 Series [maintenance schedule](https://www.bmwtigard.com/service/service-and-parts-tips/bmw-recommended-maintenance-schedule/) is a must if you want your vehicle to perform at its best for as long as possible. We understand that keeping track of BMW 3 Series oil change intervals and more can be a challenge. That is why we have created this guide to the BMW 3 Series service schedule. Simply follow this guide, and your vehicle should be prepared and safe for the roads of Portland and Tigard.

[View 3 Series Inventory](https://www.bmwtigard.com/new-vehicles/3-series/) [Contact Us](https://www.bmwtigard.com/contact-us/)

## BMW 3 Series Service Schedule

The BMW 3 Series service schedule includes BMW 3 Series oil change intervals and more to help you track the maintenance your vehicle requires. Let’s break it down more in-depth below.

### Bi-Annual Services

The services listed below should be performed approximately 6 months after you take your new vehicle home, at the 5,000 to 10,000-mile mark. They should then be performed at least twice a year for the duration you own the vehicle.

- Oil and Filter Change
- Tire Rotation
- Brake Inspection

### Every 30,000 Miles

At the 30,000-mile mark in the BMW 3 Series maintenance schedule, you’ll want to head back to the shop for a variety of inspections and maintenance care checks.

- Air filter changes: Air filters get clogged over time, so at this point, they are no longer working at their best. If you travel in particularly dusty environments, you’ll want to change the filter approximately every 15,000 miles.
- Fuel filter inspection: Your technician can perform a pressure test to determine if the fuel filter needs replacement.

### Every 60,000 Miles

Your 60,000-mile maintenance service will happen at around four or five years into ownership for the average driver. Here is what it will include:

- Brake Rotor, Pads, and Shoes Inspections and Replacements
- Brake Fluid Replacement
- Coolant Replacement
- Transmission Fluid Replacement

Keep in mind that this is also around the time your battery will start wearing down, so it is a good idea to have it looked at and possibly replaced.

### Every 90,000 Miles

At this service interval, we will take care of inspecting hoses, belts, and spark plugs. Power steering fluid should also be replaced when we perform these tasks:

- Timing belt replacement
- Replace hoses
- Replace spark plugs
- Rotate rotors or replace rotors
- Fuel system cleaning
- Complete inspection

# BMW SERVICE

BMW recommends you have your maintenance and repair work performed by an authorized BMW center.

# MAINTAINING YOUR BMW VEHICLE

A well-maintained vehicle will help safeguard its operational performance, road-safety and its reliability. This is why it is important to follow and perform BMW’s recommended periodic vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks as indicated by your vehicle’s Maintenance Service Display, along with the other maintenance work described in this booklet.

A improper maintenance is not covered under the BMW New Vehicle Damage, including consequential damage, which results from lack of or Limited Warranty for Passenger Cars and Light Trucks.

# MAINTENANCE INTERVALS

Maintenance intervals on motor vehicles were conventionally based solely on a fixed time period or a specified amount of accumulated driving mileage.

However, operational and driving conditions have a major influence on your vehicle’s routine maintenance requirements; the distance traveled is only one of these significant factors. A vehicle used for short trips in the city with numerous cold starts, prolonged periods of idling, stop-and-go driving, and high engine speeds during acceleration may require more frequent maintenance intervals than a vehicle that is driven long distances at moderate engine speeds.

Your BMW vehicle uses sensors and algorithms together with the elapsed time and the driving distance/profile to monitor and evaluate your vehicle’s maintenance service needs. This information is then used to adapt dynamically the parameters used to forecast the applicable maintenance service task intervals.

# THE BMW MAINTENANCE SYSTEM

All BMW vehicles are equipped with an integrated BMW Maintenance System. This maintenance “reminder” system helps ensure that the vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks are performed at the forecasted intervals that apply to your vehicle.

The BMW Maintenance System display provides the vehicle operator access to the current status information for the following maintenance service tasks:

$\\triangleright$ Engine oil (date and miles)\*

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle check (date and miles)

$\\triangleright$ Front brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Rear brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid (date)

$\\triangleright$ 1200 Mile running-in service (date and miles) (Applicable to BMW M vehicles only)\*

For each specific maintenance service task, either the future date (month/ year), remaining miles or both are provided as noted above. The system monitors variable inputs to forecast the intervals and alert the driver when one or more specific maintenance tasks should be performed.

NOTE: For certain vehicles, the status of the front and rear brake pads will only be observable in the maintenance system’s display when there are approximately 2,000 miles or less remaining before a brake service will be required to be performed.

For information about the vehicle’s maintenance system displays, please refer to the Maintenance Service Display Overview section beginning on page 5.

The following “combine with Engine oil”\* maintenance service tasks may be identified as needing to be performed with a specific occurrence of the “Engine oil” service task (service counter number):

$\\triangleright$ Cabin Microfilter(s)

$\\triangleright$ Engine air filter(s)\*

$\\triangleright$ Spark plugs\*

$\\triangleright$ Final drive oil (Applicable M vehicles only)

\\* Does not apply to BEV

Although these items do not appear in the BMW Maintenance System’s display in the vehicle, these services should be performed when your vehicle’s engine oil is changed in accordance with the interval identified by your vehicle’s BMW Maintenance System.

For more information on your vehicle’s maintenance services requirements, procedures and intervals, please refer the Maintenance Service Summary section beginning on page 10.

The BMW Maintenance System also includes an option to set service reminders for the following state-specific mandatory vehicle inspections, including:

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle safety inspection; and/or $\\triangleright$ Emissions test

The corresponding interval data for these inspections can be inputted into the BMW Maintenance System by a service provider; they are not determined by the vehicle.

For your convenience, you may also wish to have your authorized BMW center perform the work necessary to fulfill these state inspection requirements in your area concurrent with the maintenance services specified above when possible.

Should you request more frequent maintenance service than is indicated by the BMW Maintenance System during the coverage period, the cost of these services will not be covered by the BMW Maintenance Program.

# SERVICE DATA — REMOTE CONTROL KEY

Maintenance service task status information for your BMW vehicle is continually updated and stored in your remote control key.

Your authorized BMW center can access this data and consult with you about applicable service procedures and tasks for your vehicle.

Therefore, always provide your service consultant with the most recent remote control key that was used to operate the vehicle when servicing your vehicle at a BMW center.

# VEHICLE STORAGE

Disconnecting the battery during periods of long-term vehicle storage will interrupt the calculation of time-dependent maintenance services.

In this situation, BMW recommends that you have all your time-based maintenance services, such as brake fluid, engine oil and cabin microfilter, brought up to the correct date by an authorized BMW center.

# ENGINE OIL

2025 model year vehicles with internal-combustion engines are factory-filled with:

Z BMW-approved fully synthetic oil for gasoline engines

Engine oil should be changed when the vehicle’s engine is at operating temperature.

If an engine oil service is being performed or you need to add engine oil between changes, please refer to the Owner’s Manual for the recommended engine oil for your BMW vehicle.

# LONG-TERM RATED FLUIDS AND OILS

The following systems and assemblies are factory-filled with long-term rated fluid and oil; fluid replacement is only necessary when repairs are being performed (unless otherwise noted):

$\\triangleright$ Engine cooling system (antifreeze/coolant) $\\triangleright$ Automatic (except for X1 and X2) and manual transmissions $\\triangleright$ All-wheel drive transfer cases (except when indicated by the vehicle)

# REGULAR CHECKS — VEHICLE OPERATOR

In addition to the maintenance service procedure information contained in this booklet, BMW recommends that you regularly check (when refueling, for example), and address when necessary, the following items:

$\\triangleright$ Washer fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Coolant level

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Tires — pressure, condition and wear

Please refer to the Owner’s Manual for additional information.

At BMW of Tigard, we often get questions from customers about their BMW maintenance schedule. And when you buy a [quality new BMW](https://www.bmwtigard.com/new-vehicles/), it’s important to stick to its BMW service schedule. That’s why we’ve provided the recommended maintenance schedule for general BMW vehicles for Portland and Tigard drivers. With this handy guide, it’ll be easy to stay on track and have your vehicle serviced. We’ll ensure that your vehicle will always be running at its best! As always, before you schedule maintenance on your vehicle, be sure to read your owner’s manual for any specific maintenance information that applies to your BMW vehicle. That way, you’ll better understand your specific model and trim’s future maintenance and repair needs.

## BMW Preventative Maintenance: Every 5,000 Miles / 6 Months

It’s important to bring in your BMW two or three times a year (or every 5,000 miles) for these preventative maintenance services:

- Front and rear brake inspection
- Brake fluid check
- Coolant check
- Engine oil check
- Cabin air filter inspection
- Engine inspection
- Vehicle inspection
- Wiper blade inspection
- Any necessary tire rotations

Your BMW also comes with something called the Condition-Based Service Monitor (CBS). Your CBS tracks the condition of important systems in your BMW, letting you know if service is required. Our technicians will also use your CBS to determine what needs to be replaced, repaired, or serviced when you schedule service. Keep in mind that just because your CBS may say that service may not be necessary at 5,000 miles doesn’t mean that you shouldn’t come in for preventative maintenance and checks. Sometimes human eyes are necessary to determine a problem or to nip any potential issues in the bud.

## Recommended BMW Maintenance Schedule

Your BMW service schedule needs will vary based on how often you drive, where you drive, and your driving conditions. Your owner’s manual can give you detailed information on common service tasks for your specific model and trim, but here’s what BMW owners can generally expect:

- **Every 10,000 miles** (or yearly): replace your vehicle’s engine oil, oil filter, and coolant.
- **Every 20,000 miles** (or every two years): inspect and replace your vehicle’s fuel filters.
- **Every 30,000 miles** (or every three years): replace your vehicle’s brake fluid (after the first replacement, **every 60,000 miles**) and replace your vehicle’s transmission fluid on manual-transmission BMWs.
- **Every 60,000 miles** (or every six years): replace your vehicle’s engine air filter and spark plugs, inspect and replace any brake pads and brake rotors, and replace transmission fluid on automatic-transmission BMWs.
- **Every 90,000 miles** (or every nine years): replace your vehicle’s timing belts and hoses.

You’ll want to repeat the cycle above after 90,000 miles and always follow the 5,000-mile maintenance schedule. Your BMW’s New Vehicle Limited Warranty will also expire at 50,000 miles, so we recommend getting in any repairs or service before this warranty expires! We also recommend replacing your BMW battery around 50,000 miles.

# BMW X3 Maintenance Schedule

* * *

Owning a BMW X3 means enjoying top-tier performance and luxury, but regular maintenance is key to keeping your vehicle running smoothly. Staying on top of your X3’s maintenance schedule will not only enhance its performance but also extend its lifespan on the roads of Norwood, Westwood, and Dedham, MA.

Here's a breakdown of what [BMW services](https://www.bmwnorwood.com/service/schedule-service/) are needed at various mileage intervals.

## Every 5,000-10,000 Miles

At the first interval after you start driving your BMW X3, typically around 5,000 to 10,000 miles, you’ll need to perform several basic yet essential maintenance tasks.

First and foremost is an oil change. Your vehicle’s oil should be changed every 10,000 miles or 12 months, depending on which comes first. However, a more regular oil check, say every 5,000 miles or so, can help ensure your X3 is always equipped with clean and healthy oil.

Some other services you may see at this interval include a quick inspection of your brakes as well as a tire rotation.

![Brake Service](https://di-uploads-pod40.dealerinspire.com/bmwnorwood/uploads/2024/10/Brake-2.jpg)

## Every 10,000-15,000 Miles

Around this mileage, you should include additional checks on essential [vehicle parts](https://www.bmwnorwood.com/parts/) like your brakes, battery, engine, and more. Additionally, you’ll see a handful of routine services such as:

- **Replace Wiper Blades**
- **Replace Key Fob Battery**
- **Inspect/Replace Coolant**
- **Inspect Brake Pads and Rotors**

## Every 60,000 Miles

The 60,000-mile mark is a fairly significant one in the lifespan of your BMW X3. At this interval, you’ll have several key components replaced.

You can expect your vehicle’s spark plugs, transmission fluid, and tires to all be replaced around this time. Be sure to keep an eye on the condition of your tires, however, as they may need to be replaced sooner.

## Every 75,000 Miles

At the 75,000-mile interval, you can expect many of the standard services like an oil change or a tire rotation. Though, there are several other components you’ll want to have inspected at this point, including:

- **Brake Pads, Calipers, and Rotors**
- **Cooling System and Hoses**
- **Suspension System**

## Every 90,000-100,000 Miles

As you near 90,000 to 100,000 miles in your BMW X3, another important set of services awaits. Here, you’ll see a complete flush and replacement of your transmission fluid. The driveshaft must also be lubricated to ensure your engine parts are moving without any issues.

The service team will also inspect a number of parts once again like the driveshaft boots, fuel injector, any belts and hoses, as well as the water pump.

# BMW SERVICE

BMW recommends you have your maintenance and repair work performed by an authorized BMW center.

# MAINTAINING YOUR BMW VEHICLE

A well-maintained vehicle will help safeguard its operational performance, road-safety and its reliability. This is why it is important to follow and perform BMW’s recommended periodic vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks as indicated by your vehicle’s Maintenance Service Display, along with the other maintenance work described in this booklet.

A improper maintenance is not covered under the BMW New Vehicle Damage, including consequential damage, which results from lack of or Limited Warranty for Passenger Cars and Light Trucks.

# MAINTENANCE INTERVALS

Maintenance intervals on motor vehicles were conventionally based solely on a fixed time period or a specified amount of accumulated driving mileage.

However, operational and driving conditions have a major influence on your vehicle’s routine maintenance requirements; the distance traveled is only one of these significant factors. A vehicle used for short trips in the city with numerous cold starts, prolonged periods of idling, stop-and-go driving, and high engine speeds during acceleration may require more frequent maintenance intervals than a vehicle that is driven long distances at moderate engine speeds.

Your BMW vehicle uses sensors and algorithms together with the elapsed time and the driving distance/profile to monitor and evaluate your vehicle’s maintenance service needs. This information is then used to adapt dynamically the parameters used to forecast the applicable maintenance service task intervals.

# THE BMW MAINTENANCE SYSTEM

All BMW vehicles are equipped with an integrated BMW Maintenance System. This maintenance “reminder” system helps ensure that the vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks are performed at the forecasted intervals that apply to your vehicle.

The BMW Maintenance System display provides the vehicle operator access to the current status information for the following maintenance service tasks:

$\\triangleright$ Engine oil (date and miles)\*

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle check (date and miles)

$\\triangleright$ Front brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Rear brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid (date)

$\\triangleright$ 1200 Mile running-in service (date and miles) (Applicable to BMW M vehicles only)\*

For each specific maintenance service task, either the future date (month/ year), remaining miles or both are provided as noted above. The system monitors variable inputs to forecast the intervals and alert the driver when one or more specific maintenance tasks should be performed.

NOTE: For certain vehicles, the status of the front and rear brake pads will only be observable in the maintenance system’s display when there are approximately 2,000 miles or less remaining before a brake service will be required to be performed.

For information about the vehicle’s maintenance system displays, please refer to the Maintenance Service Display Overview section beginning on page 5.

The following “combine with Engine oil”\* maintenance service tasks may be identified as needing to be performed with a specific occurrence of the “Engine oil” service task (service counter number):

$\\triangleright$ Cabin Microfilter(s)

$\\triangleright$ Engine air filter(s)\*

$\\triangleright$ Spark plugs\*

$\\triangleright$ Final drive oil (Applicable M vehicles only)

\\* Does not apply to BEV

Although these items do not appear in the BMW Maintenance System’s display in the vehicle, these services should be performed when your vehicle’s engine oil is changed in accordance with the interval identified by your vehicle’s BMW Maintenance System.

For more information on your vehicle’s maintenance services requirements, procedures and intervals, please refer the Maintenance Service Summary section beginning on page 10.

The BMW Maintenance System also includes an option to set service reminders for the following state-specific mandatory vehicle inspections, including:

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle safety inspection; and/or $\\triangleright$ Emissions test

The corresponding interval data for these inspections can be inputted into the BMW Maintenance System by a service provider; they are not determined by the vehicle.

For your convenience, you may also wish to have your authorized BMW center perform the work necessary to fulfill these state inspection requirements in your area concurrent with the maintenance services specified above when possible.

Should you request more frequent maintenance service than is indicated by the BMW Maintenance System during the coverage period, the cost of these services will not be covered by the BMW Maintenance Program.

# SERVICE DATA — REMOTE CONTROL KEY

Maintenance service task status information for your BMW vehicle is continually updated and stored in your remote control key.

Your authorized BMW center can access this data and consult with you about applicable service procedures and tasks for your vehicle.

Therefore, always provide your service consultant with the most recent remote control key that was used to operate the vehicle when servicing your vehicle at a BMW center.

# VEHICLE STORAGE

Disconnecting the battery during periods of long-term vehicle storage will interrupt the calculation of time-dependent maintenance services.

In this situation, BMW recommends that you have all your time-based maintenance services, such as brake fluid, engine oil and cabin microfilter, brought up to the correct date by an authorized BMW center.

# ENGINE OIL

2025 model year vehicles with internal-combustion engines are factory-filled with:

Z BMW-approved fully synthetic oil for gasoline engines

Engine oil should be changed when the vehicle’s engine is at operating temperature.

If an engine oil service is being performed or you need to add engine oil between changes, please refer to the Owner’s Manual for the recommended engine oil for your BMW vehicle.

# LONG-TERM RATED FLUIDS AND OILS

The following systems and assemblies are factory-filled with long-term rated fluid and oil; fluid replacement is only necessary when repairs are being performed (unless otherwise noted):

$\\triangleright$ Engine cooling system (antifreeze/coolant) $\\triangleright$ Automatic (except for X1 and X2) and manual transmissions $\\triangleright$ All-wheel drive transfer cases (except when indicated by the vehicle)

# REGULAR CHECKS — VEHICLE OPERATOR

In addition to the maintenance service procedure information contained in this booklet, BMW recommends that you regularly check (when refueling, for example), and address when necessary, the following items:

$\\triangleright$ Washer fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Coolant level

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Tires — pressure, condition and wear

Please refer to the Owner’s Manual for additional information.

## BMW X3 Service Intervals

What tasks are included as part of your BMW X3 service schedule? Here is what to expect at each visit.

**Every 5,000-10,000 Miles:**

- Refill All Fluid Levels
- Inspect Your Brakes
- Rotate/Inspect Tires
- Change Oil and Filter

**Every 10,000-15,000 Miles:**

- Replace the Windshield Wipers
- Inspect/Replace Engine Coolant
- Replace Your Key Fob’s Battery

**Every 30,000 Miles:**

- Check Fuel Lines/Battery Connections
- Replace Cabin and Engine Air Filters
- Check and Refill Your Brake Fluid

**Every 60,000 Miles:**

- Replace Engine Spark Plugs
- Replace Transmission Fluid
- Replace All Your Tires

**Every 75,000 Miles:**

- Inspect Suspension System
- Inspect Cooling System/Hoses
- Inspect/Replace Calipers/Rotors
- Inspect/Replace Your Brake Pads

**Every 90,000-100,000 Miles:**

- Inspect Fuel Injector
- Lubricate the Driveshaft
- Inspect Driveshaft Boots
- Inspect/Replace Belts, Hoses, and Water Pump
- Flush and Replace All the Transmission Fluid

## Benefits of BMW Service

- Regular service visits keep your vehicle running as efficiently as possible on the roads of Fort Lauderdale and Hollywood.
- Drive with confidence behind the wheel of a well-maintained vehicle.
- If you plan to sell your vehicle in the future, one that is up to date on the BMW X3 service schedule will be more appealing to potential buyers.

# BMW X3 Maintenance Schedule

* * *

Owning a BMW X3 means enjoying top-tier performance and luxury, but regular maintenance is key to keeping your vehicle running smoothly. Staying on top of your X3’s maintenance schedule will not only enhance its performance but also extend its lifespan on the roads of Norwood, Westwood, and Dedham, MA.

Here's a breakdown of what [BMW services](https://www.bmwnorwood.com/service/schedule-service/) are needed at various mileage intervals.

## Every 5,000-10,000 Miles

At the first interval after you start driving your BMW X3, typically around 5,000 to 10,000 miles, you’ll need to perform several basic yet essential maintenance tasks.

First and foremost is an oil change. Your vehicle’s oil should be changed every 10,000 miles or 12 months, depending on which comes first. However, a more regular oil check, say every 5,000 miles or so, can help ensure your X3 is always equipped with clean and healthy oil.

Some other services you may see at this interval include a quick inspection of your brakes as well as a tire rotation.

![Brake Service](https://di-uploads-pod40.dealerinspire.com/bmwnorwood/uploads/2024/10/Brake-2.jpg)

## Every 10,000-15,000 Miles

Around this mileage, you should include additional checks on essential [vehicle parts](https://www.bmwnorwood.com/parts/) like your brakes, battery, engine, and more. Additionally, you’ll see a handful of routine services such as:

- **Replace Wiper Blades**
- **Replace Key Fob Battery**
- **Inspect/Replace Coolant**
- **Inspect Brake Pads and Rotors**

## Every 60,000 Miles

The 60,000-mile mark is a fairly significant one in the lifespan of your BMW X3. At this interval, you’ll have several key components replaced.

You can expect your vehicle’s spark plugs, transmission fluid, and tires to all be replaced around this time. Be sure to keep an eye on the condition of your tires, however, as they may need to be replaced sooner.

## Every 75,000 Miles

At the 75,000-mile interval, you can expect many of the standard services like an oil change or a tire rotation. Though, there are several other components you’ll want to have inspected at this point, including:

- **Brake Pads, Calipers, and Rotors**
- **Cooling System and Hoses**
- **Suspension System**

## Every 90,000-100,000 Miles

As you near 90,000 to 100,000 miles in your BMW X3, another important set of services awaits. Here, you’ll see a complete flush and replacement of your transmission fluid. The driveshaft must also be lubricated to ensure your engine parts are moving without any issues.

The service team will also inspect a number of parts once again like the driveshaft boots, fuel injector, any belts and hoses, as well as the water pump.

Those manufactured between 2011 and 2022 hold approximately 13 quarts (12.3 liters). A Ford F-650 and F-750 produced between 2015 and 2022 can hold a maximum of 15 quarts (14.2 liters) of oil. For newer models released in 2023 and later, the oil capacity increases slightly to 17 quarts (16 liters). When performing an oil change, it is crucial to use the correct type of oil and adhere to the recommended capacity. Ford recommends using oils that meet its WSS-M2C17-F1 specification for the 6.7 Powerstroke. ## VW Atlas Service Schedule

## 10,000 Miles or One Year

The base of your VW Atlas service schedule will consist of the following maintenance tasks:

- Inspect the Brake Pads
- VW Atlas Oil Change
- New Oil Filter
- Service Interval Display Rest (if needed)

## 20,000 Miles or Two Years

Two-year maintenance should also include a VW Atlas oil change and oil filter replacement. The following must also be checked so you can stay safe on Vienna roads:

- Horn
- Tire Repair Kit
- Engine and Engine Compartment Components
- Brake Fluid
- Tire Pressure
- Service Interval Display
- Exterior Lighting
- Battery
- Tires
- Windshield Wiper/Washer System
- Automatic headlight control
- Headlight Washing System
- Wiper Blades
- Coolant Level and Frost Protection
- Brake Pads
- Transmission
- Second Battery
- Tire Pressure Monitoring System

## 30,000 Miles or Three Years

The following VW Atlas routine maintenance tasks will be required every three years or 30,000 miles:

- Oil Change
- New Oil Filter
- Inspect Brake Pads
- Service Interval Display Rest (if needed)

## 40,000 Miles or Four Years

At 40,000 miles, you’ll get a VW Atlas oil change and a new oil filter, plus everything from the 20,000 service interval. These things will also be checked as part of your VW Atlas maintenance schedule:

- Tie Rod Ends
- Stabilizer Bushings
- New Dust and Pollen Filter
- Front and Rear Coil Springs and Shock Absorbers
- Sunroof and Panoramic Sunroof
- Ball Joints
- Wheel Bearings
- Axles
- Coupling Rods

## 50,000 Miles or Five Years

The 50,000 VW Atlas service interval includes:

- Engine Oil Change
- New Oil Filter
- Check Your Brake Pads
- Service Interval Display Rest (if needed)

## 60,000 Miles or 6 Years

Your safety is paramount as you drive around Fairfax, so along with new engine oil, oil filter, air filter, and snow filter, these components will be inspected:

- Fuel filter Replacement
- Dust and Pollen Filter Replacement
- Battery inspection
- Check the Tires
- Brake System Inspection
- Check the Tire fFller Bottle Expiration Date

## 70,000 Miles or 7 Years

The 70,000-mile mark of the VW Atlas maintenance schedule includes the following tasks:

- Engine Oil Filter Change
- Motor Oil Change
- Brake Pad Check
- Service Interval Display Rest (if needed)

## 80,000 Miles or 8 Years

All the same components from the 20,000-mile inspection are inspected, as well as:

- Ball Joints
- Transmission
- Wheel Bearings
- Axles
- Interior Lighting
- Ribbed V-belt
- Front and Rear Coil Springs
- Shock Absorbers
- Sunroof and Panoramic Sunroof
- Underbody

## 90,000 Miles or 9 Years

- Brake Discs
- Clutch Unit
- Engine Oil Change
- Engine Oil Filter Change
- Brake Pad Inspection
- Service Interval Display Rest (if needed)

## 100,000 Miles or 10 Years

At 100,000 miles, you’ll get a VW Atlas oil change and new oil filter, and the same things as the 20,000-mile inspection will be inspected.

## 110,000 Miles or 11 Years

- Brake Pad Check
- Engine Oil Change
- New Oil Filter
- Service Interval Display Rest (if needed)

## 120,000 Miles or 12 Years

Our certified VW Technicians will replace your engine oil, oil filter, and snow and air filter and check all the same components from the 20,000-mile inspection, plus:

- Underbody
- Wheel Bearings
- Axles
- Tie Rod Ends,
- Stabilizer Bushings
- Front and Rear Coil Springs
- Shock Absorbers
- Ball Joints
- Interior Lighting
- Coupling Rods
- Ribbed V-Belt
- Sunroof and Panoramic Sunroof

# Volkswagen Atlas Oil Type & Capacity

![Oil Change](https://dealerinspire-image-library-prod.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/images/dPDQ8g69kRnC3TrrSgdDfloXOa5eUuOdriCxjktZ.jpg)

From keeping engine components lubricated to reducing heat and friction to minimizing wear and tear, using the automaker’s recommended oil will help you get the most out of your [Atlas](https://www.volkswagenofdesmoines.com/new-vehicles/atlas/) on every Des Moines and Waukee drive. But what kind of oil does the Volkswagen Atlas use? Lithia Volkswagen of Des Moines answers this question below, covering the suggested Volkswagen Atlas oil type, as well as the Volkswagen Atlas oil capacity.

[More Service Tips](https://www.volkswagenofdesmoines.com/service/service-tips/) [Schedule Oil Change](https://www.volkswagenofdesmoines.com/schedule-service/)

## What Kind Of Oil Does The Volkswagen Atlas Use?

It’s no secret that routine oil changes are an essential part of [VW maintenance](https://www.volkswagenofdesmoines.com/service/service-tips/volkswagen-maintenance-schedule/). At your next oil change, request the preferred Volkswagen Atlas oil type, which is a full synthetic 0W-30.\* The manufacturer specifically recommends Castrol brand motor oil.

## How Much Oil Does The Volkswagen Atlas Need?

Now that you know what kind of oil the Volkswagen Atlas uses, you are likely curious about exactly how much oil you’ll need. The Volkswagen Atlas oil capacity rings in at 6.02 quarts, which includes the filter.

## Why Choose Synthetic Over Conventional Oil?

The VW Atlas requires full synthetic motor oil due to its sophisticated engine design, which demands premium lubrication for optimal performance on West Des Moines roads and beyond. Here are a few key advantages of synthetic over conventional motor oil:

- **Superior Engine Protection** – Synthetic oils contain additives that create a protective barrier against wear.
- **Smoother Flow** – The structure of synthetic oil maintains better fluidity across temperature extremes, resulting in proper circulation during cold starts and consistent lubrication under high heat.
- **Turbocharged Engine Support** – For Atlas models equipped with turbochargers, synthetic oil provides crucial safeguards for these high-performance components that operate at extreme temperatures and speeds.
- **Extended Oil Life** – Synthetic oil resists thermal breakdown and maintains its protective qualities longer than conventional oil, which can mean more time between oil changes.
- **A Cleaner Oil Supply** – The composition of synthetic oil keeps carbon buildup and sludge formation to a minimum, which, in turn, keeps internal engine parts cleaner and functioning more efficiently.

## Schedule An Oil Change In Johnston

It’s a good idea to schedule an oil change with the suggested Volkswagen Atlas oil type every 10,000 miles. Make an appointment by [contacting us](https://www.volkswagenofdesmoines.com/service/contact-service/) directly or [reserving a time](https://www.volkswagenofdesmoines.com/schedule-service/) online, and don’t hesitate to reach out if you have any further questions about the Volkswagen Atlas oil capacity or type. Our service technicians are here to provide the quality service you need to enjoy your Atlas for years to come.

# Volkswagen Tiguan Recommended Maintenance Schedule

The Volkswagen Tiguan stands out as one of Volkswagen's most popular vehicles, and for good reason. It offers a smooth ride, responsive handling, and a practical design, all of which have made it the go-to model for those who want a compact crossover.

The best way to protect your investment and keep your Tiguan running at its best? Keeping up with routine maintenance. We recommend following this VW Tiguan maintenance schedule to protect performance and extend your vehicle's lifespan.

![](https://pictures.dealer.com/h/hoovervolkswagenlithiaspringvw/1234/f5c328b76bb0498498c2e1ecd26148b9.jpeg?impolicy=downsize_bkpt&w=2500)

## Volkswagen Tiguan Maintenance Schedule

* * *

Most new Volkswagen Tiguan models follow a recommended service interval of every 10,000 miles or 12 months, whichever comes first, with the first scheduled service at 10,000 miles.

Older models may have different maintenance needs, so it's always a good idea to check your owner's manual to confirm the correct VW Tiguan maintenance schedule for your specific vehicle.

For Tiguans using synthetic oil, oil changes are typically recommended every 10,000 miles or once a year, though this can vary depending on your driving habits, commute length, and overall usage.

Here is a general VW Tiguan maintenance schedule to help you stay on track:

### Every 10,000 Miles (or 12 Months)

This is your most frequent service visit and focuses on routine upkeep.

- Engine oil and filter change (synthetic oil)
- Tire rotation
- Brake inspection
- Multi-point vehicle inspection
- Check fluid levels and top off as needed
- Inspect lights, wipers, and battery condition

### Every 20,000 Miles

In addition to the 10,000-mile services:

- Replace the cabin air filter
- Inspect the engine air filter
- Inspect suspension and steering components
- Check the cooling system and hoses

### Every 30,000-40,000 Miles

Along with previous maintenance items:

- Replace engine air filter (if needed)
- Brake service inspection
- Wheel alignment check
- Battery and charging system test
- Inspect the exhaust system

### Every 50,000 Miles

In addition to routine oil changes and tire rotations, this service interval typically includes:

- Brake system inspection
- Battery and charging system test
- Suspension and steering evaluation
- Engine air filter replacement (if needed)
- Cooling system inspection
- Wheel alignment check

### Every 60,000 Miles

This is a larger service interval that may include:

- Spark plug replacement (varies by model year)
- Transmission service (model-dependent)
- Coolant system inspection or service
- More in-depth brake and suspension evaluation

### Beyond 60,000 Miles

As mileage increases, your Tiguan may also need:

- Additional drivetrain inspections
- Timing-related component checks (model dependent)
- Continued fluid services
- Suspension and steering repairs as needed

**Important note:** Older Volkswagen Tiguan models and certain driving habits (frequent short trips, stop-and-go traffic, towing, or extreme weather) may require more frequent service. Always refer to your owner's manual for the exact maintenance requirements for your specific vehicle. If you still have questions, don't hesitate to contact us!

Your first regular service is at about 10,000 miles or 12 months, whichever comes first. ## Why the F‑150 Lightning Maintenance Schedule Looks Different All‑electric Fords, including the F‑150 Lightning, need far less scheduled maintenance than comparable gas trucks. Ford’s EV care guidance focuses on **tire rotation every 10,000 miles or 12 months**, brake inspections, fluid checks, and periodic coolant and drive‑unit fluid changes rather than the frequent oil changes and tune‑ups that internal‑combustion F‑150s require. ### Fewer Moving Parts The Lightning’s dual electric drive units have far fewer moving parts than a V6 or V8 engine and traditional transmission. There are no spark plugs, fuel injectors, or exhaust components to service, which eliminates many classic truck maintenance items. ### New Priorities: Tires & Thermal Management Because of the battery’s weight and instant torque, **tires and alignment** take center stage. And while you don’t service an engine, you do have **coolant for the battery and power electronics** that needs attention at long intervals to keep the thermal‑management system healthy. ### F‑150 Lightning Maintenance at a Glance ~10,000 mi Basic service interval Ford’s EV guidance calls for tire rotation and inspection about every 10,000 miles or 12 months. 150,000 mi First major fluid Transmission/drive‑unit fluid typically isn’t due until around 150,000 miles in Ford EV schedules. Fewer visits Vs. gas F‑150 No routine oil changes or spark‑plug services mean fewer shop visits over the life of the truck. Lower Routine costs Most owners report modest costs for inspections, tire rotations, and occasional alignments. ## Core Ford F‑150 Lightning Maintenance Intervals Ford publishes official maintenance charts in the Lightning’s owner’s manual, but when you distill those down, a clear pattern appears. Below are the **core intervals most owners actually use**, closely aligned with Ford’s broader EV care recommendations. ### Core F‑150 Lightning Maintenance Intervals Key service intervals you’ll see throughout the Lightning maintenance schedule. Think of this as a translation of Ford’s maintenance guidance into plain English, with real‑world context from Lightning owners. ### 0–10,000 Miles: New Truck Baseline #### Initial inspection and tire rotation At around 10,000 miles or 12 months, plan your first service. The visit typically includes a tire rotation, visual brake inspection, and a multi‑point vehicle check. Some owners choose to rotate tires at a tire shop instead if it’s more convenient. #### Check alignment early Because the Lightning is heavy, a slight misalignment can chew tires quickly. Many dealers suggest an alignment around this first visit, especially if you notice any pull, uneven wear, or if you’ve hit a big pothole. #### Software updates and inspections Over‑the‑air updates will install themselves, but a dealer visit is a good time for technicians to confirm control modules, the 12‑volt battery, and charging hardware are in good shape. ### 10,000–30,000 Miles: Establishing a Rhythm #### Every 10,000 miles: repeat rotation & inspection Plan on tire rotation, brake inspection, and a multi‑point inspection roughly every 10,000 miles. With an EV’s instant torque, staying on top of rotations helps prevent cupping and inside‑edge wear. #### At ~20,000 miles: cabin air filter Ford EV schedules commonly call for cabin air filter service around 20,000 miles. That filter clears pollen, dust, and road grime from the air you breathe. Many owners DIY this in a few minutes behind the glovebox. #### Around 2–3 years: brake fluid check By the 2–3 year mark (often 20,000–30,000 miles for typical drivers), it’s smart to check and replace brake fluid if it has absorbed moisture. Clean fluid protects ABS and stability‑control hardware. ### 30,000–60,000 Miles: Tires, Brakes, and Suspension #### Tire replacement window Depending on driving style and towing, many Lightning owners will see their first set of tires wear out between 30,000 and 50,000 miles. An all‑electric truck is hard on rubber; budget accordingly. #### Alignment every 15,000–30,000 miles Ford dealers often recommend a wheel alignment about every 15,000 miles, or anytime you mount new tires or feel wandering, pulling, or steering‑wheel vibration. #### Brake fluid service if you skipped earlier If you didn’t change brake fluid around 30,000 miles, have it serviced by 60,000 miles. Even though regenerative braking reduces pad and rotor wear, the fluid itself ages regardless of how often you brake. #### Detailed suspension and steering check By this mileage, ask your shop to look closely at control‑arm bushings, tie‑rod ends, wheel bearings, and shocks. Heavy trucks plus rough roads can accelerate wear in these areas. ### 60,000–120,000 Miles: Long‑Term Reliability #### Ongoing 10,000‑mile checkups Continue your 10,000‑mile rotation and inspection pattern. At this age, those visits also help catch early signs of 12‑volt battery fatigue, charging‑port wear, or coolant seepage. #### Second set of tires and possibly pads Expect another complete set of tires in this window. They’ll also examine the steering linkage, joints, and wheels to ensure smooth operation. Our service team will change the oil and oil filter. This important maintenance task protects your F-150’s engine by flushing out old, dirty oil and replacing it with fresh oil. Other services performed during this visit include a tire rotation, a tire pressure check, an assessment of the transmission fluid level, and lubrication of the axles and joints. These services help maintain your truck’s peak performance and prevent potential issues down the road. ### 20,000 Miles At 20,000 miles, our technicians will repeat the services of the 10,000-mile visit, and they’ll replace the cabin air filter. This part ensures the interior air remains clean, fresh, and free of allergens and pollutants. These services are repeated every 20,000 miles. ### 30,000 Miles When your Ford F-150 reaches 30,000 miles, our service team will replace the engine air filter. This component is crucial for ensuring your truck’s engine receives clean air. Dirty air entering the engine reduces fuel economy and can hamper performance. ### 100,000 Miles Our service technicians will carefully inspect the accessory drive belt when your truck hits 100,000 miles. While a replacement isn’t usually needed at this point, catching wear early prevents future problems. This milestone service also includes coolant checks and spark plug replacements. ### 150,000 Miles Reaching 150,000 miles in your 2025 Ford F-150 demonstrates that you understand the value of proper maintenance. This milestone service focuses on key components that ensure your truck’s continued reliability. Our technicians will replace the accessory drive belt that powers vital systems like the alternator, power steering pump, water pump, and A/C compressor. Fresh rear axle lubricant protects the differential components for smooth, efficient operation. New transmission fluid and filters round out this major service, helping maintain transmission performance and durability. # BMW 3 Series Maintenance Schedule

![](https://dealerimages.dealereprocess.com/image/upload/3734739)

## Maintenance Schedule

Keeping up with your vehicle’s routine maintenance schedule is crucial to the health and longevity of your car. Routine maintenance services are done about once or twice a year, and are usually just a quick stop by the shop to change your oil and make sure everything is working properly.

**Here at BMW of Westchester we know how important it is to stay on top of these services in order to keep your car on the streets of Westchester County and Yonkers, NY, for years to come. Check out our breakdown of the BMW 3 Series maintenance schedule below!  [Schedule a service appointment](https://www.westchesterbmw.com/service-appointment/) for more assistance.**

## Annual Routine Maintenance Services

Your first[BMW 3 Series](https://www.westchesterbmw.com/search/new-bmw-3-series-white-plains-ny/?cy=10607&md=33&tp=new) routine maintenance service will happen about 6 months in, or once you hit around 5,000-10,000 miles, whichever happens to come first. This first service will be relatively quick. It will include:

- **An oil and filter change**

- **Tire rotation**

- **Brake inspection**


You’ll want to get these services done once or twice a year for the duration of the vehicle’s life.

Staying on top of your regular oil and oil filter changes is crucial to your car’s health because as your engine runs, tiny bits of dirt and dust will build up in it, which can cause excessive wear and tear.

**Additionally, yearly [tire rotations](https://www.westchesterbmw.com/service-appointment/) are important to maintain traction control, because they prevent your wheels from having uneven tread. Tread and traction control helps your vehicle stop quicker, and provides you with safer travels over rough terrain.**

![](https://dealerimages.dealereprocess.com/image/upload/3734763)

![](https://dealerimages.dealereprocess.com/image/upload/3734769)

## 30,000-Mile Maintenance Services

Once your BMW 3 Series hits 30,000 miles, it’s time to head back to the shop for a variety of inspections and maintenance care checks. To start, you’re going to need:

- **Your air filter changed, over time your air filter can become clogged, and a replacement will be needed in order for it to work at its best. If you travel in particularly dusty environments, you’ll want this changed around 15,000 miles rather than 30,000.**

- **Next, you’ll need your fuel filter inspected; your technician can perform a pressure test to determine if you’ll need it replaced.**


## 60,000-Mile Maintenance Services

Your 60,000-mile maintenance service will happen at around four or five years into ownership for the average driver. At this service, you’ll need:

- **Brake Rotor, Pads, and Shoes Inspections and Replacements**

- **Brake Fluid Replacement**

- **Coolant Replacement**

- **Transmission Fluid Replacement**

- **Your BMW 3 Series battery and brakes will start to wear out around the 60,000-mile mark, which is why it’s so important to get them inspected, and possibly replaced.**


![](https://dealerimages.dealereprocess.com/image/upload/3734756)

![](https://dealerimages.dealereprocess.com/image/upload/3734759)

## 90,000-Mile Maintenance Services

Your 90,000-mile maintenance check will include an inspection of your hoses, belts, and spark plugs. If they’re not up to par, they’ll need to be replaced. Additionally, you’ll also need to replace your power steering fluid to keep your steering wheel working properly. You should also get the following done:

- **Timing belt replacement**

- **Replace hoses**

- **Replace spark plugs**

- **Rotate rotors or replace rotors**

- **Fuel system cleaning**

- **Complete inspection**

Staying on top of your routine maintenance services is imperative to your vehicle’s health, and will help you get the most out of it. Call or stop by to schedule your next appointment!

## [Century West BMW – Recommended service and maintenance schedule for BMW 3 Series](https://www.centurywestbmw.com/service/)

Your BMW 3 Series thrives on precision. A thoughtful, consistent maintenance plan keeps its TwinPower Turbo engines, xDrive components, and chassis systems performing the way Munich intended. At Century West BMW, our BMW M Certified technicians combine factory training, OEM diagnostics, and Genuine BMW Parts to deliver service that fits your model year and driving style. We read your vehicle’s Condition Based Service (CBS) data through iDrive, verify with a multi-point inspection, and then tailor a plan that protects performance, efficiency, and resale value—without recommending work you do not need. From oil and filter changes to brake fluid exchanges, tire services, alignments, and software updates, we complete work to BMW specifications and reset onboard service counters so your reminders stay accurate. Because Los Angeles traffic, short trips, and heat can accelerate wear, we also check cooling performance, battery health, and brake life at each visit. With online scheduling, clear recommendations, and quick turnaround, our team makes it simple to stay current. As a local resource serving North Hollywood, we are here to help you enjoy every mile in your 3 Series.

- **Every 10,000 miles or 12 months**: BMW Longlife oil and filter; inspect brakes and tires; top off fluids; road test.
- **Every 20,000 miles or 2 years**: Cabin microfilter replacement; brake fluid exchange; comprehensive multi-point inspection.
- **Every 30,000 miles**: Engine air filter; fuel system check; inspect PCV and induction plumbing.
- **Every 60,000 miles**: Spark plugs; coolant inspection and service as applicable; accessory belt check.
- **Every 75,000 to 90,000 miles**: Transmission and differential fluid service where applicable; cooling system service; suspension, steering, and alignment.
- **Every visit or seasonally**: Battery test; tire rotation if non-staggered; set pressures; wiper blades; software updates; visual leak check.

Use the general schedule above as a baseline, then adjust based on CBS alerts, mileage, and conditions. A few smart habits go a long way: set reminders for time-based items like brake fluid, rotate tires if your setup allows, align annually to safeguard run-flat tires and driver-assistance calibrations, and keep a simple maintenance log in your BMW App or glovebox. If your 3 Series is driven mainly in stop-and-go or on short trips, shorten intervals. If it tows, sees spirited canyon drives, track time, or uses staggered performance tires, ask our advisors for a customized plan. Intervals vary by engine, transmission, and model year—including plug-in hybrid variants—so always review your Owner’s Manual and BMW maintenance program, and contact the manufacturer or our service team for details. When you are ready, schedule service or request more information, and we will map out the right plan, provide clear next steps, and keep your BMW 3 Series feeling like The Ultimate Driving Machine.

# BMW SERVICE

BMW recommends you have your maintenance and repair work performed by an authorized BMW center.

# MAINTAINING YOUR BMW VEHICLE

A well-maintained vehicle will help safeguard its operational performance, road-safety and its reliability. This is why it is important to follow and perform BMW’s recommended periodic vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks as indicated by your vehicle’s Maintenance Service Display, along with the other maintenance work described in this booklet.

A improper maintenance is not covered under the BMW New Vehicle Damage, including consequential damage, which results from lack of or Limited Warranty for Passenger Cars and Light Trucks.

# MAINTENANCE INTERVALS

Maintenance intervals on motor vehicles were conventionally based solely on a fixed time period or a specified amount of accumulated driving mileage.

However, operational and driving conditions have a major influence on your vehicle’s routine maintenance requirements; the distance traveled is only one of these significant factors. A vehicle used for short trips in the city with numerous cold starts, prolonged periods of idling, stop-and-go driving, and high engine speeds during acceleration may require more frequent maintenance intervals than a vehicle that is driven long distances at moderate engine speeds.

Your BMW vehicle uses sensors and algorithms together with the elapsed time and the driving distance/profile to monitor and evaluate your vehicle’s maintenance service needs. This information is then used to adapt dynamically the parameters used to forecast the applicable maintenance service task intervals.

# THE BMW MAINTENANCE SYSTEM

All BMW vehicles are equipped with an integrated BMW Maintenance System. This maintenance “reminder” system helps ensure that the vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks are performed at the forecasted intervals that apply to your vehicle.

The BMW Maintenance System display provides the vehicle operator access to the current status information for the following maintenance service tasks:

$\\triangleright$ Engine oil (date and miles)\*

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle check (date and miles)

$\\triangleright$ Front brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Rear brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid (date)

$\\triangleright$ 1200 Mile running-in service (date and miles) (Applicable to BMW M vehicles only)\*

For each specific maintenance service task, either the future date (month/ year), remaining miles or both are provided as noted above. The system monitors variable inputs to forecast the intervals and alert the driver when one or more specific maintenance tasks should be performed.

NOTE: For certain vehicles, the status of the front and rear brake pads will only be observable in the maintenance system’s display when there are approximately 2,000 miles or less remaining before a brake service will be required to be performed.

For information about the vehicle’s maintenance system displays, please refer to the Maintenance Service Display Overview section beginning on page 5.

The following “combine with Engine oil”\* maintenance service tasks may be identified as needing to be performed with a specific occurrence of the “Engine oil” service task (service counter number):

$\\triangleright$ Cabin Microfilter(s)

$\\triangleright$ Engine air filter(s)\*

$\\triangleright$ Spark plugs\*

$\\triangleright$ Final drive oil (Applicable M vehicles only)

\\* Does not apply to BEV

Although these items do not appear in the BMW Maintenance System’s display in the vehicle, these services should be performed when your vehicle’s engine oil is changed in accordance with the interval identified by your vehicle’s BMW Maintenance System.

For more information on your vehicle’s maintenance services requirements, procedures and intervals, please refer the Maintenance Service Summary section beginning on page 10.

The BMW Maintenance System also includes an option to set service reminders for the following state-specific mandatory vehicle inspections, including:

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle safety inspection; and/or $\\triangleright$ Emissions test

The corresponding interval data for these inspections can be inputted into the BMW Maintenance System by a service provider; they are not determined by the vehicle.

For your convenience, you may also wish to have your authorized BMW center perform the work necessary to fulfill these state inspection requirements in your area concurrent with the maintenance services specified above when possible.

Should you request more frequent maintenance service than is indicated by the BMW Maintenance System during the coverage period, the cost of these services will not be covered by the BMW Maintenance Program.

# SERVICE DATA — REMOTE CONTROL KEY

Maintenance service task status information for your BMW vehicle is continually updated and stored in your remote control key.

Your authorized BMW center can access this data and consult with you about applicable service procedures and tasks for your vehicle.

Therefore, always provide your service consultant with the most recent remote control key that was used to operate the vehicle when servicing your vehicle at a BMW center.

# VEHICLE STORAGE

Disconnecting the battery during periods of long-term vehicle storage will interrupt the calculation of time-dependent maintenance services.

In this situation, BMW recommends that you have all your time-based maintenance services, such as brake fluid, engine oil and cabin microfilter, brought up to the correct date by an authorized BMW center.

# ENGINE OIL

2025 model year vehicles with internal-combustion engines are factory-filled with:

Z BMW-approved fully synthetic oil for gasoline engines

Engine oil should be changed when the vehicle’s engine is at operating temperature.

If an engine oil service is being performed or you need to add engine oil between changes, please refer to the Owner’s Manual for the recommended engine oil for your BMW vehicle.

# LONG-TERM RATED FLUIDS AND OILS

The following systems and assemblies are factory-filled with long-term rated fluid and oil; fluid replacement is only necessary when repairs are being performed (unless otherwise noted):

$\\triangleright$ Engine cooling system (antifreeze/coolant) $\\triangleright$ Automatic (except for X1 and X2) and manual transmissions $\\triangleright$ All-wheel drive transfer cases (except when indicated by the vehicle)

# REGULAR CHECKS — VEHICLE OPERATOR

In addition to the maintenance service procedure information contained in this booklet, BMW recommends that you regularly check (when refueling, for example), and address when necessary, the following items:

$\\triangleright$ Washer fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Coolant level

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Tires — pressure, condition and wear

Your [BMW 3 Series](https://www.bmwtigard.com/new-vehicles/3-series/) is a finely-crafted piece of machinery, but it will still require routine service from time to time. Keeping up with the BMW 3 Series [maintenance schedule](https://www.bmwtigard.com/service/service-and-parts-tips/bmw-recommended-maintenance-schedule/) is a must if you want your vehicle to perform at its best for as long as possible. We understand that keeping track of BMW 3 Series oil change intervals and more can be a challenge. That is why we have created this guide to the BMW 3 Series service schedule. Simply follow this guide, and your vehicle should be prepared and safe for the roads of Portland and Tigard.

## BMW 3 Series Service Schedule

The BMW 3 Series service schedule includes BMW 3 Series oil change intervals and more to help you track the maintenance your vehicle requires. Let’s break it down more in-depth below.

### Bi-Annual Services

The services listed below should be performed approximately 6 months after you take your new vehicle home, at the 5,000 to 10,000-mile mark. They should then be performed at least twice a year for the duration you own the vehicle.

- Oil and Filter Change
- Tire Rotation
- Brake Inspection

### Every 30,000 Miles

At the 30,000-mile mark in the BMW 3 Series maintenance schedule, you’ll want to head back to the shop for a variety of inspections and maintenance care checks.

- Air filter changes: Air filters get clogged over time, so at this point, they are no longer working at their best. If you travel in particularly dusty environments, you’ll want to change the filter approximately every 15,000 miles.
- Fuel filter inspection: Your technician can perform a pressure test to determine if the fuel filter needs replacement.

### Every 60,000 Miles

Your 60,000-mile maintenance service will happen at around four or five years into ownership for the average driver. Here is what it will include:

- Brake Rotor, Pads, and Shoes Inspections and Replacements
- Brake Fluid Replacement
- Coolant Replacement
- Transmission Fluid Replacement

Keep in mind that this is also around the time your battery will start wearing down, so it is a good idea to have it looked at and possibly replaced.

### Every 90,000 Miles

At this service interval, we will take care of inspecting hoses, belts, and spark plugs. Power steering fluid should also be replaced when we perform these tasks:

- Timing belt replacement
- Replace hoses
- Replace spark plugs
- Rotate rotors or replace rotors
- Fuel system cleaning
- Complete inspection

## Maintenance Schedule

Keeping up with your vehicle’s routine maintenance schedule is crucial to the health and longevity of your car. Routine maintenance services are done about once or twice a year, and are usually just a quick stop by the shop to change your oil and make sure everything is working properly.

**Here at BMW of Westchester we know how important it is to stay on top of these services in order to keep your car on the streets of Westchester County and Yonkers, NY, for years to come. Check out our breakdown of the BMW 3 Series maintenance schedule below!  [Schedule a service appointment](https://www.westchesterbmw.com/service-appointment/) for more assistance.**

## Annual Routine Maintenance Services

Your first[BMW 3 Series](https://www.westchesterbmw.com/search/new-bmw-3-series-white-plains-ny/?cy=10607&md=33&tp=new) routine maintenance service will happen about 6 months in, or once you hit around 5,000-10,000 miles, whichever happens to come first. This first service will be relatively quick. It will include:

- **An oil and filter change**

- **Tire rotation**

- **Brake inspection**


You’ll want to get these services done once or twice a year for the duration of the vehicle’s life.

Staying on top of your regular oil and oil filter changes is crucial to your car’s health because as your engine runs, tiny bits of dirt and dust will build up in it, which can cause excessive wear and tear.

**Additionally, yearly [tire rotations](https://www.westchesterbmw.com/service-appointment/) are important to maintain traction control, because they prevent your wheels from having uneven tread. Tread and traction control helps your vehicle stop quicker, and provides you with safer travels over rough terrain.**

![](https://dealerimages.dealereprocess.com/image/upload/3734763)

![](https://dealerimages.dealereprocess.com/image/upload/3734769)

## 30,000-Mile Maintenance Services

Once your BMW 3 Series hits 30,000 miles, it’s time to head back to the shop for a variety of inspections and maintenance care checks. To start, you’re going to need:

- **Your air filter changed, over time your air filter can become clogged, and a replacement will be needed in order for it to work at its best. If you travel in particularly dusty environments, you’ll want this changed around 15,000 miles rather than 30,000.**

- **Next, you’ll need your fuel filter inspected; your technician can perform a pressure test to determine if you’ll need it replaced.**


## 60,000-Mile Maintenance Services

Your 60,000-mile maintenance service will happen at around four or five years into ownership for the average driver. At this service, you’ll need:

- **Brake Rotor, Pads, and Shoes Inspections and Replacements**

- **Brake Fluid Replacement**

- **Coolant Replacement**

- **Transmission Fluid Replacement**

- **Your BMW 3 Series battery and brakes will start to wear out around the 60,000-mile mark, which is why it’s so important to get them inspected, and possibly replaced.**


![](https://dealerimages.dealereprocess.com/image/upload/3734756)

![](https://dealerimages.dealereprocess.com/image/upload/3734759)

## 90,000-Mile Maintenance Services

Your 90,000-mile maintenance check will include an inspection of your hoses, belts, and spark plugs. If they’re not up to par, they’ll need to be replaced. Additionally, you’ll also need to replace your power steering fluid to keep your steering wheel working properly. You should also get the following done:

- **Timing belt replacement**

- **Replace hoses**

- **Replace spark plugs**

- **Rotate rotors or replace rotors**

- **Fuel system cleaning**

- **Complete inspection**

## Engine Oil Filter

- Description:
Your Engine Oil Filter does exactly as the name suggests it filtrates the oil in your Nissan engine. As Motor oil circulates through and Reduces friction between engine parts, the filter Captures and traps impurities, so they won't reach your vehicle's engine.
While the engine Maintains your Nissan, it burns fuel and eventually makes things such as sludge and debris. If your vehicle cannot properly filter out these contaminants because you have a grimy or blocked Engine Oil Filter, these contaminants may blend w/ your oil and may lead to very pricey repair costs.
When your Nissan's Engine Oil Filter hasn't been replaced, it can become clogged due to excess excessive gunk. So what happens when an Engine Oil Filter becomes too dirty? Your fuel efficiency and fluid pressure may decLine, and your car's ventilation system may become damaged and begin to emit a burning oil smell.
But when is the best time to get a new Engine Oil Filter installed? Typically, your Engine Oil Filter change should occur as often as you change your engine oil. If you frequently take short trips or if you do tons of interstate driving, it's likely that you will need to change it out more frequently to Maintain your car's engine health.
Are you able to install your Engine Oil Filter on your own? Maybe, but it may require some tricky finagling through the engine in order to find the filter location.
Consult your Nissan owner's Manual before starting to prevent injuring yourself or ruining critical engine pieces. Overall, it may be better to have it installed by a licensed Nissan service center instead.
Help extend the life of your Nissan engine by buying a genuine OEM Engine Oil Filter From Nissan Parts and it will fit your vehicle seamlessly.
