# BMW SERVICE

BMW recommends you have your maintenance and repair work performed by an authorized BMW center.

# MAINTAINING YOUR BMW VEHICLE

A well-maintained vehicle will help safeguard its operational performance, road-safety and its reliability. This is why it is important to follow and perform BMW’s recommended periodic vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks as indicated by your vehicle’s Maintenance Service Display, along with the other maintenance work described in this booklet.

A improper maintenance is not covered under the BMW New Vehicle Damage, including consequential damage, which results from lack of or Limited Warranty for Passenger Cars and Light Trucks.

# MAINTENANCE INTERVALS

Maintenance intervals on motor vehicles were conventionally based solely on a fixed time period or a specified amount of accumulated driving mileage.

However, operational and driving conditions have a major influence on your vehicle’s routine maintenance requirements; the distance traveled is only one of these significant factors. A vehicle used for short trips in the city with numerous cold starts, prolonged periods of idling, stop-and-go driving, and high engine speeds during acceleration may require more frequent maintenance intervals than a vehicle that is driven long distances at moderate engine speeds.

Your BMW vehicle uses sensors and algorithms together with the elapsed time and the driving distance/profile to monitor and evaluate your vehicle’s maintenance service needs. This information is then used to adapt dynamically the parameters used to forecast the applicable maintenance service task intervals.

# THE BMW MAINTENANCE SYSTEM

All BMW vehicles are equipped with an integrated BMW Maintenance System. This maintenance “reminder” system helps ensure that the vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks are performed at the forecasted intervals that apply to your vehicle.

The BMW Maintenance System display provides the vehicle operator access to the current status information for the following maintenance service tasks:

$\\triangleright$ Engine oil (date and miles)\*

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle check (date and miles)

$\\triangleright$ Front brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Rear brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid (date)

$\\triangleright$ 1200 Mile running-in service (date and miles) (Applicable to BMW M vehicles only)\*

For each specific maintenance service task, either the future date (month/ year), remaining miles or both are provided as noted above. The system monitors variable inputs to forecast the intervals and alert the driver when one or more specific maintenance tasks should be performed.

NOTE: For certain vehicles, the status of the front and rear brake pads will only be observable in the maintenance system’s display when there are approximately 2,000 miles or less remaining before a brake service will be required to be performed.

For information about the vehicle’s maintenance system displays, please refer to the Maintenance Service Display Overview section beginning on page 5.

The following “combine with Engine oil”\* maintenance service tasks may be identified as needing to be performed with a specific occurrence of the “Engine oil” service task (service counter number):

$\\triangleright$ Cabin Microfilter(s)

$\\triangleright$ Engine air filter(s)\*

$\\triangleright$ Spark plugs\*

$\\triangleright$ Final drive oil (Applicable M vehicles only)

\\* Does not apply to BEV

Although these items do not appear in the BMW Maintenance System’s display in the vehicle, these services should be performed when your vehicle’s engine oil is changed in accordance with the interval identified by your vehicle’s BMW Maintenance System.

For more information on your vehicle’s maintenance services requirements, procedures and intervals, please refer the Maintenance Service Summary section beginning on page 10.

The BMW Maintenance System also includes an option to set service reminders for the following state-specific mandatory vehicle inspections, including:

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle safety inspection; and/or $\\triangleright$ Emissions test

The corresponding interval data for these inspections can be inputted into the BMW Maintenance System by a service provider; they are not determined by the vehicle.

For your convenience, you may also wish to have your authorized BMW center perform the work necessary to fulfill these state inspection requirements in your area concurrent with the maintenance services specified above when possible.

Should you request more frequent maintenance service than is indicated by the BMW Maintenance System during the coverage period, the cost of these services will not be covered by the BMW Maintenance Program.

# SERVICE DATA — REMOTE CONTROL KEY

Maintenance service task status information for your BMW vehicle is continually updated and stored in your remote control key.

Your authorized BMW center can access this data and consult with you about applicable service procedures and tasks for your vehicle.

Therefore, always provide your service consultant with the most recent remote control key that was used to operate the vehicle when servicing your vehicle at a BMW center.

# VEHICLE STORAGE

Disconnecting the battery during periods of long-term vehicle storage will interrupt the calculation of time-dependent maintenance services.

In this situation, BMW recommends that you have all your time-based maintenance services, such as brake fluid, engine oil and cabin microfilter, brought up to the correct date by an authorized BMW center.

# ENGINE OIL

2025 model year vehicles with internal-combustion engines are factory-filled with:

Z BMW-approved fully synthetic oil for gasoline engines

Engine oil should be changed when the vehicle’s engine is at operating temperature.

If an engine oil service is being performed or you need to add engine oil between changes, please refer to the Owner’s Manual for the recommended engine oil for your BMW vehicle.

# LONG-TERM RATED FLUIDS AND OILS

The following systems and assemblies are factory-filled with long-term rated fluid and oil; fluid replacement is only necessary when repairs are being performed (unless otherwise noted):

$\\triangleright$ Engine cooling system (antifreeze/coolant) $\\triangleright$ Automatic (except for X1 and X2) and manual transmissions $\\triangleright$ All-wheel drive transfer cases (except when indicated by the vehicle)

# REGULAR CHECKS — VEHICLE OPERATOR

In addition to the maintenance service procedure information contained in this booklet, BMW recommends that you regularly check (when refueling, for example), and address when necessary, the following items:

$\\triangleright$ Washer fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Coolant level

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Tires — pressure, condition and wear

Please refer to the Owner’s Manual for additional information.

## Keep Your BMW 2 Series Performing at it's Best

**Basic BMW 2-Series Preventative Maintenance: Every 5,000 Miles**

BMW’s maintenance schedule is built around a standard 5,000-mile interval, guided by your vehicle’s pre-installed Condition-Based Service (CBS) monitor. This intelligent system tracks critical areas of your car and alerts you when additional services are needed.

The regular BMW recommended maintenance schedule includes the following:

- Vehicle check and inspection
- Engine oil check
- Coolant check
- Tire rotation
- Brake fluid check
- Front and rear brake inspection
- Inspection of the engine and cabin air filters
- Wiper blade inspection
- Standard scope

Not every part inspected will need replacement during your visit. Our BMW-certified maintenance experts use the CBS monitor to identify exactly what requires attention, ensuring precise and efficient service.

**BMW 2-Series Recommended Maintenance Services**

Maintenance needs can vary depending on your model and driving habits. For tailored recommendations, consult your owner’s manual or speak with one of our knowledgeable service advisors. Below is a general guideline for BMW 2 Series maintenance milestones:

**BMW 2-Series 10,000-Mile Maintenance**

- Replace the engine oil, oil filter and coolant
- Repeat every 10,000 miles

**BMW 2-Series 20,000-Mile Maintenance**

- Inspect and replace the oil filters
- Repeat every 20,000 miles

**BMW 2-Series 30,000-Mile Maintenance**

- Replace brake fluid. After the first service, schedule brake fluid replacement every 60,000 miles.
- If equipped with a manual transmission, replace transmission fluid every 30,000 miles.

**BMW 2-Series 60,000-mile maintenance**

- Replace the engine air filter and spark plugs
- Inspect and replace brake pads and rotors as needed
- For automatic transmissions, replace the transmission fluid every 60,000 miles.

**BMW 2-Series 90,000-Mile Maintenance**

- Replace the timing belt and hoses
- Repeat every 90,000 miles

**BMW 2-Series Maintenance after 90,000 Miles**

Continue following the BMW 2 Series maintenance schedule with 5,000-mile intervals and adhere to service milestones as listed above to ensure optimal performance.

**BMW 2-Series Recommended Maintenance Services**

Maintenance needs can vary depending on your model and driving habits. For tailored recommendations, consult your owner’s manual or speak with one of our knowledgeable service advisors. Below is a general guideline for BMW 2 Series maintenance milestones:

**BMW 2-Series 10,000-Mile Maintenance**

- Replace the engine oil, oil filter and coolant
- Repeat every 10,000 miles

**BMW 2-Series 20,000-Mile Maintenance**

- Inspect and replace the oil filters
- Repeat every 20,000 miles

**BMW 2-Series 30,000-Mile Maintenance**

- Replace brake fluid. After the first service, schedule brake fluid replacement every 60,000 miles.
- If equipped with a manual transmission, replace transmission fluid every 30,000 miles.

**BMW 2-Series 60,000-mile maintenance**

- Replace the engine air filter and spark plugs
- Inspect and replace brake pads and rotors as needed
- For automatic transmissions, replace the transmission fluid every 60,000 miles.

**BMW 2-Series 90,000-Mile Maintenance**

- Replace the timing belt and hoses
- Repeat every 90,000 miles

**BMW 2-Series Maintenance after 90,000 Miles**

Continue following the BMW 2 Series maintenance schedule with 5,000-mile intervals and adhere to service milestones as listed above to ensure optimal performance.

# BMW iX Maintenance Schedule

### Your Local BMW iX Experts

The BMW iX maintenance schedule is a list of time-based and usage-based service items designed to keep your vehicle reliable and efficient over time. By following the BMW iX maintenance schedule at designated intervals, you can help improve the health and range of your EV, and help prevent small issues from becoming bigger service items down the road. Learn about these essential services below, and book your next service at BMW of Carlsbad

[Schedule Service](https://www.bmwcarlsbad.com/ServiceApptForm.htm)

## BMW iX Service Intervals (2022-Current)

Since the BMW iX is an electric vehicle, it benefits from having fewer required services as compared to a traditional gas-powered vehicle. That being said, servicing your BMW iX at least once every two years is crucial to help identify any issues and inspect wear items such as tires or brakes.

### Time-Based Services

#### Every Two Years (or sooner based on usage)

- **Cabin Air Filter** \- Replace the interior cabin air filter.
- **Brake Fluid** \- Flush and replace brake fluid.
- **Key Fob** \- Replace remote control key battery.
- **Vehicle Check** \- Test basic vehicle functions, inspect tires, top off fluid levels. inspect high-voltage charging port, inspect brakes and lines, and conduct a road test.

#### Every Four Years (or sooner based on usage)

- **Supplemental Vehicle Check** \- Inspect tie rod ends, steering boots and clamps, warning light functionality, and inspect the Mobility Kit components.
- **Cabin Air Filter** \- Replace the interior cabin air filter.
- **Brake Fluid** \- Flush and replace brake fluid.
- **Key Fob** \- Replace remote control key battery.
- **Vehicle Check** \- Test basic vehicle functions, inspect tires, top off fluid levels. inspect high-voltage charging port, inspect brakes and lines, and conduct a road test.

### Condition-Based Services

Based on your overall vehicle usage, which factors in mileage and driving hours, some services will be called out by your vehicle's onboard computer. In addition to the services listed above, the Condition-Based Service system (CBS) will suggest these brake services over time:

- **Front Brakes** \- Replace brake pads and wear sensors, grease mating surfaces, and check front brake disc condition.
- **Rear Brakes** \- Replace brake pads and wear sensors, grease mating surfaces, check front brake disc condition, and test parking brake functions.

# MAINTAINING YOUR BMW VEHICLE

A well-maintained vehicle will help safeguard its operational performance, road-safety and its reliability. This is why it is important to follow and perform BMW’s recommended periodic vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks as indicated by your vehicle’s Maintenance Service Display, along with the other maintenance work described in this booklet.

A improper maintenance is not covered under the BMW New Vehicle Damage, including consequential damage, which results from lack of or Limited Warranty for Passenger Cars and Light Trucks.

# MAINTENANCE INTERVALS

Maintenance intervals on motor vehicles were conventionally based solely on a fixed time period or a specified amount of accumulated driving mileage.

However, operational and driving conditions have a major influence on your vehicle’s routine maintenance requirements; the distance traveled is only one of these significant factors. A vehicle used for short trips in the city with numerous cold starts, prolonged periods of idling, stop-and-go driving, and high engine speeds during acceleration may require more frequent maintenance intervals than a vehicle that is driven long distances at moderate engine speeds.

Your BMW vehicle uses sensors and algorithms together with the elapsed time and the driving distance/profile to monitor and evaluate your vehicle’s maintenance service needs. This information is then used to adapt dynamically the parameters used to forecast the applicable maintenance service task intervals.

# THE BMW MAINTENANCE SYSTEM

All BMW vehicles are equipped with an integrated BMW Maintenance System. This maintenance “reminder” system helps ensure that the vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks are performed at the forecasted intervals that apply to your vehicle.

The BMW Maintenance System display provides the vehicle operator access to the current status information for the following maintenance service tasks:

$\\triangleright$ Engine oil (date and miles)\*

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle check (date and miles)

$\\triangleright$ Front brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Rear brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid (date)

$\\triangleright$ 1200 Mile running-in service (date and miles) (Applicable to BMW M vehicles only)\*

For more information on your vehicle’s maintenance services requirements, procedures and intervals, please refer the Maintenance Service Summary section beginning on page 10.

The BMW Maintenance System also includes an option to set service reminders for the following state-specific mandatory vehicle inspections, including:

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle safety inspection; and/or $\\triangleright$ Emissions test

The corresponding interval data for these inspections can be inputted into the BMW Maintenance System by a service provider; they are not determined by the vehicle.

For your convenience, you may also wish to have your authorized BMW center perform the work necessary to fulfill these state inspection requirements in your area concurrent with the maintenance services specified above when possible.

Should you request more frequent maintenance service than is indicated by the BMW Maintenance System during the coverage period, the cost of these services will not be covered by the BMW Maintenance Program.

# SERVICE DATA — REMOTE CONTROL KEY

Maintenance service task status information for your BMW vehicle is continually updated and stored in your remote control key.

Your authorized BMW center can access this data and consult with you about applicable service procedures and tasks for your vehicle.

Therefore, always provide your service consultant with the most recent remote control key that was used to operate the vehicle when servicing your vehicle at a BMW center.

# VEHICLE STORAGE

Disconnecting the battery during periods of long-term vehicle storage will interrupt the calculation of time-dependent maintenance services.

In this situation, BMW recommends that you have all your time-based maintenance services, such as brake fluid, engine oil and cabin microfilter, brought up to the correct date by an authorized BMW center.

If you’re coming from a gas BMW, the **BMW iX maintenance schedule** can feel almost too simple: no oil changes, no spark plugs, no exhaust system. But “less maintenance” doesn’t mean “no maintenance.” To protect your battery, brakes, warranty, and resale value, especially if you ever plan to sell or trade your iX, you still need a clear plan.

### Good news for iX owners

The BMW iX typically needs a comprehensive check only about every two years, with far fewer wear items than a comparable X5. That saves money over time, if you understand what actually needs attention and when.

## BMW iX maintenance overview

The iX is built like a modern BMW SUV on the outside, but under the skin it’s a very different machine. There’s no engine oil, transmission fluid, or fuel system to service. Most of your scheduled maintenance revolves around **tires**, **brakes**, **cabin filters**, **brake fluid**, and periodic checks of the high‑voltage battery’s cooling system and software.

### BMW iX maintenance at a glance

~50%

Fewer wear items

Compared with a similar gas BMW SUV, because there’s no engine or transmission to service.

2 years

Typical service interval

Most iX cars only need a scheduled inspection and brake fluid service about every two years.

4 yr/50k

New-car warranty

Standard BMW warranty coverage on new iX models in the U.S.

3 yr/36k

Included maintenance

BMW Ultimate Care covers factory‑recommended maintenance for most new BMWs, including EVs.

BMW wraps those tasks into a mix of **time-based** items (like a brake‑fluid flush every two years) and **usage-based** items that depend on how you actually drive. The iX tracks all of this with BMW’s Condition Based Service (CBS) system, so you’re not guessing, or blindly following a generic 5,000‑mile schedule that doesn’t really apply to an EV.

## How the BMW iX maintenance schedule actually works

Unlike older BMWs that followed fixed 7,500‑ or 10,000‑mile intervals, the BMW iX relies on **Condition Based Service (CBS)**. Sensors monitor component wear, fluid age, and your driving style. The car then calculates when a specific service is due and shows it in the iDrive menu and instrument cluster.

### BMW iX Condition Based Service vs. old-school schedules

Why you shouldn’t blindly follow a generic 5,000 or 10,000‑mile reminder

#### Condition Based Service (CBS)

**What the iX uses today**

- Monitors brake wear, fluid age, and time.
- Shows specific items due (e.g., "Brake fluid" or "Vehicle check").
- Intervals can change based on how and where you drive.
- Prevents unnecessary visits triggered by generic mileage emails from dealers.

#### Fixed mileage schedule

**What many owners are used to**

- Every 5,000 or 10,000 miles, regardless of use.
- Designed around engine oil changes and fuel systems.
- Doesn’t reflect EV realities like regenerative braking.
- Can lead to over‑servicing an iX and wasting time and money.

### Ignore generic dealer emails

Many dealers still send automatic “10,000‑mile service due” emails that assume you drive a gas BMW. For an iX, always trust the **service menu in the car** over marketing messages in your inbox.

To see what your iX actually needs, go into the iDrive menu, open **Vehicle status → Service requirements**, and you’ll see a list with due dates and remaining mileage or time for each item. That CBS list is effectively your **personalized BMW iX maintenance schedule**.

## Recommended BMW iX maintenance intervals

Because CBS is personalized, there isn’t a single fixed schedule that covers every BMW iX. But we can outline a realistic baseline for U.S. owners, based on BMW’s EV guidelines and what dealers and owners are actually seeing in 2024–2025.

### Typical BMW iX maintenance intervals (2022–current)

Use this as a planning guide. Always follow what your specific iX shows in the Service menu.

| Interval | What usually happens | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Every 10,000–12,000 miles or 12 months | Tire inspection & possible rotation; basic safety check | More about tire wear than fluids, schedule sooner if you drive hard or long distances. |
| Every 20,000 miles or 2 years | Brake fluid replacement; cabin (pollen) filter; comprehensive inspection | These are the big recurring items for most iX drivers. |
| Every 40,000 miles or 4 years | Additional brake inspections, possible pad/rotor replacement depending on driving style | Many iX owners go longer on pads thanks to regen braking. |
| Around 60,000 miles+ | Coolant check for high‑voltage battery thermal system; possible replacement per BMW guidance | This is less frequent but important for long‑term battery health. |
| As needed | Tires, wiper blades, software updates, alignment, glass, etc. | CBS or your own inspections will flag these. |

Time‑based intervals matter more than mileage for many iX owners, since EVs often see lower annual miles.

### Think in years, not just miles

Plenty of iX owners put only 6,000–8,000 miles per year on the odometer. Even if you’re under the mileage, **time‑based items like brake fluid and cabin filters still age out**. Don’t ignore a two‑year service reminder just because you haven’t hit a mileage milestone.

## BMW iX maintenance checklist by mileage & time

### Practical maintenance checklist for your BMW iX

#### Every month

Check tire pressures (especially before long trips), look for uneven wear, and confirm that there are no warning lights. EVs are heavy; running low tire pressure can eat range and tires quickly.

#### Every 10,000–12,000 miles or 1 year

Have tires inspected and rotated if wear patterns allow, check brake pads and rotors, inspect suspension components and steering, and confirm there are no outstanding software recalls or service campaigns.

#### Every 20,000 miles or 2 years

Schedule a <strong>brake fluid flush</strong>, replace the cabin microfilter / pollen filter, inspect the high‑voltage wiring and connectors, and have a technician review the battery cooling system for leaks or issues.

#### Every 40,000 miles or 4 years

Expect a deeper brake inspection; depending on how much you rely on regenerative braking, you may or may not need pads and rotors. It’s also a good time to check alignment, especially if you’ve hit potholes or curbs.

#### Around 60,000 miles+

Discuss high‑voltage battery coolant service with a BMW EV‑certified shop. Many BMW EV guides treat this as a long‑term item, but if components are replaced, coolant will be changed at that time.

#### Before warranty expires (4 yrs/50k mi)

Have the car thoroughly inspected for any warranty‑eligible issues: minor leaks on the battery cooling system, odd noises, pixel issues in displays, charge‑port door problems, etc.

## Common BMW iX service items explained

### Tires & alignment

The iX is a heavy, high‑torque SUV, and that shows up in tire wear. Staggered wheel setups on some trims limit front‑to‑rear rotation options, so you may be replacing tires sooner than you expected, especially if you run performance rubber or drive aggressively.

- **Check pressures monthly**, especially in winter.
- Ask about **rotation options** for your exact wheel and tire size.
- Do an alignment check if you notice pulling, vibration, or rapid shoulder wear.

### Brakes on an EV

Thanks to **regenerative braking**, the iX can go much longer on brake pads than a comparable gas SUV. But that same light mechanical brake use means the system still needs preventive care.

The BMW iX maintenance schedule is a list of time-based and usage-based service items designed to keep your vehicle reliable and efficient over time. By following the BMW iX maintenance schedule at designated intervals, you can help improve the health and range of your EV, and help prevent small issues from becoming bigger service items down the road. Learn about these essential services below, and book your next service at BMW of Carlsbad

[Schedule Service](https://www.bmwcarlsbad.com/ServiceApptForm.htm)

## BMW iX Service Intervals (2022-Current)

Since the BMW iX is an electric vehicle, it benefits from having fewer required services as compared to a traditional gas-powered vehicle. That being said, servicing your BMW iX at least once every two years is crucial to help identify any issues and inspect wear items such as tires or brakes.

### Time-Based Services

#### Every Two Years (or sooner based on usage)

- **Cabin Air Filter** \- Replace the interior cabin air filter.
- **Brake Fluid** \- Flush and replace brake fluid.
- **Key Fob** \- Replace remote control key battery.
- **Vehicle Check** \- Test basic vehicle functions, inspect tires, top off fluid levels. inspect high-voltage charging port, inspect brakes and lines, and conduct a road test.

#### Every Four Years (or sooner based on usage)

- **Supplemental Vehicle Check** \- Inspect tie rod ends, steering boots and clamps, warning light functionality, and inspect the Mobility Kit components.
- **Cabin Air Filter** \- Replace the interior cabin air filter.
- **Brake Fluid** \- Flush and replace brake fluid.
- **Key Fob** \- Replace remote control key battery.
- **Vehicle Check** \- Test basic vehicle functions, inspect tires, top off fluid levels. inspect high-voltage charging port, inspect brakes and lines, and conduct a road test.

### Condition-Based Services

Based on your overall vehicle usage, which factors in mileage and driving hours, some services will be called out by your vehicle's onboard computer. In addition to the services listed above, the Condition-Based Service system (CBS) will suggest these brake services over time:

- **Front Brakes** \- Replace brake pads and wear sensors, grease mating surfaces, and check front brake disc condition.
- **Rear Brakes** \- Replace brake pads and wear sensors, grease mating surfaces, check front brake disc condition, and test parking brake functions.

# 2025 VW Jetta: Updated Service Recommendations & Tech Calibration

December 22nd, 2025 by[Christian Huckaby](https://www.vwsb.com/author/chuckabymartingp-com/ "Posts by Christian Huckaby")

Share this Post:
Share on FacebookShare on Twitter

_![2024 Volkswagen Jetta](https://di-uploads-pod44.dealerinspire.com/volkswagensanbernardino/uploads/2025/12/dec-19.webp)_

_Last month, a 2024 Jetta came in with its entire IQ.DRIVE safety system disabled after the owner had their windshield replaced at a discount glass shop. The shop installed the glass but never recalibrated the forward-facing camera, leaving the driver without automatic emergency braking, lane keeping assist, or adaptive cruise control for 4,200 miles. The recalibration took two hours and cost $320._ **_The proper calibration that should have been included with windshield replacement? Typically $180-220 when done immediately after glass installation._**

Your 2025 Volkswagen Jetta represents significant technological advancement over previous model years. The updated IQ.DRIVE driver assistance systems, revised engine management software, new electrical architecture, and enhanced safety features all deliver a more sophisticated driving experience than earlier Jettas.

But here’s what catches most Jetta owners completely off guard: these technological improvements come with updated maintenance requirements and calibration needs that differ from previous model years. Following outdated service schedules or ignoring calibration requirements puts your safety systems at risk and potentially voids warranty coverage.

This matters especially in San Bernardino, where our unique driving conditions create specific maintenance challenges. The temperature extremes from desert heat to mountain elevation, stop-and-go traffic on the I-10 and I-215, and air quality all affect how your Jetta needs to be maintained and calibrated.

## **What’s Actually New for 2025**

Your 2025 Jetta features Volkswagen’s latest generation IQ.DRIVE system with enhanced camera resolution, improved processing power, and additional radar coverage. These upgrades deliver better performance in challenging conditions, but they also require more frequent calibration verification than previous systems. The cameras and sensors need to be positioned with extreme precision to function correctly.

The engine management system received significant software updates that affect how the 1.5-liter turbocharged engine delivers power and manages emissions. These updates changed oil consumption patterns, modified fuel injection timing, and adjusted how the engine responds to varying fuel quality. What worked for your 2023 or earlier Jetta doesn’t necessarily apply to your 2025.

Volkswagen updated the electrical architecture with new control modules and revised communication protocols. This affects everything from how software updates are performed to how diagnostic procedures work. Your 2025 Jetta communicates differently with diagnostic equipment than previous models, which is why Volkswagen-specific service becomes more critical than ever.

The brake-by-wire system integration with your IQ.DRIVE features means your braking and safety systems work together in ways previous Jettas didn’t. This integration requires proper calibration after any brake service, wheel alignment, or suspension work to ensure all systems coordinate correctly.

An early adopter brought his 2025 Jetta to us last fall after noticing his adaptive cruise control behaving erratically. The system would brake suddenly when approaching slower traffic, then accelerate too aggressively once traffic cleared. During inspection, we found the forward radar sensor had never been properly calibrated after delivery. The dealership where he purchased the vehicle hadn’t performed the post-delivery calibration procedure required for 2025 models.

**His situation breakdown:**

- Driving for three months with improperly calibrated safety systems
- Adaptive cruise and emergency braking functioning outside parameters
- Increased accident risk from system behavior
- Post-delivery calibration: $280
- Total consequence: Three months of compromised safety plus calibration cost

**What should have happened:**

- Proper post-delivery calibration before customer delivery: included in vehicle prep
- All safety systems functioning as designed from day one: priceless
- Smart total: Zero cost, proper protection from start

## **The Updated Service Schedule You Need**

Your 2025 Jetta follows Volkswagen’s revised maintenance schedule with base intervals of 10,000 miles or one year for oil changes. However, Southern California driving conditions qualify as severe duty in multiple categories, which can modify these intervals significantly. The combination of heat, stop-and-go traffic, and air quality affects service needs.

Every 10,000 miles or annually, your Jetta requires oil and filter service using VW 508 00/509 00 approved synthetic oil. This low-SAPS specification protects your turbocharged engine and emissions equipment. The 2025 model year specifically requires this updated oil specification, which differs slightly from oils used in previous years. Using older specification oils, even if they’re “close,” provides inadequate protection for your engine’s updated components.

_“The biggest confusion we’re seeing with 2025 models is owners assuming nothing changed from their previous Jetta,” says Carlos Mendoza, Lead Technician at our Camino Real location. “They use the same oil, follow the same intervals, ignore calibration needs. Then we find camera systems out of alignment, engine wear from incorrect oil specs, and safety features not working as intended. The 2025 is different enough that old habits create real problems.”_

At each service interval, your IQ.DRIVE system requires verification. This doesn’t mean full recalibration every time, but technicians need to check that cameras are clean, sensors are functioning, and no fault codes are stored. We’ve found systems degrading gradually from dirty cameras or slightly misaligned sensors that owners never noticed until complete failure occurred.

Every 20,000 miles brings comprehensive inspection including brake system evaluation, tire rotation and inspection, cabin air filter replacement, and underbody inspection. Southern California’s unique combination of dust, heat, and occasional rain creates conditions where brake dust accumulation and rotor surface oxidation happen faster than in more humid climates.

At 30,000 miles, your Jetta needs spark plug inspection, engine air filter replacement, and what Volkswagen calls the “major inspection service.” For 2025 models, this service also includes mandatory IQ.DRIVE calibration verification to ensure all safety systems maintain factory specifications. This comprehensive service typically runs $450-650 depending on what’s actually needed.

Every 40,000 miles, if equipped with the DSG transmission, fluid service becomes due. The conventional six-speed automatic doesn’t require service until 60,000 miles under normal conditions, but severe duty operation can shorten this interval. Your brake fluid needs testing for moisture content, which accumulates even in dry climates from temperature cycling.

## **The IQ.DRIVE Calibration Reality**

Your 2025 Jetta’s IQ.DRIVE system includes forward collision warning with automatic emergency braking, lane keeping assist, blind spot monitoring, and rear traffic alert. These features rely on cameras and radar sensors that must be positioned with extreme precision to function correctly. Even slight misalignment causes system degradation or complete failure.

# How Often Should You Change Your Mercedes-Benz Oil in Bedford, OH?

![Blue Mercedes-Benz C-Class](https://di-uploads-pod7.dealerinspire.com/mercedesbenzofbedford/uploads/2019/11/Blue-Mercedes-Benz-C-Class-1024x298.png)

## How Often Do You Need a Mercedes-Benz Oil Change?

Most Mercedes-Benz vehicles require an oil change every 10,000 miles or once per year, whichever comes first. This interval applies to newer models equipped with synthetic oil, which offers longer-lasting protection compared to conventional oil. However, driving conditions, climate, and vehicle age may require more frequent service.

At Mercedes-Benz of Bedford, we recommend following the specific guidelines found in your owner’s manual and checking with our certified technicians to create a maintenance schedule that fits your lifestyle.

## What Are Signs That You Need an Oil Change?

Even if you haven’t reached the 10,000-mile mark, certain signs may indicate it’s time to schedule Mercedes-Benz oil change service in Bedford, OH:

- Dashboard oil warning light appears.
- Engine is louder than usual or knocks when accelerating.
- Oil looks dark or gritty on the dipstick.
- You smell burning oil under the hood.
- Reduced fuel efficiency or sluggish performance.

If you experience any of these, it’s time to check your Mercedes-Benz oil and book service promptly to avoid long-term engine damage.

## What Impacts Your Oil Change Schedule?

While the 10,000-mile rule is a general benchmark, some situations may require more frequent changes. You may need an oil change sooner if you:

- Frequently drive in stop-and-go traffic or short trips.
- Tow heavy loads or drive in high temperatures.
- Experience cold starts during Ohio winters.
- Have an older or high-mileage Mercedes-Benz model.

For peace of mind, our service team will inspect your oil, filters, and service records during your visit and recommend the best timing based on your vehicle’s needs.

## Why Choose Mercedes-Benz of Bedford for Oil Change Service?

When it comes to protecting your engine and preserving performance, trust the experts at Mercedes-Benz of Bedford:

- Factory-trained technicians using Mercedes-Benz approved synthetic oil.
- OEM filters and parts designed specifically for your model.
- Complimentary multi-point inspections with every visit.
- Online service scheduling and flexible appointment times.
- Transparent pricing and Service A / B package options.

Your luxury vehicle deserves nothing less than certified Mercedes-Benz service—and we’re here to deliver it.

## Schedule Your Mercedes-Benz Oil Change in Bedford, OH

Regular oil changes are one of the most important steps in preserving your Mercedes-Benz. If you’re due—or unsure—contact Mercedes-Benz of Bedford today. Schedule service online, or speak to one of our specialists for personalized guidance.

## Mercedes-Benz Service A & Mercedes-Benz Service B

At 12 months or 10,000 miles, you’ll need to take your vehicle in for Mercedes-Benz Service A. At 24 months or 20,000 miles, it’s time for Mercedes-Benz Service B. From there, you’ll rotate each time, switching off between the two at 12-month/10,000-mile increments. **It’s vital that you stick to your service schedule**. After all, your Mercedes-Benz is a lucrative investment, and without a consistent service record, your vehicle depreciates much more quickly.

# Choosing The Proper Engine Coolant For Your Mercedes

[![FCP Euro](https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/blt75c85f063ac4ae63/bltc4a28df56e6b0f77/69badf2b321ab582e6603c15/2025_More_Parts_More_Support_Website_Banner_2098x250.jpg?width=1000&format=webp)](https://www.fcpeuro.com/current_car)

Choosing the correct fluids for your car is one of the most daunting tasks for a new DIYer. The local auto parts store will have walls lined with oils, solvents, and fluids as far as the eye can see without the definitive information you need. Choosing the right engine coolant is no different. Is it the green kind or the pink kind? Maybe the blue one? In [Mercedes](https://www.fcpeuro.com/Mercedes~Benz-parts/)’ case, it could be any of the three depending on which engine you have. Coolant composition has changed over the years as engine system materials have evolved for better efficiency, so you’ll need to know which one is for your Mercedes before topping up your cooling system.

## What Are Antifreeze & Coolant?

Every diesel and gasoline-powered engine contains a constant series of small explosions while running. The fuel igniting in the cylinders creates the power that drives the car and sends us on our way, but as you might imagine, those explosions make things hot. Those explosions can weaken and warp the metal around it if left long enough, effectively destroying the engine components. Coolant and cooling systems prevent that, so your engine can last as long as it’s taken care of.

Circulating through the radiator of your Mercedes-Benz or Mercedes-AMG is a mixture of distilled water and antifreeze. The terms coolant and antifreeze aren’t as interchangeable as some believe, but their use in a given situation will usually get the point across. In official Mercedes terms, coolant is the blend of antifreeze and water needed to keep engines at their optimal operating temperature in all weather conditions. Antifreeze is a unique blend of concentrated chemicals that lowers the freezing point and raises the boiling point of water. It also has a few chemicals that prevent corrosion which is especially important when mixed with non-distilled water. There is [**much more to coolant**](https://www.fcpeuro.com/blog/how-to-pick-the-right-coolant-for-your-car) than those basics, but just know that you’ll likely be fine as long as there’s enough coolant in your system and it’s not leaking out.

![](https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/blt75c85f063ac4ae63/blt3a4faecfe45d1f27/65f8b1b7151cf37fa17dc7dc/450sl_coolant_1.jpg)

Low engine coolant or a leaky system can be detrimental to your engine’s health, especially turbocharged engines. Turbochargers and other forms of forced induction create far more heat than a normally aspirated one, making a case for a properly functioning cooling system that is much more important. A cooling line or pipe crack can introduce air into the system and let coolant leak out. The system’s newly introduced air will likely get trapped, causing a part of the engine to experience significantly more heat than the rest.

A low coolant level is a much easier fix than a cracked pipe, but it still requires knowing which coolant you need and how you’ll have to prepare it.

## Which Coolant Does My Mercedes Take?

Just about every Mercedes engine in the last 25 years will take one of two possible coolant specifications, according to Mercedes. The difference between them resides in a couple of chemicals that have been removed from the newer coolant specification: Borate and 2- 2- ethyl hexanoic acid, to be specific. The new coolant is compatible with older engines, but the old formulation shouldn’t be used in a newer application.

Mercedes also has a funky way of labeling their coolants. The most important identifying number is the one after the decimal. The earlier ones, 325 and 326, signify whether you’re buying a jug of concentrated antifreeze or pre-mixed coolant, respectively. Concentrated antifreeze must be diluted 50/50 with water before finding its way into a cooling system. Running pure antifreeze is not recommended as it can cause engine damage, so read carefully before purchase.

### Mercedes Specification [**325.0/326.0**](https://www.fcpeuro.com/Parts/?keywords=325.0)

The Mercedes 325.0 specification coolant was the standard formula during the early ’00s. It was a Hybrid Organic Acid Technology (HOAT) formula that Mercedes used right up until the 2014 model year. Any engine built after that will use the coolant listed in the next section. You can convert the pre-2015 engines to the newer coolant style; however, that takes an entire system flush and refill, which can be expensive and time-consuming.

![Choosing The Proper Engine Coolant For Your Mercedes](https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/blt75c85f063ac4ae63/bltd16fc0c7eab25b1e/65f8b1b80c5eaed6d7e3f48c/Screenshot_33.jpg)

The original formula from Mercedes, a yellow color, carried the Q1030002 part number and was interchangeable with a G05-type coolant. Mercedes has since introduced a new, blue-colored antifreeze as a replacement that carries the Q1030004 part number and is interchangeable with a G48-spec antifreeze. You can mix the two in a pinch, but the yellow stuff hasn’t been sold for the last decade. Seriously consider draining and refilling your cooling system if your coolant is that old; its cooling and anticorrosion properties have deteriorated.

#### 325.0/326.0-Compatible Engines (Pre-2014):

- M111/112/113
- M266
- M27X
- OM607/608
- OM611/612/613
- OM622.9
- OM628/629
- OM639
- OM640
- OM642
- OM653

### Mercedes Specification [**325.6/326.6**](https://www.fcpeuro.com/Parts/?keywords=325.5)

Following an emission update banning particular chemicals from automotive use, Mercedes revised their engine coolant formula in line with the new regulations. The new formula uses a Si-OAT (Silicate Organic Additive Technology) compound free of the borates in the .0-spec antifreeze. This pink-colored coolant originally carried the 325.5 and 326.5 designations before being superseded with the .6 formula and remains the current standard in the Mercedes-Benz and Mercedes-AMG engines. If you can’t get your hands on the official Mercedes stuff, any G40-spec coolant should do the trick.

![Mercedes Coolant Reservoir](https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/blt75c85f063ac4ae63/bltf0fbc9a676fc8025/65f8b1b9fcf4c030cdd34ecd/Mercedes_Coolant_Reservoir.jpg)

The older Q1030004, G48-spec stuff can be used in a newer engine like these, but only if the cooling system is completely drained and refilled. We strongly advise against mixing the two, which can lead to damaged cooling system components.

#### 325.6/326.6-Compatible Engines (2014-Present):

- M111/112/113
- M133
- M137
- M139
- M15X
- M176
- M177
- M178 (AMG GT Black Series Excluded)
- M254
- M256
- M260
- M264
- M266
- M27X
- M282
- OM607/608
- OM611/612/613
- OM622.8
- OM622.9
- OM626
- OM628/629
- OM639
- OM640
- OM642
- OM653
- OM654
- OM656

## What Kind Of Coolant Should I Use?

As we know, not all engine coolants are identical. Different cars require different formulas with different colors to meet the manufacturer’s specifications. However, once you determine which formula you need, you can choose whichever brand you’d like. We offer the latest specification stuff in its concentrated form in a gallon jug. EVs skip oil changes and timing belts, but that doesn’t mean they’re maintenance‑free, especially when you’re shopping used. ### Quick takeaway Audi recommends time‑ and mileage‑based service for the e-tron GT, with major inspections roughly every 2 years/20,000 miles, regular brake fluid changes, cabin filters, and detailed high‑voltage system checks. Tires, brakes, and suspension still matter just as much as any performance Audi. ## How Audi e-tron GT maintenance works The e-tron GT is built like a high‑performance Audi but maintained like a modern EV. Instead of the familiar A6 or S5 routine of **oil changes every 10,000 miles**, the electric GT leans on long inspection intervals and software‑driven checks. The car’s service reminder in the cockpit display is your referee, counting down to the next visit based on time and mileage. - There’s no engine oil, spark plugs, or exhaust system to service. - The big-ticket item, the high‑voltage battery, is monitored constantly by onboard software. - Most scheduled visits center around inspections, filters, fluids, tires, and brake components. - Audi typically structures service as flexible inspections rather than long lists of parts to replace. ### Tip for first-time EV owners On an e-tron GT, time matters as much as miles. Even if you only drive a few thousand miles a year, you’ll still want those 2‑year inspections for things like brake fluid, seals, and suspension wear. ## Audi e-tron GT maintenance schedule overview Exact intervals can vary slightly by model year and market, but most Audi e-tron GT schedules in the U.S. follow this general rhythm. Always confirm with the owner’s manual or Audi dealer for your specific VIN, but this overview will get you 95% of the way there. ![Audi e-tron GT on a lift in a service bay during a scheduled inspection](https://recharged.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fd365moeqy2c2l.cloudfront.net%2Fimages%2Fcontent%2Feebb01bf70db2e32ec581d22b03e813e-content.png&w=3840&q=75) Most e-tron GT scheduled services are inspections and fluid checks rather than big mechanical repairs. ### Audi e-tron GT service interval table Common U.S. market inspection and replacement intervals for key e-tron GT maintenance items. Always verify against the service booklet for your car. | Interval (time / miles) | What usually happens | EV‑specific notes | | --- | --- | --- | | Every 1 year / 10,000 miles | General inspection, tire rotation, visual brake check, fluids top‑off | High‑voltage cables and underbody shield visually checked. | | Every 2 years / 20,000 miles | Comprehensive inspection, brake fluid change, cabin filter replacement | High‑voltage system and battery cooling circuit checked with diagnostics. | | Every 3 years | Air conditioning service check, refrigerant leak inspection | Heat pump and battery thermal management performance evaluated. | | Every 4 years / ~40,000 miles | More detailed suspension/steering check, alignment check recommended | Extra attention to weight‑related wear on tires, bushings, and control arms. | | Every 6 years / 60,000+ miles | Possible coolant exchange depending on Audi guidance and climate | Battery coolant condition and thermal system capacity reviewed. | | As needed | Tires, brake pads/rotors, wiper blades, 12‑V battery | Tire wear can be quicker than on non‑performance EVs; regen doesn’t eliminate brake service. | Intervals shown are typical guidelines; local schedules and warranty plans may differ. ## Key maintenance items on the Audi e-tron GT, explained ### What your e-tron GT actually needs serviced Think inspections and wear items, not constant fluid changes. #### Annual inspections Audi techs scan for software faults, check steering and suspension, inspect axle boots and underbody panels, and look for leaks or physical damage to the high‑voltage system. #### Brake fluid & hydraulics Even with strong regenerative braking, the car still relies on a conventional hydraulic system. Fluid ages with time and moisture and typically gets replaced about every 2 years. #### Cabin & 12‑V battery The high‑voltage pack powers the car, but the 12‑V battery runs control modules. Expect conventional 12‑V battery replacement every few years plus cabin air filter changes for clean HVAC performance. Beyond those basics, expect the usual wear items: tires, wiper blades, and, over time, brake pads and rotors. Because the e-tron GT is heavy and very quick, it can chew through tires faster than a regular sedan, especially on performance rubber. ### Don’t skip tire rotations With dual‑motor all‑wheel drive and instant torque, uneven tire wear can sneak up on you. Regular rotations (often every 5,000–10,000 miles) keep the car tracking straight and protect those expensive 20‑ or 21‑inch tires. ## Battery health checks for the e-tron GT The high‑voltage battery is the e-tron GT’s heart and its most expensive single component. Day to day, you’ll see only a percentage and range estimate on the dash, but during scheduled service Audi technicians can pull detailed diagnostic data, including fault codes, temperature behavior, and any cell‑level issues. ### What Audi checks at service - Battery control module fault codes and thermal alerts. - Cooling system performance and coolant level/condition. - High‑voltage wiring and connectors for damage or corrosion. - Sealing and underbody protection around the pack. ### What you can watch at home - Sudden loss of range with the same driving pattern. - Charging behavior that’s much slower than usual on the same charger. - Warning lights related to the electrical system or drive system. - Unusual fan noise or frequent cooling activity when parked. ### How Recharged helps on used e-tron GTs Every EV sold through Recharged includes a **Recharged Score Report** with verified battery health, so you’re not guessing how the last owner treated the pack. That’s a big advantage over a generic used‑car inspection. ## Typical Audi e-tron GT maintenance costs You’re driving a flagship Audi, so service visits won’t be bargain‑basement. The good news is that **EVs shift more of your budget from maintenance to tires** rather than piling on fluid changes and engine work. Actual prices vary by dealer and region, but this is a realistic way to think about costs in the U.S. ### Typical U.S. e-tron GT maintenance and wear costs $200–$350 Minor visit Basic inspection with cabin filter and rotation at an Audi dealer. $400–$800 Major service 2‑year/20,000‑mile type visit with brake fluid and deeper checks. $1,200–$2,000+ Tire set High‑performance 20–21" tires, including mounting and alignment. Low Drivetrain upkeep No timing belt, spark plugs, or engine oil changes vs gas Audi. ### Budgeting tip If you’re planning long‑term ownership, set aside a tire fund and assume one major service every 2 years. Compared with a V6 or V8 Audi, you’re likely to come out ahead over 5–7 years of driving. ## Maintenance differences: e-tron GT vs gas Audi If you’re coming out of a gas‑powered S or RS model, the e-tron GT will feel strangely low‑maintenance. Even if you only drive a few thousand miles a year, you’ll still want those 2‑year inspections for things like brake fluid, seals, and suspension wear. ## Audi e-tron GT maintenance schedule overview Exact intervals can vary slightly by model year and market, but most Audi e-tron GT schedules in the U.S. follow this general rhythm. Always confirm with the owner’s manual or Audi dealer for your specific VIN, but this overview will get you 95% of the way there. ![Audi e-tron GT on a lift in a service bay during a scheduled inspection](https://recharged.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fd365moeqy2c2l.cloudfront.net%2Fimages%2Fcontent%2Feebb01bf70db2e32ec581d22b03e813e-content.png&w=3840&q=75) Most e-tron GT scheduled services are inspections and fluid checks rather than big mechanical repairs. ### Audi e-tron GT service interval table Common U.S. market inspection and replacement intervals for key e-tron GT maintenance items. Always verify against the service booklet for your car. | Interval (time / miles) | What usually happens | EV‑specific notes | | --- | --- | --- | | Every 1 year / 10,000 miles | General inspection, tire rotation, visual brake check, fluids top‑off | High‑voltage cables and underbody shield visually checked. | | Every 2 years / 20,000 miles | Comprehensive inspection, brake fluid change, cabin filter replacement | High‑voltage system and battery cooling circuit checked with diagnostics. | | Every 3 years | Air conditioning service check, refrigerant leak inspection | Heat pump and battery thermal management performance evaluated. | | Every 4 years / ~40,000 miles | More detailed suspension/steering check, alignment check recommended | Extra attention to weight‑related wear on tires, bushings, and control arms. | | Every 6 years / 60,000+ miles | Possible coolant exchange depending on Audi guidance and climate | Battery coolant condition and thermal system capacity reviewed. | | As needed | Tires, brake pads/rotors, wiper blades, 12‑V battery | Tire wear can be quicker than on non‑performance EVs; regen doesn’t eliminate brake service. | Intervals shown are typical guidelines; local schedules and warranty plans may differ. ## Key maintenance items on the Audi e-tron GT, explained ### What your e-tron GT actually needs serviced Think inspections and wear items, not constant fluid changes. #### Annual inspections Audi techs scan for software faults, check steering and suspension, inspect axle boots and underbody panels, and look for leaks or physical damage to the high‑voltage system. #### Brake fluid & hydraulics Even with strong regenerative braking, the car still relies on a conventional hydraulic system. Fluid ages with time and moisture and typically gets replaced about every 2 years. #### Cabin & 12‑V battery The high‑voltage pack powers the car, but the 12‑V battery runs control modules. Expect conventional 12‑V battery replacement every few years plus cabin air filter changes for clean HVAC performance. Beyond those basics, expect the usual wear items: tires, wiper blades, and, over time, brake pads and rotors. Because the e-tron GT is heavy and very quick, it can chew through tires faster than a regular sedan, especially on performance rubber. ### Don’t skip tire rotations With dual‑motor all‑wheel drive and instant torque, uneven tire wear can sneak up on you. Regular rotations (often every 5,000–10,000 miles) keep the car tracking straight and protect those expensive 20‑ or 21‑inch tires. ## Battery health checks for the e-tron GT The high‑voltage battery is the e-tron GT’s heart and its most expensive single component. Day to day, you’ll see only a percentage and range estimate on the dash, but during scheduled service Audi technicians can pull detailed diagnostic data, including fault codes, temperature behavior, and any cell‑level issues. ### What Audi checks at service - Battery control module fault codes and thermal alerts. - Cooling system performance and coolant level/condition. - High‑voltage wiring and connectors for damage or corrosion. - Sealing and underbody protection around the pack. ### What you can watch at home - Sudden loss of range with the same driving pattern. - Charging behavior that’s much slower than usual on the same charger. - Warning lights related to the electrical system or drive system. - Unusual fan noise or frequent cooling activity when parked. ### How Recharged helps on used e-tron GTs Every EV sold through Recharged includes a **Recharged Score Report** with verified battery health, so you’re not guessing how the last owner treated the pack. That’s a big advantage over a generic used‑car inspection. ## Typical Audi e-tron GT maintenance costs You’re driving a flagship Audi, so service visits won’t be bargain‑basement. The good news is that **EVs shift more of your budget from maintenance to tires** rather than piling on fluid changes and engine work. Actual prices vary by dealer and region, but this is a realistic way to think about costs in the U.S. ### Typical U.S. e-tron GT maintenance and wear costs $200–$350 Minor visit Basic inspection with cabin filter and rotation at an Audi dealer. $400–$800 Major service 2‑year/20,000‑mile type visit with brake fluid and deeper checks. $1,200–$2,000+ Tire set High‑performance 20–21" tires, including mounting and alignment. Low Drivetrain upkeep No timing belt, spark plugs, or engine oil changes vs gas Audi. ### Budgeting tip If you’re planning long‑term ownership, set aside a tire fund and assume one major service every 2 years. Compared with a V6 or V8 Audi, you’re likely to come out ahead over 5–7 years of driving. ## Maintenance differences: e-tron GT vs gas Audi If you’re coming out of a gas‑powered S or RS model, the e-tron GT will feel strangely low‑maintenance. # 2024 Volkswagen Tiguan Maintenance Schedule

![hero image](https://dealerimages.dealereprocess.com/image/upload/3483350)

# 2024 Volkswagen Tiguan Maintenance Schedule

The 2024 Volkswagen Tiguan is crafted for long-term reliability, but to keep it performing at its
best, regular maintenance is essential. Routine service tasks not only extend your Tiguan’s lifespan
but also ensure your peace of mind. By bringing your SUV in for scheduled check-ups, our skilled
technicians can identify and resolve potential issues early, preventing them from escalating into
more significant problems and saving you time and money.

![](https://dealerimages.dealereprocess.com/image/upload/3483347)

[Schedule Service](https://www.pohankavw.com/online-service-scheduler/)

## 10,000-Mile Maintenance

According to the Volkswagen maintenance schedule, your 2024 Tiguan recommends minor maintenance every
10,000 miles. If you drive in severe weather, tow a trail often, or otherwise operate the vehicle under
more rigorous than average conditions, more frequent maintenance may be advisable (when in doubt, ask
your service advisor). This visit is straightforward, consisting of a tire rotation and oil (and oil
filter) change.

## 20,000-Mile Maintenance

This will be a repeat of the 10,000-mile service (tire rotation and oil change). If your Tiguan has a
sunroof, the drains need to be cleaned and inspected for blockage at this service interval (every 20,000
miles or 2 years, whichever occurs first).

## 30,000-Mile Maintenance

For this appointment, technicians repeat the 10,000-mile minor maintenance schedule, consisting of an
engine oil/filter change and tire rotation.

## 40,000-Mile Maintenance

This service combines the 10,000- and 20,000-mile visits, with a couple of additional tasks:

- change engine oil/filter
- rotate tires
- clean sunroof drains and lubricate panoramic sliding sunroof
- replace in-cabin air filter replacement (every 40,000 miles or two years, whichever comes first)


## 50,000-Mile Maintenance

This visit calls for a repeat of the 10,000-mile service, consisting of an engine oil and filter change
plus a tire rotation.

## 60,000-Mile Maintenance

This visit repeats the 10,000- and 20,000-mile services, with one additional task: replacing the engine
air filter replaced and cleaning its screen.

## 70,000-Mile Maintenance

As another 10,000-mile interval, this visit calls for just a tire rotation and oil change.

## 80,000-Mile Maintenance

Along with the 10,000-, 20,000-, and 40,000-mile services, a couple more tasks are added in at this time.
Altogether, now is the time to perform the following:

- change engine oil/filter
- rotate tire
- clean sunroof drains
- replace in-cabin air filter
- clean and grease panoramic sliding sunroof
- change spark plugs
- drain and replace automatic transmission fluid

## 90,000-Mile Maintenance

The 90,000-mile service is simple, consisting of a tire rotation and engine oil/filter change.

## 100,000-Mile Maintenance

You’ve reached your first 100K miles with your Tiguan: congratulations! The 10,000- and 20,000-mile
intervals will be repeated at this time. Our technicians will change the oil and perform a tire
rotation. If your Tiguan has a sunroof, its drains will also be cleaned.

## 110,000-Mile Maintenance

Minor servicing occurs at this point, with a straightforward oil and filter change and tire rotation.

## 120,000-Mile Maintenance

This more extensive service interval combines the 40,000- and 60,000-mile tasks:

- rotate tires
- clean sunroof drains
- change engine oil and filter
- replace engine air filter and clean the screen
- clean and grease panorama sliding sunroof
- replace in-cabin dust/pollen filter

## Post-120K Miles & Time-Based Services

Your Tiguan has been built for longevity, and continued maintenance will keep it running well through
more significant milestones. After 120,000 miles, the same task intervals apply, with a few additional
requirements recommended, as well as time-based services. For example:

- Replace coolant pump toothed belt every 180,000 miles.
- Change AWD clutch fluid (if equipped) every 3 years.
- Replace tire filler bottle in mobility kit every 4 years.
- Change brake fluid every 2 years (after the first 3 years).

## Regular Inspections (Every Visit)

During every maintenance appointment, our factory-trained Volkswagen technicians will perform a complete
inspection of your Tiguan’s major components. They will check that the vehicle is operating as intended
and make sure that any issues they detect are corrected before they become more serious. Here are some
of the components and systems that are routinely inspected:

- brake system (pad thickness, rotor wear, brake lines, fluid levels, etc.)
- interior lights and electronics
- tire tread/wear
- battery
- windshield, wipers, and washer fluid
- exterior lighting
- horn
- suspension system (ball joints, control arms, stabilizer bar, struts, springs, bearings, etc.)
- cooling system
- air conditioning/heater
- exhaust system
- transmission fluid
- chassis
- steering system

## What Does the BMW Maintenance Schedule Include?

BMW maintenance is broken down into intervals, based on time or mileage. Below are general service milestones for most BMW models:

### BMW 10,000-Mile Maintenance

- At 10,000 miles or 12 months, schedule an oil change, brake inspection, and tire rotation.

### BMW 20,000-Mile Maintenance

- At 20,000 miles, replace the cabin air filter and perform a more comprehensive inspection.

### BMW 30,000-Mile Maintenance

- At 30,000-40,000 miles, inspect suspension, steering components, coolant, and belts.
- If manual transmission: replace [transmission fluid](https://www.bmwofturnersville.com/service/service-tips/check-your-transmission-fluid/) every 30,000 miles

### BMW 60,000-Mile Maintenance

- At 60,000 miles, flush and replace brake fluid, inspect spark plugs, and change the engine air filter.

### Additional BMW Maintenance

Every two years, replace the cabin microfilter and test battery performance.

Additional services like coolant flushes, differential fluid replacement, or transmission service may vary depending on your BMW model and driving habits.

We recommend checking your BMW iDrive system or owner’s manual, or speaking with a certified technician at our Turnersville location, for a custom plan.

# BMW SERVICE

BMW recommends you have your maintenance and repair work performed by an authorized BMW center.

# MAINTAINING YOUR BMW VEHICLE

A well-maintained vehicle will help safeguard its operational performance, road-safety and its reliability. This is why it is important to follow and perform BMW’s recommended periodic vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks as indicated by your vehicle’s Maintenance Service Display, along with the other maintenance work described in this booklet.

A improper maintenance is not covered under the BMW New Vehicle Damage, including consequential damage, which results from lack of or Limited Warranty for Passenger Cars and Light Trucks.

# MAINTENANCE INTERVALS

Maintenance intervals on motor vehicles were conventionally based solely on a fixed time period or a specified amount of accumulated driving mileage.

However, operational and driving conditions have a major influence on your vehicle’s routine maintenance requirements; the distance traveled is only one of these significant factors. A vehicle used for short trips in the city with numerous cold starts, prolonged periods of idling, stop-and-go driving, and high engine speeds during acceleration may require more frequent maintenance intervals than a vehicle that is driven long distances at moderate engine speeds.

Your BMW vehicle uses sensors and algorithms together with the elapsed time and the driving distance/profile to monitor and evaluate your vehicle’s maintenance service needs. This information is then used to adapt dynamically the parameters used to forecast the applicable maintenance service task intervals.

# THE BMW MAINTENANCE SYSTEM

All BMW vehicles are equipped with an integrated BMW Maintenance System. This maintenance “reminder” system helps ensure that the vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks are performed at the forecasted intervals that apply to your vehicle.

The BMW Maintenance System display provides the vehicle operator access to the current status information for the following maintenance service tasks:

$\\triangleright$ Engine oil (date and miles)\*

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle check (date and miles)

$\\triangleright$ Front brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Rear brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid (date)

$\\triangleright$ 1200 Mile running-in service (date and miles) (Applicable to BMW M vehicles only)\*

For each specific maintenance service task, either the future date (month/ year), remaining miles or both are provided as noted above. The system monitors variable inputs to forecast the intervals and alert the driver when one or more specific maintenance tasks should be performed.

NOTE: For certain vehicles, the status of the front and rear brake pads will only be observable in the maintenance system’s display when there are approximately 2,000 miles or less remaining before a brake service will be required to be performed.

For information about the vehicle’s maintenance system displays, please refer to the Maintenance Service Display Overview section beginning on page 5.

The following “combine with Engine oil”\* maintenance service tasks may be identified as needing to be performed with a specific occurrence of the “Engine oil” service task (service counter number):

$\\triangleright$ Cabin Microfilter(s)

$\\triangleright$ Engine air filter(s)\*

$\\triangleright$ Spark plugs\*

$\\triangleright$ Final drive oil (Applicable M vehicles only)

\\* Does not apply to BEV

Although these items do not appear in the BMW Maintenance System’s display in the vehicle, these services should be performed when your vehicle’s engine oil is changed in accordance with the interval identified by your vehicle’s BMW Maintenance System.

For more information on your vehicle’s maintenance services requirements, procedures and intervals, please refer the Maintenance Service Summary section beginning on page 10.

The BMW Maintenance System also includes an option to set service reminders for the following state-specific mandatory vehicle inspections, including:

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle safety inspection; and/or $\\triangleright$ Emissions test

The corresponding interval data for these inspections can be inputted into the BMW Maintenance System by a service provider; they are not determined by the vehicle.

For your convenience, you may also wish to have your authorized BMW center perform the work necessary to fulfill these state inspection requirements in your area concurrent with the maintenance services specified above when possible.

Should you request more frequent maintenance service than is indicated by the BMW Maintenance System during the coverage period, the cost of these services will not be covered by the BMW Maintenance Program.

# SERVICE DATA — REMOTE CONTROL KEY

Maintenance service task status information for your BMW vehicle is continually updated and stored in your remote control key.

Your authorized BMW center can access this data and consult with you about applicable service procedures and tasks for your vehicle.

Therefore, always provide your service consultant with the most recent remote control key that was used to operate the vehicle when servicing your vehicle at a BMW center.

# VEHICLE STORAGE

Disconnecting the battery during periods of long-term vehicle storage will interrupt the calculation of time-dependent maintenance services.

In this situation, BMW recommends that you have all your time-based maintenance services, such as brake fluid, engine oil and cabin microfilter, brought up to the correct date by an authorized BMW center.

# ENGINE OIL

2025 model year vehicles with internal-combustion engines are factory-filled with:

Z BMW-approved fully synthetic oil for gasoline engines

Engine oil should be changed when the vehicle’s engine is at operating temperature.

If an engine oil service is being performed or you need to add engine oil between changes, please refer to the Owner’s Manual for the recommended engine oil for your BMW vehicle.

# LONG-TERM RATED FLUIDS AND OILS

The following systems and assemblies are factory-filled with long-term rated fluid and oil; fluid replacement is only necessary when repairs are being performed (unless otherwise noted):

$\\triangleright$ Engine cooling system (antifreeze/coolant) $\\triangleright$ Automatic (except for X1 and X2) and manual transmissions $\\triangleright$ All-wheel drive transfer cases (except when indicated by the vehicle)

# REGULAR CHECKS — VEHICLE OPERATOR

In addition to the maintenance service procedure information contained in this booklet, BMW recommends that you regularly check (when refueling, for example), and address when necessary, the following items:

$\\triangleright$ Washer fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Coolant level

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Tires — pressure, condition and wear

Please refer to the Owner’s Manual for additional information.

## Keep Your BMW 2 Series Performing at it's Best

**Basic BMW 2-Series Preventative Maintenance: Every 5,000 Miles**

BMW’s maintenance schedule is built around a standard 5,000-mile interval, guided by your vehicle’s pre-installed Condition-Based Service (CBS) monitor. This intelligent system tracks critical areas of your car and alerts you when additional services are needed.

The regular BMW recommended maintenance schedule includes the following:

- Vehicle check and inspection
- Engine oil check
- Coolant check
- Tire rotation
- Brake fluid check
- Front and rear brake inspection
- Inspection of the engine and cabin air filters
- Wiper blade inspection
- Standard scope

Not every part inspected will need replacement during your visit. Our BMW-certified maintenance experts use the CBS monitor to identify exactly what requires attention, ensuring precise and efficient service.

**BMW 2-Series Recommended Maintenance Services**

Maintenance needs can vary depending on your model and driving habits. For tailored recommendations, consult your owner’s manual or speak with one of our knowledgeable service advisors. Below is a general guideline for BMW 2 Series maintenance milestones:

**BMW 2-Series 10,000-Mile Maintenance**

- Replace the engine oil, oil filter and coolant
- Repeat every 10,000 miles

**BMW 2-Series 20,000-Mile Maintenance**

- Inspect and replace the oil filters
- Repeat every 20,000 miles

**BMW 2-Series 30,000-Mile Maintenance**

- Replace brake fluid. After the first service, schedule brake fluid replacement every 60,000 miles.
- If equipped with a manual transmission, replace transmission fluid every 30,000 miles.

**BMW 2-Series 60,000-mile maintenance**

- Replace the engine air filter and spark plugs
- Inspect and replace brake pads and rotors as needed
- For automatic transmissions, replace the transmission fluid every 60,000 miles.

**BMW 2-Series 90,000-Mile Maintenance**

- Replace the timing belt and hoses
- Repeat every 90,000 miles

**BMW 2-Series Maintenance after 90,000 Miles**

Continue following the BMW 2 Series maintenance schedule with 5,000-mile intervals and adhere to service milestones as listed above to ensure optimal performance.

Mercedes-Benz Service A\*\* and Service B\*\* are part of the [maintenance schedule](https://www.fjmercedes.com/service/service-maintenance-guide-menu/) that is prescribed for all Mercedes-Benz models. Your first Mercedes-Benz GLE SUV Service A will be needed at 10,000 miles or 1 year. After that, your vehicle will require Service A every 20,000 miles or 2 years.

## Mercedes-Benz GLE SUV Service B

At 20,000 miles or 1 year after your first Service A, your Mercedes-Benz GLE SUV will require Service B\* maintenance. Service B will then be needed every 20,000 miles or 2 years going forward.

# MAINTAINING YOUR BMW VEHICLE

A well-maintained vehicle will help safeguard its operational performance, road-safety and its reliability. This is why it is important to follow and perform BMW’s recommended periodic vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks as indicated by your vehicle’s Maintenance Service Display, along with the other maintenance work described in this booklet.

A improper maintenance is not covered under the BMW New Vehicle Damage, including consequential damage, which results from lack of or Limited Warranty for Passenger Cars and Light Trucks.

# MAINTENANCE INTERVALS

# BMW 3 Series Maintenance Schedule

![](https://dealerimages.dealereprocess.com/image/upload/3734739)

## Maintenance Schedule

Keeping up with your vehicle’s routine maintenance schedule is crucial to the health and longevity of your car. Routine maintenance services are done about once or twice a year, and are usually just a quick stop by the shop to change your oil and make sure everything is working properly.

**Here at BMW of Westchester we know how important it is to stay on top of these services in order to keep your car on the streets of Westchester County and Yonkers, NY, for years to come. Check out our breakdown of the BMW 3 Series maintenance schedule below!  [Schedule a service appointment](https://www.westchesterbmw.com/service-appointment/) for more assistance.**

## Annual Routine Maintenance Services

Your first[BMW 3 Series](https://www.westchesterbmw.com/search/new-bmw-3-series-white-plains-ny/?cy=10607&md=33&tp=new) routine maintenance service will happen about 6 months in, or once you hit around 5,000-10,000 miles, whichever happens to come first. This first service will be relatively quick. It will include:

- **An oil and filter change**

- **Tire rotation**

- **Brake inspection**


You’ll want to get these services done once or twice a year for the duration of the vehicle’s life.

Staying on top of your regular oil and oil filter changes is crucial to your car’s health because as your engine runs, tiny bits of dirt and dust will build up in it, which can cause excessive wear and tear.

**Additionally, yearly [tire rotations](https://www.westchesterbmw.com/service-appointment/) are important to maintain traction control, because they prevent your wheels from having uneven tread. Tread and traction control helps your vehicle stop quicker, and provides you with safer travels over rough terrain.**

![](https://dealerimages.dealereprocess.com/image/upload/3734763)

![](https://dealerimages.dealereprocess.com/image/upload/3734769)

## 30,000-Mile Maintenance Services

Once your BMW 3 Series hits 30,000 miles, it’s time to head back to the shop for a variety of inspections and maintenance care checks. To start, you’re going to need:

- **Your air filter changed, over time your air filter can become clogged, and a replacement will be needed in order for it to work at its best. If you travel in particularly dusty environments, you’ll want this changed around 15,000 miles rather than 30,000.**

- **Next, you’ll need your fuel filter inspected; your technician can perform a pressure test to determine if you’ll need it replaced.**


## 60,000-Mile Maintenance Services

Your 60,000-mile maintenance service will happen at around four or five years into ownership for the average driver. At this service, you’ll need:

- **Brake Rotor, Pads, and Shoes Inspections and Replacements**

- **Brake Fluid Replacement**

- **Coolant Replacement**

- **Transmission Fluid Replacement**

- **Your BMW 3 Series battery and brakes will start to wear out around the 60,000-mile mark, which is why it’s so important to get them inspected, and possibly replaced.**


![](https://dealerimages.dealereprocess.com/image/upload/3734756)

![](https://dealerimages.dealereprocess.com/image/upload/3734759)

## 90,000-Mile Maintenance Services

Your 90,000-mile maintenance check will include an inspection of your hoses, belts, and spark plugs. If they’re not up to par, they’ll need to be replaced. Additionally, you’ll also need to replace your power steering fluid to keep your steering wheel working properly. You should also get the following done:

- **Timing belt replacement**

- **Replace hoses**

- **Replace spark plugs**

- **Rotate rotors or replace rotors**

- **Fuel system cleaning**

- **Complete inspection**

Your [BMW 3 Series](https://www.bmwtigard.com/new-vehicles/3-series/) is a finely-crafted piece of machinery, but it will still require routine service from time to time.
