## BMW 3 Series Service Schedule

The BMW 3 Series service schedule includes BMW 3 Series oil change intervals and more to help you track the maintenance your vehicle requires. Let’s break it down more in-depth below.

### Bi-Annual Services

The services listed below should be performed approximately 6 months after you take your new vehicle home, at the 5,000 to 10,000-mile mark. They should then be performed at least twice a year for the duration you own the vehicle.

- Oil and Filter Change
- Tire Rotation
- Brake Inspection

### Every 30,000 Miles

At the 30,000-mile mark in the BMW 3 Series maintenance schedule, you’ll want to head back to the shop for a variety of inspections and maintenance care checks.

- Air filter changes: Air filters get clogged over time, so at this point, they are no longer working at their best. If you travel in particularly dusty environments, you’ll want to change the filter approximately every 15,000 miles.
- Fuel filter inspection: Your technician can perform a pressure test to determine if the fuel filter needs replacement.

### Every 60,000 Miles

Your 60,000-mile maintenance service will happen at around four or five years into ownership for the average driver. Here is what it will include:

- Brake Rotor, Pads, and Shoes Inspections and Replacements
- Brake Fluid Replacement
- Coolant Replacement
- Transmission Fluid Replacement

Keep in mind that this is also around the time your battery will start wearing down, so it is a good idea to have it looked at and possibly replaced.

### Every 90,000 Miles

At this service interval, we will take care of inspecting hoses, belts, and spark plugs. Power steering fluid should also be replaced when we perform these tasks:

- Timing belt replacement
- Replace hoses
- Replace spark plugs
- Rotate rotors or replace rotors
- Fuel system cleaning
- Complete inspection

# **BMW 3 Series Maintenance Schedule**

Date: April 19th, 2023

![2023 BMW 3 Series](https://dealerinspire-image-library-prod.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/images/oQNj43gWWpbDX49jH1rgvQGxo94MTLo8jKbCVaRn.jpg)

Your [BMW 3 Series](https://www.bmwtigard.com/new-vehicles/3-series/) is a finely-crafted piece of machinery, but it will still require routine service from time to time. Keeping up with the BMW 3 Series [maintenance schedule](https://www.bmwtigard.com/service/service-and-parts-tips/bmw-recommended-maintenance-schedule/) is a must if you want your vehicle to perform at its best for as long as possible. We understand that keeping track of BMW 3 Series oil change intervals and more can be a challenge. That is why we have created this guide to the BMW 3 Series service schedule. Simply follow this guide, and your vehicle should be prepared and safe for the roads of Portland and Tigard.

[View 3 Series Inventory](https://www.bmwtigard.com/new-vehicles/3-series/) [Contact Us](https://www.bmwtigard.com/contact-us/)

## BMW 3 Series Service Schedule

The BMW 3 Series service schedule includes BMW 3 Series oil change intervals and more to help you track the maintenance your vehicle requires. Let’s break it down more in-depth below.

### Bi-Annual Services

The services listed below should be performed approximately 6 months after you take your new vehicle home, at the 5,000 to 10,000-mile mark. They should then be performed at least twice a year for the duration you own the vehicle.

- Oil and Filter Change
- Tire Rotation
- Brake Inspection

### Every 30,000 Miles

At the 30,000-mile mark in the BMW 3 Series maintenance schedule, you’ll want to head back to the shop for a variety of inspections and maintenance care checks.

- Air filter changes: Air filters get clogged over time, so at this point, they are no longer working at their best. If you travel in particularly dusty environments, you’ll want to change the filter approximately every 15,000 miles.
- Fuel filter inspection: Your technician can perform a pressure test to determine if the fuel filter needs replacement.

### Every 60,000 Miles

Your 60,000-mile maintenance service will happen at around four or five years into ownership for the average driver. Here is what it will include:

- Brake Rotor, Pads, and Shoes Inspections and Replacements
- Brake Fluid Replacement
- Coolant Replacement
- Transmission Fluid Replacement

Keep in mind that this is also around the time your battery will start wearing down, so it is a good idea to have it looked at and possibly replaced.

### Every 90,000 Miles

At this service interval, we will take care of inspecting hoses, belts, and spark plugs. Power steering fluid should also be replaced when we perform these tasks:

- Timing belt replacement
- Replace hoses
- Replace spark plugs
- Rotate rotors or replace rotors
- Fuel system cleaning
- Complete inspection

## VW Atlas Service Schedule

## 10,000 Miles or One Year

The base of your VW Atlas service schedule will consist of the following maintenance tasks:

- Inspect the Brake Pads
- VW Atlas Oil Change
- New Oil Filter
- Service Interval Display Rest (if needed)

## 20,000 Miles or Two Years

Two-year maintenance should also include a VW Atlas oil change and oil filter replacement. The following must also be checked so you can stay safe on Vienna roads:

- Horn
- Tire Repair Kit
- Engine and Engine Compartment Components
- Brake Fluid
- Tire Pressure
- Service Interval Display
- Exterior Lighting
- Battery
- Tires
- Windshield Wiper/Washer System
- Automatic headlight control
- Headlight Washing System
- Wiper Blades
- Coolant Level and Frost Protection
- Brake Pads
- Transmission
- Second Battery
- Tire Pressure Monitoring System

## 30,000 Miles or Three Years

The following VW Atlas routine maintenance tasks will be required every three years or 30,000 miles:

- Oil Change
- New Oil Filter
- Inspect Brake Pads
- Service Interval Display Rest (if needed)

## 40,000 Miles or Four Years

At 40,000 miles, you’ll get a VW Atlas oil change and a new oil filter, plus everything from the 20,000 service interval. These things will also be checked as part of your VW Atlas maintenance schedule:

- Tie Rod Ends
- Stabilizer Bushings
- New Dust and Pollen Filter
- Front and Rear Coil Springs and Shock Absorbers
- Sunroof and Panoramic Sunroof
- Ball Joints
- Wheel Bearings
- Axles
- Coupling Rods

## 50,000 Miles or Five Years

The 50,000 VW Atlas service interval includes:

- Engine Oil Change
- New Oil Filter
- Check Your Brake Pads
- Service Interval Display Rest (if needed)

## 60,000 Miles or 6 Years

Your safety is paramount as you drive around Fairfax, so along with new engine oil, oil filter, air filter, and snow filter, these components will be inspected:

- Fuel filter Replacement
- Dust and Pollen Filter Replacement
- Battery inspection
- Check the Tires
- Brake System Inspection
- Check the Tire fFller Bottle Expiration Date

## 70,000 Miles or 7 Years

The 70,000-mile mark of the VW Atlas maintenance schedule includes the following tasks:

- Engine Oil Filter Change
- Motor Oil Change
- Brake Pad Check
- Service Interval Display Rest (if needed)

## 80,000 Miles or 8 Years

All the same components from the 20,000-mile inspection are inspected, as well as:

- Ball Joints
- Transmission
- Wheel Bearings
- Axles
- Interior Lighting
- Ribbed V-belt
- Front and Rear Coil Springs
- Shock Absorbers
- Sunroof and Panoramic Sunroof
- Underbody

## 90,000 Miles or 9 Years

- Brake Discs
- Clutch Unit
- Engine Oil Change
- Engine Oil Filter Change
- Brake Pad Inspection
- Service Interval Display Rest (if needed)

## 100,000 Miles or 10 Years

At 100,000 miles, you’ll get a VW Atlas oil change and new oil filter, and the same things as the 20,000-mile inspection will be inspected.

## 110,000 Miles or 11 Years

- Brake Pad Check
- Engine Oil Change
- New Oil Filter
- Service Interval Display Rest (if needed)

## 120,000 Miles or 12 Years

Our certified VW Technicians will replace your engine oil, oil filter, and snow and air filter and check all the same components from the 20,000-mile inspection, plus:

- Underbody
- Wheel Bearings
- Axles
- Tie Rod Ends,
- Stabilizer Bushings
- Front and Rear Coil Springs
- Shock Absorbers
- Ball Joints
- Interior Lighting
- Coupling Rods
- Ribbed V-Belt
- Sunroof and Panoramic Sunroof

## What is the Volkswagen Atlas Maintenance Schedule?

Your [new VW Atlas](https://www.carolinavw.com/new-vehicles/atlas/) service intervals occur every 10,000 miles. Older Volkswagen models might have different maintenance requirements, so check your owner’s manual for the correct VW Atlas maintenance schedule. However, world-class engineering means longer VW Atlas service intervals when you have a late-model vehicle.

Every 10,000 miles represents the VW Atlas oil change interval, so expect to get a full synthetic oil change every 10,000 miles of driving unless you drive in less-than-ideal conditions regularly in Concord.

Below is the general VW Atlas maintenance schedule you should follow.

### **VW Atlas Maintenance Schedule: 10,000 Miles or One Year**

Your first Volkswagen Atlas service in Charlotte will get this:

- Inspect the Brake Pads
- Oil Change
- New Oil Filter
- Fluid Level Check
- Service Interval Display Reset (if needed)

### **VW Atlas Maintenance Schedule: 20,000 Miles or Two Years**

For this VW Atlas service interval, we will do everything from the first service at 10,000 miles, plus some extras:

- Automatic headlight control
- Headlight Washing System
- Wiper Blades
- Coolant Level and Frost Protection
- Brake Pads
- Transmission
- Second Battery
- Engine Air Filter Check
- Tire Pressure Monitoring System
- Horn
- Tire Repair Kit
- Engine and Engine Compartment Components
- Brake Fluid
- Tire Pressure
- Service Interval Display
- Exterior Lighting
- Battery
- Tires
- Windshield Wiper/Washer System

### **VW Atlas Maintenance Schedule: 30,000 Miles or Three Years**

Here’s what our team will do for your three-year Volkswagen Atlas service near Indian Trail:

- Oil Change
- New Oil Filter
- Inspect Brake Pads
- Service Interval Display Reset (if needed)

### **VW Atlas Maintenance Schedule: 40,000 Miles or Four Years**

At 40,000 miles, we’ll take care of the VW Atlas oil change interval, just like the other one-year maintenance. We’ll also check everything from the 20,000-mile VW Atlas service interval. Our team will also look over these things for your Atlas for four years:

- Sunroof and Panoramic Sunroof
- Ball Joints
- Wheel Bearings
- Axles
- Coupling Rods
- Tie Rod Ends
- Stabilizer Bushings
- New Dust and Pollen Filter for the Cabin
- Front and Rear Coil Springs and Shock Absorbers

### **VW Atlas Maintenance Schedule: 50,000 Miles or Five Years**

At the 50,000-mile mark, this service interval includes everything from the initial service interval:

- VW Atlas Oil Change Interval
- New Oil Filter
- Check Your Brake Pads
- Fluid Levels
- Service Interval Display Reset (if needed)

At this point in your SUV ownership, you might need a new battery, new tires, or new brake parts, depending on the condition of your Volkswagen Atlas. We’ll discuss your options with you if we see anything that needs service at this interval.

Moving forward, we’ll also inspect the drive belts, the condition of the transmission, and the radiator, as these parts might show more signs of wear. If our service technicians detect any looming issues that need to be resolved soon, we’ll suggest a way to remedy the situation.

Your [brakes](https://vw.oempartsonline.com/brakes) stop your [Volkswagen](https://vw.oempartsonline.com/v-volkswagen) vehicle. They do it by clamping their calipers and brake rotors together. This is what creates the friction, or resistance, that slows your vehicle's wheels and tires. However, calipers can't press rotors without brake pads, or else they'd get damaged. Your VW has one of four types of pads, depending on its model. Organic brake pads are for everyday driving. They're reliable, they don't wear rotors down as badly, and they don't create much dust. Best of all, they're inexpensive. Ceramic brake pads work better in bad weather, they don't make much noise, and their dust isn't as sticky. Metallic brake pads, however, stand up to higher heat, feel firmer, and resist brake fade. Carbon fiber brake pads are the strongest and best performers, tolerant of high temperatures and providing the most stopping power. Most cars and SUVs use either metallic or organic pads. However, many sports cars and performance vehicles use ceramic or carbon fiber pads because they do the best job of expelling heat.

## How Long Do Volkswagen Brake Pads Last?

However, no brake pad lasts forever, not even those Volkswagen makes. You should change yours every 40,000 to 50,000 miles or so. Otherwise, figure out when to replace them by looking for the signs your brakes are going bad. They include warning lights, worn pad surfaces, pad damage, whiny brakes, and taking longer to stop. The worst are vibration and grinding, as they indicate your rotors are warped and getting damaged because your brake pads have degraded.

# Volkswagen Tiguan Service Schedule

![2021 Volkswagen Tiguan](https://dealerinspire-image-library-prod.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/images/l6ArqlcCl44aBh7sErWf9aFzUF3yFnOEkHLuMSF8.jpg)

The Volkswagen Tiguan is a great addition to your family trips around Vienna. However, to maintain your smooth family adventures, it’s necessary to stay on top of your VW Tiguan maintenance plans. Let’s take a look at the Tiguan service intervals with the team at Stohlman Volkswagen service, and trust your service to the certified technicians in our [service center](https://www.stohlman-vw.com/department-fod33-1906).

[Schedule Service](https://www.stohlman-vw.com/online-service-scheduler/) [Contact Us](https://www.stohlman-vw.com/contact-us/)

## VW Tiguan Maintenance Plan

The specifics to your Tiguan service intervals vary depending on your driving habits around Fairfax, but here are the recommended service you should schedule each year or mileage:

### 10,000 Miles/1 Year

**Oil change­­**: Oil is essential to your smooth engine performance, so it’s likely that whenever you [schedule service](https://www.stohlman-vw.com/online-service-scheduler/), it’s also time for an oil change.

**Brake pad inspection:** Our individual driving style affects the wear of your brake pads, and it makes sense that the more you use them, the sooner they’ll need to be replaced. The technicians will inspect the brake pad to see if a replacement is needed.

**Safety inspection**: You and your family should feel safe on your daily commute. Each year, your airbags, seatbelts, and driver-assisting features are inspected to ensure your safety on the road.

**Rotate your tires**: As your tires wear over time, regular tire rotations will help them wear evenly, and lengthen the lifespan of your tires.

**Check light bulbs**: Your VW Tiguan maintenance schedule helps you maintain visibility on your trips, too. Technicians will check your interior and exterior lights to ensure you’re not left in the dark when you really need them.

### 20,000 Miles/2 Year

Service for your VW Tiguan is recommended every 10,000 miles. On top of the previous inspections, the 20,000-mile mark includes a more complete brake system inspection that includes examining brake pads, brake discs, and brake-fluid levels. This Tiguan service interval also includes:

- **Battery inspection:** From your TV remote to your car battery, every battery needs to be replaced eventually. At this point in the Volkswagen Tiguan service schedule, your battery will be checked for any sign of leaks, cracks, or corrosion.
- **Tire inspection:** As mentioned above, rotating tires helps extend the lifespan of your tires, but eventually they will take on too much wear. They’ll be inspected for signs of holes, tearing, and bulging along the sidewall, as well as a tire pressure check for each wheel, including the spare.
- **Coolant replacement:** Coolant is essential in removing heat from the vital components of your engine, so it’s important to check coolant levels and replace as needed.

### 30,000 Miles/3 Year

When you’ve reached 30,000 miles, you’ll receive the same checks found in the 20,000-mile Tiguan service interval. A service technician will also replace your oil, replace the engine oil filter, and perform a brake pad inspection to get you back on Alexandria roads without a problem.

### 40,000 Miles/4 Year

- **Check and replace spark plugs:** A properly functioning spark plug means you can fire up the engine quickly and get on the road.
- **Inspect the electrical system:** On top of a spark plug and battery check, technicians will check to make sure your other electrical components are performing as they should.
- **Inspect for signs of body corrosion:** Vienna weather and accidents may have left their mark on your vehicle. A check to your interior exterior, and parts under the hood will allow your car to like new again.
- **Check the exhaust system:** The cycle from your spark plugs to the exhaust system completes the ignition sequence. This inspection makes sure your engine is firing on all cylinders.

### 50,000 Miles/5 Year

At the five-year or 50,000-mile mark in your Volkswagen Tiguan service schedule, it’s recommended you perform all the service mentioned above, along with extra attention to your brake pads, battery, and engine. As your vehicle puts on more mileage, our technicians will continue to thoroughly check to make sure you’re heading out in the best possible condition.

### 60,000 Miles/6 Year

At this point in the VW Tiguan maintenance plan, service should continue to be performed as mentioned as you progress to the 100k-mile mark. However, it is recommended that you replace your air filter. Not only will it bring a refresh to your cabin air quality, but replacing the air filter helps the spark plugs draw clean air into the engine, and help the ignition sequence run smoothly.

## 2024 Ford F-250 Super Duty Maintenance Schedule

Scheduled maintenance is critical for maintaining the performance and longevity of your 2024 Ford F-250 Super Duty. Regularly servicing your truck at Winslow Ford, the Show Low Ford dealer, according to Ford’s recommended intervals ensures it will operate reliably. This routine care can prevent breakdowns and costly repairs by addressing potential issues early.

According to the Show Low Ford dealership, adhering to the maintenance schedule also helps retain the vehicle’s resale value and keeps it in compliance with warranty requirements. It’s a small investment of time and care that pays dividends in the form of uninterrupted service and peace of mind on the road.

Here’s a rundown of the services performed during key maintenance milestones.

[Schedule Service](https://www.winslowford.com/serviceapptform)

[Service Specials](https://www.winslowford.com/service-parts-specials.html)

[Model Overview](https://www.winslowford.com/2024-Ford-F-250-Super-Duty-Overview)

[Trim Levels](https://www.winslowford.com/2024-Ford-F-250-Super-Duty-Trim-Levels)

### 7,500 Miles

At the 7,500-mile mark, your Ford F-250 Super Duty is due for its initial maintenance visit. The session starts with an oil change to keep the engine running cleanly, followed by replacing the oil filter. Our certified service technicians rotate the tires, inspect them for damage, and adjust the pressure. They also inspect the wheels, steering mechanisms, suspension joints, brakes, cooling system, exhaust system, and half-shaft boots, checking for signs of wear or malfunction. These services are repeated during subsequent visits to help maintain your truck’s reliability and driving quality.

### 15,000 Miles

At 15,000 miles, your Ford F-250 Super Duty undergoes a more in-depth examination on top of the standard services provided earlier. The service technicians check the vehicle’s fluids, including the automatic transmission fluid. They proceed with an inspection of the brake system’s components for wear and safety. Cooling system checks involve evaluating the engine coolant and the integrity of its hoses. The exhaust system and heat shields are inspected for damage or leaks. The undercarriage receives a thorough examination, including the front axle, U-joints, steering linkage, as well as suspension components like ball joints, driveshafts, and tie-rod ends. The engine air filter and cabin air filter are replaced at this stage to ensure clean airflow into the engine and the vehicle’s cabin.

### 100,000 Miles

When your 2024 Ford F-250 Super Duty reaches 100,000 miles, the service team will replace the spark plugs, a crucial component for engine efficiency and smooth operation. They’ll also evaluate and potentially replace the engine coolant to ensure the cooling system remains effective. An inspection of the accessory drive belt is also conducted to identify any wear or damage—replacement isn’t always required at this point, but early detection of issues can prevent future breakdowns.

### 150,000 Miles

Reaching the 150,000-mile mark is a testament to the care invested in your Ford F-250 Super Duty. Our service technicians will perform several key replacements during this visit to ensure your truck keeps running strong. They’ll replace the accessory drive belt, which is essential for powering various engine accessories, along with the front wheel bearings and seals, which are critical for wheel stability and rotation. This maintenance visit also includes replacing the fluids in the transfer case and axle to protect these components and maintain optimal performance.

If you have any questions about maintaining your 2024 Ford F-250 Super Duty or need to schedule an appointment, contact the professionals at the Winslow Ford Service Center at 928-237-9767. Our team is ready to assist with all your service needs and ensure your vehicle continues to perform at its best.

Looking through my manual for my 2024 F250 Lariat I can't seem to find a declared oil change interval.

The manual directs me to another website:

Quote:


Scheduled Maintenance Service Intervals For your scheduled maintenance service intervals, visit [https://www.ford.com/](https://www.ford.com/) support/maintenance-schedule.



That website tells me

I know that most folks are changing at 5000 miles but _**is there an actual milieage/elapsed time interval that is officially declared for these trucks?**_

The iOLM will adjust for engine use. If you tow a lot it will decrease the interval for sooner changes, and on the flip side if you do a lot of unloaded highway, it will increase the interval. It bases the intervals on engine load, time, fuel use, drive cycles, etc. On my 19 F450 I do a lot of 62 MPH highway, 95% of the time, so it has a LONG interval of over 10,000 miles, but if I tow my 5th it will drop it quite a bit. It was sitting at 12% after almost 10K, then I took my 5th wheel to the dealer, about a 9 mile trip and it went from 12% to change oil soon.

I also confirmed the oil life with samples taken over time and analyzed. By the time it needs an oil change the old oil is used up, but not enough to be a problem. No sense wasting good oil.

# 6.7 Power Stroke Oil Capacity

### **How Much Oil Does a Powerstroke 6.7 Hold?**

The oil capacity of a [6.7 Powerstroke engine varies by year of manufacture](https://www.hotshotsecret.com/top-powerstroke-engines/) and the specific vehicle model.  If you own a Ford F-250 to F-650 manufactured after 2022, its Powerstroke 6.7L will hold 15 quarts (14.2 liters) of oil. Those manufactured between 2011 and 2022 hold approximately 13 quarts (12.3 liters).

A Ford F-650 and F-750 produced between 2015 and 2022 can hold a maximum of 15 quarts (14.2 liters) of oil. For newer models released in 2023 and later, the oil capacity increases slightly to 17 quarts (16 liters).

When performing an oil change, it is crucial to use the correct type of oil and adhere to the recommended capacity. Ford recommends using oils that meet its WSS-M2C17-F1 specification for the 6.7 Powerstroke. Always refer to your owner’s manual for exact information about the type and weight of oil that best suits your truck and application.

# BMW SERVICE

BMW recommends you have your maintenance and repair work performed by an authorized BMW center.

# MAINTAINING YOUR BMW VEHICLE

A well-maintained vehicle will help safeguard its operational performance, road-safety and its reliability. This is why it is important to follow and perform BMW’s recommended periodic vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks as indicated by your vehicle’s Maintenance Service Display, along with the other maintenance work described in this booklet.

A improper maintenance is not covered under the BMW New Vehicle Damage, including consequential damage, which results from lack of or Limited Warranty for Passenger Cars and Light Trucks.

# MAINTENANCE INTERVALS

Maintenance intervals on motor vehicles were conventionally based solely on a fixed time period or a specified amount of accumulated driving mileage.

However, operational and driving conditions have a major influence on your vehicle’s routine maintenance requirements; the distance traveled is only one of these significant factors. A vehicle used for short trips in the city with numerous cold starts, prolonged periods of idling, stop-and-go driving, and high engine speeds during acceleration may require more frequent maintenance intervals than a vehicle that is driven long distances at moderate engine speeds.

Your BMW vehicle uses sensors and algorithms together with the elapsed time and the driving distance/profile to monitor and evaluate your vehicle’s maintenance service needs. This information is then used to adapt dynamically the parameters used to forecast the applicable maintenance service task intervals.

# THE BMW MAINTENANCE SYSTEM

All BMW vehicles are equipped with an integrated BMW Maintenance System. This maintenance “reminder” system helps ensure that the vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks are performed at the forecasted intervals that apply to your vehicle.

The BMW Maintenance System display provides the vehicle operator access to the current status information for the following maintenance service tasks:

$\\triangleright$ Engine oil (date and miles)\*

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle check (date and miles)

$\\triangleright$ Front brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Rear brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid (date)

$\\triangleright$ 1200 Mile running-in service (date and miles) (Applicable to BMW M vehicles only)\*

For each specific maintenance service task, either the future date (month/ year), remaining miles or both are provided as noted above. The system monitors variable inputs to forecast the intervals and alert the driver when one or more specific maintenance tasks should be performed.

NOTE: For certain vehicles, the status of the front and rear brake pads will only be observable in the maintenance system’s display when there are approximately 2,000 miles or less remaining before a brake service will be required to be performed.

For information about the vehicle’s maintenance system displays, please refer to the Maintenance Service Display Overview section beginning on page 5.

The following “combine with Engine oil”\* maintenance service tasks may be identified as needing to be performed with a specific occurrence of the “Engine oil” service task (service counter number):

$\\triangleright$ Engine air filter(s)\*

$\\triangleright$ Spark plugs\*

$\\triangleright$ Final drive oil (Applicable M vehicles only)

\\* Does not apply to BEV

Although these items do not appear in the BMW Maintenance System’s display in the vehicle, these services should be performed when your vehicle’s engine oil is changed in accordance with the interval identified by your vehicle’s BMW Maintenance System.

For more information on your vehicle’s maintenance services requirements, procedures and intervals, please refer the Maintenance Service Summary section beginning on page 10.

The BMW Maintenance System also includes an option to set service reminders for the following state-specific mandatory vehicle inspections, including:

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle safety inspection; and/or $\\triangleright$ Emissions test

The corresponding interval data for these inspections can be inputted into the BMW Maintenance System by a service provider; they are not determined by the vehicle.

For your convenience, you may also wish to have your authorized BMW center perform the work necessary to fulfill these state inspection requirements in your area concurrent with the maintenance services specified above when possible.

Should you request more frequent maintenance service than is indicated by the BMW Maintenance System during the coverage period, the cost of these services will not be covered by the BMW Maintenance Program.

# SERVICE DATA — REMOTE CONTROL KEY

Maintenance service task status information for your BMW vehicle is continually updated and stored in your remote control key.

Your authorized BMW center can access this data and consult with you about applicable service procedures and tasks for your vehicle.

Therefore, always provide your service consultant with the most recent remote control key that was used to operate the vehicle when servicing your vehicle at a BMW center.

Disconnecting the battery during periods of long-term vehicle storage will interrupt the calculation of time-dependent maintenance services.

In this situation, BMW recommends that you have all your time-based maintenance services, such as brake fluid, engine oil and cabin microfilter, brought up to the correct date by an authorized BMW center.

The **BMW i5 maintenance schedule** looks very different from a gas-powered 5 Series. There’s no engine oil, spark plugs, or timing chain to worry about, but you still have brakes, tires, coolant, software, and a sophisticated high-voltage system that all need attention. If you’re driving or shopping for a BMW i5, understanding the real service intervals and long‑term maintenance picture can save you time, money, and stress.

### Quick take

Compared with a gasoline 5 Series, a BMW i5 typically needs fewer scheduled services and less routine maintenance. Most owners will visit a service center about once a year for inspections, fluids, and software, plus wear items like tires and brakes as they age.

## BMW i5 maintenance overview

The BMW i5 is built on the same platform as the current 5 Series, but its **electric powertrain dramatically changes the maintenance profile**. You still follow a factory schedule, but the high‑value items are:

\- Safety inspections (suspension, steering, brakes)
\- Brake fluid changes
\- Cabin air filter and other filters
\- Coolant for the battery and power electronics
\- High‑voltage system checks
\- Software and firmware updates

For most U.S. drivers, you’re looking at **annual visits** rather than old‑school 5,000–7,500‑mile oil changes.

### How BMW i5 maintenance compares to gas cars

## BMW i5 service intervals by mileage and time

BMW doesn’t publish a simple one‑page chart for every market; instead, the i5 uses **Condition Based Service (CBS)**. The car monitors mileage, time, and driving style, then tells you when service is due. That said, most i5s in the U.S. will follow patterns that look roughly like this:

- Every 10,000–12,000 miles or 12 months: General inspection and basic service
- Every 2 years: Brake fluid replacement and broader safety checks
- Every 3–4 years: Cabin air filter, key coolant checks, 12‑volt battery health review
- Around 5–6 years: Deeper coolant service and more detailed high‑voltage inspections

### Always defer to your i5’s on‑screen reminders

Use this guide as a planning tool, not a substitute for the factory schedule. Your i5’s digital service reminders and your BMW service advisor have the final word on what’s actually due.

## BMW i5 maintenance schedule at a glance

Here’s a simplified BMW i5 maintenance schedule to help you visualize what’s coming. Actual mileage can vary a bit by model year, driving style, and market, but this table gives you a realistic roadmap.

### Typical BMW i5 maintenance schedule (planning guide)

Approximate intervals for common BMW i5 service items. Always confirm with your vehicle’s on‑board service menu and owner’s manual.

| Mileage / Time | Main Service Items | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 10,000–12,000 miles or 12 months | Multi‑point inspection, tire rotation (if applicable), brake check, fluid level check | First full check‑in; some owners may see this closer to 8,000–10,000 miles |
| 20,000–24,000 miles or 2 years | Inspection, brake fluid change, cabin filter (if needed), software updates | Brake fluid interval is usually time‑based (about every 2 years) |
| 30,000–36,000 miles or 3 years | Inspection, alignment check if needed, coolant checks, 12‑volt battery test | May coincide with tire replacement depending on driving style |
| 40,000–48,000 miles or 4 years | Inspection, brake fluid change, cabin filter, more detailed suspension/brake check | Good time to evaluate brake pad/rotor wear |
| 60,000–72,000 miles or 6 years | Inspection, brake fluid, coolant service as recommended, high‑voltage system check | Heavier service visit; budget extra for any wear items |
| \> 75,000 miles | Ongoing annual inspections, fluids as due, tires/brakes as needed | Battery and drive units typically inspected, not routinely replaced |

High‑voltage battery and drive units are generally inspected, not replaced, during normal ownership.

### Use the BMW app to stay ahead

The BMW app can show upcoming service items and help you schedule visits. Syncing your car and app makes it easier to plan maintenance around your life instead of the other way around.

Even with fewer moving parts than a gas car, a BMW i5 still needs regular inspections for brakes, suspension, and tires.

## Key BMW i5 EV maintenance items explained

The BMW i5 eliminates many traditional services, but a few EV‑specific items matter more. Understanding them helps you read your maintenance schedule with confidence, and avoid approving work you don’t need.

### Core BMW i5 maintenance items

What they are, why they matter, and when to expect them

#### Brake fluid

EVs still use hydraulic brakes. Over time, brake fluid absorbs moisture, which can corrode components and reduce performance.

**Typical pattern:** Every ~2 years, regardless of mileage.

#### Cabin air filter

Keeps dust and pollutants out of the cabin and HVAC system.

**Typical pattern:** About every 2–3 years, or sooner in dusty or urban environments.

#### Coolant for battery & power electronics

Liquid coolant manages temperatures for the high‑voltage battery, inverter, and other components.

**Typical pattern:** Inspected regularly; partial or full replacement tends to show up around the 5–6 year mark.

#### High‑voltage battery checks

Technicians monitor battery health, seal integrity, and software diagnostics rather than swapping major components.

**Typical pattern:** Inspected during scheduled services or when the car flags an issue.

#### Suspension & steering

i5s are heavy, powerful sedans. Bushings, tie rods, and other hardware still wear over time.

**Typical pattern:** Inspected annually; replacement is mileage and road‑condition dependent.

#### Software & firmware updates

Updates can improve efficiency, charging behavior, and even add features.

**Typical pattern:** Applied over‑the‑air or during dealer visits as they become available.

### Don’t ignore brake warnings

Because EVs use regenerative braking, physical brake pads can last a long time, but when your i5 flags a brake issue, it’s critical. Delaying brake service risks rotor damage and safety problems that are far more expensive than a timely repair.

## BMW i5 maintenance costs and what actually wears out

With no oil changes or exhaust system, a BMW i5’s **routine maintenance costs** often undercut a gas 5 Series over the first several years. Where EVs catch up, or even surpass, traditional cars is in **wear items** like tires, brakes, and out‑of‑warranty electronics.

### Lower‑frequency, lower‑cost items

- Annual inspections and fluid checks
- Brake fluid every ~2 years
- Cabin air filter every few years
- Basic software updates during visits

These visits are predictable and usually modest in cost compared with major ICE services like spark plug replacement or timing components.

### Big‑ticket wear items to budget for

- **Tires:** Instant torque and weight can wear them faster, especially on performance trims.

In case of severe conditions, such as extremely low temperatures, excessive dust, etc., it is necessary for certain operations to be carried out in between the given intervals.  Horn: Check function

 Removable trailer hitch: Check function and inspect for damage (if equipped)

 Ribbed Belt and Tensioning Roller for Belt Starter Generator - Check condition

 Service Interval Display: Reset

 Test drive: Check braking, kickdown, steering, electrical, heating/ventilation systems, air conditioning, handling, and parking brake

# Volkswagen Tiguan Service Schedule

![2021 Volkswagen Tiguan](https://dealerinspire-image-library-prod.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/images/l6ArqlcCl44aBh7sErWf9aFzUF3yFnOEkHLuMSF8.jpg)

The Volkswagen Tiguan is a great addition to your family trips around Vienna. However, to maintain your smooth family adventures, it’s necessary to stay on top of your VW Tiguan maintenance plans. Let’s take a look at the Tiguan service intervals with the team at Stohlman Volkswagen service, and trust your service to the certified technicians in our [service center](https://www.stohlman-vw.com/department-fod33-1906).

[Schedule Service](https://www.stohlman-vw.com/online-service-scheduler/) [Contact Us](https://www.stohlman-vw.com/contact-us/)

## VW Tiguan Maintenance Plan

The specifics to your Tiguan service intervals vary depending on your driving habits around Fairfax, but here are the recommended service you should schedule each year or mileage:

### 10,000 Miles/1 Year

**Oil change­­**: Oil is essential to your smooth engine performance, so it’s likely that whenever you [schedule service](https://www.stohlman-vw.com/online-service-scheduler/), it’s also time for an oil change.

**Brake pad inspection:** Our individual driving style affects the wear of your brake pads, and it makes sense that the more you use them, the sooner they’ll need to be replaced. The technicians will inspect the brake pad to see if a replacement is needed.

**Safety inspection**: You and your family should feel safe on your daily commute. Each year, your airbags, seatbelts, and driver-assisting features are inspected to ensure your safety on the road.

**Rotate your tires**: As your tires wear over time, regular tire rotations will help them wear evenly, and lengthen the lifespan of your tires.

**Check light bulbs**: Your VW Tiguan maintenance schedule helps you maintain visibility on your trips, too. Technicians will check your interior and exterior lights to ensure you’re not left in the dark when you really need them.

### 20,000 Miles/2 Year

Service for your VW Tiguan is recommended every 10,000 miles. On top of the previous inspections, the 20,000-mile mark includes a more complete brake system inspection that includes examining brake pads, brake discs, and brake-fluid levels. This Tiguan service interval also includes:

- **Battery inspection:** From your TV remote to your car battery, every battery needs to be replaced eventually. At this point in the Volkswagen Tiguan service schedule, your battery will be checked for any sign of leaks, cracks, or corrosion.
- **Tire inspection:** As mentioned above, rotating tires helps extend the lifespan of your tires, but eventually they will take on too much wear. They’ll be inspected for signs of holes, tearing, and bulging along the sidewall, as well as a tire pressure check for each wheel, including the spare.
- **Coolant replacement:** Coolant is essential in removing heat from the vital components of your engine, so it’s important to check coolant levels and replace as needed.

### 30,000 Miles/3 Year

When you’ve reached 30,000 miles, you’ll receive the same checks found in the 20,000-mile Tiguan service interval. A service technician will also replace your oil, replace the engine oil filter, and perform a brake pad inspection to get you back on Alexandria roads without a problem.

### 40,000 Miles/4 Year

- **Check and replace spark plugs:** A properly functioning spark plug means you can fire up the engine quickly and get on the road.
- **Inspect the electrical system:** On top of a spark plug and battery check, technicians will check to make sure your other electrical components are performing as they should.
- **Inspect for signs of body corrosion:** Vienna weather and accidents may have left their mark on your vehicle. A check to your interior exterior, and parts under the hood will allow your car to like new again.
- **Check the exhaust system:** The cycle from your spark plugs to the exhaust system completes the ignition sequence. This inspection makes sure your engine is firing on all cylinders.

### 50,000 Miles/5 Year

At the five-year or 50,000-mile mark in your Volkswagen Tiguan service schedule, it’s recommended you perform all the service mentioned above, along with extra attention to your brake pads, battery, and engine. As your vehicle puts on more mileage, our technicians will continue to thoroughly check to make sure you’re heading out in the best possible condition.

### 60,000 Miles/6 Year

At this point in the VW Tiguan maintenance plan, service should continue to be performed as mentioned as you progress to the 100k-mile mark. However, it is recommended that you replace your air filter. Not only will it bring a refresh to your cabin air quality, but replacing the air filter helps the spark plugs draw clean air into the engine, and help the ignition sequence run smoothly.

Ford redefines the midsize pickup with the launch of the 2024
Ranger, a fifth-generation model that boasts a fresh, modern design
and enhanced features, including the introduction of the exhilarating
Ranger Raptor variant. Available solely in a four-door crew cab
configuration with a five-foot bed at dealerships like the Tusayan
Ford dealer, the 2024 Ford Ranger takes design inspiration
from the best-selling F-150, featuring a distinctive wide grille and
signature C-Clamp headlights.

Scheduled maintenance is a crucial aspect of owning a 2024 Ford
Ranger. When you bring your Ranger to the professionals at Winslow Ford, the
Tusayan Ford dealership, you guarantee that your vehicle
benefits from thorough and expert care. Our service center boasts a
team of factory-trained technicians who are experts in Ford's
latest engineering advancements. They’ll perform detailed inspections
of the engine and transmission, safeguard the vehicle’s towing and
hauling performance, and adhere strictly to Ford's recommended
maintenance protocols. This meticulous approach ensures that every
Ranger retains its strength, efficiency, and dependability.

[Schedule Service](https://www.winslowford.com/serviceapptform)

[Service Specials](https://www.winslowford.com/service-parts-specials.html)

[Model Overview](https://www.winslowford.com/2024-ford-ranger-overview)

[Trim Levels](https://www.winslowford.com/2024-ford-ranger-trim-levels)

We’ll explore the key stages of your 2024 Ford Ranger’s routine
maintenance schedule.

## 10,000 Miles

The initial service appointment for your Ranger is set at 10,000
miles. Our skilled service team will perform a comprehensive
multi-point inspection during this visit. This includes an inspection
of the braking, exhaust, and cooling systems and an examination of the
half-shaft boots. The team will also check the Ranger’s steering
mechanisms, joints, and wheels to ensure they’re in top condition. Our
service technicians will also change the oil, replace the oil filter,
rotate the tires, check the tire pressure, and lubricate the axles and
joints. Finally, the transmission fluid level will be checked.

These procedures are carried out at each service interval to help keep
your Ranger running smoothly and identify and address potential issues
early on.

### 20,000 Miles

In addition to the regular services provided at 10,000 miles, at the
20,000-mile mark, our service professionals will replace the cabin air
filter of your 2024 Ford Ranger. This essential maintenance task is
scheduled every 20,000 miles to ensure the air quality inside your
vehicle remains clean and fresh.

### 30,000 Miles

When your 2024 Ford Ranger hits the 30,000-mile mark, our service team
will replace the engine air filter. This is a crucial step in vehicle
maintenance, as a clean engine air filter is vital for providing your
truck’s engine with a steady flow of clean air. This ensures that your
Ranger’s engine operates optimally, maintaining its performance and
longevity.

### 100,000 Miles

At the 100,000-mile threshold, our focus for your 2024 Ford Ranger
shifts to the accessory drive belt. While it’s often the case that
replacement isn’t needed yet, this inspection is crucial for early
detection of any potential problems. Additionally, the 100,000-mile
maintenance service typically includes replacing the spark plugs and
coolant, which are pivotal steps in ensuring your Ranger continues to
operate smoothly and efficiently.

Contact the Winslow Ford Service Center at 928-406-0046 to schedule your
service appointment or if you have any inquiries regarding the upkeep
of your 2024 Ford Ranger. Our team is here to assist you with any
questions or needs related to your vehicle’s maintenance.

# The Ultimate Guide to Ford’s Oil Change Intervals and Maintenance

May 22nd, 2025 by[walong@modernauto.com](https://www.modernfordofboone.com/author/walongmodernauto-com/ "Posts by walong@modernauto.com")

Share this Post:

### The Ultimate Guide to Ford’s Oil Change Intervals and Maintenance

Maintaining your Ford vehicle is crucial to ensure its longevity and performance. One of the most essential aspects of vehicle maintenance is regular oil changes. This guide will explore Ford’s recommended oil change intervals, the importance of timely oil changes, and how to determine the best schedule for your vehicle. We’ll also provide insights into the benefits of using Ford’s Intelligent Oil-Life Monitor (IOLM) system and how it can assist you in keeping your vehicle in top shape. Whether you’re in Boone, Hickory, or Wilkesboro, understanding these key maintenance practices will help you keep your Ford running smoothly.

  - [Factors Influencing Oil Change Frequency](https://www.modernfordofboone.com/ford-oil-change-guide-boone/#factors-influencing-oil-change-frequency): Discover how driving habits, engine type, and oil type can affect your oil change schedule.
  - [The Importance of Regular Oil Changes](https://www.modernfordofboone.com/ford-oil-change-guide-boone/#the-importance-of-regular-oil-changes): Understand why timely oil changes are critical for engine health and performance.
  - [Mileage vs. Time: What Matters More?](https://www.modernfordofboone.com/ford-oil-change-guide-boone/#mileage-vs-time-what-matters-more): Explore the debate between mileage and time intervals for oil changes and learn which is more important for your Ford.
  - [Maximizing Your Ford’s Longevity with the IOLM](https://www.modernfordofboone.com/ford-oil-change-guide-boone/#maximizing-your-fords-longevity-with-the-iolm): See how the Intelligent Oil-Life Monitor can help optimize your maintenance schedule.
  - [Scheduling Your Oil Change at Modern Ford of Boone](https://www.modernfordofboone.com/ford-oil-change-guide-boone/#scheduling-your-oil-change-at-modern-ford-of-boone): Find out how to schedule your next service appointment and why Modern Ford of Boone is the best choice for your maintenance needs.

## Ford’s Recommended Oil Change Intervals

Ford recommends changing your vehicle’s oil every 7,500 miles or six months, whichever comes first. This general guideline ensures that your engine remains well-lubricated and free from contaminants. However, depending on your specific model and driving conditions, this interval may vary. For instance, newer Ford models equipped with the **Intelligent Oil-Life Monitor (IOLM)** system can calculate the optimal oil change interval based on real-time data, including mileage, speed, temperature, and driving habits. This advanced system allows you to extend the time between oil changes without compromising engine health.

For older Ford models or those without the IOLM, you might need to adhere to a more traditional schedule of every 3,000 to 5,000 miles, especially if your driving conditions are severe. Severe conditions include frequent short trips, towing heavy loads, or driving in extremely hot or cold weather. Always consult your vehicle’s owner’s manual for specific maintenance recommendations tailored to your model.

If you’re uncertain about the best oil change interval for your Ford, consider visiting the **[Service Department at Modern Ford of Boone](https://api.connectcdk.com/api/nc-cosa-consumer-ui/v1/?subscriptionId=&cid=2000096)**. Our experienced technicians can provide personalized advice based on your vehicle’s needs and your driving habits.

## Factors Influencing Oil Change Frequency

Several factors can influence how often you should change your oil. Understanding these can help you maintain your Ford vehicle more effectively:

- **Driving Habits**: If you frequently drive in stop-and-go traffic, tow heavy loads, or take short trips, your engine may accumulate contaminants faster, necessitating more frequent oil changes.
- **Engine Type**: Different engines have varying requirements. For example, turbocharged engines might require more frequent oil changes due to higher operating temperatures.
- **Oil Type**: Using **synthetic oil** can extend the time between oil changes compared to conventional oil. Synthetic oils are designed to last longer and withstand extreme temperatures better.

For drivers in areas like Lenoir or Morganton, where the terrain might involve more hills and curves, these factors become even more critical. Always ensure that your oil type matches your driving conditions and engine specifications for optimal performance.

## The Importance of Regular Oil Changes

Regular oil changes are vital for maintaining your engine’s health. Oil lubricates engine components, reduces friction, and helps manage heat. Over time, oil degrades and becomes contaminated with particles and debris, which can lead to engine wear and reduced performance. Failing to change your oil regularly can result in:

- **Engine Overheating**: Dirty oil can’t effectively dissipate heat, leading to overheating.
- **Increased Friction**: Without proper lubrication, engine parts can wear down more quickly.
- **Reduced Fuel Efficiency**: A well-lubricated engine runs more efficiently, saving you money at the pump.

In regions like Wilkesboro or Ashe County, where temperatures can vary significantly, maintaining clean oil is crucial for adapting to changing conditions. If you notice signs like a knocking engine or the oil change light illuminating, it’s time to schedule an oil change.

## Mileage vs. Time: What Matters More?

When considering oil change intervals, both mileage and time are important. Oil degrades over time due to oxidation and the breakdown of additives, even if the vehicle isn’t driven frequently. Conversely, higher mileage means more exposure to contaminants. Therefore, you should follow the interval that comes first, whether it’s mileage or time.

For example, if your Ford’s manual recommends an oil change every 5,000 miles or six months, change the oil if you reach either milestone. This approach ensures that your engine remains protected, regardless of driving frequency. For vehicles using synthetic oil, the interval might extend up to 15,000 miles, but always verify with your owner’s manual.

Residents in Boone or Blowing Rock, who may use their vehicles less frequently due to work-from-home arrangements or seasonal use, should still adhere to the time-based interval to prevent oil degradation.

## Maximizing Your Ford’s Longevity with the IOLM

The **Intelligent Oil-Life Monitor (IOLM)** is a feature in many newer Ford models that takes the guesswork out of oil changes. By analyzing your driving conditions and habits, the IOLM provides accurate recommendations for when to change your oil. This system helps you avoid unnecessary changes while ensuring your engine is protected.

For example, if you frequently drive in mountainous areas like Boone or Hickory, the IOLM will account for the increased engine strain and adjust the oil change interval accordingly. This tailored approach not only saves you time and money but also enhances your vehicle’s performance and longevity.

If you’re interested in learning more about how the IOLM works or need assistance with your vehicle, contact the **[Service Department at Modern Ford of Boone](https://api.connectcdk.com/api/nc-cosa-consumer-ui/v1/?subscriptionId=&cid=2000096)** for expert guidance.

# Volkswagen Jetta Recommended Maintenance Schedule

![2023 Volkswagen Jetta](https://dealerinspire-image-library-prod.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/images/Ul0f8P7h06keJCujiQSKVvyMiTtkjRbSVGr1DQQy.jpg)

The Volkswagen Jetta is one of the stalwarts of the brand. It gives you excellent fuel economy yet a powerful engine. Maintaining your [new vehicle](https://www.carolinavw.com/new-vehicles/) in its best shape for every Monroe drive means bringing your car in for Volkswagen Jetta service at least once a year. We recommend following the VW Jetta maintenance schedule for the best results.

Discover everything about the VW Jetta service intervals with our comprehensive guide!

[Schedule Volkswagen Jetta Service](https://www.carolinavw.com/online-service-scheduler/) [Service Department](https://www.carolinavw.com/service/)

## What Is the Volkswagen Jetta Maintenance Schedule?

Your [new VW Jetta](https://www.carolinavw.com/new-vehicles/jetta/) service intervals occur every 10,000 miles. Older Volkswagen models might have different maintenance requirements. Check your owner’s manual for the correct VW Jetta maintenance schedule. However, world-class engineering for newer vehicles means longer VW Jetta service intervals, lowering overall ownership costs.

Every 10,000 miles is also the VW Jetta oil change interval, so expect a full synthetic oil change every 10,000 miles of driving. The exception is if you frequently drive in less-than-ideal conditions in Concord. If you repeatedly hit the brakes hard, you might need new tires or new brakes sooner than expected.

Below is the VW Jetta maintenance schedule you should follow.

### **VW Jetta Maintenance Schedule: 10,000 Miles or One Year**

Your first Volkswagen Jetta service in Charlotte will consist of the following:

- Oil and filter change
- Brake pad inspection
- Brake disc inspection
- Service interval reset

### **VW Jetta Maintenance Schedule: 20,000 Miles or Two Years**

For this VW Jetta service interval, we will do everything from the first service at 10,000 miles, plus some extras:

- Engine compartment and transmission inspection
- Battery inspection
- Fluid level adjustments (brake fluid and coolant)
- Tire pressure and TPMS inspection
- Tire tread depth inspection
- Tire repair kit inspection
- Exterior lighting systems inspection
- Windshield wiper and washer system inspection
- Check for sunroof drain blockage
- Horn test
- Road test

### **VW Jetta Maintenance Schedule: 30,000 Miles or Three Years**

This is what our team will do for your three-year Volkswagen Jetta service near Indian Trail to keep your sedan in top shape:

- Oil and filter change
- Brake pad inspection
- Brake disc inspection
- Service interval reset

### **VW Jetta Maintenance Schedule: 40,000 Miles or Four Years**

At 40,000 miles, we’ll take care of the VW Jetta oil change interval, just like the other one-year maintenance. We’ll also check everything from the 20,000-mile VW Jetta service interval. Our team will also look over these things for your Jetta for four years:

**Replacements:**

- Dust and pollen filter
- Spark plugs

**Inspections:**

- Suspension components
- Corrosion inside and out
- Brake system
- Underbody
- Windshield
- Exhaust system
- Interior lighting
- Ribbed V-belt
- Sunroof

### **VW Jetta Maintenance Schedule: 50,000 Miles or Five Years**

At the 50,000-mile mark, this service interval includes everything from the first one:

- VW Jetta Oil Change Interval
- New Oil Filter
- Check Your Brake Pads

# Routine Car Maintenance Schedule By Mileage

July 14th, 2024 by[Spitzer SEO](https://www.spitzervw.com/author/seospitzer-com/ "Posts by Spitzer SEO")

![](https://dealerinspire-image-library-prod.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/images/aC7yitO0dbb2DHg0RCDxkcTTz99WaV7V6KPz3Pqf.jpg)

Proactively managing regular maintenance tasks is essential to maximizing your vehicle’s lifespan. To ensure you stay on top of it, refer to the information provided to determine when your Volkswagen needs an oil change, battery inspection, fluid top-up or replacement, belt examination, brake inspection, new air filter, wheel alignment, and more.

While numerous services are recommended at 10,000 and 5,000-mile intervals, some may be necessary sooner, depending on your driving patterns and circumstances. For instance, hot and rainy weather may increase wear and tear on brake pads, air conditioning filters, and windshield wiper blades. By adhering to the schedule above and heeding the advice of your Volkswagen service advisor, you’ll be able to maintain your Volkswagen in excellent condition for many years.

## 5,000 Mile Service

Your Volkswagen should have its motor oil and oil filter changed every 5,000 miles or six months, whichever comes first. You should also rotate the tires, enabling them to maintain equalized road wear that theoretically allows them to wear out simultaneously, hopefully in the 35-to-40,000-mile range.

## 10,000 Mile Service

Change the oil and oil filter and rotate the tires once again. Beginning at the 10,000-mile mark, the brake pads and rotors should be inspected to ensure proper stopping power. Inspect and top off (if needed) the Continuously Variable Transmission (CVT) fluid and inspect the front driveshaft boots for tears that can allow dust, dirt, and debris inside. Replace windshield wiper blades every year or 10,000 miles, whichever comes first. Check the vehicle’s alignment; it should be realigned at least once a year after rotating the tires.

## 15,000 Mile Service

Two or three times before your car reaches 15,000 miles, it will go in for an oil change. Depending on how long it’s been since you got the last oil change, your car may be due for another one at 15,000 miles. If you’ve recently purchased your vehicle, you should take it within the first year to be serviced and checked. The oil filter and engine oil will also be changed at this milestone along with the oil change. The mechanic will also change the air filters, brake, and washer fluid. This keeps contaminants at bay and maximizes engine performance.

## 20,000 Mile Service

Replace the engine oil, oil filter, and brake fluid, and inspect the brake system, pads, and rotors. Examine the exhaust system to ensure against leaks or damage. Go over the steering gear and linkage and axle and suspension parts. Rotate the tires once again and inspect and refill (if necessary) all of the vehicle’s fluid levels.

## 30,000 Mile Service

When you bring your car in for service at 30,000 miles, you’ll get the same service as you did at 15,000 miles and more. With the 15,000-mile checks, you’ll get a new fuel filter when your car reaches 30,000 miles. The car’s engine coolant fluid will be changed now, and the transmission fluid will be replaced. This keeps your engine from overheating, and the fluid changes keep your car performing at its best. Most likely, the tires will be rotated, too. Other possible services are a brake check, battery replacement, spark plug replacement, transmission service, etc.

## 40,000 Mile Service

You should inspect your %% di\_makes%%’s drive belts and replace the motor oil and filter with fresh versions. At the same time, inspect the EVAP vapor lines and fuel lines. Replace the brake fluid and inspect the CVT fluid for topping off if needed. Rotate the tires, examine windshield wiper blades, and visually inspect the brake pads and rotors once again.

## 60,000 Mile Service

The 60,000-mile service builds on the other two. At this service, you’ll get the same parts replaced as you did before. You’ll probably get the power steering fluid flushed and changed now. If you’ve never had the battery replaced, your mechanic will check its performance level to ensure it’s still going strong. The spark plugs should be checked at 60,000 miles, as should the significant systems, such as brakes and the transmission. Hoses, belts, and valves, which can wear out now, will also be evaluated.

## 90,000 Mile Service

If your car reaches this milestone, rest assured you’re doing something right! Some mechanics will tell you to have your car serviced at 90,000 miles, but others will hold off until 100,000 miles. Despite what you might think, this service only adds more to what was previously done. You should have all the same items checked and replaced that you did at 60,000 miles. The coolant fluid should be flushed and changed at this service time, and the spark plugs will be replaced if they weren’t checked at the previous service. Any hoses and belts that weren’t replaced at 60,000 miles will probably be changed at this point, and your mechanic should also check the condition of your tires.

When it comes to car maintenance, a little goes a long way in preventing problems before they happen. In addition to enhancing your car’s performance, keeping up with routine maintenance reduces safety problems, too. While it’s essential to go in for these service milestones, you should also address issues that arise in the meantime, as your driving habits and driving conditions can affect how often car components need to be replaced. Remember, regular maintenance not only keeps your car running smoothly but also ensures your safety on the road.

# What is the VW Atlas Maintenance Schedule?

![2023 Volkswagen Atlas](https://dealerinspire-image-library-prod.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/images/qnoccVlqnYXcpKsMLB8poK6c7eWZdnzOFdm2DLEX.jpg)

* * *

Following your VW Atlas maintenance schedule is essential to keeping it in top condition on Tysons Corner roads for years to come. If you don’t know the VW Atlas service schedule, don’t worry. Stohlman Volkswagen is here to help. Below, you’ll find detailed information on the VW Atlas service intervals, including when to get a VW Atlas oil change. If you have questions about the VW Atlas service schedule, don’t hesitate to contact us. And, when it comes time for VW Atlas routine maintenance, you can easily [schedule an appointment](https://www.stohlman-vw.com/online-service-scheduler/) with us online.

## VW Atlas Service Schedule

## 10,000 Miles or One Year

The base of your VW Atlas service schedule will consist of the following maintenance tasks:

- Inspect the Brake Pads
- VW Atlas Oil Change
- New Oil Filter
- Service Interval Display Rest (if needed)

## 20,000 Miles or Two Years

Two-year maintenance should also include a VW Atlas oil change and oil filter replacement. The following must also be checked so you can stay safe on Vienna roads:

- Horn
- Tire Repair Kit
- Engine and Engine Compartment Components
- Brake Fluid
- Tire Pressure
- Service Interval Display
- Exterior Lighting
- Battery
- Tires
- Windshield Wiper/Washer System
- Automatic headlight control
- Headlight Washing System
- Wiper Blades
- Coolant Level and Frost Protection
- Brake Pads
- Transmission
- Second Battery
- Tire Pressure Monitoring System

## 30,000 Miles or Three Years

The following VW Atlas routine maintenance tasks will be required every three years or 30,000 miles:

- Oil Change
- New Oil Filter
- Inspect Brake Pads
- Service Interval Display Rest (if needed)

## 40,000 Miles or Four Years

At 40,000 miles, you’ll get a VW Atlas oil change and a new oil filter, plus everything from the 20,000 service interval. These things will also be checked as part of your VW Atlas maintenance schedule:

- Tie Rod Ends
- Stabilizer Bushings
- New Dust and Pollen Filter
- Front and Rear Coil Springs and Shock Absorbers
- Sunroof and Panoramic Sunroof
- Ball Joints
- Wheel Bearings
- Axles
- Coupling Rods

## 50,000 Miles or Five Years

The 50,000 VW Atlas service interval includes:

- Engine Oil Change
- New Oil Filter
- Check Your Brake Pads
- Service Interval Display Rest (if needed)

## 60,000 Miles or 6 Years

Your safety is paramount as you drive around Fairfax, so along with new engine oil, oil filter, air filter, and snow filter, these components will be inspected:

- Fuel filter Replacement
- Dust and Pollen Filter Replacement
- Battery inspection
- Check the Tires
- Brake System Inspection
- Check the Tire fFller Bottle Expiration Date

## 70,000 Miles or 7 Years

The 70,000-mile mark of the VW Atlas maintenance schedule includes the following tasks:

- Engine Oil Filter Change
- Motor Oil Change
- Brake Pad Check
- Service Interval Display Rest (if needed)

## 80,000 Miles or 8 Years

All the same components from the 20,000-mile inspection are inspected, as well as:

- Ball Joints
- Transmission
- Wheel Bearings
- Axles
- Interior Lighting
- Ribbed V-belt
- Front and Rear Coil Springs
- Shock Absorbers
- Sunroof and Panoramic Sunroof
- Underbody

## 90,000 Miles or 9 Years

- Brake Discs
- Clutch Unit
- Engine Oil Change
- Engine Oil Filter Change
- Brake Pad Inspection
- Service Interval Display Rest (if needed)

## 100,000 Miles or 10 Years

At 100,000 miles, you’ll get a VW Atlas oil change and new oil filter, and the same things as the 20,000-mile inspection will be inspected.

## 110,000 Miles or 11 Years

- Brake Pad Check
- Engine Oil Change
- New Oil Filter
- Service Interval Display Rest (if needed)

## 120,000 Miles or 12 Years

Our certified VW Technicians will replace your engine oil, oil filter, and snow and air filter and check all the same components from the 20,000-mile inspection, plus:

- Underbody
- Wheel Bearings
- Axles
- Tie Rod Ends,
- Stabilizer Bushings
- Front and Rear Coil Springs
- Shock Absorbers
- Ball Joints
- Interior Lighting
- Coupling Rods
- Ribbed V-Belt
- Sunroof and Panoramic Sunroof

# Volkswagen Atlas Oil Type & Capacity

![Oil Change](https://dealerinspire-image-library-prod.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/images/dPDQ8g69kRnC3TrrSgdDfloXOa5eUuOdriCxjktZ.jpg)

From keeping engine components lubricated to reducing heat and friction to minimizing wear and tear, using the automaker’s recommended oil will help you get the most out of your [Atlas](https://www.volkswagenofdesmoines.com/new-vehicles/atlas/) on every Des Moines and Waukee drive. But what kind of oil does the Volkswagen Atlas use? Lithia Volkswagen of Des Moines answers this question below, covering the suggested Volkswagen Atlas oil type, as well as the Volkswagen Atlas oil capacity.

[More Service Tips](https://www.volkswagenofdesmoines.com/service/service-tips/) [Schedule Oil Change](https://www.volkswagenofdesmoines.com/schedule-service/)

## What Kind Of Oil Does The Volkswagen Atlas Use?

It’s no secret that routine oil changes are an essential part of [VW maintenance](https://www.volkswagenofdesmoines.com/service/service-tips/volkswagen-maintenance-schedule/). At your next oil change, request the preferred Volkswagen Atlas oil type, which is a full synthetic 0W-30.\* The manufacturer specifically recommends Castrol brand motor oil.

## How Much Oil Does The Volkswagen Atlas Need?

Now that you know what kind of oil the Volkswagen Atlas uses, you are likely curious about exactly how much oil you’ll need. The Volkswagen Atlas oil capacity rings in at 6.02 quarts, which includes the filter.

## Why Choose Synthetic Over Conventional Oil?

The VW Atlas requires full synthetic motor oil due to its sophisticated engine design, which demands premium lubrication for optimal performance on West Des Moines roads and beyond. Here are a few key advantages of synthetic over conventional motor oil:

- **Superior Engine Protection** – Synthetic oils contain additives that create a protective barrier against wear.
- **Smoother Flow** – The structure of synthetic oil maintains better fluidity across temperature extremes, resulting in proper circulation during cold starts and consistent lubrication under high heat.
- **Turbocharged Engine Support** – For Atlas models equipped with turbochargers, synthetic oil provides crucial safeguards for these high-performance components that operate at extreme temperatures and speeds.
- **Extended Oil Life** – Synthetic oil resists thermal breakdown and maintains its protective qualities longer than conventional oil, which can mean more time between oil changes.
- **A Cleaner Oil Supply** – The composition of synthetic oil keeps carbon buildup and sludge formation to a minimum, which, in turn, keeps internal engine parts cleaner and functioning more efficiently.

## Schedule An Oil Change In Johnston

It’s a good idea to schedule an oil change with the suggested Volkswagen Atlas oil type every 10,000 miles. Make an appointment by [contacting us](https://www.volkswagenofdesmoines.com/service/contact-service/) directly or [reserving a time](https://www.volkswagenofdesmoines.com/schedule-service/) online, and don’t hesitate to reach out if you have any further questions about the Volkswagen Atlas oil capacity or type. Our service technicians are here to provide the quality service you need to enjoy your Atlas for years to come.

# 2024 Ford Expedition Maintenance Schedule

![white 2024 Ford expedition SUV parked at the Chalmers Ford dealership in Albuquerque, NM](https://service.secureoffersites.com/images/GetLibraryImage?fileNameOrId=359816)

Following a maintenance schedule can prolong the life of your vehicle, keep fuel efficiency at its best, and cut down on costly repairs over time. A well-maintained vehicle also has a higher resale value. At Chalmers Ford in Rio Rancho, our expert technicians will give your vehicle the exceptional care it needs so it lasts as long as possible. Below we explain the recommended maintenance schedule for your vehicle and the services we provide.

## Understanding Your Ford Expedition's Maintenance Needs

Some maintenance requirements vary based on how you use the vehicle. For example, smart technology calculates the right time for an oil change. The Intelligent Oil-life Monitor takes into account elements such as driving conditions and towing and idling habits to determine when to remind you to change the oil. This system uses a percentage reading to indicate the remaining oil life. You'll see a Change Engine Oil Soon message at 5%. If oil life reaches 0%, it will tell you to change the oil now.

In addition to changing the oil for you when it's due, we'll perform other key maintenance tasks at recommended intervals.

### Every 7,500 Miles or 6 Months

When you hit 7,500 miles or six months, we'll do the following:

- **Tire rotation:** Rotating tires helps them wear evenly and last longer.
- **Brake inspection:** We'll perform a comprehensive brake inspection, examining pads, rotors, hoses, and the parking brake to ensure optimal stopping power.
- **Cooling system check:** This is a thorough examination of the engine's cooling system. We'll replace any damaged hoses and replenish the coolant as needed to prevent overheating problems that can leave you stranded.
- **Suspension check:** This includes checking the steering parts, ball joints, suspension, and tie-rod ends to keep your ride smooth.
- **Wheel inspection:** Finally, we'll inspect your wheels and associated components, listening for unusual sounds and checking for indications of wear, loose parts, or drag. This helps us catch small issues before they turn into major problems.

### Every 15,000 Miles or 12 Months

At the 15,000-mile or 12-month mark, our team will perform the same checks as after 7,500 miles or six months. In addition, we'll replace the cabin air filter, which boosts airflow and improves fuel efficiency. For models with a dipstick, we'll check the automatic transmission fluid level to maintain good transmission health. We'll also check the exhaust system and heat shields. These components regulate emissions and guard against fire risks.

### 30,000 Miles and Beyond

Upon reaching the 30,000-mile point, your Expedition requires even more care. Aside from all the maintenance tasks mentioned above, we'll replace the engine air filter and spark plugs.

Once you've made it to 100,000 miles, the time will have come for another round of spark plug replacements and a comprehensive systems check. We'll also replace the engine coolant to prevent rust and replace the transmission fluid to ensure the gears shift smoothly.

If your Expedition is a four-wheel-drive model, then you should pay special attention to the transfer case fluid, which needs replacing every 30,000 to 60,000 miles depending on your driving habits. The more frequently you drive off-road or tow heavy loads, the sooner you'll need to replace the transfer case fluid. This lubricant is crucial to protect your drivetrain and maintain the highest level of performance for years to come.

## The Importance of Following Ford's Recommended Schedule

Ford's maintenance plan for your Expedition serves as a crucial guide for optimal performance, with its well-designed 10,000-mile system aiming to keep your SUV running smoothly. Check your owner's manual for recommendations. Regular care can save you money on fuel and add years to your vehicle's life. Failing to follow this plan could void your warranty and lead to unexpected expenses. By maintaining detailed records of all the services performed, you'll preserve your warranty and have documentation to support a higher resale value for your vehicle.

Check out our [service specials](https://www.chalmersford.com/specials/service-specials), such as our low-price tire guarantee and lifetime brake pad guarantee. Our deals save you time, money, and worry. Our [service center](https://www.chalmersford.com/service-department) uses advanced tools and performs all repairs using genuine Ford parts, which means everything fits and works just right.

## Trust Chalmers Ford for Your Expedition's Maintenance Needs

At Chalmers Ford, our brand-certified mechanics know your Expedition inside and out. Trust us to give your vehicle the expert care and attention it needs. When you bring it in, we'll service it while you wait in our comfortable lounge. We're open from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. Monday through Friday and from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturday. Come in or contact us today.

## 2024 Ford Expedition Maintenance Schedule

The 2024 Ford Expedition continues to dominate the full-size SUV segment with its combination of
power, spaciousness, and modern technology. According to the Payson Ford dealer, the Expedition’s
robust 3.5-liter EcoBoost V6 engine delivers impressive performance, making it a top choice for families and
adventure enthusiasts alike. With seating for up to eight passengers, a long list of advanced
driver-assistance features, and an array of luxurious options, this SUV is designed to handle everything
from daily commuting to long road trips. Whether towing heavy loads or navigating tough terrains, the 2024
Expedition proves itself to be a versatile and reliable vehicle.

Bringing your Ford Expedition to the Winslow Ford Service Center for scheduled maintenance is crucial for
ensuring it remains reliable, safe, and efficient over the long haul. Regular maintenance, such as oil
changes, brake inspections, and tire rotations, helps prevent costly repairs by addressing minor issues
before they become major problems. At Winslow Ford, the Payson Ford dealership, our certified technicians
use genuine Ford parts and specialized equipment to ensure your Expedition operates at peak
performance. Keeping up with your maintenance schedule not only extends the life of your SUV but also
preserves its resale value, giving you peace of mind on every drive.

These are the milestones of your 2024 Ford Expedition’s scheduled maintenance visits.

## 10,000 Miles

At 10,000 miles, your 2024 Ford Expedition will require its first major scheduled
maintenance. Our certified service technicians will perform an oil and filter change to ensure the
engine runs smoothly and maintains optimal performance. The service team will also rotate the tires
to promote even wear and inspect the brakes, checking for any issues. Fluid levels for vital
systems, such as the transmission and power steering, will be topped off as needed. This visit is
key to preventing early wear on crucial parts.

## 20,000 Miles

At the 20,000-mile mark, our service technicians will focus on inspecting and servicing the
vehicle’s steering and suspension system, making sure everything is aligned and functioning
properly. This includes potential fluid flushes and replenishments for the power steering system. If
necessary, they’ll replace the cabin air filter to maintain proper air circulation.

## 30,000 Miles

For the 30,000-mile service, your certified team will thoroughly inspect the vehicle’s braking
system, paying close attention to the brake pads and rotors for signs of wear. If any issues are
detected, repairs or replacements will be recommended. Additionally, this service will include
checking the battery, and a more detailed inspection of the engine cooling and air conditioning
system will be performed.

## 50,000 Miles

At 50,000 miles, along with the routine oil change and tire rotation, the certified service
technicians will inspect the Expedition’s drivetrain components. They may flush the transmission
fluid to ensure longevity. Suspension parts, such as shocks and struts, will be checked for wear and
may need replacement at this stage.

## 100,000 Miles

When your 2024 Ford Expedition reaches 100,000 miles, the service team will focus on replacing
high-mileage items such as the spark plugs, which are crucial for maintaining engine efficiency.
Additionally, the technicians will inspect and, if necessary, replace the serpentine belt and other
wear-prone components. This visit ensures the longevity of the Expedition as it enters its later life
stages.
