## VW Atlas Service Schedule

## 10,000 Miles or One Year

The base of your VW Atlas service schedule will consist of the following maintenance tasks:

- Inspect the Brake Pads
- VW Atlas Oil Change
- New Oil Filter
- Service Interval Display Rest (if needed)

## 20,000 Miles or Two Years

Two-year maintenance should also include a VW Atlas oil change and oil filter replacement. The following must also be checked so you can stay safe on Vienna roads:

- Horn
- Tire Repair Kit
- Engine and Engine Compartment Components
- Brake Fluid
- Tire Pressure
- Service Interval Display
- Exterior Lighting
- Battery
- Tires
- Windshield Wiper/Washer System
- Automatic headlight control
- Headlight Washing System
- Wiper Blades
- Coolant Level and Frost Protection
- Brake Pads
- Transmission
- Second Battery
- Tire Pressure Monitoring System

## 30,000 Miles or Three Years

The following VW Atlas routine maintenance tasks will be required every three years or 30,000 miles:

- Oil Change
- New Oil Filter
- Inspect Brake Pads
- Service Interval Display Rest (if needed)

## 40,000 Miles or Four Years

At 40,000 miles, you’ll get a VW Atlas oil change and a new oil filter, plus everything from the 20,000 service interval. These things will also be checked as part of your VW Atlas maintenance schedule:

- Tie Rod Ends
- Stabilizer Bushings
- New Dust and Pollen Filter
- Front and Rear Coil Springs and Shock Absorbers
- Sunroof and Panoramic Sunroof
- Ball Joints
- Wheel Bearings
- Axles
- Coupling Rods

## 50,000 Miles or Five Years

The 50,000 VW Atlas service interval includes:

- Engine Oil Change
- New Oil Filter
- Check Your Brake Pads
- Service Interval Display Rest (if needed)

## 60,000 Miles or 6 Years

Your safety is paramount as you drive around Fairfax, so along with new engine oil, oil filter, air filter, and snow filter, these components will be inspected:

- Fuel filter Replacement
- Dust and Pollen Filter Replacement
- Battery inspection
- Check the Tires
- Brake System Inspection
- Check the Tire fFller Bottle Expiration Date

## 70,000 Miles or 7 Years

The 70,000-mile mark of the VW Atlas maintenance schedule includes the following tasks:

- Engine Oil Filter Change
- Motor Oil Change
- Brake Pad Check
- Service Interval Display Rest (if needed)

## 80,000 Miles or 8 Years

All the same components from the 20,000-mile inspection are inspected, as well as:

- Ball Joints
- Transmission
- Wheel Bearings
- Axles
- Interior Lighting
- Ribbed V-belt
- Front and Rear Coil Springs
- Shock Absorbers
- Sunroof and Panoramic Sunroof
- Underbody

## 90,000 Miles or 9 Years

- Brake Discs
- Clutch Unit
- Engine Oil Change
- Engine Oil Filter Change
- Brake Pad Inspection
- Service Interval Display Rest (if needed)

## 100,000 Miles or 10 Years

At 100,000 miles, you’ll get a VW Atlas oil change and new oil filter, and the same things as the 20,000-mile inspection will be inspected.

## 110,000 Miles or 11 Years

- Brake Pad Check
- Engine Oil Change
- New Oil Filter
- Service Interval Display Rest (if needed)

## 120,000 Miles or 12 Years

Our certified VW Technicians will replace your engine oil, oil filter, and snow and air filter and check all the same components from the 20,000-mile inspection, plus:

- Underbody
- Wheel Bearings
- Axles
- Tie Rod Ends,
- Stabilizer Bushings
- Front and Rear Coil Springs
- Shock Absorbers
- Ball Joints
- Interior Lighting
- Coupling Rods
- Ribbed V-Belt
- Sunroof and Panoramic Sunroof

# 2024 Volkswagen Atlas Maintenance Schedule

![hero image](https://dealerimages.dealereprocess.com/image/upload/3416655)

# 2024 Volkswagen Atlas Maintenance Schedule

Regular maintenance is vital to ensuring the longevity and efficiency of your 2024 Atlas. By adhering to the manufacturer's recommended maintenance schedule, you can prevent costly repairs down the road and prolong its resale value. Scheduled maintenance also increases overall safety by addressing potential issues before they escalate. The VW-certified technicians at Pohanka Volkswagen of Capitol Heights always prioritize your safety and satisfaction. Here, we summarize the maintenance schedule recommended by Volkswagen to keep the 2024 Atlas running its best.

![](https://dealerimages.dealereprocess.com/image/upload/3382164)

[Schedule Service](https://www.pohankavw.com/online-service-scheduler/)

## 10,000 Miles

At the 10,000-mile mark, your 2024 Atlas will require its first maintenance visit. During this service, our technicians will look over the vehicle's systems to ensure that everything is functioning properly. They will also take care of the scheduled oil and filter change, along with a tire rotation to promote even tread wear.

## 20,000 Miles

When your Atlas reaches 20,000 miles, it will be time for another round of essential maintenance. Our service technicians will conduct a more thorough examination, this time including elements such as the battery’s well-being (including how well it is charging), the coolant level, transmission function, and operation of all lights. Once again, your Atlas will receive an oil and filter change, as well as a tire rotation, brake inspection, and comprehensive check of all fluid levels and components.

## 40,000 Miles

When the odometer on your Atlas reads 40,000 miles, it will be time once again for our certified technicians to perform all the services included in the previous intervals (oil change, tire rotation, and multipoint inspection). They will also replace the dust and pollen filters.

## 60,000 Miles

The 60,000-mile service interval for the 2024 Atlas will cover everything performed at the 20,000-mile mark, in addition to replacing the cabin air filter to make sure you and your passengers are breathing clean air.

## 80,000 Miles

The 80,000-mile mark means it’s time for a more comprehensive maintenance service, as well as a complete mechanical check to monitor the vehicle’s continued reliability and performance. Besides repeating all of the services mentioned for the previous intervals, they will put in a fresh set of spark plugs and drain and replace the transmission fluid.

## What is the Volkswagen Atlas Maintenance Schedule?

Your [new VW Atlas](https://www.carolinavw.com/new-vehicles/atlas/) service intervals occur every 10,000 miles. Older Volkswagen models might have different maintenance requirements, so check your owner’s manual for the correct VW Atlas maintenance schedule. However, world-class engineering means longer VW Atlas service intervals when you have a late-model vehicle.

Every 10,000 miles represents the VW Atlas oil change interval, so expect to get a full synthetic oil change every 10,000 miles of driving unless you drive in less-than-ideal conditions regularly in Concord.

Below is the general VW Atlas maintenance schedule you should follow.

### **VW Atlas Maintenance Schedule: 10,000 Miles or One Year**

Your first Volkswagen Atlas service in Charlotte will get this:

- Inspect the Brake Pads
- Oil Change
- New Oil Filter
- Fluid Level Check
- Service Interval Display Reset (if needed)

### **VW Atlas Maintenance Schedule: 20,000 Miles or Two Years**

For this VW Atlas service interval, we will do everything from the first service at 10,000 miles, plus some extras:

- Automatic headlight control
- Headlight Washing System
- Wiper Blades
- Coolant Level and Frost Protection
- Brake Pads
- Transmission
- Second Battery
- Engine Air Filter Check
- Tire Pressure Monitoring System
- Horn
- Tire Repair Kit
- Engine and Engine Compartment Components
- Brake Fluid
- Tire Pressure
- Service Interval Display
- Exterior Lighting
- Battery
- Tires
- Windshield Wiper/Washer System

### **VW Atlas Maintenance Schedule: 30,000 Miles or Three Years**

Here’s what our team will do for your three-year Volkswagen Atlas service near Indian Trail:

- Oil Change
- New Oil Filter
- Inspect Brake Pads
- Service Interval Display Reset (if needed)

### **VW Atlas Maintenance Schedule: 40,000 Miles or Four Years**

At 40,000 miles, we’ll take care of the VW Atlas oil change interval, just like the other one-year maintenance. We’ll also check everything from the 20,000-mile VW Atlas service interval. Our team will also look over these things for your Atlas for four years:

- Sunroof and Panoramic Sunroof
- Ball Joints
- Wheel Bearings
- Axles
- Coupling Rods
- Tie Rod Ends
- Stabilizer Bushings
- New Dust and Pollen Filter for the Cabin
- Front and Rear Coil Springs and Shock Absorbers

### **VW Atlas Maintenance Schedule: 50,000 Miles or Five Years**

At the 50,000-mile mark, this service interval includes everything from the initial service interval:

- VW Atlas Oil Change Interval
- New Oil Filter
- Check Your Brake Pads
- Fluid Levels
- Service Interval Display Reset (if needed)

At this point in your SUV ownership, you might need a new battery, new tires, or new brake parts, depending on the condition of your Volkswagen Atlas. We’ll discuss your options with you if we see anything that needs service at this interval.

Moving forward, we’ll also inspect the drive belts, the condition of the transmission, and the radiator, as these parts might show more signs of wear. If our service technicians detect any looming issues that need to be resolved soon, we’ll suggest a way to remedy the situation.

## 2025 FORD BRONCO SPORT MAINTENANCE SCHEDULE

The 2025 Ford Bronco Sport blends tough off-road ability with an eye-catching design. According to the Prescott Ford dealer, this compact SUV is ready for action, with standard all-wheel drive, raised ground clearance, and specialized traction settings. Its spacious interior and generous cargo hold make it ideal for buyers who want a daily driver that's also trail-ready.

Regular maintenance keeps your Bronco Sport performing at its best while protecting your investment. The service team at Winslow Ford, the Prescott Ford dealership, has outlined key maintenance milestones that help prevent costly repairs and maintain vehicle value. Following Ford's recommended service schedule helps ensure your SUV provides years of reliable performance. Each maintenance visit allows our certified service technicians to thoroughly inspect your vehicle and address potential issues before they develop into serious problems.

### Every 7,500 Miles

Your Bronco Sport needs fresh oil every 7,500 miles or six months, whichever comes first. This fundamental service ensures proper engine lubrication, promotes fuel efficiency, and guards against premature wear. Clean oil helps remove contaminants that build up during normal operation while safeguarding vital engine components.

### Every 10,000 Miles

At 10,000 miles, technicians perform basic maintenance, including an oil filter change and tire rotation. They also thoroughly inspect multiple systems, including tires and tire pressure, engine coolant, exhaust system and heat shields, transmission fluid levels, rear axle and u-joints, half-shaft boots, brakes, suspension, and steering.

### Every 20,000 Miles

At 20,000 miles, your Bronco Sport needs a fresh cabin air filter. This maintenance step significantly impacts interior air quality by removing dust, pollen, and other airborne particles from the air. A clean filter improves cabin air quality and helps the climate control system work efficiently.

### 30,000 Miles

The 30,000-mile service focuses on an engine air filter replacement. The filter stops dirt and debris from getting into your engine. Replacing it on schedule keeps your engine running strong, prevents stalling, and helps with fuel economy.

### 100,000 Miles

The 100,000-mile service marks a major maintenance milestone. Your Bronco Sport requires fresh coolant to prevent overheating and protect against corrosion. New spark plugs ensure reliable starting and smooth operation. Our service technicians will also thoroughly inspect the accessory drive belt system for wear.

### 150,000 Miles

At 150,000 miles, crucial drivetrain components need attention. The service includes fresh automatic transmission fluid to maintain smooth shifting and protect transmission components. Our service team will also check the condition of the accessory drive belt. This major service helps maintain reliability and prevents unexpected mechanical issues that could leave you stranded.

Regular inspection and maintenance help ensure your 2025 Ford Bronco Sport maintains its performance throughout its life. Following the recommended maintenance schedule protects your investment while helping avoid costly repairs down the road.

Schedule your Bronco Sport's next service through our website or by calling the Winslow Ford Service Center. Our factory-trained technicians use genuine Ford parts and follow factory service procedures to maintain your SUV's performance and reliability. With proper care, your Bronco Sport will continue delivering the capability and comfort you expect for years to come.

# Volkswagen Jetta Recommended Maintenance Schedule

![2023 Volkswagen Jetta](https://dealerinspire-image-library-prod.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/images/Ul0f8P7h06keJCujiQSKVvyMiTtkjRbSVGr1DQQy.jpg)

* * *

The Volkswagen Jetta is one of the stalwarts of the brand. It gives you excellent fuel economy yet a powerful engine. Maintaining your [new vehicle](https://www.carolinavw.com/new-vehicles/) in its best shape for every Monroe drive means bringing your car in for Volkswagen Jetta service at least once a year. We recommend following the VW Jetta maintenance schedule for the best results.

Discover everything about the VW Jetta service intervals with our comprehensive guide!

[Schedule Volkswagen Jetta Service](https://www.carolinavw.com/online-service-scheduler/) [Service Department](https://www.carolinavw.com/service/)

## What Is the Volkswagen Jetta Maintenance Schedule?

Your [new VW Jetta](https://www.carolinavw.com/new-vehicles/jetta/) service intervals occur every 10,000 miles. Older Volkswagen models might have different maintenance requirements. Check your owner’s manual for the correct VW Jetta maintenance schedule. However, world-class engineering for newer vehicles means longer VW Jetta service intervals, lowering overall ownership costs.

Every 10,000 miles is also the VW Jetta oil change interval, so expect a full synthetic oil change every 10,000 miles of driving. The exception is if you frequently drive in less-than-ideal conditions in Concord. If you repeatedly hit the brakes hard, you might need new tires or new brakes sooner than expected.

Below is the VW Jetta maintenance schedule you should follow.

### **VW Jetta Maintenance Schedule: 10,000 Miles or One Year**

Your first Volkswagen Jetta service in Charlotte will consist of the following:

- Oil and filter change
- Brake pad inspection
- Brake disc inspection
- Service interval reset

### **VW Jetta Maintenance Schedule: 20,000 Miles or Two Years**

For this VW Jetta service interval, we will do everything from the first service at 10,000 miles, plus some extras:

- Engine compartment and transmission inspection
- Battery inspection
- Fluid level adjustments (brake fluid and coolant)
- Tire pressure and TPMS inspection
- Tire tread depth inspection
- Tire repair kit inspection
- Exterior lighting systems inspection
- Windshield wiper and washer system inspection
- Check for sunroof drain blockage
- Horn test
- Road test

### **VW Jetta Maintenance Schedule: 30,000 Miles or Three Years**

This is what our team will do for your three-year Volkswagen Jetta service near Indian Trail to keep your sedan in top shape:

- Oil and filter change
- Brake pad inspection
- Brake disc inspection
- Service interval reset

### **VW Jetta Maintenance Schedule: 40,000 Miles or Four Years**

At 40,000 miles, we’ll take care of the VW Jetta oil change interval, just like the other one-year maintenance. We’ll also check everything from the 20,000-mile VW Jetta service interval. Our team will also look over these things for your Jetta for four years:

**Replacements:**

- Dust and pollen filter
- Spark plugs

**Inspections:**

- Suspension components
- Corrosion inside and out
- Brake system
- Underbody
- Windshield
- Exhaust system
- Interior lighting
- Ribbed V-belt
- Sunroof

### **VW Jetta Maintenance Schedule: 50,000 Miles or Five Years**

At the 50,000-mile mark, this service interval includes everything from the first one:

- VW Jetta Oil Change Interval
- New Oil Filter
- Check Your Brake Pads
- Fluid Levels
- Service Interval Display Reset (if needed)

At this point in your sedan ownership, you might need a new battery, new tires, or new brake parts, depending on the condition of your Volkswagen Jetta. We’ll discuss your options with you if we see anything that needs service at this interval.

# Routine Car Maintenance Schedule By Mileage

July 14th, 2024 by[Spitzer SEO](https://www.spitzervw.com/author/seospitzer-com/ "Posts by Spitzer SEO")

Share this Post:
Share on FacebookShare on Twitter

![](https://dealerinspire-image-library-prod.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/images/aC7yitO0dbb2DHg0RCDxkcTTz99WaV7V6KPz3Pqf.jpg)

[Schedule Service](https://www.spitzervw.com/schedule-service/) [Contact Us](https://www.spitzervw.com/contact-us/)

Proactively managing regular maintenance tasks is essential to maximizing your vehicle’s lifespan. To ensure you stay on top of it, refer to the information provided to determine when your Volkswagen needs an oil change, battery inspection, fluid top-up or replacement, belt examination, brake inspection, new air filter, wheel alignment, and more.

While numerous services are recommended at 10,000 and 5,000-mile intervals, some may be necessary sooner, depending on your driving patterns and circumstances. For instance, hot and rainy weather may increase wear and tear on brake pads, air conditioning filters, and windshield wiper blades. By adhering to the schedule above and heeding the advice of your Volkswagen service advisor, you’ll be able to maintain your Volkswagen in excellent condition for many years.

## 5,000 Mile Service

Your Volkswagen should have its motor oil and oil filter changed every 5,000 miles or six months, whichever comes first. You should also rotate the tires, enabling them to maintain equalized road wear that theoretically allows them to wear out simultaneously, hopefully in the 35-to-40,000-mile range.

## 10,000 Mile Service

Change the oil and oil filter and rotate the tires once again. Beginning at the 10,000-mile mark, the brake pads and rotors should be inspected to ensure proper stopping power. Inspect and top off (if needed) the Continuously Variable Transmission (CVT) fluid and inspect the front driveshaft boots for tears that can allow dust, dirt, and debris inside. Replace windshield wiper blades every year or 10,000 miles, whichever comes first. Check the vehicle’s alignment; it should be realigned at least once a year after rotating the tires.

## 15,000 Mile Service

Two or three times before your car reaches 15,000 miles, it will go in for an oil change. Depending on how long it’s been since you got the last oil change, your car may be due for another one at 15,000 miles. If you’ve recently purchased your vehicle, you should take it within the first year to be serviced and checked. The oil filter and engine oil will also be changed at this milestone along with the oil change. The mechanic will also change the air filters, brake, and washer fluid. This keeps contaminants at bay and maximizes engine performance.

## 20,000 Mile Service

Replace the engine oil, oil filter, and brake fluid, and inspect the brake system, pads, and rotors. Examine the exhaust system to ensure against leaks or damage. Go over the steering gear and linkage and axle and suspension parts. Rotate the tires once again and inspect and refill (if necessary) all of the vehicle’s fluid levels.

## 30,000 Mile Service

When you bring your car in for service at 30,000 miles, you’ll get the same service as you did at 15,000 miles and more. With the 15,000-mile checks, you’ll get a new fuel filter when your car reaches 30,000 miles. The car’s engine coolant fluid will be changed now, and the transmission fluid will be replaced. This keeps your engine from overheating, and the fluid changes keep your car performing at its best. Most likely, the tires will be rotated, too. Other possible services are a brake check, battery replacement, spark plug replacement, transmission service, etc.

## 40,000 Mile Service

You should inspect your %% di\_makes%%’s drive belts and replace the motor oil and filter with fresh versions. At the same time, inspect the EVAP vapor lines and fuel lines. Replace the brake fluid and inspect the CVT fluid for topping off if needed. Rotate the tires, examine windshield wiper blades, and visually inspect the brake pads and rotors once again.

## 60,000 Mile Service

The 60,000-mile service builds on the other two. At this service, you’ll get the same parts replaced as you did before. You’ll probably get the power steering fluid flushed and changed now. If you’ve never had the battery replaced, your mechanic will check its performance level to ensure it’s still going strong. The spark plugs should be checked at 60,000 miles, as should the significant systems, such as brakes and the transmission. Hoses, belts, and valves, which can wear out now, will also be evaluated.

## 90,000 Mile Service

If your car reaches this milestone, rest assured you’re doing something right! Some mechanics will tell you to have your car serviced at 90,000 miles, but others will hold off until 100,000 miles. Despite what you might think, this service only adds more to what was previously done. You should have all the same items checked and replaced that you did at 60,000 miles. The coolant fluid should be flushed and changed at this service time, and the spark plugs will be replaced if they weren’t checked at the previous service. Any hoses and belts that weren’t replaced at 60,000 miles will probably be changed at this point, and your mechanic should also check the condition of your tires.

When it comes to car maintenance, a little goes a long way in preventing problems before they happen. In addition to enhancing your car’s performance, keeping up with routine maintenance reduces safety problems, too. While it’s essential to go in for these service milestones, you should also address issues that arise in the meantime, as your driving habits and driving conditions can affect how often car components need to be replaced. Remember, regular maintenance not only keeps your car running smoothly but also ensures your safety on the road.

Following your VW Atlas maintenance schedule is essential to keeping it in top condition on Tysons Corner roads for years to come. If you don’t know the VW Atlas service schedule, don’t worry. Stohlman Volkswagen is here to help. Below, you’ll find detailed information on the VW Atlas service intervals, including when to get a VW Atlas oil change. If you have questions about the VW Atlas service schedule, don’t hesitate to contact us. And, when it comes time for VW Atlas routine maintenance, you can easily [schedule an appointment](https://www.stohlman-vw.com/online-service-scheduler/) with us online.

## VW Atlas Service Schedule

## 10,000 Miles or One Year

The base of your VW Atlas service schedule will consist of the following maintenance tasks:

- Inspect the Brake Pads
- VW Atlas Oil Change
- New Oil Filter
- Service Interval Display Rest (if needed)

## 20,000 Miles or Two Years

Two-year maintenance should also include a VW Atlas oil change and oil filter replacement. The following must also be checked so you can stay safe on Vienna roads:

- Horn
- Tire Repair Kit
- Engine and Engine Compartment Components
- Brake Fluid
- Tire Pressure
- Service Interval Display
- Exterior Lighting
- Battery
- Tires
- Windshield Wiper/Washer System
- Automatic headlight control
- Headlight Washing System
- Wiper Blades
- Coolant Level and Frost Protection
- Brake Pads
- Transmission
- Second Battery
- Tire Pressure Monitoring System

## 30,000 Miles or Three Years

The following VW Atlas routine maintenance tasks will be required every three years or 30,000 miles:

- Oil Change
- New Oil Filter
- Inspect Brake Pads
- Service Interval Display Rest (if needed)

## 40,000 Miles or Four Years

At 40,000 miles, you’ll get a VW Atlas oil change and a new oil filter, plus everything from the 20,000 service interval. These things will also be checked as part of your VW Atlas maintenance schedule:

- Tie Rod Ends
- Stabilizer Bushings
- New Dust and Pollen Filter
- Front and Rear Coil Springs and Shock Absorbers
- Sunroof and Panoramic Sunroof
- Ball Joints
- Wheel Bearings
- Axles
- Coupling Rods

## 50,000 Miles or Five Years

The 50,000 VW Atlas service interval includes:

- Engine Oil Change
- New Oil Filter
- Check Your Brake Pads
- Service Interval Display Rest (if needed)

## 60,000 Miles or 6 Years

Your safety is paramount as you drive around Fairfax, so along with new engine oil, oil filter, air filter, and snow filter, these components will be inspected:

- Fuel filter Replacement
- Dust and Pollen Filter Replacement
- Battery inspection
- Check the Tires
- Brake System Inspection
- Check the Tire fFller Bottle Expiration Date

## 70,000 Miles or 7 Years

The 70,000-mile mark of the VW Atlas maintenance schedule includes the following tasks:

- Engine Oil Filter Change
- Motor Oil Change
- Brake Pad Check
- Service Interval Display Rest (if needed)

## 80,000 Miles or 8 Years

All the same components from the 20,000-mile inspection are inspected, as well as:

- Ball Joints
- Transmission
- Wheel Bearings
- Axles
- Interior Lighting
- Ribbed V-belt
- Front and Rear Coil Springs
- Shock Absorbers
- Sunroof and Panoramic Sunroof
- Underbody

## 90,000 Miles or 9 Years

- Brake Discs
- Clutch Unit
- Engine Oil Change
- Engine Oil Filter Change
- Brake Pad Inspection
- Service Interval Display Rest (if needed)

## 100,000 Miles or 10 Years

At 100,000 miles, you’ll get a VW Atlas oil change and new oil filter, and the same things as the 20,000-mile inspection will be inspected.

## 110,000 Miles or 11 Years

- Brake Pad Check
- Engine Oil Change
- New Oil Filter
- Service Interval Display Rest (if needed)

## 120,000 Miles or 12 Years

Our certified VW Technicians will replace your engine oil, oil filter, and snow and air filter and check all the same components from the 20,000-mile inspection, plus:

- Underbody
- Wheel Bearings
- Axles
- Tie Rod Ends,
- Stabilizer Bushings
- Front and Rear Coil Springs
- Shock Absorbers
- Ball Joints
- Interior Lighting
- Coupling Rods
- Ribbed V-Belt
- Sunroof and Panoramic Sunroof

# Volkswagen Atlas Recommended Maintenance Schedule

![2024 Volkswagen Atlas Cross Sport](https://dealerinspire-image-library-prod.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/images/HCVHpYQ40O5omvhZPfsFjwslXoPDGyijs1wj9AW6.png)

* * *

The Volkswagen Atlas gives you everything you want in a [new vehicle](https://www.carolinavw.com/new-vehicles/) thanks to a family-friendly SUV with excellent fuel economy and a powerful engine. Keeping your SUV in excellent shape for every Monroe drive means bringing your vehicle in for Volkswagen Atlas service occasionally. We highly recommend following the VW Atlas maintenance schedule for the best results.

Learn everything you need to know about the VW Atlas service intervals with our guide!

[Schedule Volkswagen Atlas Service](https://www.carolinavw.com/online-service-scheduler/) [Service Department](https://www.carolinavw.com/service/)

## What is the Volkswagen Atlas Maintenance Schedule?

Your [new VW Atlas](https://www.carolinavw.com/new-vehicles/atlas/) service intervals occur every 10,000 miles. Older Volkswagen models might have different maintenance requirements, so check your owner’s manual for the correct VW Atlas maintenance schedule. However, world-class engineering means longer VW Atlas service intervals when you have a late-model vehicle.

Every 10,000 miles represents the VW Atlas oil change interval, so expect to get a full synthetic oil change every 10,000 miles of driving unless you drive in less-than-ideal conditions regularly in Concord.

Below is the general VW Atlas maintenance schedule you should follow.

### **VW Atlas Maintenance Schedule: 10,000 Miles or One Year**

Your first Volkswagen Atlas service in Charlotte will get this:

- Inspect the Brake Pads
- Oil Change
- New Oil Filter
- Fluid Level Check
- Service Interval Display Reset (if needed)

### **VW Atlas Maintenance Schedule: 20,000 Miles or Two Years**

For this VW Atlas service interval, we will do everything from the first service at 10,000 miles, plus some extras:

- Automatic headlight control
- Headlight Washing System
- Wiper Blades
- Coolant Level and Frost Protection
- Brake Pads
- Transmission
- Second Battery
- Engine Air Filter Check
- Tire Pressure Monitoring System
- Horn
- Tire Repair Kit
- Engine and Engine Compartment Components
- Brake Fluid
- Tire Pressure
- Service Interval Display
- Exterior Lighting
- Battery
- Tires
- Windshield Wiper/Washer System

### **VW Atlas Maintenance Schedule: 30,000 Miles or Three Years**

Here’s what our team will do for your three-year Volkswagen Atlas service near Indian Trail:

- Oil Change
- New Oil Filter
- Inspect Brake Pads
- Service Interval Display Reset (if needed)

### **VW Atlas Maintenance Schedule: 40,000 Miles or Four Years**

At 40,000 miles, we’ll take care of the VW Atlas oil change interval, just like the other one-year maintenance. We’ll also check everything from the 20,000-mile VW Atlas service interval. Our team will also look over these things for your Atlas for four years:

- Sunroof and Panoramic Sunroof
- Ball Joints
- Wheel Bearings
- Axles
- Coupling Rods
- Tie Rod Ends
- Stabilizer Bushings
- New Dust and Pollen Filter for the Cabin
- Front and Rear Coil Springs and Shock Absorbers

### **VW Atlas Maintenance Schedule: 50,000 Miles or Five Years**

At the 50,000-mile mark, this service interval includes everything from the initial service interval:

- VW Atlas Oil Change Interval
- New Oil Filter
- Check Your Brake Pads
- Fluid Levels
- Service Interval Display Reset (if needed)

At this point in your SUV ownership, you might need a new battery, new tires, or new brake parts, depending on the condition of your Volkswagen Atlas. We’ll discuss your options with you if we see anything that needs service at this interval.

Moving forward, we’ll also inspect the drive belts, the condition of the transmission, and the radiator, as these parts might show more signs of wear. If our service technicians detect any looming issues that need to be resolved soon, we’ll suggest a way to remedy the situation.

# BMW 3 Series Maintenance Schedule

![](https://dealerimages.dealereprocess.com/image/upload/3734739)

## Maintenance Schedule

Keeping up with your vehicle’s routine maintenance schedule is crucial to the health and longevity of your car. Routine maintenance services are done about once or twice a year, and are usually just a quick stop by the shop to change your oil and make sure everything is working properly.

**Here at BMW of Westchester we know how important it is to stay on top of these services in order to keep your car on the streets of Westchester County and Yonkers, NY, for years to come. Check out our breakdown of the BMW 3 Series maintenance schedule below!  [Schedule a service appointment](https://www.westchesterbmw.com/service-appointment/) for more assistance.**

## Annual Routine Maintenance Services

Your first[BMW 3 Series](https://www.westchesterbmw.com/search/new-bmw-3-series-white-plains-ny/?cy=10607&md=33&tp=new) routine maintenance service will happen about 6 months in, or once you hit around 5,000-10,000 miles, whichever happens to come first. This first service will be relatively quick. It will include:

- **An oil and filter change**

- **Tire rotation**

- **Brake inspection**


You’ll want to get these services done once or twice a year for the duration of the vehicle’s life.

Staying on top of your regular oil and oil filter changes is crucial to your car’s health because as your engine runs, tiny bits of dirt and dust will build up in it, which can cause excessive wear and tear.

**Additionally, yearly [tire rotations](https://www.westchesterbmw.com/service-appointment/) are important to maintain traction control, because they prevent your wheels from having uneven tread. Tread and traction control helps your vehicle stop quicker, and provides you with safer travels over rough terrain.**

![](https://dealerimages.dealereprocess.com/image/upload/3734763)

![](https://dealerimages.dealereprocess.com/image/upload/3734769)

## 30,000-Mile Maintenance Services

Once your BMW 3 Series hits 30,000 miles, it’s time to head back to the shop for a variety of inspections and maintenance care checks. To start, you’re going to need:

- **Your air filter changed, over time your air filter can become clogged, and a replacement will be needed in order for it to work at its best. If you travel in particularly dusty environments, you’ll want this changed around 15,000 miles rather than 30,000.**

- **Next, you’ll need your fuel filter inspected; your technician can perform a pressure test to determine if you’ll need it replaced.**


## 60,000-Mile Maintenance Services

Your 60,000-mile maintenance service will happen at around four or five years into ownership for the average driver. At this service, you’ll need:

- **Brake Rotor, Pads, and Shoes Inspections and Replacements**

- **Brake Fluid Replacement**

- **Coolant Replacement**

- **Transmission Fluid Replacement**

- **Your BMW 3 Series battery and brakes will start to wear out around the 60,000-mile mark, which is why it’s so important to get them inspected, and possibly replaced.**


![](https://dealerimages.dealereprocess.com/image/upload/3734756)

![](https://dealerimages.dealereprocess.com/image/upload/3734759)

## 90,000-Mile Maintenance Services

Your 90,000-mile maintenance check will include an inspection of your hoses, belts, and spark plugs. If they’re not up to par, they’ll need to be replaced. Additionally, you’ll also need to replace your power steering fluid to keep your steering wheel working properly. You should also get the following done:

- **Timing belt replacement**

- **Replace hoses**

- **Replace spark plugs**

- **Rotate rotors or replace rotors**

- **Fuel system cleaning**

- **Complete inspection**


## Stop by for Your Next Maintenance Service!

Staying on top of your routine maintenance services is imperative to your vehicle’s health, and will help you get the most out of it. Here at BMW of Westchester we’re dedicated to providing the drivers of Westchester County and Yonkers, NY, with high quality service every time they come in. Call or stop by to schedule your next appointment!

## [Century West BMW – Recommended service and maintenance schedule for BMW 3 Series](https://www.centurywestbmw.com/service/)

Your BMW 3 Series thrives on precision. A thoughtful, consistent maintenance plan keeps its TwinPower Turbo engines, xDrive components, and chassis systems performing the way Munich intended. At Century West BMW, our BMW M Certified technicians combine factory training, OEM diagnostics, and Genuine BMW Parts to deliver service that fits your model year and driving style. We read your vehicle’s Condition Based Service (CBS) data through iDrive, verify with a multi-point inspection, and then tailor a plan that protects performance, efficiency, and resale value—without recommending work you do not need. From oil and filter changes to brake fluid exchanges, tire services, alignments, and software updates, we complete work to BMW specifications and reset onboard service counters so your reminders stay accurate. Because Los Angeles traffic, short trips, and heat can accelerate wear, we also check cooling performance, battery health, and brake life at each visit. With online scheduling, clear recommendations, and quick turnaround, our team makes it simple to stay current. As a local resource serving North Hollywood, we are here to help you enjoy every mile in your 3 Series.

- **Every 10,000 miles or 12 months**: BMW Longlife oil and filter; inspect brakes and tires; top off fluids; road test.
- **Every 20,000 miles or 2 years**: Cabin microfilter replacement; brake fluid exchange; comprehensive multi-point inspection.
- **Every 30,000 miles**: Engine air filter; fuel system check; inspect PCV and induction plumbing.
- **Every 60,000 miles**: Spark plugs; coolant inspection and service as applicable; accessory belt check.
- **Every 75,000 to 90,000 miles**: Transmission and differential fluid service where applicable; cooling system service; suspension, steering, and alignment.
- **Every visit or seasonally**: Battery test; tire rotation if non-staggered; set pressures; wiper blades; software updates; visual leak check.

Use the general schedule above as a baseline, then adjust based on CBS alerts, mileage, and conditions. A few smart habits go a long way: set reminders for time-based items like brake fluid, rotate tires if your setup allows, align annually to safeguard run-flat tires and driver-assistance calibrations, and keep a simple maintenance log in your BMW App or glovebox. If your 3 Series is driven mainly in stop-and-go or on short trips, shorten intervals. If it tows, sees spirited canyon drives, track time, or uses staggered performance tires, ask our advisors for a customized plan. Intervals vary by engine, transmission, and model year—including plug-in hybrid variants—so always review your Owner’s Manual and BMW maintenance program, and contact the manufacturer or our service team for details. When you are ready, schedule service or request more information, and we will map out the right plan, provide clear next steps, and keep your BMW 3 Series feeling like The Ultimate Driving Machine.

# BMW SERVICE

BMW recommends you have your maintenance and repair work performed by an authorized BMW center.

# MAINTAINING YOUR BMW VEHICLE

A well-maintained vehicle will help safeguard its operational performance, road-safety and its reliability. This is why it is important to follow and perform BMW’s recommended periodic vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks as indicated by your vehicle’s Maintenance Service Display, along with the other maintenance work described in this booklet.

A improper maintenance is not covered under the BMW New Vehicle Damage, including consequential damage, which results from lack of or Limited Warranty for Passenger Cars and Light Trucks.

# MAINTENANCE INTERVALS

Maintenance intervals on motor vehicles were conventionally based solely on a fixed time period or a specified amount of accumulated driving mileage.

However, operational and driving conditions have a major influence on your vehicle’s routine maintenance requirements; the distance traveled is only one of these significant factors. A vehicle used for short trips in the city with numerous cold starts, prolonged periods of idling, stop-and-go driving, and high engine speeds during acceleration may require more frequent maintenance intervals than a vehicle that is driven long distances at moderate engine speeds.

Your BMW vehicle uses sensors and algorithms together with the elapsed time and the driving distance/profile to monitor and evaluate your vehicle’s maintenance service needs. This information is then used to adapt dynamically the parameters used to forecast the applicable maintenance service task intervals.

# THE BMW MAINTENANCE SYSTEM

All BMW vehicles are equipped with an integrated BMW Maintenance System. This maintenance “reminder” system helps ensure that the vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks are performed at the forecasted intervals that apply to your vehicle.

The BMW Maintenance System display provides the vehicle operator access to the current status information for the following maintenance service tasks:

$\\triangleright$ Engine oil (date and miles)\*

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle check (date and miles)

$\\triangleright$ Front brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Rear brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid (date)

$\\triangleright$ 1200 Mile running-in service (date and miles) (Applicable to BMW M vehicles only)\*

For each specific maintenance service task, either the future date (month/ year), remaining miles or both are provided as noted above. The system monitors variable inputs to forecast the intervals and alert the driver when one or more specific maintenance tasks should be performed.

NOTE: For certain vehicles, the status of the front and rear brake pads will only be observable in the maintenance system’s display when there are approximately 2,000 miles or less remaining before a brake service will be required to be performed.

For information about the vehicle’s maintenance system displays, please refer to the Maintenance Service Display Overview section beginning on page 5.

The following “combine with Engine oil”\* maintenance service tasks may be identified as needing to be performed with a specific occurrence of the “Engine oil” service task (service counter number):

$\\triangleright$ Cabin Microfilter(s)

$\\triangleright$ Engine air filter(s)\*

$\\triangleright$ Spark plugs\*

$\\triangleright$ Final drive oil (Applicable M vehicles only)

\\* Does not apply to BEV

Although these items do not appear in the BMW Maintenance System’s display in the vehicle, these services should be performed when your vehicle’s engine oil is changed in accordance with the interval identified by your vehicle’s BMW Maintenance System.

For more information on your vehicle’s maintenance services requirements, procedures and intervals, please refer the Maintenance Service Summary section beginning on page 10.

The BMW Maintenance System also includes an option to set service reminders for the following state-specific mandatory vehicle inspections, including:

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle safety inspection; and/or $\\triangleright$ Emissions test

The corresponding interval data for these inspections can be inputted into the BMW Maintenance System by a service provider; they are not determined by the vehicle.

For your convenience, you may also wish to have your authorized BMW center perform the work necessary to fulfill these state inspection requirements in your area concurrent with the maintenance services specified above when possible.

Should you request more frequent maintenance service than is indicated by the BMW Maintenance System during the coverage period, the cost of these services will not be covered by the BMW Maintenance Program.

# SERVICE DATA — REMOTE CONTROL KEY

Maintenance service task status information for your BMW vehicle is continually updated and stored in your remote control key.

Your authorized BMW center can access this data and consult with you about applicable service procedures and tasks for your vehicle.

Therefore, always provide your service consultant with the most recent remote control key that was used to operate the vehicle when servicing your vehicle at a BMW center.

# VEHICLE STORAGE

Disconnecting the battery during periods of long-term vehicle storage will interrupt the calculation of time-dependent maintenance services.

In this situation, BMW recommends that you have all your time-based maintenance services, such as brake fluid, engine oil and cabin microfilter, brought up to the correct date by an authorized BMW center.

# ENGINE OIL

2025 model year vehicles with internal-combustion engines are factory-filled with:

Z BMW-approved fully synthetic oil for gasoline engines

Engine oil should be changed when the vehicle’s engine is at operating temperature.

If an engine oil service is being performed or you need to add engine oil between changes, please refer to the Owner’s Manual for the recommended engine oil for your BMW vehicle.

# LONG-TERM RATED FLUIDS AND OILS

The following systems and assemblies are factory-filled with long-term rated fluid and oil; fluid replacement is only necessary when repairs are being performed (unless otherwise noted):

$\\triangleright$ Engine cooling system (antifreeze/coolant) $\\triangleright$ Automatic (except for X1 and X2) and manual transmissions $\\triangleright$ All-wheel drive transfer cases (except when indicated by the vehicle)

# REGULAR CHECKS — VEHICLE OPERATOR

In addition to the maintenance service procedure information contained in this booklet, BMW recommends that you regularly check (when refueling, for example), and address when necessary, the following items:

$\\triangleright$ Washer fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Coolant level

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Tires — pressure, condition and wear

Please refer to the Owner’s Manual for additional information.

Your [BMW 3 Series](https://www.bmwtigard.com/new-vehicles/3-series/) is a finely-crafted piece of machinery, but it will still require routine service from time to time. Keeping up with the BMW 3 Series [maintenance schedule](https://www.bmwtigard.com/service/service-and-parts-tips/bmw-recommended-maintenance-schedule/) is a must if you want your vehicle to perform at its best for as long as possible. ## BMW 3 Series Service Schedule

The BMW 3 Series service schedule includes BMW 3 Series oil change intervals and more to help you track the maintenance your vehicle requires. Let’s break it down more in-depth below.

### Bi-Annual Services

The services listed below should be performed approximately 6 months after you take your new vehicle home, at the 5,000 to 10,000-mile mark. They should then be performed at least twice a year for the duration you own the vehicle.

- Oil and Filter Change
- Tire Rotation
- Brake Inspection

### Every 30,000 Miles

At the 30,000-mile mark in the BMW 3 Series maintenance schedule, you’ll want to head back to the shop for a variety of inspections and maintenance care checks.

- Air filter changes: Air filters get clogged over time, so at this point, they are no longer working at their best. If you travel in particularly dusty environments, you’ll want to change the filter approximately every 15,000 miles.
- Fuel filter inspection: Your technician can perform a pressure test to determine if the fuel filter needs replacement.

### Every 60,000 Miles

Your 60,000-mile maintenance service will happen at around four or five years into ownership for the average driver. Here is what it will include:

- Brake Rotor, Pads, and Shoes Inspections and Replacements
- Brake Fluid Replacement
- Coolant Replacement
- Transmission Fluid Replacement

Keep in mind that this is also around the time your battery will start wearing down, so it is a good idea to have it looked at and possibly replaced.

### Every 90,000 Miles

At this service interval, we will take care of inspecting hoses, belts, and spark plugs. Power steering fluid should also be replaced when we perform these tasks:

- Timing belt replacement
- Replace hoses
- Replace spark plugs
- Rotate rotors or replace rotors
- Fuel system cleaning
- Complete inspection

# BMW 3 Series Maintenance Schedule

![](https://dealerimages.dealereprocess.com/image/upload/3734739)

## Maintenance Schedule

Keeping up with your vehicle’s routine maintenance schedule is crucial to the health and longevity of your car. Routine maintenance services are done about once or twice a year, and are usually just a quick stop by the shop to change your oil and make sure everything is working properly.

**Here at BMW of Westchester we know how important it is to stay on top of these services in order to keep your car on the streets of Westchester County and Yonkers, NY, for years to come. Check out our breakdown of the BMW 3 Series maintenance schedule below!  [Schedule a service appointment](https://www.westchesterbmw.com/service-appointment/) for more assistance.**

## Annual Routine Maintenance Services

Your first[BMW 3 Series](https://www.westchesterbmw.com/search/new-bmw-3-series-white-plains-ny/?cy=10607&md=33&tp=new) routine maintenance service will happen about 6 months in, or once you hit around 5,000-10,000 miles, whichever happens to come first. This first service will be relatively quick. It will include:

- **An oil and filter change**

- **Tire rotation**

- **Brake inspection**


You’ll want to get these services done once or twice a year for the duration of the vehicle’s life.

Staying on top of your regular oil and oil filter changes is crucial to your car’s health because as your engine runs, tiny bits of dirt and dust will build up in it, which can cause excessive wear and tear.

**Additionally, yearly [tire rotations](https://www.westchesterbmw.com/service-appointment/) are important to maintain traction control, because they prevent your wheels from having uneven tread. Tread and traction control helps your vehicle stop quicker, and provides you with safer travels over rough terrain.**

![](https://dealerimages.dealereprocess.com/image/upload/3734763)

![](https://dealerimages.dealereprocess.com/image/upload/3734769)

## 30,000-Mile Maintenance Services

Once your BMW 3 Series hits 30,000 miles, it’s time to head back to the shop for a variety of inspections and maintenance care checks. To start, you’re going to need:

- **Your air filter changed, over time your air filter can become clogged, and a replacement will be needed in order for it to work at its best. If you travel in particularly dusty environments, you’ll want this changed around 15,000 miles rather than 30,000.**

- **Next, you’ll need your fuel filter inspected; your technician can perform a pressure test to determine if you’ll need it replaced.**


## 60,000-Mile Maintenance Services

Your 60,000-mile maintenance service will happen at around four or five years into ownership for the average driver. At this service, you’ll need:

- **Brake Rotor, Pads, and Shoes Inspections and Replacements**

- **Brake Fluid Replacement**

- **Coolant Replacement**

- **Transmission Fluid Replacement**

- **Your BMW 3 Series battery and brakes will start to wear out around the 60,000-mile mark, which is why it’s so important to get them inspected, and possibly replaced.**


![](https://dealerimages.dealereprocess.com/image/upload/3734756)

![](https://dealerimages.dealereprocess.com/image/upload/3734759)

## 90,000-Mile Maintenance Services

Your 90,000-mile maintenance check will include an inspection of your hoses, belts, and spark plugs. If they’re not up to par, they’ll need to be replaced. Additionally, you’ll also need to replace your power steering fluid to keep your steering wheel working properly. You should also get the following done:

- **Timing belt replacement**

- **Replace hoses**

- **Replace spark plugs**

- **Rotate rotors or replace rotors**

- **Fuel system cleaning**

- **Complete inspection**

# What is the Recommended BMW Maintenance Schedule?

![Mechanic fixing BMW](https://dealerinspire-image-library-prod.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/images/qOCqBJVRI2dmLPMZp2H4nX2vvpahYMjkkgG6QC7e.jpg)

* * *

At BMW of Tigard, we often get questions from customers about their BMW maintenance schedule. And when you buy a [quality new BMW](https://www.bmwtigard.com/new-vehicles/), it’s important to stick to its BMW service schedule. That’s why we’ve provided the recommended maintenance schedule for general BMW vehicles for Portland and Tigard drivers. With this handy guide, it’ll be easy to stay on track and have your vehicle serviced. We’ll ensure that your vehicle will always be running at its best! As always, before you schedule maintenance on your vehicle, be sure to read your owner’s manual for any specific maintenance information that applies to your BMW vehicle. That way, you’ll better understand your specific model and trim’s future maintenance and repair needs.

[BMW X3 SERVICE SCHEDULE](https://www.bmwtigard.com/service/service-and-parts-tips/bmw-x3-service-schedule/) [Service & Parts Specials](https://www.bmwtigard.com/service-parts-specials/)

* * *

## BMW Preventative Maintenance: Every 5,000 Miles / 6 Months

It’s important to bring in your BMW two or three times a year (or every 5,000 miles) for these preventative maintenance services:

- Front and rear brake inspection
- Brake fluid check
- Coolant check
- Engine oil check
- Cabin air filter inspection
- Engine inspection
- Vehicle inspection
- Wiper blade inspection
- Any necessary tire rotations

Your BMW also comes with something called the Condition-Based Service Monitor (CBS). Your CBS tracks the condition of important systems in your BMW, letting you know if service is required. Our technicians will also use your CBS to determine what needs to be replaced, repaired, or serviced when you schedule service. Keep in mind that just because your CBS may say that service may not be necessary at 5,000 miles doesn’t mean that you shouldn’t come in for preventative maintenance and checks. Sometimes human eyes are necessary to determine a problem or to nip any potential issues in the bud.

## Recommended BMW Maintenance Schedule

Your BMW service schedule needs will vary based on how often you drive, where you drive, and your driving conditions. Your owner’s manual can give you detailed information on common service tasks for your specific model and trim, but here’s what BMW owners can generally expect:

- **Every 10,000 miles** (or yearly): replace your vehicle’s engine oil, oil filter, and coolant.
- **Every 20,000 miles** (or every two years): inspect and replace your vehicle’s fuel filters.
- **Every 30,000 miles** (or every three years): replace your vehicle’s brake fluid (after the first replacement, **every 60,000 miles**) and replace your vehicle’s transmission fluid on manual-transmission BMWs.
- **Every 60,000 miles** (or every six years): replace your vehicle’s engine air filter and spark plugs, inspect and replace any brake pads and brake rotors, and replace transmission fluid on automatic-transmission BMWs.
- **Every 90,000 miles** (or every nine years): replace your vehicle’s timing belts and hoses.

You’ll want to repeat the cycle above after 90,000 miles and always follow the 5,000-mile maintenance schedule. Your BMW’s New Vehicle Limited Warranty will also expire at 50,000 miles, so we recommend getting in any repairs or service before this warranty expires! We also recommend replacing your BMW battery around 50,000 miles.

## What is BMW Value Service?

BMW of Tigard understands that your BMW service isn’t a one-size-fits-all situation. That’s why we offer BMW’s [BMW Value Service](https://www.bmwtigard.com/value-service/) as an option for Lake Oswego drivers and beyond. No matter the miles on your BMW, you’ll receive the benefit of BMW-trained technicians, genuine BMW OEM parts, and up-front pricing. BMW Value Service applies to select services and models, so it’s important to [contact us today](https://www.bmwtigard.com/contact-us/) to see if your vehicle qualifies and to better understand the specific services available for your model and trim.

At BMW of Fort Lauderdale, we understand the importance of your BMW in your daily life, and our service team is here to ensure that it remains in top condition for all your adventures around Miami and Hollywood. If you’re wondering about the maintenance schedule for your [BMW 5 Series](https://www.bmwoffortlauderdale.com/new-vehicles/5-series/), our team has got you covered. We’ll provide you with all the information you need about the BMW 5 Series service schedule and to [schedule your next service appointment](https://consumer.xtime.com/scheduling/?webKey=bmw201507090323&skipRedirect=true&VARIANT=BMWUSA&WMODE=true). ## BMW Ultimate Care

First things first, we dive into the BMW Ultimate Care plan, which is a 3-year or 36,000-mile complimentary BMW maintenance plan for eligible BMW 5 Series models. This care plan includes the following maintenance items:

- **Engine oil**
- **Oil filters**
- **Brake fluid**
- **Spark plug changes**

Additionally, with BMW Teleservices, you have the ability to contact our team at BMW of Fort Lauderdale when you are in need of service. You also get Unlimited Mileage Roadside Assistance for four years and 4-year/50,000-mile coverage under the new vehicle warranty. After getting familiar with the BMW Ultimate Care offerings, we’re going to cover the BMW 5 Series service schedule and when you can expect service.

## BMW 5 Series Service Schedule: 10,000 Miles

The BMW 5 Series uses a sensor-based maintenance guideline based on its Condition Based Service (CBS) system. Every 10,000 miles, the intuitive technology prompts an [oil change](https://www.bmwoffortlauderdale.com/service-and-parts-tips/bmw-oil-change-cost/) and tire rotation. Depending on driving conditions and frequency, other standard services may be detected. You can consult your BMW owner’s manual for more information on initial maintenance and decoding service lights. The intelligent CBS system will notify you of any upcoming service needs, but you can always contact our service department for assistance.

## BMW 5 Series Service Schedule: 30,000 Miles

At around 30,000 miles, it’s recommended to replace the brake fluid in your BMW 5 Series. It’s also a good idea to consider having the fuel filter changed, which typically occurs between 20,000 to 40,000 miles. Tasks performed at the first service interval may also be repeated:

- **Oil change**
- **Fluid level check**
- **Tire rotation**

## BMW 5 Series Service Schedule: 60,000 Miles

At 60,000 miles, it will be time for your BMW 5 Series to have its engine air filter and spark plugs replaced. In addition to the 60,000-mile service, the first two service intervals previously mentioned will also apply at this service appointment for your Coconut Creek vehicle.

## Follow Your BMW 5 Series Service Schedule with BMW of Fort Lauderdale!

[Maintaining your BMW 5 Series](https://www.bmwoffortlauderdale.com/service-and-parts-tips) is essential to keep it running smoothly and safely for years to come. Regular maintenance not only ensures a smooth ride but also gives you the peace of mind that your BMW is in top-notch condition. Neglecting maintenance can lead to future problems and compromise your safety. It is always advisable to schedule service at recommended intervals or whenever issues arise to avoid any potential risks.

## What Does the BMW Maintenance Schedule Include?

BMW maintenance is broken down into intervals, based on time or mileage. Below are general service milestones for most BMW models:

### BMW 10,000-Mile Maintenance

- At 10,000 miles or 12 months, schedule an oil change, brake inspection, and tire rotation.

### BMW 20,000-Mile Maintenance

- At 20,000 miles, replace the cabin air filter and perform a more comprehensive inspection.

### BMW 30,000-Mile Maintenance

- At 30,000-40,000 miles, inspect suspension, steering components, coolant, and belts.
- If manual transmission: replace [transmission fluid](https://www.bmwofturnersville.com/service/service-tips/check-your-transmission-fluid/) every 30,000 miles

### BMW 60,000-Mile Maintenance

- At 60,000 miles, flush and replace brake fluid, inspect spark plugs, and change the engine air filter.

### Additional BMW Maintenance

Every two years, replace the cabin microfilter and test battery performance.

Additional services like coolant flushes, differential fluid replacement, or transmission service may vary depending on your BMW model and driving habits.

We recommend checking your BMW iDrive system or owner’s manual, or speaking with a certified technician at our Turnersville location, for a custom plan.

Avoid unexpected issues by staying proactive, especially in varying New Jersey weather conditions.

# BMW SERVICE

BMW recommends you have your maintenance and repair work performed by an authorized BMW center.

# MAINTAINING YOUR BMW VEHICLE

A well-maintained vehicle will help safeguard its operational performance, road-safety and its reliability. This is why it is important to follow and perform BMW’s recommended periodic vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks as indicated by your vehicle’s Maintenance Service Display, along with the other maintenance work described in this booklet.

A improper maintenance is not covered under the BMW New Vehicle Damage, including consequential damage, which results from lack of or Limited Warranty for Passenger Cars and Light Trucks.

# MAINTENANCE INTERVALS

Maintenance intervals on motor vehicles were conventionally based solely on a fixed time period or a specified amount of accumulated driving mileage.

However, operational and driving conditions have a major influence on your vehicle’s routine maintenance requirements; the distance traveled is only one of these significant factors. A vehicle used for short trips in the city with numerous cold starts, prolonged periods of idling, stop-and-go driving, and high engine speeds during acceleration may require more frequent maintenance intervals than a vehicle that is driven long distances at moderate engine speeds.

Your BMW vehicle uses sensors and algorithms together with the elapsed time and the driving distance/profile to monitor and evaluate your vehicle’s maintenance service needs. This information is then used to adapt dynamically the parameters used to forecast the applicable maintenance service task intervals.

# THE BMW MAINTENANCE SYSTEM

All BMW vehicles are equipped with an integrated BMW Maintenance System. This maintenance “reminder” system helps ensure that the vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks are performed at the forecasted intervals that apply to your vehicle.

The BMW Maintenance System display provides the vehicle operator access to the current status information for the following maintenance service tasks:

$\\triangleright$ Engine oil (date and miles)\*

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle check (date and miles)

$\\triangleright$ Front brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Rear brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid (date)

$\\triangleright$ 1200 Mile running-in service (date and miles) (Applicable to BMW M vehicles only)\*

For each specific maintenance service task, either the future date (month/ year), remaining miles or both are provided as noted above. The system monitors variable inputs to forecast the intervals and alert the driver when one or more specific maintenance tasks should be performed.

NOTE: For certain vehicles, the status of the front and rear brake pads will only be observable in the maintenance system’s display when there are approximately 2,000 miles or less remaining before a brake service will be required to be performed.

For information about the vehicle’s maintenance system displays, please refer to the Maintenance Service Display Overview section beginning on page 5.

The following “combine with Engine oil”\* maintenance service tasks may be identified as needing to be performed with a specific occurrence of the “Engine oil” service task (service counter number):

$\\triangleright$ Cabin Microfilter(s)

$\\triangleright$ Engine air filter(s)\*

$\\triangleright$ Spark plugs\*

$\\triangleright$ Final drive oil (Applicable M vehicles only)

\\* Does not apply to BEV

Although these items do not appear in the BMW Maintenance System’s display in the vehicle, these services should be performed when your vehicle’s engine oil is changed in accordance with the interval identified by your vehicle’s BMW Maintenance System.

For more information on your vehicle’s maintenance services requirements, procedures and intervals, please refer the Maintenance Service Summary section beginning on page 10.

The BMW Maintenance System also includes an option to set service reminders for the following state-specific mandatory vehicle inspections, including:

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle safety inspection; and/or $\\triangleright$ Emissions test

The corresponding interval data for these inspections can be inputted into the BMW Maintenance System by a service provider; they are not determined by the vehicle.

For your convenience, you may also wish to have your authorized BMW center perform the work necessary to fulfill these state inspection requirements in your area concurrent with the maintenance services specified above when possible.

Should you request more frequent maintenance service than is indicated by the BMW Maintenance System during the coverage period, the cost of these services will not be covered by the BMW Maintenance Program.

# SERVICE DATA — REMOTE CONTROL KEY

Maintenance service task status information for your BMW vehicle is continually updated and stored in your remote control key.

Your authorized BMW center can access this data and consult with you about applicable service procedures and tasks for your vehicle.

Therefore, always provide your service consultant with the most recent remote control key that was used to operate the vehicle when servicing your vehicle at a BMW center.

# VEHICLE STORAGE

Disconnecting the battery during periods of long-term vehicle storage will interrupt the calculation of time-dependent maintenance services.

In this situation, BMW recommends that you have all your time-based maintenance services, such as brake fluid, engine oil and cabin microfilter, brought up to the correct date by an authorized BMW center.

# ENGINE OIL

2025 model year vehicles with internal-combustion engines are factory-filled with:

Z BMW-approved fully synthetic oil for gasoline engines

Engine oil should be changed when the vehicle’s engine is at operating temperature.

If an engine oil service is being performed or you need to add engine oil between changes, please refer to the Owner’s Manual for the recommended engine oil for your BMW vehicle.

# LONG-TERM RATED FLUIDS AND OILS

The following systems and assemblies are factory-filled with long-term rated fluid and oil; fluid replacement is only necessary when repairs are being performed (unless otherwise noted):

$\\triangleright$ Engine cooling system (antifreeze/coolant) $\\triangleright$ Automatic (except for X1 and X2) and manual transmissions $\\triangleright$ All-wheel drive transfer cases (except when indicated by the vehicle)

# REGULAR CHECKS — VEHICLE OPERATOR

In addition to the maintenance service procedure information contained in this booklet, BMW recommends that you regularly check (when refueling, for example), and address when necessary, the following items:

$\\triangleright$ Washer fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Coolant level

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Tires — pressure, condition and wear

Please refer to the Owner’s Manual for additional information.

## Keep Your BMW 2 Series Performing at it's Best

**Basic BMW 2-Series Preventative Maintenance: Every 5,000 Miles**

BMW’s maintenance schedule is built around a standard 5,000-mile interval, guided by your vehicle’s pre-installed Condition-Based Service (CBS) monitor. This intelligent system tracks critical areas of your car and alerts you when additional services are needed.

The regular BMW recommended maintenance schedule includes the following:

- Vehicle check and inspection
- Engine oil check
- Coolant check
- Tire rotation
- Brake fluid check
- Front and rear brake inspection
- Inspection of the engine and cabin air filters
- Wiper blade inspection
- Standard scope

Not every part inspected will need replacement during your visit. Our BMW-certified maintenance experts use the CBS monitor to identify exactly what requires attention, ensuring precise and efficient service.

**BMW 2-Series Recommended Maintenance Services**

Maintenance needs can vary depending on your model and driving habits. For tailored recommendations, consult your owner’s manual or speak with one of our knowledgeable service advisors. Below is a general guideline for BMW 2 Series maintenance milestones:

**BMW 2-Series 10,000-Mile Maintenance**

- Replace the engine oil, oil filter and coolant
- Repeat every 10,000 miles

**BMW 2-Series 20,000-Mile Maintenance**

- Inspect and replace the oil filters
- Repeat every 20,000 miles

**BMW 2-Series 30,000-Mile Maintenance**

- Replace brake fluid. After the first service, schedule brake fluid replacement every 60,000 miles.
- If equipped with a manual transmission, replace transmission fluid every 30,000 miles.

**BMW 2-Series 60,000-mile maintenance**

- Replace the engine air filter and spark plugs
- Inspect and replace brake pads and rotors as needed
- For automatic transmissions, replace the transmission fluid every 60,000 miles.

**BMW 2-Series 90,000-Mile Maintenance**

- Replace the timing belt and hoses
- Repeat every 90,000 miles

**BMW 2-Series Maintenance after 90,000 Miles**

Continue following the BMW 2 Series maintenance schedule with 5,000-mile intervals and adhere to service milestones as listed above to ensure optimal performance.

# Volkswagen Jetta Recommended Maintenance Schedule

![2023 Volkswagen Jetta](https://dealerinspire-image-library-prod.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/images/Ul0f8P7h06keJCujiQSKVvyMiTtkjRbSVGr1DQQy.jpg)

* * *

The Volkswagen Jetta is one of the stalwarts of the brand. It gives you excellent fuel economy yet a powerful engine. Maintaining your [new vehicle](https://www.carolinavw.com/new-vehicles/) in its best shape for every Monroe drive means bringing your car in for Volkswagen Jetta service at least once a year. We recommend following the VW Jetta maintenance schedule for the best results.

Discover everything about the VW Jetta service intervals with our comprehensive guide!

[Schedule Volkswagen Jetta Service](https://www.carolinavw.com/online-service-scheduler/) [Service Department](https://www.carolinavw.com/service/)

## What Is the Volkswagen Jetta Maintenance Schedule?

Your [new VW Jetta](https://www.carolinavw.com/new-vehicles/jetta/) service intervals occur every 10,000 miles. Older Volkswagen models might have different maintenance requirements. Check your owner’s manual for the correct VW Jetta maintenance schedule. However, world-class engineering for newer vehicles means longer VW Jetta service intervals, lowering overall ownership costs.

Every 10,000 miles is also the VW Jetta oil change interval, so expect a full synthetic oil change every 10,000 miles of driving. The exception is if you frequently drive in less-than-ideal conditions in Concord. If you repeatedly hit the brakes hard, you might need new tires or new brakes sooner than expected.

Below is the VW Jetta maintenance schedule you should follow.

### **VW Jetta Maintenance Schedule: 10,000 Miles or One Year**

Your first Volkswagen Jetta service in Charlotte will consist of the following:

- Oil and filter change
- Brake pad inspection
- Brake disc inspection
- Service interval reset

### **VW Jetta Maintenance Schedule: 20,000 Miles or Two Years**

For this VW Jetta service interval, we will do everything from the first service at 10,000 miles, plus some extras:

- Engine compartment and transmission inspection
- Battery inspection
- Fluid level adjustments (brake fluid and coolant)
- Tire pressure and TPMS inspection
- Tire tread depth inspection
- Tire repair kit inspection
- Exterior lighting systems inspection
- Windshield wiper and washer system inspection
- Check for sunroof drain blockage
- Horn test
- Road test

### **VW Jetta Maintenance Schedule: 30,000 Miles or Three Years**

This is what our team will do for your three-year Volkswagen Jetta service near Indian Trail to keep your sedan in top shape:

- Oil and filter change
- Brake pad inspection
- Brake disc inspection
- Service interval reset

### **VW Jetta Maintenance Schedule: 40,000 Miles or Four Years**

At 40,000 miles, we’ll take care of the VW Jetta oil change interval, just like the other one-year maintenance. We’ll also check everything from the 20,000-mile VW Jetta service interval. Our team will also look over these things for your Jetta for four years:

**Replacements:**

- Dust and pollen filter
- Spark plugs

**Inspections:**

- Suspension components
- Corrosion inside and out
- Brake system
- Underbody
- Windshield
- Exhaust system
- Interior lighting
- Ribbed V-belt
- Sunroof

### **VW Jetta Maintenance Schedule: 50,000 Miles or Five Years**

At the 50,000-mile mark, this service interval includes everything from the first one:

- VW Jetta Oil Change Interval
- New Oil Filter
- Check Your Brake Pads
- Fluid Levels
- Service Interval Display Reset (if needed)

At this point in your sedan ownership, you might need a new battery, new tires, or new brake parts, depending on the condition of your Volkswagen Jetta. We’ll discuss your options with you if we see anything that needs service at this interval.

## Services at 80,000 to 150,000 Miles

Your Volkswagen maintenance schedule continues with routine maintenance, as we already discussed. Services at 80,000 to 150,000 miles are on the simple side, thankfully. Your VW Jetta warranty is for four years and 50,000 miles. Keep that in mind as you keep your car in fantastic condition.

## Contact Us for Volkswagen Jetta Service in Charlotte!

Remember, this is the ideal and expected Volkswagen Jetta maintenance schedule for driving in ideal conditions. Driving in dusty conditions or driving too fast might require shorter service intervals. Have questions? Feel free to [contact us](https://www.carolinavw.com/contact-us/) or call 980-221-0753. We want you to get the most out of your VW ownership!

## 2023 VW Jetta Coolant

Coolant, as it relates to vehicles, is frequently a liquid or gas substance used to regulate the temperature of your engine. Liquid coolants are usually half water and half ethylene glycol. Water is used to transfer heat while ethylene glycol is used to lower the freezing point of the liquid. In colder climates, this is immensely vital. This undoubtedly isn't the first time you've heard of ethylene glycol as it is the central ingredient in the popular term "antifreeze". Keep in mind, you never want to pour antifreeze or water by themselves into your engine system. They need to be mixed to construct the proper coolant.

You can purchase ready-made mixtures of coolant that already have water added, or you can purchase full-strength antifreeze which needs to be diluted with distilled water before being added to the engine system. Give the experts at Nalley Volkswagen of Alpharetta a call at 7706299081 or [schedule service online](https://www.nalleyvw.com/service/schedule-appointment.htm) and let one of our mechanics and service specialists handle your coolant flush.

There are many colors of coolants to help distinguish each including red, green, yellow, purple blue, and orange. ## How long does 2023 VW Jetta coolant last?

How frequently you need to flush and replenish your vehicle's coolant relies on the type of coolant. There are many types of coolants. Up until the mid-1990s there was essentially only a single type of coolant. It was a green formula coolant that contained corrosion inhibitors that only lasted between 24,000 - 36,000 miles or between two to three years. This type of coolant is not suggested for newer vehicles which come equipped with a longer-lasting coolant.

Newer coolants use an Organic Acid Technology (OAT) and last up to twice as long as older coolant. In some cases these long-life coolants can last over 5 years or 100,000 miles.

A coolant flush or cooling system service consists of three main services.

- Adding a cleaner compound to get rid of particles, sediment, corrosion,and rust
- Replenishing the system with the appropriate coolant and cautiously measuring the dilution percentage
- Flushing the whole system thoroughly

## What happens if my 2023 VW Jetta runs out of coolant?

Your 2023 VW Jetta doesn't have to run out of coolant for troubles to start. Dilution levels need to be within a specific percentage range or your 2023 VW Jetta engine components can start to rust, break, or become irreplaceably damaged. If you run out of coolant utterly due to a leak or poor fluid levels, your complete engine system can be compromised from the gaskets to the pistons or even the engine block itself.

## How often should you change coolant in a 2023 VW Jetta?

Normally, you should have your 2023 VW Jetta coolant flush completed every 30,000 miles or every two years. There are certain instances where your vehicle can go without a flush for a longer period of time. It's vital to have this checked every 15,000 miles to make sure you catch any issues before they cause dramatic damage. When it comes to your 2023 VW Jetta engine, it's better safe than sorry.

## How do I know if I need a coolant flush in my 2023 VW Jetta?

Common symptoms that your 2023 VW Jetta needs a coolant flush are:

- Your check engine light may turn on
- Sediment or rust will be visible in the coolant
- Steam will come from the radiator or hood
- Coolant will normally leak out when the engine is running. Check the ground when you park.
- Sometimes, albeit unlikely, you'll be able to smell an odd burning odor coming from under the hood.
- Your temperature gauge will read far above normal with the engine on for a few minutes.
- Unexpected grinding noises can come from the engine
- Your heater may stop working
