  - [Factors Influencing Oil Change Frequency](https://www.modernfordofboone.com/ford-oil-change-guide-boone/#factors-influencing-oil-change-frequency): Discover how driving habits, engine type, and oil type can affect your oil change schedule.
  - [The Importance of Regular Oil Changes](https://www.modernfordofboone.com/ford-oil-change-guide-boone/#the-importance-of-regular-oil-changes): Understand why timely oil changes are critical for engine health and performance.

  - [Maximizing Your Ford’s Longevity with the IOLM](https://www.modernfordofboone.com/ford-oil-change-guide-boone/#maximizing-your-fords-longevity-with-the-iolm): See how the Intelligent Oil-Life Monitor can help optimize your maintenance schedule.

## Ford’s Recommended Oil Change Intervals

Ford recommends changing your vehicle’s oil every 7,500 miles or six months, whichever comes first. This general guideline ensures that your engine remains well-lubricated and free from contaminants. However, depending on your specific model and driving conditions, this interval may vary. For instance, newer Ford models equipped with the **Intelligent Oil-Life Monitor (IOLM)** system can calculate the optimal oil change interval based on real-time data, including mileage, speed, temperature, and driving habits. This advanced system allows you to extend the time between oil changes without compromising engine health.

For older Ford models or those without the IOLM, you might need to adhere to a more traditional schedule of every 3,000 to 5,000 miles, especially if your driving conditions are severe. Severe conditions include frequent short trips, towing heavy loads, or driving in extremely hot or cold weather. Always consult your vehicle’s owner’s manual for specific maintenance recommendations tailored to your model.

If you’re uncertain about the best oil change interval for your Ford, consider visiting the **[Service Department at Modern Ford of Boone](https://api.connectcdk.com/api/nc-cosa-consumer-ui/v1/?subscriptionId=&cid=2000096)**. Our experienced technicians can provide personalized advice based on your vehicle’s needs and your driving habits.

## Factors Influencing Oil Change Frequency

Several factors can influence how often you should change your oil. Understanding these can help you maintain your Ford vehicle more effectively:

- **Driving Habits**: If you frequently drive in stop-and-go traffic, tow heavy loads, or take short trips, your engine may accumulate contaminants faster, necessitating more frequent oil changes.
- **Engine Type**: Different engines have varying requirements. For example, turbocharged engines might require more frequent oil changes due to higher operating temperatures.
- **Oil Type**: Using **synthetic oil** can extend the time between oil changes compared to conventional oil. Synthetic oils are designed to last longer and withstand extreme temperatures better.

For drivers in areas like Lenoir or Morganton, where the terrain might involve more hills and curves, these factors become even more critical. Always ensure that your oil type matches your driving conditions and engine specifications for optimal performance.

## The Importance of Regular Oil Changes

Regular oil changes are vital for maintaining your engine’s health. Oil lubricates engine components, reduces friction, and helps manage heat. Over time, oil degrades and becomes contaminated with particles and debris, which can lead to engine wear and reduced performance. Failing to change your oil regularly can result in:

- **Engine Overheating**: Dirty oil can’t effectively dissipate heat, leading to overheating.
- **Increased Friction**: Without proper lubrication, engine parts can wear down more quickly.
- **Reduced Fuel Efficiency**: A well-lubricated engine runs more efficiently, saving you money at the pump.

In regions like Wilkesboro or Ashe County, where temperatures can vary significantly, maintaining clean oil is crucial for adapting to changing conditions. If you notice signs like a knocking engine or the oil change light illuminating, it’s time to schedule an oil change.

## Mileage vs. Time: What Matters More?

When considering oil change intervals, both mileage and time are important. Oil degrades over time due to oxidation and the breakdown of additives, even if the vehicle isn’t driven frequently. Conversely, higher mileage means more exposure to contaminants. Therefore, you should follow the interval that comes first, whether it’s mileage or time.

For example, if your Ford’s manual recommends an oil change every 5,000 miles or six months, change the oil if you reach either milestone. This approach ensures that your engine remains protected, regardless of driving frequency. For vehicles using synthetic oil, the interval might extend up to 15,000 miles, but always verify with your owner’s manual.

Residents in Boone or Blowing Rock, who may use their vehicles less frequently due to work-from-home arrangements or seasonal use, should still adhere to the time-based interval to prevent oil degradation.

## Maximizing Your Ford’s Longevity with the IOLM

The **Intelligent Oil-Life Monitor (IOLM)** is a feature in many newer Ford models that takes the guesswork out of oil changes. By analyzing your driving conditions and habits, the IOLM provides accurate recommendations for when to change your oil. This system helps you avoid unnecessary changes while ensuring your engine is protected.

For example, if you frequently drive in mountainous areas like Boone or Hickory, the IOLM will account for the increased engine strain and adjust the oil change interval accordingly. This tailored approach not only saves you time and money but also enhances your vehicle’s performance and longevity.

If you’re interested in learning more about how the IOLM works or need assistance with your vehicle, contact the **[Service Department at Modern Ford of Boone](https://api.connectcdk.com/api/nc-cosa-consumer-ui/v1/?subscriptionId=&cid=2000096)** for expert guidance.

# BMW SERVICE

# MAINTAINING YOUR BMW VEHICLE

A well-maintained vehicle will help safeguard its operational performance, road-safety and its reliability. This is why it is important to follow and perform BMW’s recommended periodic vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks as indicated by your vehicle’s Maintenance Service Display, along with the other maintenance work described in this booklet.

A improper maintenance is not covered under the BMW New Vehicle Damage, including consequential damage, which results from lack of or Limited Warranty for Passenger Cars and Light Trucks.

# MAINTENANCE INTERVALS

Maintenance intervals on motor vehicles were conventionally based solely on a fixed time period or a specified amount of accumulated driving mileage.

However, operational and driving conditions have a major influence on your vehicle’s routine maintenance requirements; the distance traveled is only one of these significant factors. A vehicle used for short trips in the city with numerous cold starts, prolonged periods of idling, stop-and-go driving, and high engine speeds during acceleration may require more frequent maintenance intervals than a vehicle that is driven long distances at moderate engine speeds.

Your BMW vehicle uses sensors and algorithms together with the elapsed time and the driving distance/profile to monitor and evaluate your vehicle’s maintenance service needs. This information is then used to adapt dynamically the parameters used to forecast the applicable maintenance service task intervals.

# THE BMW MAINTENANCE SYSTEM

All BMW vehicles are equipped with an integrated BMW Maintenance System. This maintenance “reminder” system helps ensure that the vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks are performed at the forecasted intervals that apply to your vehicle.

The BMW Maintenance System display provides the vehicle operator access to the current status information for the following maintenance service tasks:

$\\triangleright$ Engine oil (date and miles)\*

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle check (date and miles)

$\\triangleright$ Front brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Rear brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid (date)

Z 1200 Mile running-in service (date and miles) (Applicable to BMW M vehicles only)\*

For each specific maintenance service task, either the future date (month/ year), remaining miles or both are provided as noted above. The system monitors variable inputs to forecast the intervals and alert the driver when one or more specific maintenance tasks should be performed.

NOTE: For certain vehicles, the status of the front and rear brake pads will only be observable in the maintenance system’s display when there are approximately 2,000 miles or less remaining before a brake service will be required to be performed.

For information about the vehicle’s maintenance system displays, please refer to the Maintenance Service Display Overview section beginning on page 5.

The following “combine with Engine oil”\* maintenance service tasks may be identified as needing to be performed with a specific occurrence of the “Engine oil” service task (service counter number):

$\\triangleright$ Cabin Microfilter(s)

$\\triangleright$ Engine air filter(s)\*

$\\triangleright$ Spark plugs\*

$\\triangleright$ Final drive oil (Applicable M vehicles only)

\\* Does not apply to BEV

Although these items do not appear in the BMW Maintenance System’s display in the vehicle, these services should be performed when your vehicle’s engine oil is changed in accordance with the interval identified by your vehicle’s BMW Maintenance System.

For more information on your vehicle’s maintenance services requirements, procedures and intervals, please refer the Maintenance Service Summary section beginning on page 10.

The BMW Maintenance System also includes an option to set service reminders for the following state-specific mandatory vehicle inspections, including:

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle safety inspection; and/or $\\triangleright$ Emissions test

The corresponding interval data for these inspections can be inputted into the BMW Maintenance System by a service provider; they are not determined by the vehicle.

For your convenience, you may also wish to have your authorized BMW center perform the work necessary to fulfill these state inspection requirements in your area concurrent with the maintenance services specified above when possible.

Should you request more frequent maintenance service than is indicated by the BMW Maintenance System during the coverage period, the cost of these services will not be covered by the BMW Maintenance Program.

# SERVICE DATA — REMOTE CONTROL KEY

Maintenance service task status information for your BMW vehicle is continually updated and stored in your remote control key.

Your authorized BMW center can access this data and consult with you about applicable service procedures and tasks for your vehicle.

Therefore, always provide your service consultant with the most recent remote control key that was used to operate the vehicle when servicing your vehicle at a BMW center.

# VEHICLE STORAGE

Disconnecting the battery during periods of long-term vehicle storage will interrupt the calculation of time-dependent maintenance services.

In this situation, BMW recommends that you have all your time-based maintenance services, such as brake fluid, engine oil and cabin microfilter, brought up to the correct date by an authorized BMW center.

# ENGINE OIL

2026 model year vehicles with internal-combustion engines are factory-filled with:

Z BMW-approved fully synthetic oil for gasoline engines

Engine oil should be changed when the vehicle’s engine is at operating temperature.

If an engine oil service is being performed or you need to add engine oil between changes, please refer to the Owner’s Manual for the recommended engine oil for your BMW vehicle.

# LONG-TERM RATED FLUIDS AND OILS

The following systems and assemblies are factory-filled with long-term rated fluid and oil; fluid replacement is only necessary when repairs are being performed (unless otherwise noted):

$\\triangleright$ Engine cooling system (antifreeze/coolant)

$\\triangleright$ Automatic (except X1, X2, and 2 Series Gran Coupe) and manual transmissions

$\\triangleright$ All-wheel drive transfer cases (except when indicated by the vehicle)

# REGULAR CHECKS — VEHICLE OPERATOR

In addition to the maintenance service procedure information contained in this booklet, BMW recommends that you regularly check (when refueling, for example), and address when necessary, the following items:

$\\triangleright$ Washer fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Coolant level

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Tires — pressure, condition and wear

Please refer to the Owner’s Manual for additional information.

### Preserving the Executive Standard.

Owning a [**2026 BMW 5 Series**](https://www.bmwofmilwaukeenorth.com/new-vehicles/5-series/) in Milwaukee requires a proactive approach to maintenance. The G60 chassis, whether equipped with the B48 4-cylinder (530i) or the B58 6-cylinder (540i/550e), is engineered for high-mileage longevity, provided it receives specific care.

Unlike older vehicles with rigid fixed intervals, your 5 Series utilizes Condition Based Service (CBS). This system uses sensors to monitor oil life, brake pad wear, and fluid quality in real-time, adapting service requirements based on how you drive. However, given our extreme Wisconsin climate, ranging from sub-zero cold starts to humid summers, we recommend adhering to a baseline schedule to ensure peak performance.

### The G60 Service Intervals.

While the CBS system will alert you via the iDrive 8.5 display when service is due, the following timeline serves as the engineering standard for long-term reliability.

#### Every 10,000 Miles (or 12 Months).

This is the “Standard Scope” service. It establishes the baseline for engine health.

- **Synthetic Oil Change:** Replacement of engine oil and filter. The B48 and B58 engines rely on clean oil not just for lubrication, but to actuate the VANOS variable valve timing system.
- **Tire Rotation:** Critical for xDrive models to ensure even tread wear and prevent strain on the transfer case.
- **Safety Inspection:** Verification of fluid levels, wiper blades, and brake pad thickness.

#### Every 30,000 Miles.

At this interval, we address hydraulic and filtration systems that degrade over time.

- **Brake Fluid Flush:** BMW brake fluid is hygroscopic (absorbs moisture). Flushing it prevents internal corrosion of the ABS module and maintains a firm pedal feel.
- **Cabin Microfilter:** Replacement is necessary to maintain airflow and remove allergens/dust from the HVAC system.

#### Every 60,000 Miles.

This is a major service milestone for the G60 chassis.

- **Spark Plugs:** Worn plugs can cause misfires and stress the ignition coils. Replacement restores optimal combustion efficiency.
- **Engine Air Filter:** A clean filter allows the turbocharger to breathe freely, maintaining throttle response.
- **Sunroof Drain Check:** Essential for vehicles parked outside to prevent water ingress during heavy storms.

### Engine-Specific Care: B48 vs. B58.

While both engines share a modular architecture, they have distinct long-term ownership considerations.

| #### B48 (530i) Considerations. | #### B58 (540i & 550e) Considerations. |
| --- | --- |
| ![2026 BMW 530i and 540i trim](https://di-uploads-pod44.dealerinspire.com/bmwofmilwaukeenorth/uploads/2026/02/530i-models-and-540i-xdrive.jpg) | ![2026 BMW 550e xDrive Trim](https://di-uploads-pod44.dealerinspire.com/bmwofmilwaukeenorth/uploads/2026/02/550e-xdrive-model.jpg) |
| The 2.0-liter B48 is a robust “baby B58,” but it operates under higher boost pressure relative to its displacement.<br>- **Coolant Circuit:** Owners should periodically check coolant levels. The system is complex, featuring multiple cooling circuits, and low levels can trigger “drivetrain malfunction” warnings.<br>- **Oil Filter Housing:** Over high mileage (typically 60k+), the plastic composite oil filter housing can become brittle from heat cycles. We inspect this component at every oil change to catch early signs of weeping. | The 3.0-liter B58 is legendary for its “bulletproof” internals, but external gaskets require monitoring.<br>- **Valve Cover Gasket:** As the engine approaches higher mileage (70k+), the valve cover gasket is a known wear item. Keeping fresh oil in the engine helps preserve the pliability of these seals.<br>- **VANOS Solenoids:** These solenoids control valve timing using oil pressure. Regular oil changes are the single best way to prevent sludge buildup that can restrict their operation. |

Every new 2026 BMW 5 Series includes [**BMW Ultimate Care**](https://bmwusaservice.com/ultimatecare), which covers scheduled maintenance for the first 3 years or 36,000 miles.

- **Included:** Engine oil, oil filter, brake fluid, cabin microfilter, engine air filter, and spark plugs.

- **Factory Training:** Our technicians are specifically trained on the G60’s 48-volt mild-hybrid systems, ensuring safe and correct handling of electrified components.

# MAINTENANCE INTERVALS

Maintenance intervals on motor vehicles were conventionally based solely on a fixed time period or a specified amount of accumulated driving mileage.

However, operational and driving conditions have a major influence on your vehicle’s routine maintenance requirements; the distance traveled is only one of these significant factors. A vehicle used for short trips in the city with numerous cold starts, prolonged periods of idling, stop-and-go driving, and high engine speeds during acceleration may require more frequent maintenance intervals than a vehicle that is driven long distances at moderate engine speeds.

Your BMW vehicle uses sensors and algorithms together with the elapsed time and the driving distance/profile to monitor and evaluate your vehicle’s maintenance service needs. This information is then used to adapt dynamically the parameters used to forecast the applicable maintenance service task intervals.

# THE BMW MAINTENANCE SYSTEM

All BMW vehicles are equipped with an integrated BMW Maintenance System. This maintenance “reminder” system helps ensure that the vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks are performed at the forecasted intervals that apply to your vehicle.

The BMW Maintenance System display provides the vehicle operator access to the current status information for the following maintenance service tasks:

$\\triangleright$ Engine oil (date and miles)\*

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle check (date and miles)

$\\triangleright$ Front brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Rear brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid (date)

Z 1200 Mile running-in service (date and miles) (Applicable to BMW M vehicles only)\*

For each specific maintenance service task, either the future date (month/ year), remaining miles or both are provided as noted above. The system monitors variable inputs to forecast the intervals and alert the driver when one or more specific maintenance tasks should be performed.

NOTE: For certain vehicles, the status of the front and rear brake pads will only be observable in the maintenance system’s display when there are approximately 2,000 miles or less remaining before a brake service will be required to be performed.

For information about the vehicle’s maintenance system displays, please refer to the Maintenance Service Display Overview section beginning on page 5.

The following “combine with Engine oil”\* maintenance service tasks may be identified as needing to be performed with a specific occurrence of the “Engine oil” service task (service counter number):

$\\triangleright$ Cabin Microfilter(s)

$\\triangleright$ Engine air filter(s)\*

$\\triangleright$ Spark plugs\*

$\\triangleright$ Final drive oil (Applicable M vehicles only)

\\* Does not apply to BEV

Although these items do not appear in the BMW Maintenance System’s display in the vehicle, these services should be performed when your vehicle’s engine oil is changed in accordance with the interval identified by your vehicle’s BMW Maintenance System.

For more information on your vehicle’s maintenance services requirements, procedures and intervals, please refer the Maintenance Service Summary section beginning on page 10.

The BMW Maintenance System also includes an option to set service reminders for the following state-specific mandatory vehicle inspections, including:

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle safety inspection; and/or $\\triangleright$ Emissions test

The corresponding interval data for these inspections can be inputted into the BMW Maintenance System by a service provider; they are not determined by the vehicle.

For your convenience, you may also wish to have your authorized BMW center perform the work necessary to fulfill these state inspection requirements in your area concurrent with the maintenance services specified above when possible.

Should you request more frequent maintenance service than is indicated by the BMW Maintenance System during the coverage period, the cost of these services will not be covered by the BMW Maintenance Program.

# SERVICE DATA — REMOTE CONTROL KEY

Maintenance service task status information for your BMW vehicle is continually updated and stored in your remote control key.

Your authorized BMW center can access this data and consult with you about applicable service procedures and tasks for your vehicle.

Therefore, always provide your service consultant with the most recent remote control key that was used to operate the vehicle when servicing your vehicle at a BMW center.

# VEHICLE STORAGE

Disconnecting the battery during periods of long-term vehicle storage will interrupt the calculation of time-dependent maintenance services.

In this situation, BMW recommends that you have all your time-based maintenance services, such as brake fluid, engine oil and cabin microfilter, brought up to the correct date by an authorized BMW center.

# ENGINE OIL

2026 model year vehicles with internal-combustion engines are factory-filled with:

Z BMW-approved fully synthetic oil for gasoline engines

Engine oil should be changed when the vehicle’s engine is at operating temperature.

If an engine oil service is being performed or you need to add engine oil between changes, please refer to the Owner’s Manual for the recommended engine oil for your BMW vehicle.

# LONG-TERM RATED FLUIDS AND OILS

The following systems and assemblies are factory-filled with long-term rated fluid and oil; fluid replacement is only necessary when repairs are being performed (unless otherwise noted):

$\\triangleright$ Engine cooling system (antifreeze/coolant)

$\\triangleright$ Automatic (except X1, X2, and 2 Series Gran Coupe) and manual transmissions

$\\triangleright$ All-wheel drive transfer cases (except when indicated by the vehicle)

# REGULAR CHECKS — VEHICLE OPERATOR

In addition to the maintenance service procedure information contained in this booklet, BMW recommends that you regularly check (when refueling, for example), and address when necessary, the following items:

$\\triangleright$ Washer fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Coolant level

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Tires — pressure, condition and wear

Please refer to the Owner’s Manual for additional information.

## VW Atlas Service Schedule

## 10,000 Miles or One Year

The base of your VW Atlas service schedule will consist of the following maintenance tasks:

- Inspect the Brake Pads
- VW Atlas Oil Change
- New Oil Filter
- Service Interval Display Rest (if needed)

## 20,000 Miles or Two Years

Two-year maintenance should also include a VW Atlas oil change and oil filter replacement. The following must also be checked so you can stay safe on Vienna roads:

- Horn
- Tire Repair Kit
- Engine and Engine Compartment Components
- Brake Fluid
- Tire Pressure
- Service Interval Display
- Exterior Lighting
- Battery
- Tires
- Windshield Wiper/Washer System
- Automatic headlight control
- Headlight Washing System
- Wiper Blades
- Coolant Level and Frost Protection
- Brake Pads
- Transmission
- Second Battery
- Tire Pressure Monitoring System

## 30,000 Miles or Three Years

The following VW Atlas routine maintenance tasks will be required every three years or 30,000 miles:

- Oil Change
- New Oil Filter
- Inspect Brake Pads
- Service Interval Display Rest (if needed)

## 40,000 Miles or Four Years

At 40,000 miles, you’ll get a VW Atlas oil change and a new oil filter, plus everything from the 20,000 service interval. These things will also be checked as part of your VW Atlas maintenance schedule:

- Tie Rod Ends
- Stabilizer Bushings
- New Dust and Pollen Filter
- Front and Rear Coil Springs and Shock Absorbers
- Sunroof and Panoramic Sunroof
- Ball Joints
- Wheel Bearings
- Axles
- Coupling Rods

## 50,000 Miles or Five Years

The 50,000 VW Atlas service interval includes:

- Engine Oil Change
- New Oil Filter
- Check Your Brake Pads
- Service Interval Display Rest (if needed)

## 60,000 Miles or 6 Years

Your safety is paramount as you drive around Fairfax, so along with new engine oil, oil filter, air filter, and snow filter, these components will be inspected:

- Fuel filter Replacement
- Dust and Pollen Filter Replacement
- Battery inspection
- Check the Tires
- Brake System Inspection
- Check the Tire fFller Bottle Expiration Date

## 70,000 Miles or 7 Years

The 70,000-mile mark of the VW Atlas maintenance schedule includes the following tasks:

- Engine Oil Filter Change
- Motor Oil Change
- Brake Pad Check
- Service Interval Display Rest (if needed)

## 80,000 Miles or 8 Years

All the same components from the 20,000-mile inspection are inspected, as well as:

- Ball Joints
- Transmission
- Wheel Bearings
- Axles
- Interior Lighting
- Ribbed V-belt
- Front and Rear Coil Springs
- Shock Absorbers
- Sunroof and Panoramic Sunroof
- Underbody

## 90,000 Miles or 9 Years

- Brake Discs
- Clutch Unit
- Engine Oil Change
- Engine Oil Filter Change
- Brake Pad Inspection
- Service Interval Display Rest (if needed)

## 100,000 Miles or 10 Years

At 100,000 miles, you’ll get a VW Atlas oil change and new oil filter, and the same things as the 20,000-mile inspection will be inspected.

## 110,000 Miles or 11 Years

- Brake Pad Check
- Engine Oil Change
- New Oil Filter
- Service Interval Display Rest (if needed)

## 120,000 Miles or 12 Years

Our certified VW Technicians will replace your engine oil, oil filter, and snow and air filter and check all the same components from the 20,000-mile inspection, plus:

- Underbody
- Wheel Bearings
- Axles
- Tie Rod Ends,
- Stabilizer Bushings
- Front and Rear Coil Springs
- Shock Absorbers
- Ball Joints
- Interior Lighting
- Coupling Rods
- Ribbed V-Belt
- Sunroof and Panoramic Sunroof

# Minor Maintenance

 Brake pads (front and rear): Check thickness and brake disc condition. Look for contact pattern and corrosion of brake discs

 Engine: Change oil and replace filter

# Standard Maintenance (Includes All Minor Maintenance Items)

 Battery: Check with battery tester (and auxiliary battery if equipped)

 Brake fluid: Check level depending on brake wear

 Brake pads (front and rear): Check thickness and brake disc condition. Look for contact pattern and corrosion of brake discs

 Cooling system: Check level and freeze protection

Engine: Change oil and replace filter

 Engine and engine compartment components (from above): Check for leaks and damage

 Engine and engine compartment components (from below): Check related components including transmission, final drive, and drive axle boots for leaks and damage

 Exterior Lighting: Check function of front and rear lights, headlights (adjust if necessary), automatic headlights (if equipped), turn signals, cornering lights, and hazard warning lights

 Headlight washing system: Check function (if equipped)

 Horn: Check function

 Removable trailer hitch: Check function and inspect for damage (if equipped)

 Ribbed Belt and Tensioning Roller for Belt Starter Generator - Check condition

 Service Interval Display: Reset

 Test drive: Check braking, kickdown, steering, electrical, heating/ventilation systems, air conditioning, handling, and parking brake

 Tire pressure monitoring system: Calibrate to correct tire pressure settings

 Tire pressure: Check LF RF\_ LR RR Spare

# Standard Maintenance (continued)

 Tire repair kit: Check for damage and prior use

 Tires: Check condition and wear pattern. Record tread depth

 Torque Splitter: Check oil deterioration using the Vehicle Diagnostic Tester (if equipped)

 Windshield wiper/washer system: Check for damage, function and adjust spray nozzle if necessary, fluid level, and freeze protection

 Wiper blades: Bring into service position, check for damage, and check park position

# Extended Maintenance

 Perform Standard Maintenance items

 Body interior and exterior: Check for corrosion

 Coil Springs and Rubber Buffer: Inspect for damage

 Exhaust system: Check for leaks, damage, and secure fittings

 Interior lighting: Check function of overhead lights, glove box lights, cigarette lighter/power outlets, luggage compartment, and all warning lights

 Ribbed belt: Check condition

 Sunroof: Check function and clean, then lubricate guide rails with VW approved lubricant (if equipped)

 Suspension and Steering: Check ball joints, wheel bearings, drive axles, coupling rods, tie rod ends, and stabilizer bar rubber bushings for damage and excessive play

 Underbody: Check underbody protection, underbody trim panels, wire routing, and plugs for damage

 Windshield: Check for damage

# Volkswagen Atlas Oil Type & Capacity

![Oil Change](https://dealerinspire-image-library-prod.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/images/dPDQ8g69kRnC3TrrSgdDfloXOa5eUuOdriCxjktZ.jpg)

From keeping engine components lubricated to reducing heat and friction to minimizing wear and tear, using the automaker’s recommended oil will help you get the most out of your [Atlas](https://www.volkswagenofdesmoines.com/new-vehicles/atlas/) on every Des Moines and Waukee drive. But what kind of oil does the Volkswagen Atlas use? Lithia Volkswagen of Des Moines answers this question below, covering the suggested Volkswagen Atlas oil type, as well as the Volkswagen Atlas oil capacity.

[More Service Tips](https://www.volkswagenofdesmoines.com/service/service-tips/) [Schedule Oil Change](https://www.volkswagenofdesmoines.com/schedule-service/)

## What Kind Of Oil Does The Volkswagen Atlas Use?

It’s no secret that routine oil changes are an essential part of [VW maintenance](https://www.volkswagenofdesmoines.com/service/service-tips/volkswagen-maintenance-schedule/). At your next oil change, request the preferred Volkswagen Atlas oil type, which is a full synthetic 0W-30.\* The manufacturer specifically recommends Castrol brand motor oil.

## How Much Oil Does The Volkswagen Atlas Need?

Now that you know what kind of oil the Volkswagen Atlas uses, you are likely curious about exactly how much oil you’ll need. The Volkswagen Atlas oil capacity rings in at 6.02 quarts, which includes the filter.

## Why Choose Synthetic Over Conventional Oil?

The VW Atlas requires full synthetic motor oil due to its sophisticated engine design, which demands premium lubrication for optimal performance on West Des Moines roads and beyond. Here are a few key advantages of synthetic over conventional motor oil:

- **Superior Engine Protection** – Synthetic oils contain additives that create a protective barrier against wear.
- **Smoother Flow** – The structure of synthetic oil maintains better fluidity across temperature extremes, resulting in proper circulation during cold starts and consistent lubrication under high heat.
- **Turbocharged Engine Support** – For Atlas models equipped with turbochargers, synthetic oil provides crucial safeguards for these high-performance components that operate at extreme temperatures and speeds.
- **Extended Oil Life** – Synthetic oil resists thermal breakdown and maintains its protective qualities longer than conventional oil, which can mean more time between oil changes.
- **A Cleaner Oil Supply** – The composition of synthetic oil keeps carbon buildup and sludge formation to a minimum, which, in turn, keeps internal engine parts cleaner and functioning more efficiently.

## Schedule An Oil Change In Johnston

It’s a good idea to schedule an oil change with the suggested Volkswagen Atlas oil type every 10,000 miles. Make an appointment by [contacting us](https://www.volkswagenofdesmoines.com/service/contact-service/) directly or [reserving a time](https://www.volkswagenofdesmoines.com/schedule-service/) online, and don’t hesitate to reach out if you have any further questions about the Volkswagen Atlas oil capacity or type. Our service technicians are here to provide the quality service you need to enjoy your Atlas for years to come.

EVs skip oil changes and timing belts, but that doesn’t mean they’re maintenance‑free, especially when you’re shopping used. ### Quick takeaway Audi recommends time‑ and mileage‑based service for the e-tron GT, with major inspections roughly every 2 years/20,000 miles, regular brake fluid changes, cabin filters, and detailed high‑voltage system checks. Tires, brakes, and suspension still matter just as much as any performance Audi. ## How Audi e-tron GT maintenance works The e-tron GT is built like a high‑performance Audi but maintained like a modern EV. Instead of the familiar A6 or S5 routine of **oil changes every 10,000 miles**, the electric GT leans on long inspection intervals and software‑driven checks. The car’s service reminder in the cockpit display is your referee, counting down to the next visit based on time and mileage. - There’s no engine oil, spark plugs, or exhaust system to service. - The big-ticket item, the high‑voltage battery, is monitored constantly by onboard software. - Most scheduled visits center around inspections, filters, fluids, tires, and brake components. - Audi typically structures service as flexible inspections rather than long lists of parts to replace. ### Tip for first-time EV owners On an e-tron GT, time matters as much as miles. Even if you only drive a few thousand miles a year, you’ll still want those 2‑year inspections for things like brake fluid, seals, and suspension wear. ## Audi e-tron GT maintenance schedule overview Exact intervals can vary slightly by model year and market, but most Audi e-tron GT schedules in the U.S. follow this general rhythm. Always confirm with the owner’s manual or Audi dealer for your specific VIN, but this overview will get you 95% of the way there. ![Audi e-tron GT on a lift in a service bay during a scheduled inspection](https://recharged.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fd365moeqy2c2l.cloudfront.net%2Fimages%2Fcontent%2Feebb01bf70db2e32ec581d22b03e813e-content.png&w=3840&q=75) Most e-tron GT scheduled services are inspections and fluid checks rather than big mechanical repairs. ### Audi e-tron GT service interval table Common U.S. market inspection and replacement intervals for key e-tron GT maintenance items. Always verify against the service booklet for your car. | Interval (time / miles) | What usually happens | EV‑specific notes | | --- | --- | --- | | Every 1 year / 10,000 miles | General inspection, tire rotation, visual brake check, fluids top‑off | High‑voltage cables and underbody shield visually checked. | | Every 2 years / 20,000 miles | Comprehensive inspection, brake fluid change, cabin filter replacement | High‑voltage system and battery cooling circuit checked with diagnostics. | | Every 3 years | Air conditioning service check, refrigerant leak inspection | Heat pump and battery thermal management performance evaluated. | | Every 4 years / ~40,000 miles | More detailed suspension/steering check, alignment check recommended | Extra attention to weight‑related wear on tires, bushings, and control arms. | | Every 6 years / 60,000+ miles | Possible coolant exchange depending on Audi guidance and climate | Battery coolant condition and thermal system capacity reviewed. | | As needed | Tires, brake pads/rotors, wiper blades, 12‑V battery | Tire wear can be quicker than on non‑performance EVs; regen doesn’t eliminate brake service. | Intervals shown are typical guidelines; local schedules and warranty plans may differ. ## Key maintenance items on the Audi e-tron GT, explained ### What your e-tron GT actually needs serviced Think inspections and wear items, not constant fluid changes. #### Annual inspections Audi techs scan for software faults, check steering and suspension, inspect axle boots and underbody panels, and look for leaks or physical damage to the high‑voltage system. #### Brake fluid & hydraulics Even with strong regenerative braking, the car still relies on a conventional hydraulic system. Fluid ages with time and moisture and typically gets replaced about every 2 years. #### Cabin & 12‑V battery The high‑voltage pack powers the car, but the 12‑V battery runs control modules. Expect conventional 12‑V battery replacement every few years plus cabin air filter changes for clean HVAC performance. Beyond those basics, expect the usual wear items: tires, wiper blades, and, over time, brake pads and rotors. Because the e-tron GT is heavy and very quick, it can chew through tires faster than a regular sedan, especially on performance rubber. ### Don’t skip tire rotations With dual‑motor all‑wheel drive and instant torque, uneven tire wear can sneak up on you. Regular rotations (often every 5,000–10,000 miles) keep the car tracking straight and protect those expensive 20‑ or 21‑inch tires. ## Battery health checks for the e-tron GT The high‑voltage battery is the e-tron GT’s heart and its most expensive single component. Day to day, you’ll see only a percentage and range estimate on the dash, but during scheduled service Audi technicians can pull detailed diagnostic data, including fault codes, temperature behavior, and any cell‑level issues. ### What Audi checks at service - Battery control module fault codes and thermal alerts. - Cooling system performance and coolant level/condition. - High‑voltage wiring and connectors for damage or corrosion. - Sealing and underbody protection around the pack. ### What you can watch at home - Sudden loss of range with the same driving pattern. - Charging behavior that’s much slower than usual on the same charger. - Warning lights related to the electrical system or drive system. - Unusual fan noise or frequent cooling activity when parked. ### How Recharged helps on used e-tron GTs Every EV sold through Recharged includes a **Recharged Score Report** with verified battery health, so you’re not guessing how the last owner treated the pack. That’s a big advantage over a generic used‑car inspection. ## Typical Audi e-tron GT maintenance costs You’re driving a flagship Audi, so service visits won’t be bargain‑basement. The good news is that **EVs shift more of your budget from maintenance to tires** rather than piling on fluid changes and engine work. Actual prices vary by dealer and region, but this is a realistic way to think about costs in the U.S. ### Typical U.S. e-tron GT maintenance and wear costs $200–$350 Minor visit Basic inspection with cabin filter and rotation at an Audi dealer. $400–$800 Major service 2‑year/20,000‑mile type visit with brake fluid and deeper checks. $1,200–$2,000+ Tire set High‑performance 20–21" tires, including mounting and alignment. Low Drivetrain upkeep No timing belt, spark plugs, or engine oil changes vs gas Audi. ### Budgeting tip If you’re planning long‑term ownership, set aside a tire fund and assume one major service every 2 years. Compared with a V6 or V8 Audi, you’re likely to come out ahead over 5–7 years of driving. ## Maintenance differences: e-tron GT vs gas Audi If you’re coming out of a gas‑powered S or RS model, the e-tron GT will feel strangely low‑maintenance. EVs skip oil changes and timing belts, but that doesn’t mean they’re maintenance‑free, especially when you’re shopping used. ### Quick takeaway Audi recommends time‑ and mileage‑based service for the e-tron GT, with major inspections roughly every 2 years/20,000 miles, regular brake fluid changes, cabin filters, and detailed high‑voltage system checks. Tires, brakes, and suspension still matter just as much as any performance Audi. ## How Audi e-tron GT maintenance works The e-tron GT is built like a high‑performance Audi but maintained like a modern EV. Instead of the familiar A6 or S5 routine of **oil changes every 10,000 miles**, the electric GT leans on long inspection intervals and software‑driven checks. The car’s service reminder in the cockpit display is your referee, counting down to the next visit based on time and mileage. - There’s no engine oil, spark plugs, or exhaust system to service. - The big-ticket item, the high‑voltage battery, is monitored constantly by onboard software. - Most scheduled visits center around inspections, filters, fluids, tires, and brake components. - Audi typically structures service as flexible inspections rather than long lists of parts to replace. ### Tip for first-time EV owners On an e-tron GT, time matters as much as miles. Even if you only drive a few thousand miles a year, you’ll still want those 2‑year inspections for things like brake fluid, seals, and suspension wear. ## Audi e-tron GT maintenance schedule overview Exact intervals can vary slightly by model year and market, but most Audi e-tron GT schedules in the U.S. follow this general rhythm. Always confirm with the owner’s manual or Audi dealer for your specific VIN, but this overview will get you 95% of the way there. ![Audi e-tron GT on a lift in a service bay during a scheduled inspection](https://recharged.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fd365moeqy2c2l.cloudfront.net%2Fimages%2Fcontent%2Feebb01bf70db2e32ec581d22b03e813e-content.png&w=3840&q=75) Most e-tron GT scheduled services are inspections and fluid checks rather than big mechanical repairs. ### Audi e-tron GT service interval table Common U.S. market inspection and replacement intervals for key e-tron GT maintenance items. Fluid ages with time and moisture and typically gets replaced about every 2 years. #### Cabin & 12‑V battery The high‑voltage pack powers the car, but the 12‑V battery runs control modules. Expect conventional 12‑V battery replacement every few years plus cabin air filter changes for clean HVAC performance. Beyond those basics, expect the usual wear items: tires, wiper blades, and, over time, brake pads and rotors. Because the e-tron GT is heavy and very quick, it can chew through tires faster than a regular sedan, especially on performance rubber. ### Don’t skip tire rotations With dual‑motor all‑wheel drive and instant torque, uneven tire wear can sneak up on you. Regular rotations (often every 5,000–10,000 miles) keep the car tracking straight and protect those expensive 20‑ or 21‑inch tires. ## Battery health checks for the e-tron GT The high‑voltage battery is the e-tron GT’s heart and its most expensive single component. Day to day, you’ll see only a percentage and range estimate on the dash, but during scheduled service Audi technicians can pull detailed diagnostic data, including fault codes, temperature behavior, and any cell‑level issues. ### What Audi checks at service - Battery control module fault codes and thermal alerts. - Cooling system performance and coolant level/condition. - High‑voltage wiring and connectors for damage or corrosion. - Sealing and underbody protection around the pack. ### What you can watch at home - Sudden loss of range with the same driving pattern. - Charging behavior that’s much slower than usual on the same charger. - Warning lights related to the electrical system or drive system. - Unusual fan noise or frequent cooling activity when parked. ### How Recharged helps on used e-tron GTs Every EV sold through Recharged includes a **Recharged Score Report** with verified battery health, so you’re not guessing how the last owner treated the pack. That’s a big advantage over a generic used‑car inspection. ## Typical Audi e-tron GT maintenance costs You’re driving a flagship Audi, so service visits won’t be bargain‑basement. The good news is that **EVs shift more of your budget from maintenance to tires** rather than piling on fluid changes and engine work. Actual prices vary by dealer and region, but this is a realistic way to think about costs in the U.S. ### Typical U.S. e-tron GT maintenance and wear costs $200–$350 Minor visit Basic inspection with cabin filter and rotation at an Audi dealer. $400–$800 Major service 2‑year/20,000‑mile type visit with brake fluid and deeper checks. $1,200–$2,000+ Tire set High‑performance 20–21" tires, including mounting and alignment. Low Drivetrain upkeep No timing belt, spark plugs, or engine oil changes vs gas Audi. ### Budgeting tip If you’re planning long‑term ownership, set aside a tire fund and assume one major service every 2 years. Compared with a V6 or V8 Audi, you’re likely to come out ahead over 5–7 years of driving. ## Maintenance differences: e-tron GT vs gas Audi If you’re coming out of a gas‑powered S or RS model, the e-tron GT will feel strangely low‑maintenance. # MAINTAINING YOUR BMW VEHICLE

A well-maintained vehicle will help safeguard its operational performance, road-safety and its reliability. This is why it is important to follow and perform BMW’s recommended periodic vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks as indicated by your vehicle’s Maintenance Service Display, along with the other maintenance work described in this booklet.

A improper maintenance is not covered under the BMW New Vehicle Damage, including consequential damage, which results from lack of or Limited Warranty for Passenger Cars and Light Trucks.

# MAINTENANCE INTERVALS

Maintenance intervals on motor vehicles were conventionally based solely on a fixed time period or a specified amount of accumulated driving mileage.

However, operational and driving conditions have a major influence on your vehicle’s routine maintenance requirements; the distance traveled is only one of these significant factors. A vehicle used for short trips in the city with numerous cold starts, prolonged periods of idling, stop-and-go driving, and high engine speeds during acceleration may require more frequent maintenance intervals than a vehicle that is driven long distances at moderate engine speeds.

Your BMW vehicle uses sensors and algorithms together with the elapsed time and the driving distance/profile to monitor and evaluate your vehicle’s maintenance service needs. This information is then used to adapt dynamically the parameters used to forecast the applicable maintenance service task intervals.

# THE BMW MAINTENANCE SYSTEM

All BMW vehicles are equipped with an integrated BMW Maintenance System. This maintenance “reminder” system helps ensure that the vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks are performed at the forecasted intervals that apply to your vehicle.

The BMW Maintenance System display provides the vehicle operator access to the current status information for the following maintenance service tasks:

$\\triangleright$ Engine oil (date and miles)\*

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle check (date and miles)

$\\triangleright$ Front brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Rear brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid (date)

$\\triangleright$ 1200 Mile running-in service (date and miles) (Applicable to BMW M vehicles only)\*

For each specific maintenance service task, either the future date (month/ year), remaining miles or both are provided as noted above. The system monitors variable inputs to forecast the intervals and alert the driver when one or more specific maintenance tasks should be performed.

NOTE: For certain vehicles, the status of the front and rear brake pads will only be observable in the maintenance system’s display when there are approximately 2,000 miles or less remaining before a brake service will be required to be performed.

For information about the vehicle’s maintenance system displays, please refer to the Maintenance Service Display Overview section beginning on page 5.

The following “combine with Engine oil”\* maintenance service tasks may be identified as needing to be performed with a specific occurrence of the “Engine oil” service task (service counter number):

$\\triangleright$ Cabin Microfilter(s)

$\\triangleright$ Engine air filter(s)\*

$\\triangleright$ Spark plugs\*

$\\triangleright$ Final drive oil (Applicable M vehicles only)

\\* Does not apply to BEV

Although these items do not appear in the BMW Maintenance System’s display in the vehicle, these services should be performed when your vehicle’s engine oil is changed in accordance with the interval identified by your vehicle’s BMW Maintenance System.

For more information on your vehicle’s maintenance services requirements, procedures and intervals, please refer the Maintenance Service Summary section beginning on page 10.

The BMW Maintenance System also includes an option to set service reminders for the following state-specific mandatory vehicle inspections, including:

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle safety inspection; and/or $\\triangleright$ Emissions test

The corresponding interval data for these inspections can be inputted into the BMW Maintenance System by a service provider; they are not determined by the vehicle.

For your convenience, you may also wish to have your authorized BMW center perform the work necessary to fulfill these state inspection requirements in your area concurrent with the maintenance services specified above when possible.

Should you request more frequent maintenance service than is indicated by the BMW Maintenance System during the coverage period, the cost of these services will not be covered by the BMW Maintenance Program.

# SERVICE DATA — REMOTE CONTROL KEY

Maintenance service task status information for your BMW vehicle is continually updated and stored in your remote control key.

Your authorized BMW center can access this data and consult with you about applicable service procedures and tasks for your vehicle.

Therefore, always provide your service consultant with the most recent remote control key that was used to operate the vehicle when servicing your vehicle at a BMW center.

# VEHICLE STORAGE

Disconnecting the battery during periods of long-term vehicle storage will interrupt the calculation of time-dependent maintenance services.

In this situation, BMW recommends that you have all your time-based maintenance services, such as brake fluid, engine oil and cabin microfilter, brought up to the correct date by an authorized BMW center.

# ENGINE OIL

2025 model year vehicles with internal-combustion engines are factory-filled with:

Z BMW-approved fully synthetic oil for gasoline engines

Engine oil should be changed when the vehicle’s engine is at operating temperature.

If an engine oil service is being performed or you need to add engine oil between changes, please refer to the Owner’s Manual for the recommended engine oil for your BMW vehicle.

# LONG-TERM RATED FLUIDS AND OILS

The following systems and assemblies are factory-filled with long-term rated fluid and oil; fluid replacement is only necessary when repairs are being performed (unless otherwise noted):

$\\triangleright$ Engine cooling system (antifreeze/coolant) $\\triangleright$ Automatic (except for X1 and X2) and manual transmissions $\\triangleright$ All-wheel drive transfer cases (except when indicated by the vehicle)

# REGULAR CHECKS — VEHICLE OPERATOR

In addition to the maintenance service procedure information contained in this booklet, BMW recommends that you regularly check (when refueling, for example), and address when necessary, the following items:

$\\triangleright$ Washer fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Coolant level

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Tires — pressure, condition and wear

Please refer to the Owner’s Manual for additional information.

# What is the Recommended BMW Maintenance Schedule?

![Mechanic fixing BMW](https://dealerinspire-image-library-prod.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/images/qOCqBJVRI2dmLPMZp2H4nX2vvpahYMjkkgG6QC7e.jpg)

* * *

At BMW of Tigard, we often get questions from customers about their BMW maintenance schedule. And when you buy a [quality new BMW](https://www.bmwtigard.com/new-vehicles/), it’s important to stick to its BMW service schedule. That’s why we’ve provided the recommended maintenance schedule for general BMW vehicles for Portland and Tigard drivers. With this handy guide, it’ll be easy to stay on track and have your vehicle serviced. We’ll ensure that your vehicle will always be running at its best! As always, before you schedule maintenance on your vehicle, be sure to read your owner’s manual for any specific maintenance information that applies to your BMW vehicle. That way, you’ll better understand your specific model and trim’s future maintenance and repair needs.

[BMW X3 SERVICE SCHEDULE](https://www.bmwtigard.com/service/service-and-parts-tips/bmw-x3-service-schedule/) [Service & Parts Specials](https://www.bmwtigard.com/service-parts-specials/)

* * *

## BMW Preventative Maintenance: Every 5,000 Miles / 6 Months

It’s important to bring in your BMW two or three times a year (or every 5,000 miles) for these preventative maintenance services:

- Front and rear brake inspection
- Brake fluid check
- Coolant check
- Engine oil check
- Cabin air filter inspection
- Engine inspection
- Vehicle inspection
- Wiper blade inspection
- Any necessary tire rotations

Your BMW also comes with something called the Condition-Based Service Monitor (CBS). Your CBS tracks the condition of important systems in your BMW, letting you know if service is required. Our technicians will also use your CBS to determine what needs to be replaced, repaired, or serviced when you schedule service. Keep in mind that just because your CBS may say that service may not be necessary at 5,000 miles doesn’t mean that you shouldn’t come in for preventative maintenance and checks. Sometimes human eyes are necessary to determine a problem or to nip any potential issues in the bud.

## Recommended BMW Maintenance Schedule

Your BMW service schedule needs will vary based on how often you drive, where you drive, and your driving conditions. Your owner’s manual can give you detailed information on common service tasks for your specific model and trim, but here’s what BMW owners can generally expect:

- **Every 10,000 miles** (or yearly): replace your vehicle’s engine oil, oil filter, and coolant.
- **Every 20,000 miles** (or every two years): inspect and replace your vehicle’s fuel filters.
- **Every 30,000 miles** (or every three years): replace your vehicle’s brake fluid (after the first replacement, **every 60,000 miles**) and replace your vehicle’s transmission fluid on manual-transmission BMWs.
- **Every 60,000 miles** (or every six years): replace your vehicle’s engine air filter and spark plugs, inspect and replace any brake pads and brake rotors, and replace transmission fluid on automatic-transmission BMWs.
- **Every 90,000 miles** (or every nine years): replace your vehicle’s timing belts and hoses.

You’ll want to repeat the cycle above after 90,000 miles and always follow the 5,000-mile maintenance schedule. Your BMW’s New Vehicle Limited Warranty will also expire at 50,000 miles, so we recommend getting in any repairs or service before this warranty expires! We also recommend replacing your BMW battery around 50,000 miles.

No matter the miles on your BMW, you’ll receive the benefit of BMW-trained technicians, genuine BMW OEM parts, and up-front pricing. Your [brakes](https://vw.oempartsonline.com/brakes) stop your [Volkswagen](https://vw.oempartsonline.com/v-volkswagen) vehicle. They do it by clamping their calipers and brake rotors together. This is what creates the friction, or resistance, that slows your vehicle's wheels and tires. However, calipers can't press rotors without brake pads, or else they'd get damaged. Your VW has one of four types of pads, depending on its model. Organic brake pads are for everyday driving. They're reliable, they don't wear rotors down as badly, and they don't create much dust. Best of all, they're inexpensive. Ceramic brake pads work better in bad weather, they don't make much noise, and their dust isn't as sticky. Metallic brake pads, however, stand up to higher heat, feel firmer, and resist brake fade. Carbon fiber brake pads are the strongest and best performers, tolerant of high temperatures and providing the most stopping power. Most cars and SUVs use either metallic or organic pads. However, many sports cars and performance vehicles use ceramic or carbon fiber pads because they do the best job of expelling heat.

## How Long Do Volkswagen Brake Pads Last?

However, no brake pad lasts forever, not even those Volkswagen makes. You should change yours every 40,000 to 50,000 miles or so. Otherwise, figure out when to replace them by looking for the signs your brakes are going bad. They include warning lights, worn pad surfaces, pad damage, whiny brakes, and taking longer to stop. The worst are vibration and grinding, as they indicate your rotors are warped and getting damaged because your brake pads have degraded.

# Volkswagen Jetta Recommended Maintenance Schedule

![2023 Volkswagen Jetta](https://dealerinspire-image-library-prod.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/images/Ul0f8P7h06keJCujiQSKVvyMiTtkjRbSVGr1DQQy.jpg)

* * *

The Volkswagen Jetta is one of the stalwarts of the brand. It gives you excellent fuel economy yet a powerful engine. Maintaining your [new vehicle](https://www.carolinavw.com/new-vehicles/) in its best shape for every Monroe drive means bringing your car in for Volkswagen Jetta service at least once a year. We recommend following the VW Jetta maintenance schedule for the best results.

Discover everything about the VW Jetta service intervals with our comprehensive guide!

[Schedule Volkswagen Jetta Service](https://www.carolinavw.com/online-service-scheduler/) [Service Department](https://www.carolinavw.com/service/)

## What Is the Volkswagen Jetta Maintenance Schedule?

Your [new VW Jetta](https://www.carolinavw.com/new-vehicles/jetta/) service intervals occur every 10,000 miles. Older Volkswagen models might have different maintenance requirements. Check your owner’s manual for the correct VW Jetta maintenance schedule. However, world-class engineering for newer vehicles means longer VW Jetta service intervals, lowering overall ownership costs.

Every 10,000 miles is also the VW Jetta oil change interval, so expect a full synthetic oil change every 10,000 miles of driving. The exception is if you frequently drive in less-than-ideal conditions in Concord. If you repeatedly hit the brakes hard, you might need new tires or new brakes sooner than expected.

Below is the VW Jetta maintenance schedule you should follow.

### **VW Jetta Maintenance Schedule: 10,000 Miles or One Year**

Your first Volkswagen Jetta service in Charlotte will consist of the following:

- Oil and filter change
- Brake pad inspection
- Brake disc inspection
- Service interval reset

### **VW Jetta Maintenance Schedule: 20,000 Miles or Two Years**

For this VW Jetta service interval, we will do everything from the first service at 10,000 miles, plus some extras:

- Engine compartment and transmission inspection
- Battery inspection
- Fluid level adjustments (brake fluid and coolant)
- Tire pressure and TPMS inspection
- Tire tread depth inspection
- Tire repair kit inspection
- Exterior lighting systems inspection
- Windshield wiper and washer system inspection
- Check for sunroof drain blockage
- Horn test
- Road test

### **VW Jetta Maintenance Schedule: 30,000 Miles or Three Years**

This is what our team will do for your three-year Volkswagen Jetta service near Indian Trail to keep your sedan in top shape:

- Oil and filter change
- Brake pad inspection
- Brake disc inspection
- Service interval reset

### **VW Jetta Maintenance Schedule: 40,000 Miles or Four Years**

At 40,000 miles, we’ll take care of the VW Jetta oil change interval, just like the other one-year maintenance. We’ll also check everything from the 20,000-mile VW Jetta service interval. Our team will also look over these things for your Jetta for four years:

**Replacements:**

- Dust and pollen filter
- Spark plugs

**Inspections:**

- Suspension components
- Corrosion inside and out
- Brake system
- Underbody
- Windshield
- Exhaust system
- Interior lighting
- Ribbed V-belt
- Sunroof

### **VW Jetta Maintenance Schedule: 50,000 Miles or Five Years**

At the 50,000-mile mark, this service interval includes everything from the first one:

- VW Jetta Oil Change Interval
- New Oil Filter
- Check Your Brake Pads
- Fluid Levels
- Service Interval Display Reset (if needed)

At this point in your sedan ownership, you might need a new battery, new tires, or new brake parts, depending on the condition of your Volkswagen Jetta. We’ll discuss your options with you if we see anything that needs service at this interval.

## Services at 80,000 to 150,000 Miles

Your Volkswagen maintenance schedule continues with routine maintenance, as we already discussed. Services at 80,000 to 150,000 miles are on the simple side, thankfully. Your VW Jetta warranty is for four years and 50,000 miles. Keep that in mind as you keep your car in fantastic condition.

## Contact Us for Volkswagen Jetta Service in Charlotte!

Remember, this is the ideal and expected Volkswagen Jetta maintenance schedule for driving in ideal conditions. Driving in dusty conditions or driving too fast might require shorter service intervals. Have questions? Feel free to [contact us](https://www.carolinavw.com/contact-us/) or call 980-221-0753. We want you to get the most out of your VW ownership!

## 2023 VW Jetta Coolant

Coolant, as it relates to vehicles, is frequently a liquid or gas substance used to regulate the temperature of your engine. Liquid coolants are usually half water and half ethylene glycol. Water is used to transfer heat while ethylene glycol is used to lower the freezing point of the liquid. In colder climates, this is immensely vital. This undoubtedly isn't the first time you've heard of ethylene glycol as it is the central ingredient in the popular term "antifreeze". Keep in mind, you never want to pour antifreeze or water by themselves into your engine system. They need to be mixed to construct the proper coolant.

You can purchase ready-made mixtures of coolant that already have water added, or you can purchase full-strength antifreeze which needs to be diluted with distilled water before being added to the engine system. ## How long does 2023 VW Jetta coolant last?

How frequently you need to flush and replenish your vehicle's coolant relies on the type of coolant. There are many types of coolants. Up until the mid-1990s there was essentially only a single type of coolant. It was a green formula coolant that contained corrosion inhibitors that only lasted between 24,000 - 36,000 miles or between two to three years. This type of coolant is not suggested for newer vehicles which come equipped with a longer-lasting coolant.

Newer coolants use an Organic Acid Technology (OAT) and last up to twice as long as older coolant. In some cases these long-life coolants can last over 5 years or 100,000 miles.

## 2023 VW Jetta Coolant Flush

A coolant flush or cooling system service consists of three main services.

- Adding a cleaner compound to get rid of particles, sediment, corrosion,and rust
- Replenishing the system with the appropriate coolant and cautiously measuring the dilution percentage
- Flushing the whole system thoroughly

## What happens if my 2023 VW Jetta runs out of coolant?

Your 2023 VW Jetta doesn't have to run out of coolant for troubles to start. Dilution levels need to be within a specific percentage range or your 2023 VW Jetta engine components can start to rust, break, or become irreplaceably damaged. If you run out of coolant utterly due to a leak or poor fluid levels, your complete engine system can be compromised from the gaskets to the pistons or even the engine block itself.

## How often should you change coolant in a 2023 VW Jetta?

Normally, you should have your 2023 VW Jetta coolant flush completed every 30,000 miles or every two years. There are certain instances where your vehicle can go without a flush for a longer period of time. When you bring your vehicle into Nalley Volkswagen of Alpharetta, we will check your fluid levels and inspect it for debris or sediment which can harm the engine, and make sure it's diluted perfectly. It's vital to have this checked every 15,000 miles to make sure you catch any issues before they cause dramatic damage. When it comes to your 2023 VW Jetta engine, it's better safe than sorry.

## How do I know if I need a coolant flush in my 2023 VW Jetta?

Common symptoms that your 2023 VW Jetta needs a coolant flush are:

- Your check engine light may turn on
- Sediment or rust will be visible in the coolant
- Steam will come from the radiator or hood
- Coolant will normally leak out when the engine is running. Check the ground when you park.
- Sometimes, albeit unlikely, you'll be able to smell an odd burning odor coming from under the hood.
- Your temperature gauge will read far above normal with the engine on for a few minutes.
- Unexpected grinding noises can come from the engine
- Your heater may stop working

# BMW SERVICE

BMW recommends you have your maintenance and repair work performed by an authorized BMW center.

# MAINTAINING YOUR BMW VEHICLE

A well-maintained vehicle will help safeguard its operational performance, road-safety and its reliability. This is why it is important to follow and perform BMW’s recommended periodic vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks as indicated by your vehicle’s Maintenance Service Display, along with the other maintenance work described in this booklet.

A improper maintenance is not covered under the BMW New Vehicle Damage, including consequential damage, which results from lack of or Limited Warranty for Passenger Cars and Light Trucks.

# MAINTENANCE INTERVALS

Maintenance intervals on motor vehicles were conventionally based solely on a fixed time period or a specified amount of accumulated driving mileage.

However, operational and driving conditions have a major influence on your vehicle’s routine maintenance requirements; the distance traveled is only one of these significant factors. A vehicle used for short trips in the city with numerous cold starts, prolonged periods of idling, stop-and-go driving, and high engine speeds during acceleration may require more frequent maintenance intervals than a vehicle that is driven long distances at moderate engine speeds.

Your BMW vehicle uses sensors and algorithms together with the elapsed time and the driving distance/profile to monitor and evaluate your vehicle’s maintenance service needs. This information is then used to adapt dynamically the parameters used to forecast the applicable maintenance service task intervals.

# THE BMW MAINTENANCE SYSTEM

All BMW vehicles are equipped with an integrated BMW Maintenance System. This maintenance “reminder” system helps ensure that the vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks are performed at the forecasted intervals that apply to your vehicle.

The BMW Maintenance System display provides the vehicle operator access to the current status information for the following maintenance service tasks:

$\\triangleright$ Engine oil (date and miles)\*

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle check (date and miles)

$\\triangleright$ Front brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Rear brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid (date)

$\\triangleright$ 1200 Mile running-in service (date and miles) (Applicable to BMW M vehicles only)\*

For each specific maintenance service task, either the future date (month/ year), remaining miles or both are provided as noted above. The system monitors variable inputs to forecast the intervals and alert the driver when one or more specific maintenance tasks should be performed.

NOTE: For certain vehicles, the status of the front and rear brake pads will only be observable in the maintenance system’s display when there are approximately 2,000 miles or less remaining before a brake service will be required to be performed.

For information about the vehicle’s maintenance system displays, please refer to the Maintenance Service Display Overview section beginning on page 5.

The following “combine with Engine oil”\* maintenance service tasks may be identified as needing to be performed with a specific occurrence of the “Engine oil” service task (service counter number):

$\\triangleright$ Cabin Microfilter(s)

$\\triangleright$ Engine air filter(s)\*

$\\triangleright$ Spark plugs\*

$\\triangleright$ Final drive oil (Applicable M vehicles only)

\\* Does not apply to BEV

Although these items do not appear in the BMW Maintenance System’s display in the vehicle, these services should be performed when your vehicle’s engine oil is changed in accordance with the interval identified by your vehicle’s BMW Maintenance System.

For more information on your vehicle’s maintenance services requirements, procedures and intervals, please refer the Maintenance Service Summary section beginning on page 10.

The BMW Maintenance System also includes an option to set service reminders for the following state-specific mandatory vehicle inspections, including:

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle safety inspection; and/or $\\triangleright$ Emissions test

The corresponding interval data for these inspections can be inputted into the BMW Maintenance System by a service provider; they are not determined by the vehicle.

For your convenience, you may also wish to have your authorized BMW center perform the work necessary to fulfill these state inspection requirements in your area concurrent with the maintenance services specified above when possible.

Should you request more frequent maintenance service than is indicated by the BMW Maintenance System during the coverage period, the cost of these services will not be covered by the BMW Maintenance Program.

# SERVICE DATA — REMOTE CONTROL KEY

Maintenance service task status information for your BMW vehicle is continually updated and stored in your remote control key.

Your authorized BMW center can access this data and consult with you about applicable service procedures and tasks for your vehicle.

Therefore, always provide your service consultant with the most recent remote control key that was used to operate the vehicle when servicing your vehicle at a BMW center.

# VEHICLE STORAGE

Disconnecting the battery during periods of long-term vehicle storage will interrupt the calculation of time-dependent maintenance services.

In this situation, BMW recommends that you have all your time-based maintenance services, such as brake fluid, engine oil and cabin microfilter, brought up to the correct date by an authorized BMW center.

# ENGINE OIL

2025 model year vehicles with internal-combustion engines are factory-filled with:

Z BMW-approved fully synthetic oil for gasoline engines

Engine oil should be changed when the vehicle’s engine is at operating temperature.

If an engine oil service is being performed or you need to add engine oil between changes, please refer to the Owner’s Manual for the recommended engine oil for your BMW vehicle.

# LONG-TERM RATED FLUIDS AND OILS

The following systems and assemblies are factory-filled with long-term rated fluid and oil; fluid replacement is only necessary when repairs are being performed (unless otherwise noted):

$\\triangleright$ Engine cooling system (antifreeze/coolant) $\\triangleright$ Automatic (except for X1 and X2) and manual transmissions $\\triangleright$ All-wheel drive transfer cases (except when indicated by the vehicle)

# REGULAR CHECKS — VEHICLE OPERATOR

In addition to the maintenance service procedure information contained in this booklet, BMW recommends that you regularly check (when refueling, for example), and address when necessary, the following items:

$\\triangleright$ Washer fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Coolant level

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Tires — pressure, condition and wear

Please refer to the Owner’s Manual for additional information.

## Keep Your BMW 2 Series Performing at it's Best

**Basic BMW 2-Series Preventative Maintenance: Every 5,000 Miles**

BMW’s maintenance schedule is built around a standard 5,000-mile interval, guided by your vehicle’s pre-installed Condition-Based Service (CBS) monitor. This intelligent system tracks critical areas of your car and alerts you when additional services are needed.

The regular BMW recommended maintenance schedule includes the following:

- Vehicle check and inspection
- Engine oil check
- Coolant check
- Tire rotation
- Brake fluid check
- Front and rear brake inspection
- Inspection of the engine and cabin air filters
- Wiper blade inspection
- Standard scope

Not every part inspected will need replacement during your visit. Our BMW-certified maintenance experts use the CBS monitor to identify exactly what requires attention, ensuring precise and efficient service.

**BMW 2-Series Recommended Maintenance Services**

Maintenance needs can vary depending on your model and driving habits. For tailored recommendations, consult your owner’s manual or speak with one of our knowledgeable service advisors. Below is a general guideline for BMW 2 Series maintenance milestones:

**BMW 2-Series 10,000-Mile Maintenance**

- Replace the engine oil, oil filter and coolant
- Repeat every 10,000 miles

**BMW 2-Series 20,000-Mile Maintenance**

- Inspect and replace the oil filters
- Repeat every 20,000 miles

**BMW 2-Series 30,000-Mile Maintenance**

- Replace brake fluid. After the first service, schedule brake fluid replacement every 60,000 miles.
- If equipped with a manual transmission, replace transmission fluid every 30,000 miles.

**BMW 2-Series 60,000-mile maintenance**

- Replace the engine air filter and spark plugs
- Inspect and replace brake pads and rotors as needed
- For automatic transmissions, replace the transmission fluid every 60,000 miles.

**BMW 2-Series 90,000-Mile Maintenance**

- Replace the timing belt and hoses
- Repeat every 90,000 miles

**BMW 2-Series Maintenance after 90,000 Miles**

Continue following the BMW 2 Series maintenance schedule with 5,000-mile intervals and adhere to service milestones as listed above to ensure optimal performance.

# What is the Recommended BMW Maintenance Schedule?

![Mechanic fixing BMW](https://dealerinspire-image-library-prod.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/images/qOCqBJVRI2dmLPMZp2H4nX2vvpahYMjkkgG6QC7e.jpg)

* * *

At BMW of Tigard, we often get questions from customers about their BMW maintenance schedule. And when you buy a [quality new BMW](https://www.bmwtigard.com/new-vehicles/), it’s important to stick to its BMW service schedule. That’s why we’ve provided the recommended maintenance schedule for general BMW vehicles for Portland and Tigard drivers. With this handy guide, it’ll be easy to stay on track and have your vehicle serviced. We’ll ensure that your vehicle will always be running at its best! As always, before you schedule maintenance on your vehicle, be sure to read your owner’s manual for any specific maintenance information that applies to your BMW vehicle. That way, you’ll better understand your specific model and trim’s future maintenance and repair needs.

[BMW X3 SERVICE SCHEDULE](https://www.bmwtigard.com/service/service-and-parts-tips/bmw-x3-service-schedule/) [Service & Parts Specials](https://www.bmwtigard.com/service-parts-specials/)

## BMW Preventative Maintenance: Every 5,000 Miles / 6 Months

It’s important to bring in your BMW two or three times a year (or every 5,000 miles) for these preventative maintenance services:

- Front and rear brake inspection
- Brake fluid check
- Coolant check
- Engine oil check
- Cabin air filter inspection
- Engine inspection
- Vehicle inspection
- Wiper blade inspection
- Any necessary tire rotations

Your BMW also comes with something called the Condition-Based Service Monitor (CBS). Your CBS tracks the condition of important systems in your BMW, letting you know if service is required. Our technicians will also use your CBS to determine what needs to be replaced, repaired, or serviced when you schedule service. Keep in mind that just because your CBS may say that service may not be necessary at 5,000 miles doesn’t mean that you shouldn’t come in for preventative maintenance and checks. Sometimes human eyes are necessary to determine a problem or to nip any potential issues in the bud.

## Recommended BMW Maintenance Schedule

Your BMW service schedule needs will vary based on how often you drive, where you drive, and your driving conditions. Your owner’s manual can give you detailed information on common service tasks for your specific model and trim, but here’s what BMW owners can generally expect:

- **Every 10,000 miles** (or yearly): replace your vehicle’s engine oil, oil filter, and coolant.
- **Every 20,000 miles** (or every two years): inspect and replace your vehicle’s fuel filters.
- **Every 30,000 miles** (or every three years): replace your vehicle’s brake fluid (after the first replacement, **every 60,000 miles**) and replace your vehicle’s transmission fluid on manual-transmission BMWs.
- **Every 60,000 miles** (or every six years): replace your vehicle’s engine air filter and spark plugs, inspect and replace any brake pads and brake rotors, and replace transmission fluid on automatic-transmission BMWs.
- **Every 90,000 miles** (or every nine years): replace your vehicle’s timing belts and hoses.

You’ll want to repeat the cycle above after 90,000 miles and always follow the 5,000-mile maintenance schedule. Your BMW’s New Vehicle Limited Warranty will also expire at 50,000 miles, so we recommend getting in any repairs or service before this warranty expires! We also recommend replacing your BMW battery around 50,000 miles.

BMW of Tigard understands that your BMW service isn’t a one-size-fits-all situation. That’s why we offer BMW’s [BMW Value Service](https://www.bmwtigard.com/value-service/) as an option for Lake Oswego drivers and beyond. No matter the miles on your BMW, you’ll receive the benefit of BMW-trained technicians, genuine BMW OEM parts, and up-front pricing. BMW Value Service applies to select services and models, so it’s important to [contact us today](https://www.bmwtigard.com/contact-us/) to see if your vehicle qualifies and to better understand the specific services available for your model and trim.

The expert technicians at BMW of Tigard have Tigard drivers covered when it comes to everything BMW. Our team has the knowledge, tools, and genuine OEM parts to keep you on pace with your BMW service schedule. And with great options like our [specials](https://www.bmwtigard.com/service-parts-specials/) and BMW Value Service, it’s a no-brainer to choose BMW of Tigard as your BMW service center.
