# BMW SERVICE

BMW recommends you have your maintenance and repair work performed by an authorized BMW center.

# MAINTAINING YOUR BMW VEHICLE

A well-maintained vehicle will help safeguard its operational performance, road-safety and its reliability. This is why it is important to follow and perform BMW’s recommended periodic vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks as indicated by your vehicle’s Maintenance Service Display, along with the other maintenance work described in this booklet.

A improper maintenance is not covered under the BMW New Vehicle Damage, including consequential damage, which results from lack of or Limited Warranty for Passenger Cars and Light Trucks.

# MAINTENANCE INTERVALS

Maintenance intervals on motor vehicles were conventionally based solely on a fixed time period or a specified amount of accumulated driving mileage.

However, operational and driving conditions have a major influence on your vehicle’s routine maintenance requirements; the distance traveled is only one of these significant factors. A vehicle used for short trips in the city with numerous cold starts, prolonged periods of idling, stop-and-go driving, and high engine speeds during acceleration may require more frequent maintenance intervals than a vehicle that is driven long distances at moderate engine speeds.

Your BMW vehicle uses sensors and algorithms together with the elapsed time and the driving distance/profile to monitor and evaluate your vehicle’s maintenance service needs. This information is then used to adapt dynamically the parameters used to forecast the applicable maintenance service task intervals.

# THE BMW MAINTENANCE SYSTEM

All BMW vehicles are equipped with an integrated BMW Maintenance System. This maintenance “reminder” system helps ensure that the vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks are performed at the forecasted intervals that apply to your vehicle.

The BMW Maintenance System display provides the vehicle operator access to the current status information for the following maintenance service tasks:

$\\triangleright$ Engine oil (date and miles)\*

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle check (date and miles)

$\\triangleright$ Front brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Rear brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid (date)

$\\triangleright$ 1200 Mile running-in service (date and miles) (Applicable to BMW M vehicles only)\*

For each specific maintenance service task, either the future date (month/ year), remaining miles or both are provided as noted above. The system monitors variable inputs to forecast the intervals and alert the driver when one or more specific maintenance tasks should be performed.

NOTE: For certain vehicles, the status of the front and rear brake pads will only be observable in the maintenance system’s display when there are approximately 2,000 miles or less remaining before a brake service will be required to be performed.

For information about the vehicle’s maintenance system displays, please refer to the Maintenance Service Display Overview section beginning on page 5.

The following “combine with Engine oil”\* maintenance service tasks may be identified as needing to be performed with a specific occurrence of the “Engine oil” service task (service counter number):

$\\triangleright$ Cabin Microfilter(s)

$\\triangleright$ Engine air filter(s)\*

$\\triangleright$ Spark plugs\*

$\\triangleright$ Final drive oil (Applicable M vehicles only)

\\* Does not apply to BEV

Although these items do not appear in the BMW Maintenance System’s display in the vehicle, these services should be performed when your vehicle’s engine oil is changed in accordance with the interval identified by your vehicle’s BMW Maintenance System.

For more information on your vehicle’s maintenance services requirements, procedures and intervals, please refer the Maintenance Service Summary section beginning on page 10.

The BMW Maintenance System also includes an option to set service reminders for the following state-specific mandatory vehicle inspections, including:

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle safety inspection; and/or $\\triangleright$ Emissions test

The corresponding interval data for these inspections can be inputted into the BMW Maintenance System by a service provider; they are not determined by the vehicle.

For your convenience, you may also wish to have your authorized BMW center perform the work necessary to fulfill these state inspection requirements in your area concurrent with the maintenance services specified above when possible.

Should you request more frequent maintenance service than is indicated by the BMW Maintenance System during the coverage period, the cost of these services will not be covered by the BMW Maintenance Program.

# SERVICE DATA — REMOTE CONTROL KEY

Maintenance service task status information for your BMW vehicle is continually updated and stored in your remote control key.

Your authorized BMW center can access this data and consult with you about applicable service procedures and tasks for your vehicle.

Therefore, always provide your service consultant with the most recent remote control key that was used to operate the vehicle when servicing your vehicle at a BMW center.

# VEHICLE STORAGE

Disconnecting the battery during periods of long-term vehicle storage will interrupt the calculation of time-dependent maintenance services.

In this situation, BMW recommends that you have all your time-based maintenance services, such as brake fluid, engine oil and cabin microfilter, brought up to the correct date by an authorized BMW center.

# ENGINE OIL

2025 model year vehicles with internal-combustion engines are factory-filled with:

Z BMW-approved fully synthetic oil for gasoline engines

Engine oil should be changed when the vehicle’s engine is at operating temperature.

If an engine oil service is being performed or you need to add engine oil between changes, please refer to the Owner’s Manual for the recommended engine oil for your BMW vehicle.

# LONG-TERM RATED FLUIDS AND OILS

The following systems and assemblies are factory-filled with long-term rated fluid and oil; fluid replacement is only necessary when repairs are being performed (unless otherwise noted):

$\\triangleright$ Engine cooling system (antifreeze/coolant) $\\triangleright$ Automatic (except for X1 and X2) and manual transmissions $\\triangleright$ All-wheel drive transfer cases (except when indicated by the vehicle)

# REGULAR CHECKS — VEHICLE OPERATOR

In addition to the maintenance service procedure information contained in this booklet, BMW recommends that you regularly check (when refueling, for example), and address when necessary, the following items:

$\\triangleright$ Washer fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Coolant level

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Tires — pressure, condition and wear

Please refer to the Owner’s Manual for additional information.

BMW’s maintenance schedule is built around a standard 5,000-mile interval, guided by your vehicle’s pre-installed Condition-Based Service (CBS) monitor. This intelligent system tracks critical areas of your car and alerts you when additional services are needed.

- Replace the engine oil, oil filter and coolant

- Inspect and replace the oil filters
- Repeat every 20,000 miles

**BMW 2-Series 30,000-Mile Maintenance**

- Replace the engine air filter and spark plugs
- Inspect and replace brake pads and rotors as needed

- Replace the timing belt and hoses
- Repeat every 90,000 miles

**BMW 2-Series Maintenance after 90,000 Miles**

# BMW 3 Series Maintenance Schedule

![](https://dealerimages.dealereprocess.com/image/upload/3734739)

## Maintenance Schedule

Keeping up with your vehicle’s routine maintenance schedule is crucial to the health and longevity of your car. Routine maintenance services are done about once or twice a year, and are usually just a quick stop by the shop to change your oil and make sure everything is working properly.

**Here at BMW of Westchester we know how important it is to stay on top of these services in order to keep your car on the streets of Westchester County and Yonkers, NY, for years to come. Check out our breakdown of the BMW 3 Series maintenance schedule below!  [Schedule a service appointment](https://www.westchesterbmw.com/service-appointment/) for more assistance.**

## Annual Routine Maintenance Services

Your first[BMW 3 Series](https://www.westchesterbmw.com/search/new-bmw-3-series-white-plains-ny/?cy=10607&md=33&tp=new) routine maintenance service will happen about 6 months in, or once you hit around 5,000-10,000 miles, whichever happens to come first. This first service will be relatively quick. It will include:

- **An oil and filter change**

- **Tire rotation**

- **Brake inspection**


You’ll want to get these services done once or twice a year for the duration of the vehicle’s life.

Staying on top of your regular oil and oil filter changes is crucial to your car’s health because as your engine runs, tiny bits of dirt and dust will build up in it, which can cause excessive wear and tear.

**Additionally, yearly [tire rotations](https://www.westchesterbmw.com/service-appointment/) are important to maintain traction control, because they prevent your wheels from having uneven tread. Tread and traction control helps your vehicle stop quicker, and provides you with safer travels over rough terrain.**

![](https://dealerimages.dealereprocess.com/image/upload/3734763)

![](https://dealerimages.dealereprocess.com/image/upload/3734769)

## 30,000-Mile Maintenance Services

Once your BMW 3 Series hits 30,000 miles, it’s time to head back to the shop for a variety of inspections and maintenance care checks. To start, you’re going to need:

- **Your air filter changed, over time your air filter can become clogged, and a replacement will be needed in order for it to work at its best. If you travel in particularly dusty environments, you’ll want this changed around 15,000 miles rather than 30,000.**

- **Next, you’ll need your fuel filter inspected; your technician can perform a pressure test to determine if you’ll need it replaced.**


## 60,000-Mile Maintenance Services

Your 60,000-mile maintenance service will happen at around four or five years into ownership for the average driver. At this service, you’ll need:

- **Brake Rotor, Pads, and Shoes Inspections and Replacements**

- **Brake Fluid Replacement**

- **Coolant Replacement**

- **Transmission Fluid Replacement**

- **Your BMW 3 Series battery and brakes will start to wear out around the 60,000-mile mark, which is why it’s so important to get them inspected, and possibly replaced.**


![](https://dealerimages.dealereprocess.com/image/upload/3734756)

![](https://dealerimages.dealereprocess.com/image/upload/3734759)

## 90,000-Mile Maintenance Services

Your 90,000-mile maintenance check will include an inspection of your hoses, belts, and spark plugs. If they’re not up to par, they’ll need to be replaced. Additionally, you’ll also need to replace your power steering fluid to keep your steering wheel working properly. You should also get the following done:

- **Timing belt replacement**

- **Replace hoses**

- **Replace spark plugs**

- **Rotate rotors or replace rotors**

- **Fuel system cleaning**

- **Complete inspection**

## [Century West BMW – Recommended service and maintenance schedule for BMW 3 Series](https://www.centurywestbmw.com/service/)

Your BMW 3 Series thrives on precision. A thoughtful, consistent maintenance plan keeps its TwinPower Turbo engines, xDrive components, and chassis systems performing the way Munich intended. At Century West BMW, our BMW M Certified technicians combine factory training, OEM diagnostics, and Genuine BMW Parts to deliver service that fits your model year and driving style. We read your vehicle’s Condition Based Service (CBS) data through iDrive, verify with a multi-point inspection, and then tailor a plan that protects performance, efficiency, and resale value—without recommending work you do not need. From oil and filter changes to brake fluid exchanges, tire services, alignments, and software updates, we complete work to BMW specifications and reset onboard service counters so your reminders stay accurate. Because Los Angeles traffic, short trips, and heat can accelerate wear, we also check cooling performance, battery health, and brake life at each visit. With online scheduling, clear recommendations, and quick turnaround, our team makes it simple to stay current. As a local resource serving North Hollywood, we are here to help you enjoy every mile in your 3 Series.

- **Every 10,000 miles or 12 months**: BMW Longlife oil and filter; inspect brakes and tires; top off fluids; road test.
- **Every 20,000 miles or 2 years**: Cabin microfilter replacement; brake fluid exchange; comprehensive multi-point inspection.
- **Every 30,000 miles**: Engine air filter; fuel system check; inspect PCV and induction plumbing.
- **Every 60,000 miles**: Spark plugs; coolant inspection and service as applicable; accessory belt check.
- **Every 75,000 to 90,000 miles**: Transmission and differential fluid service where applicable; cooling system service; suspension, steering, and alignment.
- **Every visit or seasonally**: Battery test; tire rotation if non-staggered; set pressures; wiper blades; software updates; visual leak check.

Use the general schedule above as a baseline, then adjust based on CBS alerts, mileage, and conditions. A few smart habits go a long way: set reminders for time-based items like brake fluid, rotate tires if your setup allows, align annually to safeguard run-flat tires and driver-assistance calibrations, and keep a simple maintenance log in your BMW App or glovebox. If your 3 Series is driven mainly in stop-and-go or on short trips, shorten intervals. If it tows, sees spirited canyon drives, track time, or uses staggered performance tires, ask our advisors for a customized plan. Intervals vary by engine, transmission, and model year—including plug-in hybrid variants—so always review your Owner’s Manual and BMW maintenance program, and contact the manufacturer or our service team for details. When you are ready, schedule service or request more information, and we will map out the right plan, provide clear next steps, and keep your BMW 3 Series feeling like The Ultimate Driving Machine.

# BMW SERVICE

BMW recommends you have your maintenance and repair work performed by an authorized BMW center.

# MAINTAINING YOUR BMW VEHICLE

A well-maintained vehicle will help safeguard its operational performance, road-safety and its reliability. This is why it is important to follow and perform BMW’s recommended periodic vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks as indicated by your vehicle’s Maintenance Service Display, along with the other maintenance work described in this booklet.

A improper maintenance is not covered under the BMW New Vehicle Damage, including consequential damage, which results from lack of or Limited Warranty for Passenger Cars and Light Trucks.

# MAINTENANCE INTERVALS

Maintenance intervals on motor vehicles were conventionally based solely on a fixed time period or a specified amount of accumulated driving mileage.

However, operational and driving conditions have a major influence on your vehicle’s routine maintenance requirements; the distance traveled is only one of these significant factors. A vehicle used for short trips in the city with numerous cold starts, prolonged periods of idling, stop-and-go driving, and high engine speeds during acceleration may require more frequent maintenance intervals than a vehicle that is driven long distances at moderate engine speeds.

Your BMW vehicle uses sensors and algorithms together with the elapsed time and the driving distance/profile to monitor and evaluate your vehicle’s maintenance service needs. This information is then used to adapt dynamically the parameters used to forecast the applicable maintenance service task intervals.

# THE BMW MAINTENANCE SYSTEM

All BMW vehicles are equipped with an integrated BMW Maintenance System. This maintenance “reminder” system helps ensure that the vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks are performed at the forecasted intervals that apply to your vehicle.

The BMW Maintenance System display provides the vehicle operator access to the current status information for the following maintenance service tasks:

$\\triangleright$ Engine oil (date and miles)\*

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle check (date and miles)

$\\triangleright$ Front brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Rear brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid (date)

$\\triangleright$ 1200 Mile running-in service (date and miles) (Applicable to BMW M vehicles only)\*

For each specific maintenance service task, either the future date (month/ year), remaining miles or both are provided as noted above. The system monitors variable inputs to forecast the intervals and alert the driver when one or more specific maintenance tasks should be performed.

NOTE: For certain vehicles, the status of the front and rear brake pads will only be observable in the maintenance system’s display when there are approximately 2,000 miles or less remaining before a brake service will be required to be performed.

For information about the vehicle’s maintenance system displays, please refer to the Maintenance Service Display Overview section beginning on page 5.

The following “combine with Engine oil”\* maintenance service tasks may be identified as needing to be performed with a specific occurrence of the “Engine oil” service task (service counter number):

$\\triangleright$ Cabin Microfilter(s)

$\\triangleright$ Engine air filter(s)\*

$\\triangleright$ Spark plugs\*

$\\triangleright$ Final drive oil (Applicable M vehicles only)

\\* Does not apply to BEV

Although these items do not appear in the BMW Maintenance System’s display in the vehicle, these services should be performed when your vehicle’s engine oil is changed in accordance with the interval identified by your vehicle’s BMW Maintenance System.

For more information on your vehicle’s maintenance services requirements, procedures and intervals, please refer the Maintenance Service Summary section beginning on page 10.

The BMW Maintenance System also includes an option to set service reminders for the following state-specific mandatory vehicle inspections, including:

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle safety inspection; and/or $\\triangleright$ Emissions test

The corresponding interval data for these inspections can be inputted into the BMW Maintenance System by a service provider; they are not determined by the vehicle.

For your convenience, you may also wish to have your authorized BMW center perform the work necessary to fulfill these state inspection requirements in your area concurrent with the maintenance services specified above when possible.

Should you request more frequent maintenance service than is indicated by the BMW Maintenance System during the coverage period, the cost of these services will not be covered by the BMW Maintenance Program.

# SERVICE DATA — REMOTE CONTROL KEY

Maintenance service task status information for your BMW vehicle is continually updated and stored in your remote control key.

Your authorized BMW center can access this data and consult with you about applicable service procedures and tasks for your vehicle.

Therefore, always provide your service consultant with the most recent remote control key that was used to operate the vehicle when servicing your vehicle at a BMW center.

# VEHICLE STORAGE

Disconnecting the battery during periods of long-term vehicle storage will interrupt the calculation of time-dependent maintenance services.

In this situation, BMW recommends that you have all your time-based maintenance services, such as brake fluid, engine oil and cabin microfilter, brought up to the correct date by an authorized BMW center.

# ENGINE OIL

2025 model year vehicles with internal-combustion engines are factory-filled with:

Z BMW-approved fully synthetic oil for gasoline engines

Engine oil should be changed when the vehicle’s engine is at operating temperature.

If an engine oil service is being performed or you need to add engine oil between changes, please refer to the Owner’s Manual for the recommended engine oil for your BMW vehicle.

# LONG-TERM RATED FLUIDS AND OILS

The following systems and assemblies are factory-filled with long-term rated fluid and oil; fluid replacement is only necessary when repairs are being performed (unless otherwise noted):

$\\triangleright$ Engine cooling system (antifreeze/coolant) $\\triangleright$ Automatic (except for X1 and X2) and manual transmissions $\\triangleright$ All-wheel drive transfer cases (except when indicated by the vehicle)

# REGULAR CHECKS — VEHICLE OPERATOR

In addition to the maintenance service procedure information contained in this booklet, BMW recommends that you regularly check (when refueling, for example), and address when necessary, the following items:

$\\triangleright$ Washer fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Coolant level

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Tires — pressure, condition and wear

Please refer to the Owner’s Manual for additional information.

Your [BMW 3 Series](https://www.bmwtigard.com/new-vehicles/3-series/) is a finely-crafted piece of machinery, but it will still require routine service from time to time. Keeping up with the BMW 3 Series [maintenance schedule](https://www.bmwtigard.com/service/service-and-parts-tips/bmw-recommended-maintenance-schedule/) is a must if you want your vehicle to perform at its best for as long as possible. We understand that keeping track of BMW 3 Series oil change intervals and more can be a challenge. That is why we have created this guide to the BMW 3 Series service schedule. Simply follow this guide, and your vehicle should be prepared and safe for the roads of Portland and Tigard.

[View 3 Series Inventory](https://www.bmwtigard.com/new-vehicles/3-series/) [Contact Us](https://www.bmwtigard.com/contact-us/)

## BMW 3 Series Service Schedule

The BMW 3 Series service schedule includes BMW 3 Series oil change intervals and more to help you track the maintenance your vehicle requires. Let’s break it down more in-depth below.

### Bi-Annual Services

The services listed below should be performed approximately 6 months after you take your new vehicle home, at the 5,000 to 10,000-mile mark. They should then be performed at least twice a year for the duration you own the vehicle.

- Oil and Filter Change
- Tire Rotation
- Brake Inspection

### Every 30,000 Miles

At the 30,000-mile mark in the BMW 3 Series maintenance schedule, you’ll want to head back to the shop for a variety of inspections and maintenance care checks.

- Air filter changes: Air filters get clogged over time, so at this point, they are no longer working at their best. If you travel in particularly dusty environments, you’ll want to change the filter approximately every 15,000 miles.
- Fuel filter inspection: Your technician can perform a pressure test to determine if the fuel filter needs replacement.

### Every 60,000 Miles

Your 60,000-mile maintenance service will happen at around four or five years into ownership for the average driver. Here is what it will include:

- Brake Rotor, Pads, and Shoes Inspections and Replacements
- Brake Fluid Replacement
- Coolant Replacement
- Transmission Fluid Replacement

Keep in mind that this is also around the time your battery will start wearing down, so it is a good idea to have it looked at and possibly replaced.

### Every 90,000 Miles

At this service interval, we will take care of inspecting hoses, belts, and spark plugs. Power steering fluid should also be replaced when we perform these tasks:

- Timing belt replacement
- Replace hoses
- Replace spark plugs
- Rotate rotors or replace rotors
- Fuel system cleaning
- Complete inspection

# BMW 3 Series Maintenance Schedule

![](https://dealerimages.dealereprocess.com/image/upload/3734739)

## Maintenance Schedule

Keeping up with your vehicle’s routine maintenance schedule is crucial to the health and longevity of your car. Routine maintenance services are done about once or twice a year, and are usually just a quick stop by the shop to change your oil and make sure everything is working properly.

**Here at BMW of Westchester we know how important it is to stay on top of these services in order to keep your car on the streets of Westchester County and Yonkers, NY, for years to come. Check out our breakdown of the BMW 3 Series maintenance schedule below!  [Schedule a service appointment](https://www.westchesterbmw.com/service-appointment/) for more assistance.**

## Annual Routine Maintenance Services

Your first[BMW 3 Series](https://www.westchesterbmw.com/search/new-bmw-3-series-white-plains-ny/?cy=10607&md=33&tp=new) routine maintenance service will happen about 6 months in, or once you hit around 5,000-10,000 miles, whichever happens to come first. This first service will be relatively quick. It will include:

- **An oil and filter change**

- **Tire rotation**

- **Brake inspection**


You’ll want to get these services done once or twice a year for the duration of the vehicle’s life.

Staying on top of your regular oil and oil filter changes is crucial to your car’s health because as your engine runs, tiny bits of dirt and dust will build up in it, which can cause excessive wear and tear.

**Additionally, yearly [tire rotations](https://www.westchesterbmw.com/service-appointment/) are important to maintain traction control, because they prevent your wheels from having uneven tread. Tread and traction control helps your vehicle stop quicker, and provides you with safer travels over rough terrain.**

![](https://dealerimages.dealereprocess.com/image/upload/3734763)

![](https://dealerimages.dealereprocess.com/image/upload/3734769)

## 30,000-Mile Maintenance Services

Once your BMW 3 Series hits 30,000 miles, it’s time to head back to the shop for a variety of inspections and maintenance care checks. To start, you’re going to need:

- **Your air filter changed, over time your air filter can become clogged, and a replacement will be needed in order for it to work at its best. If you travel in particularly dusty environments, you’ll want this changed around 15,000 miles rather than 30,000.**

- **Next, you’ll need your fuel filter inspected; your technician can perform a pressure test to determine if you’ll need it replaced.**


## 60,000-Mile Maintenance Services

Your 60,000-mile maintenance service will happen at around four or five years into ownership for the average driver. At this service, you’ll need:

- **Brake Rotor, Pads, and Shoes Inspections and Replacements**

- **Brake Fluid Replacement**

- **Coolant Replacement**

- **Transmission Fluid Replacement**

- **Your BMW 3 Series battery and brakes will start to wear out around the 60,000-mile mark, which is why it’s so important to get them inspected, and possibly replaced.**


![](https://dealerimages.dealereprocess.com/image/upload/3734756)

![](https://dealerimages.dealereprocess.com/image/upload/3734759)

## 90,000-Mile Maintenance Services

Your 90,000-mile maintenance check will include an inspection of your hoses, belts, and spark plugs. If they’re not up to par, they’ll need to be replaced. Additionally, you’ll also need to replace your power steering fluid to keep your steering wheel working properly. You should also get the following done:

- **Timing belt replacement**

- **Replace hoses**

- **Replace spark plugs**

- **Rotate rotors or replace rotors**

- **Fuel system cleaning**

- **Complete inspection**


## Stop by for Your Next Maintenance Service!

Staying on top of your routine maintenance services is imperative to your vehicle’s health, and will help you get the most out of it. Here at BMW of Westchester we’re dedicated to providing the drivers of Westchester County and Yonkers, NY, with high quality service every time they come in. Call or stop by to schedule your next appointment!

# BMW SERVICE

BMW recommends you have your maintenance and repair work performed by an authorized BMW center.

# MAINTAINING YOUR BMW VEHICLE

A well-maintained vehicle will help safeguard its operational performance, road-safety and its reliability. This is why it is important to follow and perform BMW’s recommended periodic vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks as indicated by your vehicle’s Maintenance Service Display, along with the other maintenance work described in this booklet.

A improper maintenance is not covered under the BMW New Vehicle Damage, including consequential damage, which results from lack of or Limited Warranty for Passenger Cars and Light Trucks.

# MAINTENANCE INTERVALS

Maintenance intervals on motor vehicles were conventionally based solely on a fixed time period or a specified amount of accumulated driving mileage.

However, operational and driving conditions have a major influence on your vehicle’s routine maintenance requirements; the distance traveled is only one of these significant factors. A vehicle used for short trips in the city with numerous cold starts, prolonged periods of idling, stop-and-go driving, and high engine speeds during acceleration may require more frequent maintenance intervals than a vehicle that is driven long distances at moderate engine speeds.

Your BMW vehicle uses sensors and algorithms together with the elapsed time and the driving distance/profile to monitor and evaluate your vehicle’s maintenance service needs. This information is then used to adapt dynamically the parameters used to forecast the applicable maintenance service task intervals.

# THE BMW MAINTENANCE SYSTEM

All BMW vehicles are equipped with an integrated BMW Maintenance System. This maintenance “reminder” system helps ensure that the vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks are performed at the forecasted intervals that apply to your vehicle.

The BMW Maintenance System display provides the vehicle operator access to the current status information for the following maintenance service tasks:

$\\triangleright$ Engine oil (date and miles)\*

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle check (date and miles)

$\\triangleright$ Front brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Rear brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid (date)

$\\triangleright$ 1200 Mile running-in service (date and miles) (Applicable to BMW M vehicles only)\*

For each specific maintenance service task, either the future date (month/ year), remaining miles or both are provided as noted above. The system monitors variable inputs to forecast the intervals and alert the driver when one or more specific maintenance tasks should be performed.

NOTE: For certain vehicles, the status of the front and rear brake pads will only be observable in the maintenance system’s display when there are approximately 2,000 miles or less remaining before a brake service will be required to be performed.

For information about the vehicle’s maintenance system displays, please refer to the Maintenance Service Display Overview section beginning on page 5.

The following “combine with Engine oil”\* maintenance service tasks may be identified as needing to be performed with a specific occurrence of the “Engine oil” service task (service counter number):

$\\triangleright$ Cabin Microfilter(s)

$\\triangleright$ Engine air filter(s)\*

$\\triangleright$ Spark plugs\*

$\\triangleright$ Final drive oil (Applicable M vehicles only)

\\* Does not apply to BEV

Although these items do not appear in the BMW Maintenance System’s display in the vehicle, these services should be performed when your vehicle’s engine oil is changed in accordance with the interval identified by your vehicle’s BMW Maintenance System.

For more information on your vehicle’s maintenance services requirements, procedures and intervals, please refer the Maintenance Service Summary section beginning on page 10.

The BMW Maintenance System also includes an option to set service reminders for the following state-specific mandatory vehicle inspections, including:

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle safety inspection; and/or $\\triangleright$ Emissions test

The corresponding interval data for these inspections can be inputted into the BMW Maintenance System by a service provider; they are not determined by the vehicle.

For your convenience, you may also wish to have your authorized BMW center perform the work necessary to fulfill these state inspection requirements in your area concurrent with the maintenance services specified above when possible.

Should you request more frequent maintenance service than is indicated by the BMW Maintenance System during the coverage period, the cost of these services will not be covered by the BMW Maintenance Program.

# SERVICE DATA — REMOTE CONTROL KEY

Maintenance service task status information for your BMW vehicle is continually updated and stored in your remote control key.

Your authorized BMW center can access this data and consult with you about applicable service procedures and tasks for your vehicle.

Therefore, always provide your service consultant with the most recent remote control key that was used to operate the vehicle when servicing your vehicle at a BMW center.

# VEHICLE STORAGE

Disconnecting the battery during periods of long-term vehicle storage will interrupt the calculation of time-dependent maintenance services.

In this situation, BMW recommends that you have all your time-based maintenance services, such as brake fluid, engine oil and cabin microfilter, brought up to the correct date by an authorized BMW center.

# ENGINE OIL

2025 model year vehicles with internal-combustion engines are factory-filled with:

Z BMW-approved fully synthetic oil for gasoline engines

Engine oil should be changed when the vehicle’s engine is at operating temperature.

If an engine oil service is being performed or you need to add engine oil between changes, please refer to the Owner’s Manual for the recommended engine oil for your BMW vehicle.

# LONG-TERM RATED FLUIDS AND OILS

The following systems and assemblies are factory-filled with long-term rated fluid and oil; fluid replacement is only necessary when repairs are being performed (unless otherwise noted):

$\\triangleright$ Engine cooling system (antifreeze/coolant) $\\triangleright$ Automatic (except for X1 and X2) and manual transmissions $\\triangleright$ All-wheel drive transfer cases (except when indicated by the vehicle)

# REGULAR CHECKS — VEHICLE OPERATOR

In addition to the maintenance service procedure information contained in this booklet, BMW recommends that you regularly check (when refueling, for example), and address when necessary, the following items:

$\\triangleright$ Washer fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Coolant level

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Tires — pressure, condition and wear

Please refer to the Owner’s Manual for additional information.

## Keep Your BMW 2 Series Performing at it's Best

**Basic BMW 2-Series Preventative Maintenance: Every 5,000 Miles**

BMW’s maintenance schedule is built around a standard 5,000-mile interval, guided by your vehicle’s pre-installed Condition-Based Service (CBS) monitor. This intelligent system tracks critical areas of your car and alerts you when additional services are needed.

The regular BMW recommended maintenance schedule includes the following:

- Vehicle check and inspection
- Engine oil check
- Coolant check
- Tire rotation
- Brake fluid check
- Front and rear brake inspection
- Inspection of the engine and cabin air filters
- Wiper blade inspection
- Standard scope

Not every part inspected will need replacement during your visit. Our BMW-certified maintenance experts use the CBS monitor to identify exactly what requires attention, ensuring precise and efficient service.

**BMW 2-Series Recommended Maintenance Services**

Maintenance needs can vary depending on your model and driving habits. For tailored recommendations, consult your owner’s manual or speak with one of our knowledgeable service advisors. Below is a general guideline for BMW 2 Series maintenance milestones:

**BMW 2-Series 10,000-Mile Maintenance**

- Inspect and replace the oil filters
- Repeat every 20,000 miles

**BMW 2-Series 30,000-Mile Maintenance**

- Replace brake fluid. After the first service, schedule brake fluid replacement every 60,000 miles.

**BMW 2-Series 60,000-mile maintenance**

- Replace the engine air filter and spark plugs
- Inspect and replace brake pads and rotors as needed

**BMW 2-Series 90,000-Mile Maintenance**

- Replace the timing belt and hoses
- Repeat every 90,000 miles

BMW recommends you have your maintenance and repair work performed by an authorized BMW center.

# MAINTAINING YOUR BMW VEHICLE

A well-maintained vehicle will help safeguard its operational performance, road-safety and its reliability. This is why it is important to follow and perform BMW’s recommended periodic vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks as indicated by your vehicle’s Maintenance Service Display, along with the other maintenance work described in this booklet.

A improper maintenance is not covered under the BMW New Vehicle Damage, including consequential damage, which results from lack of or Limited Warranty for Passenger Cars and Light Trucks.

# MAINTENANCE INTERVALS

Maintenance intervals on motor vehicles were conventionally based solely on a fixed time period or a specified amount of accumulated driving mileage.

However, operational and driving conditions have a major influence on your vehicle’s routine maintenance requirements; the distance traveled is only one of these significant factors. A vehicle used for short trips in the city with numerous cold starts, prolonged periods of idling, stop-and-go driving, and high engine speeds during acceleration may require more frequent maintenance intervals than a vehicle that is driven long distances at moderate engine speeds.

Your BMW vehicle uses sensors and algorithms together with the elapsed time and the driving distance/profile to monitor and evaluate your vehicle’s maintenance service needs. This information is then used to adapt dynamically the parameters used to forecast the applicable maintenance service task intervals.

# THE BMW MAINTENANCE SYSTEM

All BMW vehicles are equipped with an integrated BMW Maintenance System. This maintenance “reminder” system helps ensure that the vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks are performed at the forecasted intervals that apply to your vehicle.

The BMW Maintenance System display provides the vehicle operator access to the current status information for the following maintenance service tasks:

$\\triangleright$ Engine oil (date and miles)\*

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle check (date and miles)

$\\triangleright$ Front brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Rear brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid (date)

$\\triangleright$ 1200 Mile running-in service (date and miles) (Applicable to BMW M vehicles only)\*

For each specific maintenance service task, either the future date (month/ year), remaining miles or both are provided as noted above. The system monitors variable inputs to forecast the intervals and alert the driver when one or more specific maintenance tasks should be performed.

NOTE: For certain vehicles, the status of the front and rear brake pads will only be observable in the maintenance system’s display when there are approximately 2,000 miles or less remaining before a brake service will be required to be performed.

For information about the vehicle’s maintenance system displays, please refer to the Maintenance Service Display Overview section beginning on page 5.

The following “combine with Engine oil”\* maintenance service tasks may be identified as needing to be performed with a specific occurrence of the “Engine oil” service task (service counter number):

$\\triangleright$ Cabin Microfilter(s)

$\\triangleright$ Engine air filter(s)\*

$\\triangleright$ Spark plugs\*

$\\triangleright$ Final drive oil (Applicable M vehicles only)

\\* Does not apply to BEV

Although these items do not appear in the BMW Maintenance System’s display in the vehicle, these services should be performed when your vehicle’s engine oil is changed in accordance with the interval identified by your vehicle’s BMW Maintenance System.

For more information on your vehicle’s maintenance services requirements, procedures and intervals, please refer the Maintenance Service Summary section beginning on page 10.

The BMW Maintenance System also includes an option to set service reminders for the following state-specific mandatory vehicle inspections, including:

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle safety inspection; and/or $\\triangleright$ Emissions test

The corresponding interval data for these inspections can be inputted into the BMW Maintenance System by a service provider; they are not determined by the vehicle.

For your convenience, you may also wish to have your authorized BMW center perform the work necessary to fulfill these state inspection requirements in your area concurrent with the maintenance services specified above when possible.

Should you request more frequent maintenance service than is indicated by the BMW Maintenance System during the coverage period, the cost of these services will not be covered by the BMW Maintenance Program.

# SERVICE DATA — REMOTE CONTROL KEY

Maintenance service task status information for your BMW vehicle is continually updated and stored in your remote control key.

Your authorized BMW center can access this data and consult with you about applicable service procedures and tasks for your vehicle.

Therefore, always provide your service consultant with the most recent remote control key that was used to operate the vehicle when servicing your vehicle at a BMW center.

# VEHICLE STORAGE

Disconnecting the battery during periods of long-term vehicle storage will interrupt the calculation of time-dependent maintenance services.

In this situation, BMW recommends that you have all your time-based maintenance services, such as brake fluid, engine oil and cabin microfilter, brought up to the correct date by an authorized BMW center.

# ENGINE OIL

2025 model year vehicles with internal-combustion engines are factory-filled with:

Z BMW-approved fully synthetic oil for gasoline engines

Engine oil should be changed when the vehicle’s engine is at operating temperature.

If an engine oil service is being performed or you need to add engine oil between changes, please refer to the Owner’s Manual for the recommended engine oil for your BMW vehicle.

# LONG-TERM RATED FLUIDS AND OILS

The following systems and assemblies are factory-filled with long-term rated fluid and oil; fluid replacement is only necessary when repairs are being performed (unless otherwise noted):

$\\triangleright$ Engine cooling system (antifreeze/coolant) $\\triangleright$ Automatic (except for X1 and X2) and manual transmissions $\\triangleright$ All-wheel drive transfer cases (except when indicated by the vehicle)

# REGULAR CHECKS — VEHICLE OPERATOR

In addition to the maintenance service procedure information contained in this booklet, BMW recommends that you regularly check (when refueling, for example), and address when necessary, the following items:

$\\triangleright$ Washer fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Coolant level

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Tires — pressure, condition and wear

Please refer to the Owner’s Manual for additional information.

## Keep Your BMW 2 Series Performing at it's Best

**Basic BMW 2-Series Preventative Maintenance: Every 5,000 Miles**

BMW’s maintenance schedule is built around a standard 5,000-mile interval, guided by your vehicle’s pre-installed Condition-Based Service (CBS) monitor. This intelligent system tracks critical areas of your car and alerts you when additional services are needed.

The regular BMW recommended maintenance schedule includes the following:

- Vehicle check and inspection
- Engine oil check
- Coolant check
- Tire rotation
- Brake fluid check
- Front and rear brake inspection
- Inspection of the engine and cabin air filters
- Wiper blade inspection
- Standard scope

Not every part inspected will need replacement during your visit. Our BMW-certified maintenance experts use the CBS monitor to identify exactly what requires attention, ensuring precise and efficient service.

**BMW 2-Series Recommended Maintenance Services**

Maintenance needs can vary depending on your model and driving habits. For tailored recommendations, consult your owner’s manual or speak with one of our knowledgeable service advisors. Below is a general guideline for BMW 2 Series maintenance milestones:

**BMW 2-Series 10,000-Mile Maintenance**

- Replace the engine oil, oil filter and coolant
- Repeat every 10,000 miles

**BMW 2-Series 20,000-Mile Maintenance**

- Inspect and replace the oil filters
- Repeat every 20,000 miles

**BMW 2-Series 30,000-Mile Maintenance**

- Replace brake fluid. After the first service, schedule brake fluid replacement every 60,000 miles.
- If equipped with a manual transmission, replace transmission fluid every 30,000 miles.

**BMW 2-Series 60,000-mile maintenance**

- Replace the engine air filter and spark plugs
- Inspect and replace brake pads and rotors as needed
- For automatic transmissions, replace the transmission fluid every 60,000 miles.

**BMW 2-Series 90,000-Mile Maintenance**

- Replace the timing belt and hoses
- Repeat every 90,000 miles

**BMW 2-Series Maintenance after 90,000 Miles**

Continue following the BMW 2 Series maintenance schedule with 5,000-mile intervals and adhere to service milestones as listed above to ensure optimal performance.

![mechanic writing on clipboard](https://di-uploads-pod24.dealerinspire.com/bmwofturnersville/uploads/2020/08/maintenance.jpg)

## Why Is Following the BMW Maintenance Schedule Important?

Your BMW is engineered for precision, performance, and longevity, but even the best vehicles need routine care. By sticking to your factory-recommended BMW Maintenance Schedule, you protect your investment, improve fuel efficiency, and avoid costly repairs. At BMW of Turnersville, we help you follow the right service timeline based on your model, mileage, and driving style.

[Schedule BMW Service](https://www.bmwofturnersville.com/scheduleservice/) [BMW Maintenance Coupons](https://www.bmwofturnersville.com/service/service-specials/)

## BMW Preventative Maintenance: Every 5,000 Miles

The current BMW maintenance schedule is based on a standard 5,000-mile interval, although a Condition Based Service monitor will track key areas and [alert you](https://www.bmwofturnersville.com/service/service-tips/bmw-warning-lights/) if other services are required. **Routine BMW recommended maintenance includes:**

- Vehicle check and inspection
- Brake fluid check
- Coolant check
- Engine oil check
- Front and rear brake inspection
- Inspection of engine and cabin air filters
- Standard scope
- Wiper blade inspection
- [Tire rotation](https://www.bmwofturnersville.com/service/service-tips/how-often-should-you-rotate-your-tires/)

Not all checked components will be replaced during your visit. With assistance from your Condition-Based Service monitor, our trained and certified BMW maintenance experts will be able to determine exactly what needs to be replaced, and when.

## What Does the BMW Maintenance Schedule Include?

BMW maintenance is broken down into intervals, based on time or mileage. Below are general service milestones for most BMW models:

### BMW 10,000-Mile Maintenance

- At 10,000 miles or 12 months, schedule an oil change, brake inspection, and tire rotation.

### BMW 20,000-Mile Maintenance

- At 20,000 miles, replace the cabin air filter and perform a more comprehensive inspection.

### BMW 30,000-Mile Maintenance

- At 30,000-40,000 miles, inspect suspension, steering components, coolant, and belts.
- If manual transmission: replace [transmission fluid](https://www.bmwofturnersville.com/service/service-tips/check-your-transmission-fluid/) every 30,000 miles

### BMW 60,000-Mile Maintenance

- At 60,000 miles, flush and replace brake fluid, inspect spark plugs, and change the engine air filter.

### Additional BMW Maintenance

Every two years, replace the cabin microfilter and test battery performance.

Additional services like coolant flushes, differential fluid replacement, or transmission service may vary depending on your BMW model and driving habits.

# BMW SERVICE

BMW recommends you have your maintenance and repair work performed by an authorized BMW center.

# MAINTAINING YOUR BMW VEHICLE

A well-maintained vehicle will help safeguard its operational performance, road-safety and its reliability. This is why it is important to follow and perform BMW’s recommended periodic vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks as indicated by your vehicle’s Maintenance Service Display, along with the other maintenance work described in this booklet.

A improper maintenance is not covered under the BMW New Vehicle Damage, including consequential damage, which results from lack of or Limited Warranty for Passenger Cars and Light Trucks.

# MAINTENANCE INTERVALS

Maintenance intervals on motor vehicles were conventionally based solely on a fixed time period or a specified amount of accumulated driving mileage.

However, operational and driving conditions have a major influence on your vehicle’s routine maintenance requirements; the distance traveled is only one of these significant factors. A vehicle used for short trips in the city with numerous cold starts, prolonged periods of idling, stop-and-go driving, and high engine speeds during acceleration may require more frequent maintenance intervals than a vehicle that is driven long distances at moderate engine speeds.

Your BMW vehicle uses sensors and algorithms together with the elapsed time and the driving distance/profile to monitor and evaluate your vehicle’s maintenance service needs. This information is then used to adapt dynamically the parameters used to forecast the applicable maintenance service task intervals.

# THE BMW MAINTENANCE SYSTEM

All BMW vehicles are equipped with an integrated BMW Maintenance System. This maintenance “reminder” system helps ensure that the vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks are performed at the forecasted intervals that apply to your vehicle.

The BMW Maintenance System display provides the vehicle operator access to the current status information for the following maintenance service tasks:

$\\triangleright$ Engine oil (date and miles)\*

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle check (date and miles)

$\\triangleright$ Front brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Rear brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid (date)

$\\triangleright$ 1200 Mile running-in service (date and miles) (Applicable to BMW M vehicles only)\*

For each specific maintenance service task, either the future date (month/ year), remaining miles or both are provided as noted above. The system monitors variable inputs to forecast the intervals and alert the driver when one or more specific maintenance tasks should be performed.

NOTE: For certain vehicles, the status of the front and rear brake pads will only be observable in the maintenance system’s display when there are approximately 2,000 miles or less remaining before a brake service will be required to be performed.

For information about the vehicle’s maintenance system displays, please refer to the Maintenance Service Display Overview section beginning on page 5.

The following “combine with Engine oil”\* maintenance service tasks may be identified as needing to be performed with a specific occurrence of the “Engine oil” service task (service counter number):

$\\triangleright$ Cabin Microfilter(s)

$\\triangleright$ Engine air filter(s)\*

$\\triangleright$ Spark plugs\*

$\\triangleright$ Final drive oil (Applicable M vehicles only)

\\* Does not apply to BEV

Although these items do not appear in the BMW Maintenance System’s display in the vehicle, these services should be performed when your vehicle’s engine oil is changed in accordance with the interval identified by your vehicle’s BMW Maintenance System.

For more information on your vehicle’s maintenance services requirements, procedures and intervals, please refer the Maintenance Service Summary section beginning on page 10.

The BMW Maintenance System also includes an option to set service reminders for the following state-specific mandatory vehicle inspections, including:

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle safety inspection; and/or $\\triangleright$ Emissions test

The corresponding interval data for these inspections can be inputted into the BMW Maintenance System by a service provider; they are not determined by the vehicle.

For your convenience, you may also wish to have your authorized BMW center perform the work necessary to fulfill these state inspection requirements in your area concurrent with the maintenance services specified above when possible.

Should you request more frequent maintenance service than is indicated by the BMW Maintenance System during the coverage period, the cost of these services will not be covered by the BMW Maintenance Program.

# SERVICE DATA — REMOTE CONTROL KEY

Maintenance service task status information for your BMW vehicle is continually updated and stored in your remote control key.

Your authorized BMW center can access this data and consult with you about applicable service procedures and tasks for your vehicle.

Therefore, always provide your service consultant with the most recent remote control key that was used to operate the vehicle when servicing your vehicle at a BMW center.

# VEHICLE STORAGE

Disconnecting the battery during periods of long-term vehicle storage will interrupt the calculation of time-dependent maintenance services.

In this situation, BMW recommends that you have all your time-based maintenance services, such as brake fluid, engine oil and cabin microfilter, brought up to the correct date by an authorized BMW center.

# ENGINE OIL

2025 model year vehicles with internal-combustion engines are factory-filled with:

Z BMW-approved fully synthetic oil for gasoline engines

Engine oil should be changed when the vehicle’s engine is at operating temperature.

If an engine oil service is being performed or you need to add engine oil between changes, please refer to the Owner’s Manual for the recommended engine oil for your BMW vehicle.

# LONG-TERM RATED FLUIDS AND OILS

The following systems and assemblies are factory-filled with long-term rated fluid and oil; fluid replacement is only necessary when repairs are being performed (unless otherwise noted):

$\\triangleright$ Engine cooling system (antifreeze/coolant) $\\triangleright$ Automatic (except for X1 and X2) and manual transmissions $\\triangleright$ All-wheel drive transfer cases (except when indicated by the vehicle)

# REGULAR CHECKS — VEHICLE OPERATOR

In addition to the maintenance service procedure information contained in this booklet, BMW recommends that you regularly check (when refueling, for example), and address when necessary, the following items:

$\\triangleright$ Washer fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Coolant level

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Tires — pressure, condition and wear

Please refer to the Owner’s Manual for additional information.

## Keep Your BMW 2 Series Performing at it's Best

**Basic BMW 2-Series Preventative Maintenance: Every 5,000 Miles**

BMW’s maintenance schedule is built around a standard 5,000-mile interval, guided by your vehicle’s pre-installed Condition-Based Service (CBS) monitor. This intelligent system tracks critical areas of your car and alerts you when additional services are needed.

The regular BMW recommended maintenance schedule includes the following:

- Vehicle check and inspection
- Engine oil check
- Coolant check
- Tire rotation
- Brake fluid check
- Front and rear brake inspection
- Inspection of the engine and cabin air filters
- Wiper blade inspection
- Standard scope

Not every part inspected will need replacement during your visit. Our BMW-certified maintenance experts use the CBS monitor to identify exactly what requires attention, ensuring precise and efficient service.

**BMW 2-Series Recommended Maintenance Services**

Maintenance needs can vary depending on your model and driving habits. For tailored recommendations, consult your owner’s manual or speak with one of our knowledgeable service advisors. Below is a general guideline for BMW 2 Series maintenance milestones:

**BMW 2-Series 10,000-Mile Maintenance**

- Replace the engine oil, oil filter and coolant
- Repeat every 10,000 miles

**BMW 2-Series 20,000-Mile Maintenance**

- Inspect and replace the oil filters
- Repeat every 20,000 miles

**BMW 2-Series 30,000-Mile Maintenance**

- Replace brake fluid. After the first service, schedule brake fluid replacement every 60,000 miles.
- If equipped with a manual transmission, replace transmission fluid every 30,000 miles.

**BMW 2-Series 60,000-mile maintenance**

- Replace the engine air filter and spark plugs
- Inspect and replace brake pads and rotors as needed
- For automatic transmissions, replace the transmission fluid every 60,000 miles.

**BMW 2-Series 90,000-Mile Maintenance**

- Replace the timing belt and hoses
- Repeat every 90,000 miles

**BMW 2-Series Maintenance after 90,000 Miles**

Continue following the BMW 2 Series maintenance schedule with 5,000-mile intervals and adhere to service milestones as listed above to ensure optimal performance.

## 2025 FORD ESCAPE MAINTENANCE SCHEDULE

The 2025 Ford Escape is a compact SUV offering a sleek design, robust performance, and advanced technology. Known for its comfortable interior and modern features, it’s built to meet the demands of an active lifestyle. Available at the Star Valley Ford dealer, the Escape comes equipped with Ford’s Sync 4 infotainment system, which includes wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, enhancing convenience and connectivity. Safety is also a major focus, with an array of advanced features designed to protect the driver and passengers.

To ensure your 2025 Ford Escape delivers optimal performance and remains reliable over time, it’s essential to adhere to a regular maintenance schedule. Following Ford’s recommended service intervals will keep your SUV running smoothly and extend its life. You can consult your vehicle’s owner’s manual for specific details, but below is an overview of key maintenance milestones for the 2025 Ford Escape. For more information, contact the experts at Winslow Ford, the Star Valley Ford dealership.

[SCHEDULE SERVICE](https://www.winslowford.com/serviceappmt.aspx)

[SERVICE SPECIALS](https://www.winslowford.com/service-parts-specials.aspx)

[CONTACT US](https://www.winslowford.com/contactus.aspx)

[MODEL OVERVIEW](https://www.winslowford.com/2025-ford-escape-overview)

[TRIM LEVELS](https://www.winslowford.com/2025-ford-escape-trim-levels)

[CALL US : 928-406-0044](tel:9284060044)

![2025 Ford Escape Red](https://www.winslowford.com/static/brand-ford/vehicle/2025/Ford/Escape/Hero/01.jpg)

### 10,000 Miles

At the 10,000-mile mark, your Ford Escape will need its first scheduled maintenance visit. This includes an oil change and a new oil filter to ensure your engine stays lubricated and runs efficiently. Additionally, the tires will be rotated to promote even wear, which helps extend their lifespan. The technicians will also inspect critical systems, such as the brakes, cooling system, and exhaust system, to identify any signs of wear or issues. Checking components like the steering linkage, suspension joints, and drive shafts will help ensure your Escape continues to handle smoothly and safely.

### 20,000 Miles

When your Escape reaches 20,000 miles, the same services from the 10,000-mile check will be performed again. However, at this interval, there’s an added focus on air quality inside the cabin. The cabin air filter will be replaced to maintain fresh, clean air for all passengers. Over time, this filter can become clogged with dust and debris, so replacing it ensures the interior air remains free of pollutants and allergens.

### 30,000 Miles

At 30,000 miles, your Ford Escape will undergo another round of essential checks and services. In addition to the routine oil change, tire rotation, and inspection of key systems, the engine air filter will be replaced. This filter keeps dirt and contaminants from entering the engine, which could otherwise reduce its efficiency or cause mechanical issues.

### 100,000 Miles

A more comprehensive maintenance service is required once your Escape reaches the 100,000-mile mark. At this stage, technicians will replace the spark plugs, which are essential for efficient engine combustion. Worn-out spark plugs can reduce engine performance and fuel efficiency. The coolant will also be replaced, and the accessory drive belt will be inspected to ensure it’s in good condition.

### 150,000 Miles

At 150,000 miles, your Ford Escape will undergo an extensive service to address critical components contributing to the vehicle’s long-term reliability. The accessory drive belt and the timing belt will be replaced if it hasn’t been done previously. Changing the automatic transmission fluid is also necessary at this stage, ensuring smooth gear shifts and preventing transmission issues over time.

Regular maintenance is critical to getting the most out of your 2025 Ford Escape. If you have questions about your vehicle’s service schedule or need to book an appointment, contact the Winslow Ford Service Center. Our certified technicians are here to help with all your maintenance needs.

# The Ultimate Guide to Ford’s Oil Change Intervals and Maintenance

May 22nd, 2025 by[walong@modernauto.com](https://www.modernfordofboone.com/author/walongmodernauto-com/ "Posts by walong@modernauto.com")

### The Ultimate Guide to Ford’s Oil Change Intervals and Maintenance

Maintaining your Ford vehicle is crucial to ensure its longevity and performance. One of the most essential aspects of vehicle maintenance is regular oil changes. This guide will explore Ford’s recommended oil change intervals, the importance of timely oil changes, and how to determine the best schedule for your vehicle. We’ll also provide insights into the benefits of using Ford’s Intelligent Oil-Life Monitor (IOLM) system and how it can assist you in keeping your vehicle in top shape. Whether you’re in Boone, Hickory, or Wilkesboro, understanding these key maintenance practices will help you keep your Ford running smoothly.

## Ford’s Recommended Oil Change Intervals

Ford recommends changing your vehicle’s oil every 7,500 miles or six months, whichever comes first. This general guideline ensures that your engine remains well-lubricated and free from contaminants. However, depending on your specific model and driving conditions, this interval may vary. For instance, newer Ford models equipped with the **Intelligent Oil-Life Monitor (IOLM)** system can calculate the optimal oil change interval based on real-time data, including mileage, speed, temperature, and driving habits. This advanced system allows you to extend the time between oil changes without compromising engine health.

For older Ford models or those without the IOLM, you might need to adhere to a more traditional schedule of every 3,000 to 5,000 miles, especially if your driving conditions are severe. Severe conditions include frequent short trips, towing heavy loads, or driving in extremely hot or cold weather. Always consult your vehicle’s owner’s manual for specific maintenance recommendations tailored to your model.

If you’re uncertain about the best oil change interval for your Ford, consider visiting the **[Service Department at Modern Ford of Boone](https://api.connectcdk.com/api/nc-cosa-consumer-ui/v1/?subscriptionId=&cid=2000096)**. Our experienced technicians can provide personalized advice based on your vehicle’s needs and your driving habits.

## Factors Influencing Oil Change Frequency

Several factors can influence how often you should change your oil. Understanding these can help you maintain your Ford vehicle more effectively:

- **Driving Habits**: If you frequently drive in stop-and-go traffic, tow heavy loads, or take short trips, your engine may accumulate contaminants faster, necessitating more frequent oil changes.
- **Engine Type**: Different engines have varying requirements. For example, turbocharged engines might require more frequent oil changes due to higher operating temperatures.
- **Oil Type**: Using **synthetic oil** can extend the time between oil changes compared to conventional oil. Synthetic oils are designed to last longer and withstand extreme temperatures better.

For drivers in areas like Lenoir or Morganton, where the terrain might involve more hills and curves, these factors become even more critical. Always ensure that your oil type matches your driving conditions and engine specifications for optimal performance.

## The Importance of Regular Oil Changes

Regular oil changes are vital for maintaining your engine’s health. Oil lubricates engine components, reduces friction, and helps manage heat. Over time, oil degrades and becomes contaminated with particles and debris, which can lead to engine wear and reduced performance. Failing to change your oil regularly can result in:

- **Engine Overheating**: Dirty oil can’t effectively dissipate heat, leading to overheating.
- **Increased Friction**: Without proper lubrication, engine parts can wear down more quickly.
- **Reduced Fuel Efficiency**: A well-lubricated engine runs more efficiently, saving you money at the pump.

In regions like Wilkesboro or Ashe County, where temperatures can vary significantly, maintaining clean oil is crucial for adapting to changing conditions. If you notice signs like a knocking engine or the oil change light illuminating, it’s time to schedule an oil change.

## Mileage vs. Time: What Matters More?

When considering oil change intervals, both mileage and time are important. Oil degrades over time due to oxidation and the breakdown of additives, even if the vehicle isn’t driven frequently. Conversely, higher mileage means more exposure to contaminants. Therefore, you should follow the interval that comes first, whether it’s mileage or time.

For example, if your Ford’s manual recommends an oil change every 5,000 miles or six months, change the oil if you reach either milestone. This approach ensures that your engine remains protected, regardless of driving frequency. For vehicles using synthetic oil, the interval might extend up to 15,000 miles, but always verify with your owner’s manual.

Residents in Boone or Blowing Rock, who may use their vehicles less frequently due to work-from-home arrangements or seasonal use, should still adhere to the time-based interval to prevent oil degradation.

## Maximizing Your Ford’s Longevity with the IOLM

The **Intelligent Oil-Life Monitor (IOLM)** is a feature in many newer Ford models that takes the guesswork out of oil changes. By analyzing your driving conditions and habits, the IOLM provides accurate recommendations for when to change your oil. This system helps you avoid unnecessary changes while ensuring your engine is protected.

For example, if you frequently drive in mountainous areas like Boone or Hickory, the IOLM will account for the increased engine strain and adjust the oil change interval accordingly. This tailored approach not only saves you time and money but also enhances your vehicle’s performance and longevity.

If you’re interested in learning more about how the IOLM works or need assistance with your vehicle, contact the **[Service Department at Modern Ford of Boone](https://api.connectcdk.com/api/nc-cosa-consumer-ui/v1/?subscriptionId=&cid=2000096)** for expert guidance.

# What is the VW Atlas Maintenance Schedule?

![2023 Volkswagen Atlas](https://dealerinspire-image-library-prod.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/images/qnoccVlqnYXcpKsMLB8poK6c7eWZdnzOFdm2DLEX.jpg)

* * *

Following your VW Atlas maintenance schedule is essential to keeping it in top condition on Tysons Corner roads for years to come. If you don’t know the VW Atlas service schedule, don’t worry. Stohlman Volkswagen is here to help. Below, you’ll find detailed information on the VW Atlas service intervals, including when to get a VW Atlas oil change. If you have questions about the VW Atlas service schedule, don’t hesitate to contact us. And, when it comes time for VW Atlas routine maintenance, you can easily [schedule an appointment](https://www.stohlman-vw.com/online-service-scheduler/) with us online.

[Service Department](https://www.stohlman-vw.com/department-fod33-1906/) [VW Maintenance Menu](https://www.stohlman-vw.com/maintenance-menu/)

* * *

## VW Atlas Service Schedule

## 10,000 Miles or One Year

The base of your VW Atlas service schedule will consist of the following maintenance tasks:

- Inspect the Brake Pads
- VW Atlas Oil Change
- New Oil Filter
- Service Interval Display Rest (if needed)

## 20,000 Miles or Two Years

# 2024 Volkswagen Atlas Maintenance Schedule

![hero image](https://dealerimages.dealereprocess.com/image/upload/3416655)

# 2024 Volkswagen Atlas Maintenance Schedule

Regular maintenance is vital to ensuring the longevity and efficiency of your 2024 Atlas. By adhering to the manufacturer's recommended maintenance schedule, you can prevent costly repairs down the road and prolong its resale value. Scheduled maintenance also increases overall safety by addressing potential issues before they escalate. The VW-certified technicians at Pohanka Volkswagen of Capitol Heights always prioritize your safety and satisfaction. Here, we summarize the maintenance schedule recommended by Volkswagen to keep the 2024 Atlas running its best.

![](https://dealerimages.dealereprocess.com/image/upload/3382164)

[Schedule Service](https://www.pohankavw.com/online-service-scheduler/)

## 10,000 Miles

At the 10,000-mile mark, your 2024 Atlas will require its first maintenance visit. During this service, our technicians will look over the vehicle's systems to ensure that everything is functioning properly. They will also take care of the scheduled oil and filter change, along with a tire rotation to promote even tread wear.

## 20,000 Miles

When your Atlas reaches 20,000 miles, it will be time for another round of essential maintenance. Our service technicians will conduct a more thorough examination, this time including elements such as the battery’s well-being (including how well it is charging), the coolant level, transmission function, and operation of all lights. Once again, your Atlas will receive an oil and filter change, as well as a tire rotation, brake inspection, and comprehensive check of all fluid levels and components.

## 40,000 Miles

When the odometer on your Atlas reads 40,000 miles, it will be time once again for our certified technicians to perform all the services included in the previous intervals (oil change, tire rotation, and multipoint inspection). They will also replace the dust and pollen filters.

## 60,000 Miles

The 60,000-mile service interval for the 2024 Atlas will cover everything performed at the 20,000-mile mark, in addition to replacing the cabin air filter to make sure you and your passengers are breathing clean air.

## 80,000 Miles

The 80,000-mile mark means it’s time for a more comprehensive maintenance service, as well as a complete mechanical check to monitor the vehicle’s continued reliability and performance. Besides repeating all of the services mentioned for the previous intervals, they will put in a fresh set of spark plugs and drain and replace the transmission fluid.

## What is the Volkswagen Atlas Maintenance Schedule?

Your [new VW Atlas](https://www.carolinavw.com/new-vehicles/atlas/) service intervals occur every 10,000 miles. Older Volkswagen models might have different maintenance requirements, so check your owner’s manual for the correct VW Atlas maintenance schedule. However, world-class engineering means longer VW Atlas service intervals when you have a late-model vehicle.

Every 10,000 miles represents the VW Atlas oil change interval, so expect to get a full synthetic oil change every 10,000 miles of driving unless you drive in less-than-ideal conditions regularly in Concord.

Below is the general VW Atlas maintenance schedule you should follow.

### **VW Atlas Maintenance Schedule: 10,000 Miles or One Year**

Your first Volkswagen Atlas service in Charlotte will get this:

- Inspect the Brake Pads
- Oil Change
- New Oil Filter
- Fluid Level Check
- Service Interval Display Reset (if needed)

### **VW Atlas Maintenance Schedule: 20,000 Miles or Two Years**

For this VW Atlas service interval, we will do everything from the first service at 10,000 miles, plus some extras:

- Automatic headlight control
- Headlight Washing System
- Wiper Blades
- Coolant Level and Frost Protection
- Brake Pads
- Transmission
- Second Battery
- Engine Air Filter Check
- Tire Pressure Monitoring System
- Horn
- Tire Repair Kit
- Engine and Engine Compartment Components
- Brake Fluid
- Tire Pressure
- Service Interval Display
- Exterior Lighting
- Battery
- Tires
- Windshield Wiper/Washer System

### **VW Atlas Maintenance Schedule: 30,000 Miles or Three Years**

Here’s what our team will do for your three-year Volkswagen Atlas service near Indian Trail:

- Oil Change
- New Oil Filter
- Inspect Brake Pads
- Service Interval Display Reset (if needed)

### **VW Atlas Maintenance Schedule: 40,000 Miles or Four Years**

At 40,000 miles, we’ll take care of the VW Atlas oil change interval, just like the other one-year maintenance. We’ll also check everything from the 20,000-mile VW Atlas service interval. Our team will also look over these things for your Atlas for four years:

- Sunroof and Panoramic Sunroof
- Ball Joints
- Wheel Bearings
- Axles
- Coupling Rods
- Tie Rod Ends
- Stabilizer Bushings
- New Dust and Pollen Filter for the Cabin
- Front and Rear Coil Springs and Shock Absorbers

### **VW Atlas Maintenance Schedule: 50,000 Miles or Five Years**

At the 50,000-mile mark, this service interval includes everything from the initial service interval:

- VW Atlas Oil Change Interval
- New Oil Filter
- Check Your Brake Pads
- Fluid Levels
- Service Interval Display Reset (if needed)

At this point in your SUV ownership, you might need a new battery, new tires, or new brake parts, depending on the condition of your Volkswagen Atlas. We’ll discuss your options with you if we see anything that needs service at this interval.

Moving forward, we’ll also inspect the drive belts, the condition of the transmission, and the radiator, as these parts might show more signs of wear. If our service technicians detect any looming issues that need to be resolved soon, we’ll suggest a way to remedy the situation.

```
In this video, we walk you through every step of changing the oil on a 2024 VW Atlas equipped with the 2.0L 4-cylinder EA888 engine. Whether you're a seasoned DIY mechanic or a beginner, our detailed guide is designed to help you maintain your vehicle with confidence and precision to keep your vehicle running and healthy.

** What You'll Learn **
 ✅ Essential Tools & Supplies: Get a rundown of all the tools needed for the job, from rhino ramps to the oil filter socket
 ✅ Step-by-Step Process: Follow along as we drain the old oil, replacing the oil filter, and add fresh oil, checking the oil level, and resetting the oil service light!
 ✅ Tips from a seasoned veteran of the automotive industry

** Please take this into account when selecting your oil and your oil change intervals. **

Volkswagen calls for VW 508 00 Spec Oil. It's suggested that if you want to run the 10,000 Mile drain intervals that you run oil that meets this specification. If you run 3,000 to 5,000 Mile oil change intervals, you can use alternative high quality synthetic oil with anti-wear, anti-friction additives like Liqui Moly or others.

Drain plug uses a T-45 Torx bit.
Drain plug torque spec: 22 FT/Lbs
Oil filter cap torque spec: 18.8 Ft/Lbs
```

## 2025 FORD BRONCO MAINTENANCE SCHEDULE

The 2025 Ford Bronco is built for adventure, thanks to its blend of off-road capability and everyday utility. With several trim levels and engines to choose from, The Bronco is ready to take on everything from rocky trails to city streets with ease. Here at Winslow Ford, the Camp Verde Ford dealer, we recommend adhering to Ford’s maintenance schedule to keep your Bronco running at its best and to help ensure it stays reliable for years to come.

The owner's manual for your 2025 Ford Bronco contains the maintenance schedule. If you’ve misplaced your manual or have questions about servicing your Bronco, the team at our Camp Verde Ford dealership is here to help. Contact our experts for advice or assistance with your vehicle's care!
