![2025 Ford Bronco On Jungle Safari](https://www.winslowford.com/static/brand-ford/vehicle/2025/Bronco/Hero/01.jpg)

### 10,000 Miles

Your 2025 Ford Bronco will be due for its first regular maintenance at 10,000 miles. This visit includes an oil change and a tire rotation, as well as checks of the transmission fluid level and a multi-point inspection. The service team will also examine the condition of key components like the brake pads, rotors, hoses, and parking brake.

Other areas that will be inspected include the rear axle, ball joints, driveshaft, tie rod ends, suspension, and steering linkage. Our certified service technicians will also check parts like the half-shaft boots, U-joints, exhaust system, and heat shields, as well as the tires and engine coolant levels. These services are repeated every 10,000 miles to keep your Bronco running smoothly and ready for the road—or the trail.

### 20,000 Miles

Your 2025 Bronco will get a cabin air filter replacement at 20,000 miles. A fresh air filter helps maintain clean, fresh air inside the cabin. It’s a quick update that keeps the interior environment comfortable and pleasant on every journey.

### 30,000 Miles

Your Bronco’s engine air filter will need to be replaced at 30,000 miles. This component ensures the engine continues to run smoothly and efficiently and helps optimize fuel economy.

### 100,000 Miles

When your Bronco reaches 100,000 miles, it will need a couple of important checks. Our certified service technicians will replace the spark plugs and inspect the accessory drive belts to help keep the engine running smoothly and ensure these key components stay reliable for the long haul. It’s all part of keeping your Bronco in top shape for the road ahead.

### 150,000 Miles

At 150,000 miles, your Bronco’s automatic transmission fluid and accessory drive belts need to be replaced. These key services help keep the transmission running smoothly and contribute to the vehicle's long-term reliability.

### 200,000 Miles

The engine coolant needs to be replaced at 200,000 miles. This essential step prevents overheating, safeguards the engine, and helps maintain performance even after all those miles.

### Every Three Years

it’s important to replace your Bronco’s brake fluid every three years, no matter how many miles you’ve driven. Fresh brake fluid ensures your braking system stays responsive and reliable, giving you the confidence you need behind the wheel.

Bring your 2025 Ford Bronco to the Winslow Ford Service Center for all your maintenance needs. Conveniently located at 840 Mike's Pike Street in Winslow, we’re easy to reach from the Camp Verde area. We look forward to helping you keep your Bronco in top shape!

# 2025 VW Jetta: Updated Service Recommendations & Tech Calibration

December 22nd, 2025 by[Christian Huckaby](https://www.vwsb.com/author/chuckabymartingp-com/ "Posts by Christian Huckaby")

Share this Post:
Share on FacebookShare on Twitter

_![2024 Volkswagen Jetta](https://di-uploads-pod44.dealerinspire.com/volkswagensanbernardino/uploads/2025/12/dec-19.webp)_

_Last month, a 2024 Jetta came in with its entire IQ.DRIVE safety system disabled after the owner had their windshield replaced at a discount glass shop. The shop installed the glass but never recalibrated the forward-facing camera, leaving the driver without automatic emergency braking, lane keeping assist, or adaptive cruise control for 4,200 miles. The recalibration took two hours and cost $320._ **_The proper calibration that should have been included with windshield replacement? Typically $180-220 when done immediately after glass installation._**

Your 2025 Volkswagen Jetta represents significant technological advancement over previous model years. The updated IQ.DRIVE driver assistance systems, revised engine management software, new electrical architecture, and enhanced safety features all deliver a more sophisticated driving experience than earlier Jettas.

But here’s what catches most Jetta owners completely off guard: these technological improvements come with updated maintenance requirements and calibration needs that differ from previous model years. Following outdated service schedules or ignoring calibration requirements puts your safety systems at risk and potentially voids warranty coverage.

This matters especially in San Bernardino, where our unique driving conditions create specific maintenance challenges. The temperature extremes from desert heat to mountain elevation, stop-and-go traffic on the I-10 and I-215, and air quality all affect how your Jetta needs to be maintained and calibrated.

## **What’s Actually New for 2025**

Your 2025 Jetta features Volkswagen’s latest generation IQ.DRIVE system with enhanced camera resolution, improved processing power, and additional radar coverage. These upgrades deliver better performance in challenging conditions, but they also require more frequent calibration verification than previous systems. The cameras and sensors need to be positioned with extreme precision to function correctly.

The engine management system received significant software updates that affect how the 1.5-liter turbocharged engine delivers power and manages emissions. These updates changed oil consumption patterns, modified fuel injection timing, and adjusted how the engine responds to varying fuel quality. What worked for your 2023 or earlier Jetta doesn’t necessarily apply to your 2025.

Volkswagen updated the electrical architecture with new control modules and revised communication protocols. This affects everything from how software updates are performed to how diagnostic procedures work. Your 2025 Jetta communicates differently with diagnostic equipment than previous models, which is why Volkswagen-specific service becomes more critical than ever.

The brake-by-wire system integration with your IQ.DRIVE features means your braking and safety systems work together in ways previous Jettas didn’t. This integration requires proper calibration after any brake service, wheel alignment, or suspension work to ensure all systems coordinate correctly.

An early adopter brought his 2025 Jetta to us last fall after noticing his adaptive cruise control behaving erratically. The system would brake suddenly when approaching slower traffic, then accelerate too aggressively once traffic cleared. During inspection, we found the forward radar sensor had never been properly calibrated after delivery. The dealership where he purchased the vehicle hadn’t performed the post-delivery calibration procedure required for 2025 models.

**His situation breakdown:**

- Driving for three months with improperly calibrated safety systems
- Adaptive cruise and emergency braking functioning outside parameters
- Increased accident risk from system behavior
- Post-delivery calibration: $280
- Total consequence: Three months of compromised safety plus calibration cost

**What should have happened:**

- Proper post-delivery calibration before customer delivery: included in vehicle prep
- All safety systems functioning as designed from day one: priceless
- Smart total: Zero cost, proper protection from start

## **The Updated Service Schedule You Need**

Your 2025 Jetta follows Volkswagen’s revised maintenance schedule with base intervals of 10,000 miles or one year for oil changes. However, Southern California driving conditions qualify as severe duty in multiple categories, which can modify these intervals significantly. The combination of heat, stop-and-go traffic, and air quality affects service needs.

Every 10,000 miles or annually, your Jetta requires oil and filter service using VW 508 00/509 00 approved synthetic oil. This low-SAPS specification protects your turbocharged engine and emissions equipment. The 2025 model year specifically requires this updated oil specification, which differs slightly from oils used in previous years. Using older specification oils, even if they’re “close,” provides inadequate protection for your engine’s updated components.

_“The biggest confusion we’re seeing with 2025 models is owners assuming nothing changed from their previous Jetta,” says Carlos Mendoza, Lead Technician at our Camino Real location. “They use the same oil, follow the same intervals, ignore calibration needs. Then we find camera systems out of alignment, engine wear from incorrect oil specs, and safety features not working as intended. The 2025 is different enough that old habits create real problems.”_

At each service interval, your IQ.DRIVE system requires verification. This doesn’t mean full recalibration every time, but technicians need to check that cameras are clean, sensors are functioning, and no fault codes are stored. We’ve found systems degrading gradually from dirty cameras or slightly misaligned sensors that owners never noticed until complete failure occurred.

Every 20,000 miles brings comprehensive inspection including brake system evaluation, tire rotation and inspection, cabin air filter replacement, and underbody inspection. Southern California’s unique combination of dust, heat, and occasional rain creates conditions where brake dust accumulation and rotor surface oxidation happen faster than in more humid climates.

At 30,000 miles, your Jetta needs spark plug inspection, engine air filter replacement, and what Volkswagen calls the “major inspection service.” For 2025 models, this service also includes mandatory IQ.DRIVE calibration verification to ensure all safety systems maintain factory specifications. This comprehensive service typically runs $450-650 depending on what’s actually needed.

Every 40,000 miles, if equipped with the DSG transmission, fluid service becomes due. The conventional six-speed automatic doesn’t require service until 60,000 miles under normal conditions, but severe duty operation can shorten this interval. Your brake fluid needs testing for moisture content, which accumulates even in dry climates from temperature cycling.

## **The IQ.DRIVE Calibration Reality**

Your 2025 Jetta’s IQ.DRIVE system includes forward collision warning with automatic emergency braking, lane keeping assist, blind spot monitoring, and rear traffic alert. These features rely on cameras and radar sensors that must be positioned with extreme precision to function correctly. Even slight misalignment causes system degradation or complete failure.

Sticking to the recommended 2026 Super Duty maintenance schedule is essential to keeping your truck operating at peak capability for years to come. Pundmann Ford is committed to helping St. Louis-area drivers stay on track with a maintenance plan that’s clear, cost-effective, and dealer-backed. ## **Oil Changes and Basic Service Intervals** Oil changes are the foundation of any good maintenance schedule, especially in a truck designed to handle tough jobs. For the [2026 Super Duty](https://www.ford.com/trucks/super-duty/models/), Ford recommends oil changes every 7,500 miles or every six months, whichever comes first, under normal driving conditions. If your Super Duty is used for towing, hauling, or off-road driving, more frequent oil changes—around every 5,000 miles—are advised. Along with oil changes, [routine maintenance services](https://www.pundmannford.com/service/) include: - Tire rotations every 7,500 miles to ensure even tread wear - Brake inspections during each oil change service - Fluid level checks, including coolant, brake fluid, and transmission fluid - Multi-point inspections provided by Pundmann Ford with every scheduled service These basic checkups keep your Super Duty running smoothly and can catch small issues before they become costly repairs. ## **Major Milestones: 30K, 60K, and 90K Service** The 2026 Super Duty maintenance schedule includes more comprehensive services at major mileage intervals to ensure long-term reliability. **At** **30,000 Miles** **:** - Replace the engine air filter - Inspect fuel system and hoses - Full brake system inspection - Rotate tires and inspect tread depth **At 60,000 Miles:** - Replace transmission fluid and filter (especially on trucks used for towing) - Service the cooling system and inspect belts/hoses - Check 4WD system (if equipped) - Replace the cabin air filter **At 90,000 Miles:** Replace spark plugs (for gas engines) - Inspect and possibly replace drive belts - Re-check suspension and steering components - Full diagnostic scan and system update (available at Pundmann Ford) Keeping up with these service points ensures your Super Duty retains its towing strength, fuel efficiency, and road handling for the long haul. Schedule your next service at Pundmann Ford and keep your 2026 Super Duty running strong with expert maintenance tailored to your truck’s needs. At Pundmann Ford, our factory-trained service team uses OEM parts, diagnostic tools, and model-specific expertise to ensure each visit supports your truck’s performance. With online scheduling, transparent pricing, and service specials, we make it simple to stay on track—whether you’re at 5,000 miles or 150,000. ## **Establish Your** **2026 Super Duty Maintenance Schedule** **With Pundmann Ford** At Pundmann Ford, we’re here to help you get the most out of your truck from day one. By following the official 2026 Super Duty maintenance schedule, you’ll extend the life of your vehicle, avoid costly repairs, and enjoy peace of mind every mile. The long-term profitability of a commercial vehicle depends entirely on strict adherence to its engineering lifecycle. Understanding the exact fluid intervals and thermal management requirements of the 2026 Ford Super Duty ensures your new truck remains structurally sound and capable of peak performance for years to come. Before diving into the critical service milestones below, you can explore the available configurations in our [**New Ford Super Duty Inventory**](https://www.sidneyford.com/new-vehicles/super-duty/). You can also learn about our dedicated commercial service bays on our [**Why Buy from Chesrown Ford**](https://www.sidneyford.com/research-hub/why-buy-a-2026-ford-super-duty/) page. ## 2026 Ford Super Duty Standard Maintenance Schedule Routine maintenance prevents internal friction from compromising your engine’s moving parts. Below is the standardized factory service interval table for the 2026 Ford Super Duty under normal driving conditions. | Mileage Interval | Required Mechanical Service | Real-World Benefit | | --- | --- | --- | | 7,500 Miles | Replace engine oil and filter. | Fresh oil maintains engine lubrication to reduce wear and preserve horsepower. | | 30,000 Miles | Replace the engine air filter and inspect the fuel system. | Maintains the proper air-to-fuel ratio to prevent poor engine performance. | | 60,000 Miles | Replace transmission fluid and service the cooling system. | Prevents internal gearbox friction and protects the transmission when towing heavy loads. | | 90,000 Miles | Replace spark plugs on gas engines and inspect drive belts. | Ensures rapid engine ignition and prevents belt failure while driving. | | 100,000 Miles | Replace engine coolant. | Protects the engine block from severe thermal degradation and overheating. | ## Intelligent Oil-Life Monitor and Thermal Stress | ![service center](https://di-uploads-pod45.dealerinspire.com/chesrownfordofsidney/uploads/2026/02/InvestInYourInvestment.jpg) | The core of long-term Super Duty reliability is proper thermal management. Ford equips the 2026 models with an advanced Intelligent Oil-Life Monitor system. This system actively calculates the proper oil change interval based on your specific driving habits and engine temperatures. When the “OIL CHANGE REQUIRED” message appears on your information display, you must perform the service within two weeks or 500 miles.
While the standard recommendation is an oil change every 7,500 miles or six months, heavy commercial use alters this timeline. If your Super Duty is used primarily for heavy towing or off-road driving, extreme temperatures accelerate oil degradation. Under these severe conditions, more frequent oil changes around every 5,000 miles are advised to protect the engine block. | ## Diesel Powertrain Specifics | If you select a model equipped with the 6.7-liter Power Stroke diesel engine, you must account for additional high-pressure components. Diesel trucks require routine fuel filter replacements to keep the fuel system clean and prevent reduced fuel efficiency. Furthermore, the diesel particulate filter (DPF) must be monitored and cleaned to prevent soot buildup that restricts exhaust flow and reduces engine power. Accurate oil volume and proper filtration are also crucial to protect the diesel turbocharger bearings from excessive heat. | ![service memeber](https://di-uploads-pod45.dealerinspire.com/chesrownfordofsidney/uploads/2026/02/FS_610x342_Service_Works.jpg) | ## Transmission and Drivetrain Longevity The 10-speed TorqShift automatic transmission relies on specialized fluid to operate its internal clutch packs. Replacing the transmission fluid and filter at the 60,000-mile mark is especially critical for trucks used for continuous towing. Clean transmission fluid prevents the gearbox from slipping or overheating when pulling a heavy trailer up a steep grade. Simultaneously, technicians must inspect the 4WD system and transfer case to ensure the internal gears remain fully lubricated. ## Protecting Your Commercial Investment in Sidney Securing a brand-new commercial vehicle requires absolute confidence in your maintenance strategy. By adhering strictly to these factory mileage intervals, Sidney contractors extract the maximum lifespan from their heavy-duty trucks while ensuring compliance with factory warranty requirements. The [**certified commercial service center**](https://www.sidneyford.com/service/) at Chesrown Ford utilizes factory diagnostic tools and [**OEM parts**](https://www.sidneyford.com/parts/) to accurately track and perform these maintenance protocols. # BMW SERVICE

BMW recommends you have your maintenance and repair work performed by an authorized BMW center.

# MAINTAINING YOUR BMW VEHICLE

A well-maintained vehicle will help safeguard its operational performance, road-safety and its reliability. This is why it is important to follow and perform BMW’s recommended periodic vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks as indicated by your vehicle’s Maintenance Service Display, along with the other maintenance work described in this booklet.

A improper maintenance is not covered under the BMW New Vehicle Damage, including consequential damage, which results from lack of or Limited Warranty for Passenger Cars and Light Trucks.

# MAINTENANCE INTERVALS

Maintenance intervals on motor vehicles were conventionally based solely on a fixed time period or a specified amount of accumulated driving mileage.

However, operational and driving conditions have a major influence on your vehicle’s routine maintenance requirements; the distance traveled is only one of these significant factors. A vehicle used for short trips in the city with numerous cold starts, prolonged periods of idling, stop-and-go driving, and high engine speeds during acceleration may require more frequent maintenance intervals than a vehicle that is driven long distances at moderate engine speeds.

Your BMW vehicle uses sensors and algorithms together with the elapsed time and the driving distance/profile to monitor and evaluate your vehicle’s maintenance service needs. This information is then used to adapt dynamically the parameters used to forecast the applicable maintenance service task intervals.

# THE BMW MAINTENANCE SYSTEM

All BMW vehicles are equipped with an integrated BMW Maintenance System. This maintenance “reminder” system helps ensure that the vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks are performed at the forecasted intervals that apply to your vehicle.

The BMW Maintenance System display provides the vehicle operator access to the current status information for the following maintenance service tasks:

$\\triangleright$ Engine oil (date and miles)\*

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle check (date and miles)

$\\triangleright$ Front brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Rear brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid (date)

$\\triangleright$ 1200 Mile running-in service (date and miles) (Applicable to BMW M vehicles only)\*

For each specific maintenance service task, either the future date (month/ year), remaining miles or both are provided as noted above. The system monitors variable inputs to forecast the intervals and alert the driver when one or more specific maintenance tasks should be performed.

NOTE: For certain vehicles, the status of the front and rear brake pads will only be observable in the maintenance system’s display when there are approximately 2,000 miles or less remaining before a brake service will be required to be performed.

For information about the vehicle’s maintenance system displays, please refer to the Maintenance Service Display Overview section beginning on page 5.

The following “combine with Engine oil”\* maintenance service tasks may be identified as needing to be performed with a specific occurrence of the “Engine oil” service task (service counter number):

$\\triangleright$ Cabin Microfilter(s)

$\\triangleright$ Engine air filter(s)\*

$\\triangleright$ Spark plugs\*

$\\triangleright$ Final drive oil (Applicable M vehicles only)

\\* Does not apply to BEV

Although these items do not appear in the BMW Maintenance System’s display in the vehicle, these services should be performed when your vehicle’s engine oil is changed in accordance with the interval identified by your vehicle’s BMW Maintenance System.

For more information on your vehicle’s maintenance services requirements, procedures and intervals, please refer the Maintenance Service Summary section beginning on page 10.

The BMW Maintenance System also includes an option to set service reminders for the following state-specific mandatory vehicle inspections, including:

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle safety inspection; and/or $\\triangleright$ Emissions test

The corresponding interval data for these inspections can be inputted into the BMW Maintenance System by a service provider; they are not determined by the vehicle.

For your convenience, you may also wish to have your authorized BMW center perform the work necessary to fulfill these state inspection requirements in your area concurrent with the maintenance services specified above when possible.

Should you request more frequent maintenance service than is indicated by the BMW Maintenance System during the coverage period, the cost of these services will not be covered by the BMW Maintenance Program.

# SERVICE DATA — REMOTE CONTROL KEY

Maintenance service task status information for your BMW vehicle is continually updated and stored in your remote control key.

Your authorized BMW center can access this data and consult with you about applicable service procedures and tasks for your vehicle.

Therefore, always provide your service consultant with the most recent remote control key that was used to operate the vehicle when servicing your vehicle at a BMW center.

# VEHICLE STORAGE

Disconnecting the battery during periods of long-term vehicle storage will interrupt the calculation of time-dependent maintenance services.

In this situation, BMW recommends that you have all your time-based maintenance services, such as brake fluid, engine oil and cabin microfilter, brought up to the correct date by an authorized BMW center.

# ENGINE OIL

2025 model year vehicles with internal-combustion engines are factory-filled with:

Z BMW-approved fully synthetic oil for gasoline engines

Engine oil should be changed when the vehicle’s engine is at operating temperature.

If an engine oil service is being performed or you need to add engine oil between changes, please refer to the Owner’s Manual for the recommended engine oil for your BMW vehicle.

# LONG-TERM RATED FLUIDS AND OILS

The following systems and assemblies are factory-filled with long-term rated fluid and oil; fluid replacement is only necessary when repairs are being performed (unless otherwise noted):

$\\triangleright$ Engine cooling system (antifreeze/coolant) $\\triangleright$ Automatic (except for X1 and X2) and manual transmissions $\\triangleright$ All-wheel drive transfer cases (except when indicated by the vehicle)

# REGULAR CHECKS — VEHICLE OPERATOR

In addition to the maintenance service procedure information contained in this booklet, BMW recommends that you regularly check (when refueling, for example), and address when necessary, the following items:

$\\triangleright$ Washer fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Coolant level

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Tires — pressure, condition and wear

Please refer to the Owner’s Manual for additional information.

## BMW Preventative Maintenance: Every 5,000 Miles / 6 Months

It’s important to bring in your BMW two or three times a year (or every 5,000 miles) for these preventative maintenance services:

- Front and rear brake inspection
- Brake fluid check
- Coolant check
- Engine oil check
- Cabin air filter inspection
- Engine inspection
- Vehicle inspection
- Wiper blade inspection
- Any necessary tire rotations

Your BMW also comes with something called the Condition-Based Service Monitor (CBS). Your CBS tracks the condition of important systems in your BMW, letting you know if service is required. Our technicians will also use your CBS to determine what needs to be replaced, repaired, or serviced when you schedule service. Keep in mind that just because your CBS may say that service may not be necessary at 5,000 miles doesn’t mean that you shouldn’t come in for preventative maintenance and checks. Sometimes human eyes are necessary to determine a problem or to nip any potential issues in the bud.

## Recommended BMW Maintenance Schedule

Your BMW service schedule needs will vary based on how often you drive, where you drive, and your driving conditions. Your owner’s manual can give you detailed information on common service tasks for your specific model and trim, but here’s what BMW owners can generally expect:

- **Every 10,000 miles** (or yearly): replace your vehicle’s engine oil, oil filter, and coolant.
- **Every 20,000 miles** (or every two years): inspect and replace your vehicle’s fuel filters.
- **Every 30,000 miles** (or every three years): replace your vehicle’s brake fluid (after the first replacement, **every 60,000 miles**) and replace your vehicle’s transmission fluid on manual-transmission BMWs.
- **Every 60,000 miles** (or every six years): replace your vehicle’s engine air filter and spark plugs, inspect and replace any brake pads and brake rotors, and replace transmission fluid on automatic-transmission BMWs.
- **Every 90,000 miles** (or every nine years): replace your vehicle’s timing belts and hoses.

You’ll want to repeat the cycle above after 90,000 miles and always follow the 5,000-mile maintenance schedule. Your BMW’s New Vehicle Limited Warranty will also expire at 50,000 miles, so we recommend getting in any repairs or service before this warranty expires! We also recommend replacing your BMW battery around 50,000 miles.

A improper maintenance is not covered under the BMW New Vehicle Damage, including consequential damage, which results from lack of or Limited Warranty for Passenger Cars and Light Trucks.

# MAINTENANCE INTERVALS

Maintenance intervals on motor vehicles were conventionally based solely on a fixed time period or a specified amount of accumulated driving mileage.

However, operational and driving conditions have a major influence on your vehicle’s routine maintenance requirements; the distance traveled is only one of these significant factors. A vehicle used for short trips in the city with numerous cold starts, prolonged periods of idling, stop-and-go driving, and high engine speeds during acceleration may require more frequent maintenance intervals than a vehicle that is driven long distances at moderate engine speeds.

Your BMW vehicle uses sensors and algorithms together with the elapsed time and the driving distance/profile to monitor and evaluate your vehicle’s maintenance service needs. This information is then used to adapt dynamically the parameters used to forecast the applicable maintenance service task intervals.

# THE BMW MAINTENANCE SYSTEM

All BMW vehicles are equipped with an integrated BMW Maintenance System. This maintenance “reminder” system helps ensure that the vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks are performed at the forecasted intervals that apply to your vehicle.

The BMW Maintenance System display provides the vehicle operator access to the current status information for the following maintenance service tasks:

$\\triangleright$ Engine oil (date and miles)\*

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle check (date and miles)

$\\triangleright$ Front brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Rear brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid (date)

$\\triangleright$ 1200 Mile running-in service (date and miles) (Applicable to BMW M vehicles only)\*

For each specific maintenance service task, either the future date (month/ year), remaining miles or both are provided as noted above. The system monitors variable inputs to forecast the intervals and alert the driver when one or more specific maintenance tasks should be performed.

NOTE: For certain vehicles, the status of the front and rear brake pads will only be observable in the maintenance system’s display when there are approximately 2,000 miles or less remaining before a brake service will be required to be performed.

For information about the vehicle’s maintenance system displays, please refer to the Maintenance Service Display Overview section beginning on page 5.

The following “combine with Engine oil”\* maintenance service tasks may be identified as needing to be performed with a specific occurrence of the “Engine oil” service task (service counter number):

$\\triangleright$ Cabin Microfilter(s)

$\\triangleright$ Engine air filter(s)\*

$\\triangleright$ Spark plugs\*

$\\triangleright$ Final drive oil (Applicable M vehicles only)

\\* Does not apply to BEV

Although these items do not appear in the BMW Maintenance System’s display in the vehicle, these services should be performed when your vehicle’s engine oil is changed in accordance with the interval identified by your vehicle’s BMW Maintenance System.

For more information on your vehicle’s maintenance services requirements, procedures and intervals, please refer the Maintenance Service Summary section beginning on page 10.

The BMW Maintenance System also includes an option to set service reminders for the following state-specific mandatory vehicle inspections, including:

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle safety inspection; and/or $\\triangleright$ Emissions test

The corresponding interval data for these inspections can be inputted into the BMW Maintenance System by a service provider; they are not determined by the vehicle.

For your convenience, you may also wish to have your authorized BMW center perform the work necessary to fulfill these state inspection requirements in your area concurrent with the maintenance services specified above when possible.

Should you request more frequent maintenance service than is indicated by the BMW Maintenance System during the coverage period, the cost of these services will not be covered by the BMW Maintenance Program.

# SERVICE DATA — REMOTE CONTROL KEY

Maintenance service task status information for your BMW vehicle is continually updated and stored in your remote control key.

Your authorized BMW center can access this data and consult with you about applicable service procedures and tasks for your vehicle.

Therefore, always provide your service consultant with the most recent remote control key that was used to operate the vehicle when servicing your vehicle at a BMW center.

# VEHICLE STORAGE

Disconnecting the battery during periods of long-term vehicle storage will interrupt the calculation of time-dependent maintenance services.

In this situation, BMW recommends that you have all your time-based maintenance services, such as brake fluid, engine oil and cabin microfilter, brought up to the correct date by an authorized BMW center.

# ENGINE OIL

2025 model year vehicles with internal-combustion engines are factory-filled with:

Z BMW-approved fully synthetic oil for gasoline engines

Engine oil should be changed when the vehicle’s engine is at operating temperature.

If an engine oil service is being performed or you need to add engine oil between changes, please refer to the Owner’s Manual for the recommended engine oil for your BMW vehicle.

# LONG-TERM RATED FLUIDS AND OILS

The following systems and assemblies are factory-filled with long-term rated fluid and oil; fluid replacement is only necessary when repairs are being performed (unless otherwise noted):

$\\triangleright$ Engine cooling system (antifreeze/coolant) $\\triangleright$ Automatic (except for X1 and X2) and manual transmissions $\\triangleright$ All-wheel drive transfer cases (except when indicated by the vehicle)

# REGULAR CHECKS — VEHICLE OPERATOR

In addition to the maintenance service procedure information contained in this booklet, BMW recommends that you regularly check (when refueling, for example), and address when necessary, the following items:

$\\triangleright$ Washer fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Coolant level

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Tires — pressure, condition and wear

Please refer to the Owner’s Manual for additional information.

#### About Genuine VW

The Volkswagen Group, also known as “VAG”, consists of Volkswagen, Audi, Lamborghini, Bentley, Bugatti, Porsche, Ducati, MAN, Scania, SEAT, and Skoda. The original parts used by VW to build your car are available as replacement parts under the “Genuine VW” brand. Manufactured under the direction of VW, expect excellent quality and a premium price since these parts are available exclusively through the VW Dealership network.

You may not realize this, but the parts that make up your VW are not necessarily manufactured by VW. Product Details

- Tested and retested under extreme conditions, Motorcraft filters are also the only filters recommended for Ford, Lincoln and Mercury vehicles.
- Helps protect against engine wear by screening out abrasives, such as carbon, sand, dust and bits of metal.
- 80% efficiency on particles 20 microns and larger.
- Cellulose and polyester blend media is formulated for high capacity and strength.
- Pressure-relief valves also help maintain the supply of oil to the engine under extreme cold conditions or if the filter gets clogged.
- Location of pressure-relief valves helps minimize the chance of contaminated oil circulating back into the engine.
- Steel cases are ironed for a precise fit, fluted to ease removal and painted to resist rust.
- Anti-drain back valves made of silicone provide greater cold/heat resistance.

Motorcraft oil filters are engineered to help screen out abrasives to help meet today's longer service intervals.

# BMW SERVICE

BMW recommends you have your maintenance and repair work performed by an authorized BMW center.

# MAINTAINING YOUR BMW VEHICLE

A well-maintained vehicle will help safeguard its operational performance, road-safety and its reliability. This is why it is important to follow and perform BMW’s recommended periodic vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks as indicated by your vehicle’s Maintenance Service Display, along with the other maintenance work described in this booklet.

A improper maintenance is not covered under the BMW New Vehicle Damage, including consequential damage, which results from lack of or Limited Warranty for Passenger Cars and Light Trucks.

# MAINTENANCE INTERVALS

Maintenance intervals on motor vehicles were conventionally based solely on a fixed time period or a specified amount of accumulated driving mileage.

However, operational and driving conditions have a major influence on your vehicle’s routine maintenance requirements; the distance traveled is only one of these significant factors. A vehicle used for short trips in the city with numerous cold starts, prolonged periods of idling, stop-and-go driving, and high engine speeds during acceleration may require more frequent maintenance intervals than a vehicle that is driven long distances at moderate engine speeds.

Your BMW vehicle uses sensors and algorithms together with the elapsed time and the driving distance/profile to monitor and evaluate your vehicle’s maintenance service needs. This information is then used to adapt dynamically the parameters used to forecast the applicable maintenance service task intervals.

# THE BMW MAINTENANCE SYSTEM

All BMW vehicles are equipped with an integrated BMW Maintenance System. This maintenance “reminder” system helps ensure that the vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks are performed at the forecasted intervals that apply to your vehicle.

The BMW Maintenance System display provides the vehicle operator access to the current status information for the following maintenance service tasks:

$\\triangleright$ Engine oil (date and miles)\*

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle check (date and miles)

$\\triangleright$ Front brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Rear brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid (date)

Z 1200 Mile running-in service (date and miles) (Applicable to BMW M vehicles only)\*

For each specific maintenance service task, either the future date (month/ year), remaining miles or both are provided as noted above. The system monitors variable inputs to forecast the intervals and alert the driver when one or more specific maintenance tasks should be performed.

NOTE: For certain vehicles, the status of the front and rear brake pads will only be observable in the maintenance system’s display when there are approximately 2,000 miles or less remaining before a brake service will be required to be performed.

For information about the vehicle’s maintenance system displays, please refer to the Maintenance Service Display Overview section beginning on page 5.

The following “combine with Engine oil”\* maintenance service tasks may be identified as needing to be performed with a specific occurrence of the “Engine oil” service task (service counter number):

$\\triangleright$ Cabin Microfilter(s)

$\\triangleright$ Engine air filter(s)\*

$\\triangleright$ Spark plugs\*

$\\triangleright$ Final drive oil (Applicable M vehicles only)

\\* Does not apply to BEV

Although these items do not appear in the BMW Maintenance System’s display in the vehicle, these services should be performed when your vehicle’s engine oil is changed in accordance with the interval identified by your vehicle’s BMW Maintenance System.

For more information on your vehicle’s maintenance services requirements, procedures and intervals, please refer the Maintenance Service Summary section beginning on page 10.

The BMW Maintenance System also includes an option to set service reminders for the following state-specific mandatory vehicle inspections, including:

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle safety inspection; and/or $\\triangleright$ Emissions test

The corresponding interval data for these inspections can be inputted into the BMW Maintenance System by a service provider; they are not determined by the vehicle.

For your convenience, you may also wish to have your authorized BMW center perform the work necessary to fulfill these state inspection requirements in your area concurrent with the maintenance services specified above when possible.

Should you request more frequent maintenance service than is indicated by the BMW Maintenance System during the coverage period, the cost of these services will not be covered by the BMW Maintenance Program.

# SERVICE DATA — REMOTE CONTROL KEY

Maintenance service task status information for your BMW vehicle is continually updated and stored in your remote control key.

Your authorized BMW center can access this data and consult with you about applicable service procedures and tasks for your vehicle.

Therefore, always provide your service consultant with the most recent remote control key that was used to operate the vehicle when servicing your vehicle at a BMW center.

# VEHICLE STORAGE

Disconnecting the battery during periods of long-term vehicle storage will interrupt the calculation of time-dependent maintenance services.

In this situation, BMW recommends that you have all your time-based maintenance services, such as brake fluid, engine oil and cabin microfilter, brought up to the correct date by an authorized BMW center.

# ENGINE OIL

2026 model year vehicles with internal-combustion engines are factory-filled with:

Z BMW-approved fully synthetic oil for gasoline engines

Engine oil should be changed when the vehicle’s engine is at operating temperature.

If an engine oil service is being performed or you need to add engine oil between changes, please refer to the Owner’s Manual for the recommended engine oil for your BMW vehicle.

# LONG-TERM RATED FLUIDS AND OILS

The following systems and assemblies are factory-filled with long-term rated fluid and oil; fluid replacement is only necessary when repairs are being performed (unless otherwise noted):

$\\triangleright$ Engine cooling system (antifreeze/coolant)

$\\triangleright$ Automatic (except X1, X2, and 2 Series Gran Coupe) and manual transmissions

$\\triangleright$ All-wheel drive transfer cases (except when indicated by the vehicle)

# REGULAR CHECKS — VEHICLE OPERATOR

In addition to the maintenance service procedure information contained in this booklet, BMW recommends that you regularly check (when refueling, for example), and address when necessary, the following items:

$\\triangleright$ Washer fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Coolant level

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Tires — pressure, condition and wear

Please refer to the Owner’s Manual for additional information.

**BMW Ultimate Care: Complimentary Maintenance for Peace of Mind**

Eligible BMW 5 Series models come with BMW Ultimate Care, a complimentary maintenance plan that covers three years or 36,000 miles. This plan includes essential services such as:

**BMW 5 Series Maintenance Schedule at 10,000 Miles**

The BMW 5 Series features a Condition-Based Service (CBS) system that monitors key components and alerts you when maintenance is required. At 10,000-mile intervals, essential tasks include:

- Engine oil and oil filter change
- Tire rotation
- Fluid level checks

Depending on your driving habits and conditions, the CBS system may also detect the need for additional services

**At 30,000 Miles**

At 30,000 miles, your BMW 5 Series requires additional care to ensure ongoing performance. Services include:

- Brake fluid replacement
- Potential fuel filter replacement (generally recommended between 20,000–40,000 miles)
- Repeating the services from earlier milestones, including:
  - Engine oil and oil filter change
  - Tire rotation
  - Fluid level checks

**At 60,000 Miles**

Reaching 60,000 miles is a significant milestone for your BMW 5 Series, requiring more extensive maintenance. Key services include:

- Engine air filter replacement
- Spark plug replacement
- Routine tasks from previous milestones, including:
  - Engine oil and filter change
  - Brake fluid replacement
  - Tire rotation

**Why Regular BMW 5 Series Maintenance Matters**

Staying on top of your BMW 5 Series maintenance schedule isn’t just about keeping your car in pristine condition—it’s about ensuring your safety and maximizing the performance and longevity of your vehicle. Regular service provides:

- **Enhanced performance:** Enjoy the rewarding driving experience BMW is known for.

## What Does the BMW Maintenance Schedule Include?

### BMW 10,000-Mile Maintenance

- At 10,000 miles or 12 months, schedule an oil change, brake inspection, and tire rotation.

### BMW 20,000-Mile Maintenance

- At 20,000 miles, replace the cabin air filter and perform a more comprehensive inspection.

### BMW 30,000-Mile Maintenance

- At 30,000-40,000 miles, inspect suspension, steering components, coolant, and belts.
- If manual transmission: replace [transmission fluid](https://www.bmwofturnersville.com/service/service-tips/check-your-transmission-fluid/) every 30,000 miles

### BMW 60,000-Mile Maintenance

- At 60,000 miles, flush and replace brake fluid, inspect spark plugs, and change the engine air filter.

### Additional BMW Maintenance

Every two years, replace the cabin microfilter and test battery performance.

Additional services like coolant flushes, differential fluid replacement, or transmission service may vary depending on your BMW model and driving habits.

[Service Department](https://www.bmwofmilwaukeenorth.com/service/)

### Preserving the Executive Standard.

Owning a [**2026 BMW 5 Series**](https://www.bmwofmilwaukeenorth.com/new-vehicles/5-series/) in Milwaukee requires a proactive approach to maintenance. The G60 chassis, whether equipped with the B48 4-cylinder (530i) or the B58 6-cylinder (540i/550e), is engineered for high-mileage longevity, provided it receives specific care.

Unlike older vehicles with rigid fixed intervals, your 5 Series utilizes Condition Based Service (CBS). This system uses sensors to monitor oil life, brake pad wear, and fluid quality in real-time, adapting service requirements based on how you drive. However, given our extreme Wisconsin climate, ranging from sub-zero cold starts to humid summers, we recommend adhering to a baseline schedule to ensure peak performance.

### The G60 Service Intervals.

While the CBS system will alert you via the iDrive 8.5 display when service is due, the following timeline serves as the engineering standard for long-term reliability.

#### Every 10,000 Miles (or 12 Months).

This is the “Standard Scope” service. It establishes the baseline for engine health.

- **Synthetic Oil Change:** Replacement of engine oil and filter. The B48 and B58 engines rely on clean oil not just for lubrication, but to actuate the VANOS variable valve timing system.
- **Tire Rotation:** Critical for xDrive models to ensure even tread wear and prevent strain on the transfer case.
- **Safety Inspection:** Verification of fluid levels, wiper blades, and brake pad thickness.

#### Every 30,000 Miles.

At this interval, we address hydraulic and filtration systems that degrade over time.

- **Brake Fluid Flush:** BMW brake fluid is hygroscopic (absorbs moisture). Flushing it prevents internal corrosion of the ABS module and maintains a firm pedal feel.
- **Cabin Microfilter:** Replacement is necessary to maintain airflow and remove allergens/dust from the HVAC system.

#### Every 60,000 Miles.

This is a major service milestone for the G60 chassis.

- **Spark Plugs:** Worn plugs can cause misfires and stress the ignition coils. Replacement restores optimal combustion efficiency.
- **Engine Air Filter:** A clean filter allows the turbocharger to breathe freely, maintaining throttle response.
- **Sunroof Drain Check:** Essential for vehicles parked outside to prevent water ingress during heavy storms.

### Engine-Specific Care: B48 vs. B58.

While both engines share a modular architecture, they have distinct long-term ownership considerations.

| #### B48 (530i) Considerations. | #### B58 (540i & 550e) Considerations. |
| --- | --- |
| ![2026 BMW 530i and 540i trim](https://di-uploads-pod44.dealerinspire.com/bmwofmilwaukeenorth/uploads/2026/02/530i-models-and-540i-xdrive.jpg) | ![2026 BMW 550e xDrive Trim](https://di-uploads-pod44.dealerinspire.com/bmwofmilwaukeenorth/uploads/2026/02/550e-xdrive-model.jpg) |
| The 2.0-liter B48 is a robust “baby B58,” but it operates under higher boost pressure relative to its displacement.<br>- **Coolant Circuit:** Owners should periodically check coolant levels. The system is complex, featuring multiple cooling circuits, and low levels can trigger “drivetrain malfunction” warnings.<br>- **Oil Filter Housing:** Over high mileage (typically 60k+), the plastic composite oil filter housing can become brittle from heat cycles. We inspect this component at every oil change to catch early signs of weeping. | The 3.0-liter B58 is legendary for its “bulletproof” internals, but external gaskets require monitoring.<br>- **Valve Cover Gasket:** As the engine approaches higher mileage (70k+), the valve cover gasket is a known wear item. Keeping fresh oil in the engine helps preserve the pliability of these seals.<br>- **VANOS Solenoids:** These solenoids control valve timing using oil pressure. Regular oil changes are the single best way to prevent sludge buildup that can restrict their operation. |

### BMW Ultimate Care & Warranty.

Every new 2026 BMW 5 Series includes [**BMW Ultimate Care**](https://bmwusaservice.com/ultimatecare), which covers scheduled maintenance for the first 3 years or 36,000 miles.

- **Included:** Engine oil, oil filter, brake fluid, cabin microfilter, engine air filter, and spark plugs.
- **Value:** This program locks in your maintenance costs and ensures only Original BMW Parts are used, maintaining your vehicle’s resale value.

### Why Service at BMW of Milwaukee North?

Servicing your 5 Series at an independent shop often means using generic fluids that don’t meet BMW’s strict “Longlife-17 FE+” oil standards.

- **Factory Training:** Our technicians are specifically trained on the G60’s 48-volt mild-hybrid systems, ensuring safe and correct handling of electrified components.
- **OEM Parts Warranty:** Repairs made with Original BMW Parts come with a two-year unlimited mileage warranty.
- **Milwaukee Expertise:** We check for region-specific issues, such as suspension wear from potholes and undercarriage corrosion from road salt, protecting your investment.

# BMW SERVICE

BMW recommends you have your maintenance and repair work performed by an authorized BMW center.

# MAINTAINING YOUR BMW VEHICLE

A well-maintained vehicle will help safeguard its operational performance, road-safety and its reliability. This is why it is important to follow and perform BMW’s recommended periodic vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks as indicated by your vehicle’s Maintenance Service Display, along with the other maintenance work described in this booklet.

A improper maintenance is not covered under the BMW New Vehicle Damage, including consequential damage, which results from lack of or Limited Warranty for Passenger Cars and Light Trucks.

# MAINTENANCE INTERVALS

Maintenance intervals on motor vehicles were conventionally based solely on a fixed time period or a specified amount of accumulated driving mileage.

However, operational and driving conditions have a major influence on your vehicle’s routine maintenance requirements; the distance traveled is only one of these significant factors. A vehicle used for short trips in the city with numerous cold starts, prolonged periods of idling, stop-and-go driving, and high engine speeds during acceleration may require more frequent maintenance intervals than a vehicle that is driven long distances at moderate engine speeds.

Your BMW vehicle uses sensors and algorithms together with the elapsed time and the driving distance/profile to monitor and evaluate your vehicle’s maintenance service needs. This information is then used to adapt dynamically the parameters used to forecast the applicable maintenance service task intervals.

# THE BMW MAINTENANCE SYSTEM

All BMW vehicles are equipped with an integrated BMW Maintenance System. This maintenance “reminder” system helps ensure that the vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks are performed at the forecasted intervals that apply to your vehicle.

The BMW Maintenance System display provides the vehicle operator access to the current status information for the following maintenance service tasks:

$\\triangleright$ Engine oil (date and miles)\*

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle check (date and miles)

$\\triangleright$ Front brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Rear brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid (date)

Z 1200 Mile running-in service (date and miles) (Applicable to BMW M vehicles only)\*

For each specific maintenance service task, either the future date (month/ year), remaining miles or both are provided as noted above. The system monitors variable inputs to forecast the intervals and alert the driver when one or more specific maintenance tasks should be performed.

NOTE: For certain vehicles, the status of the front and rear brake pads will only be observable in the maintenance system’s display when there are approximately 2,000 miles or less remaining before a brake service will be required to be performed.

For information about the vehicle’s maintenance system displays, please refer to the Maintenance Service Display Overview section beginning on page 5.

The following “combine with Engine oil”\* maintenance service tasks may be identified as needing to be performed with a specific occurrence of the “Engine oil” service task (service counter number):

$\\triangleright$ Cabin Microfilter(s)

$\\triangleright$ Engine air filter(s)\*

$\\triangleright$ Spark plugs\*

$\\triangleright$ Final drive oil (Applicable M vehicles only)

\\* Does not apply to BEV

Although these items do not appear in the BMW Maintenance System’s display in the vehicle, these services should be performed when your vehicle’s engine oil is changed in accordance with the interval identified by your vehicle’s BMW Maintenance System.

For more information on your vehicle’s maintenance services requirements, procedures and intervals, please refer the Maintenance Service Summary section beginning on page 10.

The BMW Maintenance System also includes an option to set service reminders for the following state-specific mandatory vehicle inspections, including:

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle safety inspection; and/or $\\triangleright$ Emissions test

The corresponding interval data for these inspections can be inputted into the BMW Maintenance System by a service provider; they are not determined by the vehicle.

For your convenience, you may also wish to have your authorized BMW center perform the work necessary to fulfill these state inspection requirements in your area concurrent with the maintenance services specified above when possible.

Should you request more frequent maintenance service than is indicated by the BMW Maintenance System during the coverage period, the cost of these services will not be covered by the BMW Maintenance Program.

# SERVICE DATA — REMOTE CONTROL KEY

Maintenance service task status information for your BMW vehicle is continually updated and stored in your remote control key.

Your authorized BMW center can access this data and consult with you about applicable service procedures and tasks for your vehicle.

Therefore, always provide your service consultant with the most recent remote control key that was used to operate the vehicle when servicing your vehicle at a BMW center.

# VEHICLE STORAGE

Disconnecting the battery during periods of long-term vehicle storage will interrupt the calculation of time-dependent maintenance services.

In this situation, BMW recommends that you have all your time-based maintenance services, such as brake fluid, engine oil and cabin microfilter, brought up to the correct date by an authorized BMW center.

# ENGINE OIL

2026 model year vehicles with internal-combustion engines are factory-filled with:

Z BMW-approved fully synthetic oil for gasoline engines

Engine oil should be changed when the vehicle’s engine is at operating temperature.

If an engine oil service is being performed or you need to add engine oil between changes, please refer to the Owner’s Manual for the recommended engine oil for your BMW vehicle.

# LONG-TERM RATED FLUIDS AND OILS

The following systems and assemblies are factory-filled with long-term rated fluid and oil; fluid replacement is only necessary when repairs are being performed (unless otherwise noted):

$\\triangleright$ Engine cooling system (antifreeze/coolant)

$\\triangleright$ Automatic (except X1, X2, and 2 Series Gran Coupe) and manual transmissions

$\\triangleright$ All-wheel drive transfer cases (except when indicated by the vehicle)

# REGULAR CHECKS — VEHICLE OPERATOR

In addition to the maintenance service procedure information contained in this booklet, BMW recommends that you regularly check (when refueling, for example), and address when necessary, the following items:

$\\triangleright$ Washer fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Coolant level

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Tires — pressure, condition and wear

Please refer to the Owner’s Manual for additional information.

## Engine Oil Filter

- Description:
Your Engine Oil Filter does exactly as the name suggests it filtrates the oil in your Nissan engine. As Motor oil circulates through and Reduces friction between engine parts, the filter Captures and traps impurities, so they won't reach your vehicle's engine.
While the engine Maintains your Nissan, it burns fuel and eventually makes things such as sludge and debris. If your vehicle cannot properly filter out these contaminants because you have a grimy or blocked Engine Oil Filter, these contaminants may blend w/ your oil and may lead to very pricey repair costs.
When your Nissan's Engine Oil Filter hasn't been replaced, it can become clogged due to excess excessive gunk. So what happens when an Engine Oil Filter becomes too dirty? Your fuel efficiency and fluid pressure may decLine, and your car's ventilation system may become damaged and begin to emit a burning oil smell.
But when is the best time to get a new Engine Oil Filter installed? Typically, your Engine Oil Filter change should occur as often as you change your engine oil. If you frequently take short trips or if you do tons of interstate driving, it's likely that you will need to change it out more frequently to Maintain your car's engine health.
Are you able to install your Engine Oil Filter on your own? Maybe, but it may require some tricky finagling through the engine in order to find the filter location.
Consult your Nissan owner's Manual before starting to prevent injuring yourself or ruining critical engine pieces. Overall, it may be better to have it installed by a licensed Nissan service center instead.
Help extend the life of your Nissan engine by buying a genuine OEM Engine Oil Filter From Nissan Parts and it will fit your vehicle seamlessly.

# What is the Recommended BMW Maintenance Schedule?

![Mechanic fixing BMW](https://dealerinspire-image-library-prod.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/images/qOCqBJVRI2dmLPMZp2H4nX2vvpahYMjkkgG6QC7e.jpg)

* * *

At BMW of Tigard, we often get questions from customers about their BMW maintenance schedule. And when you buy a [quality new BMW](https://www.bmwtigard.com/new-vehicles/), it’s important to stick to its BMW service schedule. That’s why we’ve provided the recommended maintenance schedule for general BMW vehicles for Portland and Tigard drivers. With this handy guide, it’ll be easy to stay on track and have your vehicle serviced. We’ll ensure that your vehicle will always be running at its best! As always, before you schedule maintenance on your vehicle, be sure to read your owner’s manual for any specific maintenance information that applies to your BMW vehicle. That way, you’ll better understand your specific model and trim’s future maintenance and repair needs.

[BMW X3 SERVICE SCHEDULE](https://www.bmwtigard.com/service/service-and-parts-tips/bmw-x3-service-schedule/) [Service & Parts Specials](https://www.bmwtigard.com/service-parts-specials/)

* * *

## BMW Preventative Maintenance: Every 5,000 Miles / 6 Months

It’s important to bring in your BMW two or three times a year (or every 5,000 miles) for these preventative maintenance services:

- Front and rear brake inspection
- Brake fluid check
- Coolant check
- Engine oil check
- Cabin air filter inspection
- Engine inspection
- Vehicle inspection
- Wiper blade inspection
- Any necessary tire rotations

Your BMW also comes with something called the Condition-Based Service Monitor (CBS). Your CBS tracks the condition of important systems in your BMW, letting you know if service is required. Our technicians will also use your CBS to determine what needs to be replaced, repaired, or serviced when you schedule service. Keep in mind that just because your CBS may say that service may not be necessary at 5,000 miles doesn’t mean that you shouldn’t come in for preventative maintenance and checks. Sometimes human eyes are necessary to determine a problem or to nip any potential issues in the bud.

## Recommended BMW Maintenance Schedule

Your BMW service schedule needs will vary based on how often you drive, where you drive, and your driving conditions. Your owner’s manual can give you detailed information on common service tasks for your specific model and trim, but here’s what BMW owners can generally expect:

- **Every 10,000 miles** (or yearly): replace your vehicle’s engine oil, oil filter, and coolant.
- **Every 20,000 miles** (or every two years): inspect and replace your vehicle’s fuel filters.
- **Every 30,000 miles** (or every three years): replace your vehicle’s brake fluid (after the first replacement, **every 60,000 miles**) and replace your vehicle’s transmission fluid on manual-transmission BMWs.
- **Every 60,000 miles** (or every six years): replace your vehicle’s engine air filter and spark plugs, inspect and replace any brake pads and brake rotors, and replace transmission fluid on automatic-transmission BMWs.
- **Every 90,000 miles** (or every nine years): replace your vehicle’s timing belts and hoses.

You’ll want to repeat the cycle above after 90,000 miles and always follow the 5,000-mile maintenance schedule. Your BMW’s New Vehicle Limited Warranty will also expire at 50,000 miles, so we recommend getting in any repairs or service before this warranty expires! We also recommend replacing your BMW battery around 50,000 miles.

## What is BMW Value Service?

BMW of Tigard understands that your BMW service isn’t a one-size-fits-all situation. That’s why we offer BMW’s [BMW Value Service](https://www.bmwtigard.com/value-service/) as an option for Lake Oswego drivers and beyond. No matter the miles on your BMW, you’ll receive the benefit of BMW-trained technicians, genuine BMW OEM parts, and up-front pricing. BMW Value Service applies to select services and models, so it’s important to [contact us today](https://www.bmwtigard.com/contact-us/) to see if your vehicle qualifies and to better understand the specific services available for your model and trim.

And with great options like our [specials](https://www.bmwtigard.com/service-parts-specials/) and BMW Value Service, it’s a no-brainer to choose BMW of Tigard as your BMW service center. # **BMW 5 Series Service Schedule**

Date: May 23rd, 2023

![Mechanic fixing BMW](https://dealerinspire-image-library-prod.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/images/cpmcf8Do0Qn84TSRDtGze4ovvPX8Gwbo1olQNgUa.jpg)

At BMW of Fort Lauderdale, we understand the importance of your BMW in your daily life, and our service team is here to ensure that it remains in top condition for all your adventures around Miami and Hollywood. If you’re wondering about the maintenance schedule for your [BMW 5 Series](https://www.bmwoffortlauderdale.com/new-vehicles/5-series/), our team has got you covered. We’ll provide you with all the information you need about the BMW 5 Series service schedule and to [schedule your next service appointment](https://consumer.xtime.com/scheduling/?webKey=bmw201507090323&skipRedirect=true&VARIANT=BMWUSA&WMODE=true). Let’s begin!

[Schedule Service](https://consumer.xtime.com/scheduling/?webKey=bmw201507090323&skipRedirect=true&VARIANT=BMWUSA&WMODE=true) [Contact BMW Service](https://www.bmwoffortlauderdale.com/service/contact-service/)

## BMW Ultimate Care

First things first, we dive into the BMW Ultimate Care plan, which is a 3-year or 36,000-mile complimentary BMW maintenance plan for eligible BMW 5 Series models. This care plan includes the following maintenance items:

- **Engine oil**
- **Oil filters**
- **Brake fluid**
- **Spark plug changes**

Additionally, with BMW Teleservices, you have the ability to contact our team at BMW of Fort Lauderdale when you are in need of service. You also get Unlimited Mileage Roadside Assistance for four years and 4-year/50,000-mile coverage under the new vehicle warranty. After getting familiar with the BMW Ultimate Care offerings, we’re going to cover the BMW 5 Series service schedule and when you can expect service.

## BMW 5 Series Service Schedule: 10,000 Miles

The BMW 5 Series uses a sensor-based maintenance guideline based on its Condition Based Service (CBS) system. Every 10,000 miles, the intuitive technology prompts an [oil change](https://www.bmwoffortlauderdale.com/service-and-parts-tips/bmw-oil-change-cost/) and tire rotation. Depending on driving conditions and frequency, other standard services may be detected. You can consult your BMW owner’s manual for more information on initial maintenance and decoding service lights. The intelligent CBS system will notify you of any upcoming service needs, but you can always contact our service department for assistance.

## BMW 5 Series Service Schedule: 30,000 Miles

At around 30,000 miles, it’s recommended to replace the brake fluid in your BMW 5 Series. It’s also a good idea to consider having the fuel filter changed, which typically occurs between 20,000 to 40,000 miles. Tasks performed at the first service interval may also be repeated:

- **Oil change**
- **Fluid level check**
- **Tire rotation**

## BMW 5 Series Service Schedule: 60,000 Miles

At 60,000 miles, it will be time for your BMW 5 Series to have its engine air filter and spark plugs replaced. In addition to the 60,000-mile service, the first two service intervals previously mentioned will also apply at this service appointment for your Coconut Creek vehicle.

## Follow Your BMW 5 Series Service Schedule with BMW of Fort Lauderdale!

[Maintaining your BMW 5 Series](https://www.bmwoffortlauderdale.com/service-and-parts-tips) is essential to keep it running smoothly and safely for years to come. Regular maintenance not only ensures a smooth ride but also gives you the peace of mind that your BMW is in top-notch condition. Neglecting maintenance can lead to future problems and compromise your safety. It is always advisable to schedule service at recommended intervals or whenever issues arise to avoid any potential risks.

## Engine Oil Filter

- Description:
Your Engine Oil Filter does exactly as the name suggests it filtrates the oil in your Nissan engine. As Motor oil circulates through and Reduces friction between engine parts, the filter Captures and traps impurities, so they won't reach your vehicle's engine.
While the engine Maintains your Nissan, it burns fuel and eventually makes things such as sludge and debris. If your vehicle cannot properly filter out these contaminants because you have a grimy or blocked Engine Oil Filter, these contaminants may blend w/ your oil and may lead to very pricey repair costs.
When your Nissan's Engine Oil Filter hasn't been replaced, it can become clogged due to excess excessive gunk. So what happens when an Engine Oil Filter becomes too dirty? Your fuel efficiency and fluid pressure may decLine, and your car's ventilation system may become damaged and begin to emit a burning oil smell.
But when is the best time to get a new Engine Oil Filter installed? Typically, your Engine Oil Filter change should occur as often as you change your engine oil. If you frequently take short trips or if you do tons of interstate driving, it's likely that you will need to change it out more frequently to Maintain your car's engine health.
Are you able to install your Engine Oil Filter on your own? Maybe, but it may require some tricky finagling through the engine in order to find the filter location.
Consult your Nissan owner's Manual before starting to prevent injuring yourself or ruining critical engine pieces. Overall, it may be better to have it installed by a licensed Nissan service center instead.
Help extend the life of your Nissan engine by buying a genuine OEM Engine Oil Filter From Nissan Parts and it will fit your vehicle seamlessly.

# BMW 3 Series Maintenance Schedule

![](https://dealerimages.dealereprocess.com/image/upload/3734739)

## Maintenance Schedule

Keeping up with your vehicle’s routine maintenance schedule is crucial to the health and longevity of your car. Routine maintenance services are done about once or twice a year, and are usually just a quick stop by the shop to change your oil and make sure everything is working properly.

**Here at BMW of Westchester we know how important it is to stay on top of these services in order to keep your car on the streets of Westchester County and Yonkers, NY, for years to come. Check out our breakdown of the BMW 3 Series maintenance schedule below!  [Schedule a service appointment](https://www.westchesterbmw.com/service-appointment/) for more assistance.**

## Annual Routine Maintenance Services

Your first[BMW 3 Series](https://www.westchesterbmw.com/search/new-bmw-3-series-white-plains-ny/?cy=10607&md=33&tp=new) routine maintenance service will happen about 6 months in, or once you hit around 5,000-10,000 miles, whichever happens to come first. This first service will be relatively quick. It will include:

- **An oil and filter change**

- **Tire rotation**

- **Brake inspection**


You’ll want to get these services done once or twice a year for the duration of the vehicle’s life.

Staying on top of your regular oil and oil filter changes is crucial to your car’s health because as your engine runs, tiny bits of dirt and dust will build up in it, which can cause excessive wear and tear.

**Additionally, yearly [tire rotations](https://www.westchesterbmw.com/service-appointment/) are important to maintain traction control, because they prevent your wheels from having uneven tread. Tread and traction control helps your vehicle stop quicker, and provides you with safer travels over rough terrain.**

![](https://dealerimages.dealereprocess.com/image/upload/3734763)

![](https://dealerimages.dealereprocess.com/image/upload/3734769)

## 30,000-Mile Maintenance Services

Once your BMW 3 Series hits 30,000 miles, it’s time to head back to the shop for a variety of inspections and maintenance care checks. To start, you’re going to need:

- **Your air filter changed, over time your air filter can become clogged, and a replacement will be needed in order for it to work at its best. If you travel in particularly dusty environments, you’ll want this changed around 15,000 miles rather than 30,000.**

- **Next, you’ll need your fuel filter inspected; your technician can perform a pressure test to determine if you’ll need it replaced.**


## 60,000-Mile Maintenance Services

Your 60,000-mile maintenance service will happen at around four or five years into ownership for the average driver. At this service, you’ll need:

- **Brake Rotor, Pads, and Shoes Inspections and Replacements**

- **Brake Fluid Replacement**

- **Coolant Replacement**

- **Transmission Fluid Replacement**

- **Your BMW 3 Series battery and brakes will start to wear out around the 60,000-mile mark, which is why it’s so important to get them inspected, and possibly replaced.**


![](https://dealerimages.dealereprocess.com/image/upload/3734756)

![](https://dealerimages.dealereprocess.com/image/upload/3734759)

## 90,000-Mile Maintenance Services

Your 90,000-mile maintenance check will include an inspection of your hoses, belts, and spark plugs. If they’re not up to par, they’ll need to be replaced. Additionally, you’ll also need to replace your power steering fluid to keep your steering wheel working properly. You should also get the following done:

- **Timing belt replacement**

- **Replace hoses**

- **Replace spark plugs**

- **Rotate rotors or replace rotors**

- **Fuel system cleaning**

- **Complete inspection**

### Bi-Annual Services

Your [BMW 3 Series](https://www.bmwtigard.com/new-vehicles/3-series/) is a finely-crafted piece of machinery, but it will still require routine service from time to time. Keeping up with the BMW 3 Series [maintenance schedule](https://www.bmwtigard.com/service/service-and-parts-tips/bmw-recommended-maintenance-schedule/) is a must if you want your vehicle to perform at its best for as long as possible. ## BMW 3 Series Service Schedule

The BMW 3 Series service schedule includes BMW 3 Series oil change intervals and more to help you track the maintenance your vehicle requires. Let’s break it down more in-depth below.

### Bi-Annual Services

The services listed below should be performed approximately 6 months after you take your new vehicle home, at the 5,000 to 10,000-mile mark. They should then be performed at least twice a year for the duration you own the vehicle.

- Oil and Filter Change
- Tire Rotation
- Brake Inspection

### Every 30,000 Miles

At the 30,000-mile mark in the BMW 3 Series maintenance schedule, you’ll want to head back to the shop for a variety of inspections and maintenance care checks.

- Air filter changes: Air filters get clogged over time, so at this point, they are no longer working at their best. If you travel in particularly dusty environments, you’ll want to change the filter approximately every 15,000 miles.
- Fuel filter inspection: Your technician can perform a pressure test to determine if the fuel filter needs replacement.

### Every 60,000 Miles

Your 60,000-mile maintenance service will happen at around four or five years into ownership for the average driver. Here is what it will include:

- Brake Rotor, Pads, and Shoes Inspections and Replacements
- Brake Fluid Replacement
- Coolant Replacement
- Transmission Fluid Replacement

Keep in mind that this is also around the time your battery will start wearing down, so it is a good idea to have it looked at and possibly replaced.

### Every 90,000 Miles

At this service interval, we will take care of inspecting hoses, belts, and spark plugs. Power steering fluid should also be replaced when we perform these tasks:

- Timing belt replacement
- Replace hoses
- Replace spark plugs
- Rotate rotors or replace rotors
- Fuel system cleaning
- Complete inspection
