# BMW SERVICE

BMW recommends you have your maintenance and repair work performed by an authorized BMW center.

# MAINTAINING YOUR BMW VEHICLE

A well-maintained vehicle will help safeguard its operational performance, road-safety and its reliability. This is why it is important to follow and perform BMW’s recommended periodic vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks as indicated by your vehicle’s Maintenance Service Display, along with the other maintenance work described in this booklet.

A improper maintenance is not covered under the BMW New Vehicle Damage, including consequential damage, which results from lack of or Limited Warranty for Passenger Cars and Light Trucks.

# MAINTENANCE INTERVALS

Maintenance intervals on motor vehicles were conventionally based solely on a fixed time period or a specified amount of accumulated driving mileage.

However, operational and driving conditions have a major influence on your vehicle’s routine maintenance requirements; the distance traveled is only one of these significant factors. A vehicle used for short trips in the city with numerous cold starts, prolonged periods of idling, stop-and-go driving, and high engine speeds during acceleration may require more frequent maintenance intervals than a vehicle that is driven long distances at moderate engine speeds.

Your BMW vehicle uses sensors and algorithms together with the elapsed time and the driving distance/profile to monitor and evaluate your vehicle’s maintenance service needs. This information is then used to adapt dynamically the parameters used to forecast the applicable maintenance service task intervals.

# THE BMW MAINTENANCE SYSTEM

All BMW vehicles are equipped with an integrated BMW Maintenance System. This maintenance “reminder” system helps ensure that the vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks are performed at the forecasted intervals that apply to your vehicle.

The BMW Maintenance System display provides the vehicle operator access to the current status information for the following maintenance service tasks:

$\\triangleright$ Engine oil (date and miles)\*

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle check (date and miles)

$\\triangleright$ Front brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Rear brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid (date)

$\\triangleright$ 1200 Mile running-in service (date and miles) (Applicable to BMW M vehicles only)\*

For each specific maintenance service task, either the future date (month/ year), remaining miles or both are provided as noted above. The system monitors variable inputs to forecast the intervals and alert the driver when one or more specific maintenance tasks should be performed.

NOTE: For certain vehicles, the status of the front and rear brake pads will only be observable in the maintenance system’s display when there are approximately 2,000 miles or less remaining before a brake service will be required to be performed.

For information about the vehicle’s maintenance system displays, please refer to the Maintenance Service Display Overview section beginning on page 5.

The following “combine with Engine oil”\* maintenance service tasks may be identified as needing to be performed with a specific occurrence of the “Engine oil” service task (service counter number):

$\\triangleright$ Cabin Microfilter(s)

$\\triangleright$ Engine air filter(s)\*

$\\triangleright$ Spark plugs\*

$\\triangleright$ Final drive oil (Applicable M vehicles only)

\\* Does not apply to BEV

Although these items do not appear in the BMW Maintenance System’s display in the vehicle, these services should be performed when your vehicle’s engine oil is changed in accordance with the interval identified by your vehicle’s BMW Maintenance System.

For more information on your vehicle’s maintenance services requirements, procedures and intervals, please refer the Maintenance Service Summary section beginning on page 10.

The BMW Maintenance System also includes an option to set service reminders for the following state-specific mandatory vehicle inspections, including:

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle safety inspection; and/or $\\triangleright$ Emissions test

The corresponding interval data for these inspections can be inputted into the BMW Maintenance System by a service provider; they are not determined by the vehicle.

For your convenience, you may also wish to have your authorized BMW center perform the work necessary to fulfill these state inspection requirements in your area concurrent with the maintenance services specified above when possible.

Should you request more frequent maintenance service than is indicated by the BMW Maintenance System during the coverage period, the cost of these services will not be covered by the BMW Maintenance Program.

# SERVICE DATA — REMOTE CONTROL KEY

Maintenance service task status information for your BMW vehicle is continually updated and stored in your remote control key.

Your authorized BMW center can access this data and consult with you about applicable service procedures and tasks for your vehicle.

Therefore, always provide your service consultant with the most recent remote control key that was used to operate the vehicle when servicing your vehicle at a BMW center.

# VEHICLE STORAGE

Disconnecting the battery during periods of long-term vehicle storage will interrupt the calculation of time-dependent maintenance services.

In this situation, BMW recommends that you have all your time-based maintenance services, such as brake fluid, engine oil and cabin microfilter, brought up to the correct date by an authorized BMW center.

# ENGINE OIL

2025 model year vehicles with internal-combustion engines are factory-filled with:

Z BMW-approved fully synthetic oil for gasoline engines

Engine oil should be changed when the vehicle’s engine is at operating temperature.

If an engine oil service is being performed or you need to add engine oil between changes, please refer to the Owner’s Manual for the recommended engine oil for your BMW vehicle.

# LONG-TERM RATED FLUIDS AND OILS

The following systems and assemblies are factory-filled with long-term rated fluid and oil; fluid replacement is only necessary when repairs are being performed (unless otherwise noted):

$\\triangleright$ Engine cooling system (antifreeze/coolant) $\\triangleright$ Automatic (except for X1 and X2) and manual transmissions $\\triangleright$ All-wheel drive transfer cases (except when indicated by the vehicle)

# REGULAR CHECKS — VEHICLE OPERATOR

In addition to the maintenance service procedure information contained in this booklet, BMW recommends that you regularly check (when refueling, for example), and address when necessary, the following items:

$\\triangleright$ Washer fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Coolant level

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Tires — pressure, condition and wear

Please refer to the Owner’s Manual for additional information.

# BMW 3 Series Maintenance Schedule

![](https://dealerimages.dealereprocess.com/image/upload/3734739)

## Maintenance Schedule

Keeping up with your vehicle’s routine maintenance schedule is crucial to the health and longevity of your car. Routine maintenance services are done about once or twice a year, and are usually just a quick stop by the shop to change your oil and make sure everything is working properly.

**Here at BMW of Westchester we know how important it is to stay on top of these services in order to keep your car on the streets of Westchester County and Yonkers, NY, for years to come. Check out our breakdown of the BMW 3 Series maintenance schedule below!  [Schedule a service appointment](https://www.westchesterbmw.com/service-appointment/) for more assistance.**

## Annual Routine Maintenance Services

Your first[BMW 3 Series](https://www.westchesterbmw.com/search/new-bmw-3-series-white-plains-ny/?cy=10607&md=33&tp=new) routine maintenance service will happen about 6 months in, or once you hit around 5,000-10,000 miles, whichever happens to come first. This first service will be relatively quick. It will include:

- **An oil and filter change**

- **Tire rotation**

- **Brake inspection**


You’ll want to get these services done once or twice a year for the duration of the vehicle’s life.

Staying on top of your regular oil and oil filter changes is crucial to your car’s health because as your engine runs, tiny bits of dirt and dust will build up in it, which can cause excessive wear and tear.

**Additionally, yearly [tire rotations](https://www.westchesterbmw.com/service-appointment/) are important to maintain traction control, because they prevent your wheels from having uneven tread. Tread and traction control helps your vehicle stop quicker, and provides you with safer travels over rough terrain.**

![](https://dealerimages.dealereprocess.com/image/upload/3734763)

![](https://dealerimages.dealereprocess.com/image/upload/3734769)

## 30,000-Mile Maintenance Services

Once your BMW 3 Series hits 30,000 miles, it’s time to head back to the shop for a variety of inspections and maintenance care checks. To start, you’re going to need:

- **Your air filter changed, over time your air filter can become clogged, and a replacement will be needed in order for it to work at its best. If you travel in particularly dusty environments, you’ll want this changed around 15,000 miles rather than 30,000.**

- **Next, you’ll need your fuel filter inspected; your technician can perform a pressure test to determine if you’ll need it replaced.**


## 60,000-Mile Maintenance Services

Your 60,000-mile maintenance service will happen at around four or five years into ownership for the average driver. At this service, you’ll need:

- **Brake Rotor, Pads, and Shoes Inspections and Replacements**

- **Brake Fluid Replacement**

- **Coolant Replacement**

- **Transmission Fluid Replacement**

- **Your BMW 3 Series battery and brakes will start to wear out around the 60,000-mile mark, which is why it’s so important to get them inspected, and possibly replaced.**


![](https://dealerimages.dealereprocess.com/image/upload/3734756)

![](https://dealerimages.dealereprocess.com/image/upload/3734759)

## 90,000-Mile Maintenance Services

Your 90,000-mile maintenance check will include an inspection of your hoses, belts, and spark plugs. If they’re not up to par, they’ll need to be replaced. Additionally, you’ll also need to replace your power steering fluid to keep your steering wheel working properly. You should also get the following done:

- **Timing belt replacement**

- **Replace hoses**

- **Replace spark plugs**

- **Rotate rotors or replace rotors**

- **Fuel system cleaning**

- **Complete inspection**

Your [BMW 3 Series](https://www.bmwtigard.com/new-vehicles/3-series/) is a finely-crafted piece of machinery, but it will still require routine service from time to time. Keeping up with the BMW 3 Series [maintenance schedule](https://www.bmwtigard.com/service/service-and-parts-tips/bmw-recommended-maintenance-schedule/) is a must if you want your vehicle to perform at its best for as long as possible. We understand that keeping track of BMW 3 Series oil change intervals and more can be a challenge. That is why we have created this guide to the BMW 3 Series service schedule. Simply follow this guide, and your vehicle should be prepared and safe for the roads of Portland and Tigard.

## BMW 3 Series Service Schedule

The BMW 3 Series service schedule includes BMW 3 Series oil change intervals and more to help you track the maintenance your vehicle requires. Let’s break it down more in-depth below.

### Bi-Annual Services

The services listed below should be performed approximately 6 months after you take your new vehicle home, at the 5,000 to 10,000-mile mark. They should then be performed at least twice a year for the duration you own the vehicle.

- Oil and Filter Change
- Tire Rotation
- Brake Inspection

### Every 30,000 Miles

At the 30,000-mile mark in the BMW 3 Series maintenance schedule, you’ll want to head back to the shop for a variety of inspections and maintenance care checks.

- Air filter changes: Air filters get clogged over time, so at this point, they are no longer working at their best. If you travel in particularly dusty environments, you’ll want to change the filter approximately every 15,000 miles.
- Fuel filter inspection: Your technician can perform a pressure test to determine if the fuel filter needs replacement.

### Every 60,000 Miles

Your 60,000-mile maintenance service will happen at around four or five years into ownership for the average driver. Here is what it will include:

- Brake Rotor, Pads, and Shoes Inspections and Replacements
- Brake Fluid Replacement
- Coolant Replacement
- Transmission Fluid Replacement

Keep in mind that this is also around the time your battery will start wearing down, so it is a good idea to have it looked at and possibly replaced.

### Every 90,000 Miles

At this service interval, we will take care of inspecting hoses, belts, and spark plugs. Power steering fluid should also be replaced when we perform these tasks:

- Timing belt replacement
- Replace hoses
- Replace spark plugs
- Rotate rotors or replace rotors
- Fuel system cleaning
- Complete inspection

For more information on your vehicle’s maintenance services requirements, procedures and intervals, please refer the Maintenance Service Summary section beginning on page 10.

The BMW Maintenance System also includes an option to set service reminders for the following state-specific mandatory vehicle inspections, including:

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle safety inspection; and/or $\\triangleright$ Emissions test

The corresponding interval data for these inspections can be inputted into the BMW Maintenance System by a service provider; they are not determined by the vehicle.

For your convenience, you may also wish to have your authorized BMW center perform the work necessary to fulfill these state inspection requirements in your area concurrent with the maintenance services specified above when possible.

Should you request more frequent maintenance service than is indicated by the BMW Maintenance System during the coverage period, the cost of these services will not be covered by the BMW Maintenance Program.

# SERVICE DATA — REMOTE CONTROL KEY

Maintenance service task status information for your BMW vehicle is continually updated and stored in your remote control key.

Your authorized BMW center can access this data and consult with you about applicable service procedures and tasks for your vehicle.

Therefore, always provide your service consultant with the most recent remote control key that was used to operate the vehicle when servicing your vehicle at a BMW center.

# VEHICLE STORAGE

Disconnecting the battery during periods of long-term vehicle storage will interrupt the calculation of time-dependent maintenance services.

In this situation, BMW recommends that you have all your time-based maintenance services, such as brake fluid, engine oil and cabin microfilter, brought up to the correct date by an authorized BMW center.

# ENGINE OIL

2025 model year vehicles with internal-combustion engines are factory-filled with:

Z BMW-approved fully synthetic oil for gasoline engines

Engine oil should be changed when the vehicle’s engine is at operating temperature.

If an engine oil service is being performed or you need to add engine oil between changes, please refer to the Owner’s Manual for the recommended engine oil for your BMW vehicle.

# LONG-TERM RATED FLUIDS AND OILS

The following systems and assemblies are factory-filled with long-term rated fluid and oil; fluid replacement is only necessary when repairs are being performed (unless otherwise noted):

$\\triangleright$ Engine cooling system (antifreeze/coolant) $\\triangleright$ Automatic (except for X1 and X2) and manual transmissions $\\triangleright$ All-wheel drive transfer cases (except when indicated by the vehicle)

# REGULAR CHECKS — VEHICLE OPERATOR

In addition to the maintenance service procedure information contained in this booklet, BMW recommends that you regularly check (when refueling, for example), and address when necessary, the following items:

$\\triangleright$ Washer fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Coolant level

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Tires — pressure, condition and wear

Please refer to the Owner’s Manual for additional information.

## BMW 3 Series Service Schedule

The BMW 3 Series service schedule includes BMW 3 Series oil change intervals and more to help you track the maintenance your vehicle requires. Let’s break it down more in-depth below.

### Bi-Annual Services

The services listed below should be performed approximately 6 months after you take your new vehicle home, at the 5,000 to 10,000-mile mark. They should then be performed at least twice a year for the duration you own the vehicle.

- Oil and Filter Change
- Tire Rotation
- Brake Inspection

### Every 30,000 Miles

At the 30,000-mile mark in the BMW 3 Series maintenance schedule, you’ll want to head back to the shop for a variety of inspections and maintenance care checks.

- Air filter changes: Air filters get clogged over time, so at this point, they are no longer working at their best. If you travel in particularly dusty environments, you’ll want to change the filter approximately every 15,000 miles.
- Fuel filter inspection: Your technician can perform a pressure test to determine if the fuel filter needs replacement.

### Every 60,000 Miles

Your 60,000-mile maintenance service will happen at around four or five years into ownership for the average driver. Here is what it will include:

- Brake Rotor, Pads, and Shoes Inspections and Replacements
- Brake Fluid Replacement
- Coolant Replacement
- Transmission Fluid Replacement

Keep in mind that this is also around the time your battery will start wearing down, so it is a good idea to have it looked at and possibly replaced.

### Every 90,000 Miles

At this service interval, we will take care of inspecting hoses, belts, and spark plugs. Power steering fluid should also be replaced when we perform these tasks:

- Timing belt replacement
- Replace hoses
- Replace spark plugs
- Rotate rotors or replace rotors
- Fuel system cleaning
- Complete inspection

# BMW SERVICE

BMW recommends you have your maintenance and repair work performed by an authorized BMW center.

# MAINTAINING YOUR BMW VEHICLE

A well-maintained vehicle will help safeguard its operational performance, road-safety and its reliability. This is why it is important to follow and perform BMW’s recommended periodic vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks as indicated by your vehicle’s Maintenance Service Display, along with the other maintenance work described in this booklet.

A improper maintenance is not covered under the BMW New Vehicle Damage, including consequential damage, which results from lack of or Limited Warranty for Passenger Cars and Light Trucks.

# MAINTENANCE INTERVALS

Maintenance intervals on motor vehicles were conventionally based solely on a fixed time period or a specified amount of accumulated driving mileage.

However, operational and driving conditions have a major influence on your vehicle’s routine maintenance requirements; the distance traveled is only one of these significant factors. A vehicle used for short trips in the city with numerous cold starts, prolonged periods of idling, stop-and-go driving, and high engine speeds during acceleration may require more frequent maintenance intervals than a vehicle that is driven long distances at moderate engine speeds.

Your BMW vehicle uses sensors and algorithms together with the elapsed time and the driving distance/profile to monitor and evaluate your vehicle’s maintenance service needs. This information is then used to adapt dynamically the parameters used to forecast the applicable maintenance service task intervals.

# THE BMW MAINTENANCE SYSTEM

All BMW vehicles are equipped with an integrated BMW Maintenance System. This maintenance “reminder” system helps ensure that the vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks are performed at the forecasted intervals that apply to your vehicle.

The BMW Maintenance System display provides the vehicle operator access to the current status information for the following maintenance service tasks:

$\\triangleright$ Engine oil (date and miles)\*

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle check (date and miles)

$\\triangleright$ Front brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Rear brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid (date)

Z 1200 Mile running-in service (date and miles) (Applicable to BMW M vehicles only)\*

For each specific maintenance service task, either the future date (month/ year), remaining miles or both are provided as noted above. The system monitors variable inputs to forecast the intervals and alert the driver when one or more specific maintenance tasks should be performed.

NOTE: For certain vehicles, the status of the front and rear brake pads will only be observable in the maintenance system’s display when there are approximately 2,000 miles or less remaining before a brake service will be required to be performed.

For information about the vehicle’s maintenance system displays, please refer to the Maintenance Service Display Overview section beginning on page 5.

The following “combine with Engine oil”\* maintenance service tasks may be identified as needing to be performed with a specific occurrence of the “Engine oil” service task (service counter number):

$\\triangleright$ Cabin Microfilter(s)

$\\triangleright$ Engine air filter(s)\*

$\\triangleright$ Spark plugs\*

$\\triangleright$ Final drive oil (Applicable M vehicles only)

\\* Does not apply to BEV

Although these items do not appear in the BMW Maintenance System’s display in the vehicle, these services should be performed when your vehicle’s engine oil is changed in accordance with the interval identified by your vehicle’s BMW Maintenance System.

For more information on your vehicle’s maintenance services requirements, procedures and intervals, please refer the Maintenance Service Summary section beginning on page 10.

The BMW Maintenance System also includes an option to set service reminders for the following state-specific mandatory vehicle inspections, including:

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle safety inspection; and/or $\\triangleright$ Emissions test

The corresponding interval data for these inspections can be inputted into the BMW Maintenance System by a service provider; they are not determined by the vehicle.

For your convenience, you may also wish to have your authorized BMW center perform the work necessary to fulfill these state inspection requirements in your area concurrent with the maintenance services specified above when possible.

Should you request more frequent maintenance service than is indicated by the BMW Maintenance System during the coverage period, the cost of these services will not be covered by the BMW Maintenance Program.

# SERVICE DATA — REMOTE CONTROL KEY

Maintenance service task status information for your BMW vehicle is continually updated and stored in your remote control key.

Your authorized BMW center can access this data and consult with you about applicable service procedures and tasks for your vehicle.

Therefore, always provide your service consultant with the most recent remote control key that was used to operate the vehicle when servicing your vehicle at a BMW center.

# VEHICLE STORAGE

Disconnecting the battery during periods of long-term vehicle storage will interrupt the calculation of time-dependent maintenance services.

In this situation, BMW recommends that you have all your time-based maintenance services, such as brake fluid, engine oil and cabin microfilter, brought up to the correct date by an authorized BMW center.

# ENGINE OIL

2026 model year vehicles with internal-combustion engines are factory-filled with:

Z BMW-approved fully synthetic oil for gasoline engines

Engine oil should be changed when the vehicle’s engine is at operating temperature.

If an engine oil service is being performed or you need to add engine oil between changes, please refer to the Owner’s Manual for the recommended engine oil for your BMW vehicle.

# LONG-TERM RATED FLUIDS AND OILS

### Preserving the Executive Standard.

Owning a [**2026 BMW 5 Series**](https://www.bmwofmilwaukeenorth.com/new-vehicles/5-series/) in Milwaukee requires a proactive approach to maintenance. The G60 chassis, whether equipped with the B48 4-cylinder (530i) or the B58 6-cylinder (540i/550e), is engineered for high-mileage longevity, provided it receives specific care.

Unlike older vehicles with rigid fixed intervals, your 5 Series utilizes Condition Based Service (CBS). This system uses sensors to monitor oil life, brake pad wear, and fluid quality in real-time, adapting service requirements based on how you drive. However, given our extreme Wisconsin climate, ranging from sub-zero cold starts to humid summers, we recommend adhering to a baseline schedule to ensure peak performance.

### The G60 Service Intervals.

While the CBS system will alert you via the iDrive 8.5 display when service is due, the following timeline serves as the engineering standard for long-term reliability.

#### Every 10,000 Miles (or 12 Months).

This is the “Standard Scope” service. It establishes the baseline for engine health.

- **Synthetic Oil Change:** Replacement of engine oil and filter. The B48 and B58 engines rely on clean oil not just for lubrication, but to actuate the VANOS variable valve timing system.
- **Tire Rotation:** Critical for xDrive models to ensure even tread wear and prevent strain on the transfer case.
- **Safety Inspection:** Verification of fluid levels, wiper blades, and brake pad thickness.

#### Every 30,000 Miles.

At this interval, we address hydraulic and filtration systems that degrade over time.

- **Brake Fluid Flush:** BMW brake fluid is hygroscopic (absorbs moisture). Flushing it prevents internal corrosion of the ABS module and maintains a firm pedal feel.
- **Cabin Microfilter:** Replacement is necessary to maintain airflow and remove allergens/dust from the HVAC system.

#### Every 60,000 Miles.

This is a major service milestone for the G60 chassis.

- **Spark Plugs:** Worn plugs can cause misfires and stress the ignition coils. Replacement restores optimal combustion efficiency.
- **Engine Air Filter:** A clean filter allows the turbocharger to breathe freely, maintaining throttle response.
- **Sunroof Drain Check:** Essential for vehicles parked outside to prevent water ingress during heavy storms.

### Engine-Specific Care: B48 vs. B58.

While both engines share a modular architecture, they have distinct long-term ownership considerations.

| #### B48 (530i) Considerations. | #### B58 (540i & 550e) Considerations. |
| --- | --- |
| ![2026 BMW 530i and 540i trim](https://di-uploads-pod44.dealerinspire.com/bmwofmilwaukeenorth/uploads/2026/02/530i-models-and-540i-xdrive.jpg) | ![2026 BMW 550e xDrive Trim](https://di-uploads-pod44.dealerinspire.com/bmwofmilwaukeenorth/uploads/2026/02/550e-xdrive-model.jpg) |
| The 2.0-liter B48 is a robust “baby B58,” but it operates under higher boost pressure relative to its displacement.<br>- **Coolant Circuit:** Owners should periodically check coolant levels. The system is complex, featuring multiple cooling circuits, and low levels can trigger “drivetrain malfunction” warnings.<br>- **Oil Filter Housing:** Over high mileage (typically 60k+), the plastic composite oil filter housing can become brittle from heat cycles. We inspect this component at every oil change to catch early signs of weeping. | The 3.0-liter B58 is legendary for its “bulletproof” internals, but external gaskets require monitoring.<br>- **Valve Cover Gasket:** As the engine approaches higher mileage (70k+), the valve cover gasket is a known wear item. Keeping fresh oil in the engine helps preserve the pliability of these seals.<br>- **VANOS Solenoids:** These solenoids control valve timing using oil pressure. Regular oil changes are the single best way to prevent sludge buildup that can restrict their operation. |

# BMW SERVICE

BMW recommends you have your maintenance and repair work performed by an authorized BMW center.

# MAINTAINING YOUR BMW VEHICLE

A well-maintained vehicle will help safeguard its operational performance, road-safety and its reliability. This is why it is important to follow and perform BMW’s recommended periodic vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks as indicated by your vehicle’s Maintenance Service Display, along with the other maintenance work described in this booklet.

A improper maintenance is not covered under the BMW New Vehicle Damage, including consequential damage, which results from lack of or Limited Warranty for Passenger Cars and Light Trucks.

# MAINTENANCE INTERVALS

Maintenance intervals on motor vehicles were conventionally based solely on a fixed time period or a specified amount of accumulated driving mileage.

However, operational and driving conditions have a major influence on your vehicle’s routine maintenance requirements; the distance traveled is only one of these significant factors. A vehicle used for short trips in the city with numerous cold starts, prolonged periods of idling, stop-and-go driving, and high engine speeds during acceleration may require more frequent maintenance intervals than a vehicle that is driven long distances at moderate engine speeds.

Your BMW vehicle uses sensors and algorithms together with the elapsed time and the driving distance/profile to monitor and evaluate your vehicle’s maintenance service needs. This information is then used to adapt dynamically the parameters used to forecast the applicable maintenance service task intervals.

# THE BMW MAINTENANCE SYSTEM

All BMW vehicles are equipped with an integrated BMW Maintenance System. This maintenance “reminder” system helps ensure that the vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks are performed at the forecasted intervals that apply to your vehicle.

The BMW Maintenance System display provides the vehicle operator access to the current status information for the following maintenance service tasks:

$\\triangleright$ Engine oil (date and miles)\*

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle check (date and miles)

$\\triangleright$ Front brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Rear brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid (date)

Z 1200 Mile running-in service (date and miles) (Applicable to BMW M vehicles only)\*

For each specific maintenance service task, either the future date (month/ year), remaining miles or both are provided as noted above. The system monitors variable inputs to forecast the intervals and alert the driver when one or more specific maintenance tasks should be performed.

NOTE: For certain vehicles, the status of the front and rear brake pads will only be observable in the maintenance system’s display when there are approximately 2,000 miles or less remaining before a brake service will be required to be performed.

For information about the vehicle’s maintenance system displays, please refer to the Maintenance Service Display Overview section beginning on page 5.

The following “combine with Engine oil”\* maintenance service tasks may be identified as needing to be performed with a specific occurrence of the “Engine oil” service task (service counter number):

$\\triangleright$ Cabin Microfilter(s)

$\\triangleright$ Engine air filter(s)\*

$\\triangleright$ Spark plugs\*

$\\triangleright$ Final drive oil (Applicable M vehicles only)

\\* Does not apply to BEV

Although these items do not appear in the BMW Maintenance System’s display in the vehicle, these services should be performed when your vehicle’s engine oil is changed in accordance with the interval identified by your vehicle’s BMW Maintenance System.

For more information on your vehicle’s maintenance services requirements, procedures and intervals, please refer the Maintenance Service Summary section beginning on page 10.

The BMW Maintenance System also includes an option to set service reminders for the following state-specific mandatory vehicle inspections, including:

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle safety inspection; and/or $\\triangleright$ Emissions test

The corresponding interval data for these inspections can be inputted into the BMW Maintenance System by a service provider; they are not determined by the vehicle.

For your convenience, you may also wish to have your authorized BMW center perform the work necessary to fulfill these state inspection requirements in your area concurrent with the maintenance services specified above when possible.

Should you request more frequent maintenance service than is indicated by the BMW Maintenance System during the coverage period, the cost of these services will not be covered by the BMW Maintenance Program.

# SERVICE DATA — REMOTE CONTROL KEY

Maintenance service task status information for your BMW vehicle is continually updated and stored in your remote control key.

Your authorized BMW center can access this data and consult with you about applicable service procedures and tasks for your vehicle.

# MAINTAINING YOUR BMW VEHICLE

A well-maintained vehicle will help safeguard its operational performance, road-safety and its reliability. This is why it is important to follow and perform BMW’s recommended periodic vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks as indicated by your vehicle’s Maintenance Service Display, along with the other maintenance work described in this booklet.

A improper maintenance is not covered under the BMW New Vehicle Damage, including consequential damage, which results from lack of or Limited Warranty for Passenger Cars and Light Trucks.

# MAINTENANCE INTERVALS

Maintenance intervals on motor vehicles were conventionally based solely on a fixed time period or a specified amount of accumulated driving mileage.

However, operational and driving conditions have a major influence on your vehicle’s routine maintenance requirements; the distance traveled is only one of these significant factors. A vehicle used for short trips in the city with numerous cold starts, prolonged periods of idling, stop-and-go driving, and high engine speeds during acceleration may require more frequent maintenance intervals than a vehicle that is driven long distances at moderate engine speeds.

Your BMW vehicle uses sensors and algorithms together with the elapsed time and the driving distance/profile to monitor and evaluate your vehicle’s maintenance service needs. This information is then used to adapt dynamically the parameters used to forecast the applicable maintenance service task intervals.

# THE BMW MAINTENANCE SYSTEM

All BMW vehicles are equipped with an integrated BMW Maintenance System. This maintenance “reminder” system helps ensure that the vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks are performed at the forecasted intervals that apply to your vehicle.

The BMW Maintenance System display provides the vehicle operator access to the current status information for the following maintenance service tasks:

$\\triangleright$ Engine oil (date and miles)\*

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle check (date and miles)

$\\triangleright$ Front brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Rear brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid (date)

$\\triangleright$ 1200 Mile running-in service (date and miles) (Applicable to BMW M vehicles only)\*

For each specific maintenance service task, either the future date (month/ year), remaining miles or both are provided as noted above. The system monitors variable inputs to forecast the intervals and alert the driver when one or more specific maintenance tasks should be performed.

NOTE: For certain vehicles, the status of the front and rear brake pads will only be observable in the maintenance system’s display when there are approximately 2,000 miles or less remaining before a brake service will be required to be performed.

For information about the vehicle’s maintenance system displays, please refer to the Maintenance Service Display Overview section beginning on page 5.

The following “combine with Engine oil”\* maintenance service tasks may be identified as needing to be performed with a specific occurrence of the “Engine oil” service task (service counter number):

$\\triangleright$ Cabin Microfilter(s)

$\\triangleright$ Engine air filter(s)\*

$\\triangleright$ Spark plugs\*

$\\triangleright$ Final drive oil (Applicable M vehicles only)

\\* Does not apply to BEV

Although these items do not appear in the BMW Maintenance System’s display in the vehicle, these services should be performed when your vehicle’s engine oil is changed in accordance with the interval identified by your vehicle’s BMW Maintenance System.

For more information on your vehicle’s maintenance services requirements, procedures and intervals, please refer the Maintenance Service Summary section beginning on page 10.

The BMW Maintenance System also includes an option to set service reminders for the following state-specific mandatory vehicle inspections, including:

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle safety inspection; and/or $\\triangleright$ Emissions test

The corresponding interval data for these inspections can be inputted into the BMW Maintenance System by a service provider; they are not determined by the vehicle.

For your convenience, you may also wish to have your authorized BMW center perform the work necessary to fulfill these state inspection requirements in your area concurrent with the maintenance services specified above when possible.

Should you request more frequent maintenance service than is indicated by the BMW Maintenance System during the coverage period, the cost of these services will not be covered by the BMW Maintenance Program.

# SERVICE DATA — REMOTE CONTROL KEY

Maintenance service task status information for your BMW vehicle is continually updated and stored in your remote control key.

Your authorized BMW center can access this data and consult with you about applicable service procedures and tasks for your vehicle.

Therefore, always provide your service consultant with the most recent remote control key that was used to operate the vehicle when servicing your vehicle at a BMW center.

## BMW Preventative Maintenance: Every 5,000 Miles / 6 Months

It’s important to bring in your BMW two or three times a year (or every 5,000 miles) for these preventative maintenance services:

- Front and rear brake inspection
- Brake fluid check
- Coolant check
- Engine oil check
- Cabin air filter inspection
- Engine inspection
- Vehicle inspection
- Wiper blade inspection
- Any necessary tire rotations

Your BMW also comes with something called the Condition-Based Service Monitor (CBS). Your CBS tracks the condition of important systems in your BMW, letting you know if service is required. Our technicians will also use your CBS to determine what needs to be replaced, repaired, or serviced when you schedule service. Keep in mind that just because your CBS may say that service may not be necessary at 5,000 miles doesn’t mean that you shouldn’t come in for preventative maintenance and checks. Sometimes human eyes are necessary to determine a problem or to nip any potential issues in the bud.

## Recommended BMW Maintenance Schedule

Your BMW service schedule needs will vary based on how often you drive, where you drive, and your driving conditions. Your owner’s manual can give you detailed information on common service tasks for your specific model and trim, but here’s what BMW owners can generally expect:

- **Every 10,000 miles** (or yearly): replace your vehicle’s engine oil, oil filter, and coolant.
- **Every 20,000 miles** (or every two years): inspect and replace your vehicle’s fuel filters.
- **Every 30,000 miles** (or every three years): replace your vehicle’s brake fluid (after the first replacement, **every 60,000 miles**) and replace your vehicle’s transmission fluid on manual-transmission BMWs.
- **Every 60,000 miles** (or every six years): replace your vehicle’s engine air filter and spark plugs, inspect and replace any brake pads and brake rotors, and replace transmission fluid on automatic-transmission BMWs.
- **Every 90,000 miles** (or every nine years): replace your vehicle’s timing belts and hoses.

You’ll want to repeat the cycle above after 90,000 miles and always follow the 5,000-mile maintenance schedule. Your BMW’s New Vehicle Limited Warranty will also expire at 50,000 miles, so we recommend getting in any repairs or service before this warranty expires! We also recommend replacing your BMW battery around 50,000 miles.

# BMW SERVICE

BMW recommends you have your maintenance and repair work performed by an authorized BMW center.

# MAINTAINING YOUR BMW VEHICLE

A well-maintained vehicle will help safeguard its operational performance, road-safety and its reliability. This is why it is important to follow and perform BMW’s recommended periodic vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks as indicated by your vehicle’s Maintenance Service Display, along with the other maintenance work described in this booklet.

A improper maintenance is not covered under the BMW New Vehicle Damage, including consequential damage, which results from lack of or Limited Warranty for Passenger Cars and Light Trucks.

# MAINTENANCE INTERVALS

Maintenance intervals on motor vehicles were conventionally based solely on a fixed time period or a specified amount of accumulated driving mileage.

However, operational and driving conditions have a major influence on your vehicle’s routine maintenance requirements; the distance traveled is only one of these significant factors. A vehicle used for short trips in the city with numerous cold starts, prolonged periods of idling, stop-and-go driving, and high engine speeds during acceleration may require more frequent maintenance intervals than a vehicle that is driven long distances at moderate engine speeds.

Your BMW vehicle uses sensors and algorithms together with the elapsed time and the driving distance/profile to monitor and evaluate your vehicle’s maintenance service needs. This information is then used to adapt dynamically the parameters used to forecast the applicable maintenance service task intervals.

# THE BMW MAINTENANCE SYSTEM

All BMW vehicles are equipped with an integrated BMW Maintenance System. This maintenance “reminder” system helps ensure that the vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks are performed at the forecasted intervals that apply to your vehicle.

The BMW Maintenance System display provides the vehicle operator access to the current status information for the following maintenance service tasks:

$\\triangleright$ Engine oil (date and miles)\*

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle check (date and miles)

$\\triangleright$ Front brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Rear brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid (date)

$\\triangleright$ 1200 Mile running-in service (date and miles) (Applicable to BMW M vehicles only)\*

For each specific maintenance service task, either the future date (month/ year), remaining miles or both are provided as noted above. The system monitors variable inputs to forecast the intervals and alert the driver when one or more specific maintenance tasks should be performed.

NOTE: For certain vehicles, the status of the front and rear brake pads will only be observable in the maintenance system’s display when there are approximately 2,000 miles or less remaining before a brake service will be required to be performed.

For information about the vehicle’s maintenance system displays, please refer to the Maintenance Service Display Overview section beginning on page 5.

The following “combine with Engine oil”\* maintenance service tasks may be identified as needing to be performed with a specific occurrence of the “Engine oil” service task (service counter number):

$\\triangleright$ Cabin Microfilter(s)

$\\triangleright$ Engine air filter(s)\*

$\\triangleright$ Spark plugs\*

$\\triangleright$ Final drive oil (Applicable M vehicles only)

\\* Does not apply to BEV

Although these items do not appear in the BMW Maintenance System’s display in the vehicle, these services should be performed when your vehicle’s engine oil is changed in accordance with the interval identified by your vehicle’s BMW Maintenance System.

For more information on your vehicle’s maintenance services requirements, procedures and intervals, please refer the Maintenance Service Summary section beginning on page 10.

The BMW Maintenance System also includes an option to set service reminders for the following state-specific mandatory vehicle inspections, including:

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle safety inspection; and/or $\\triangleright$ Emissions test

The corresponding interval data for these inspections can be inputted into the BMW Maintenance System by a service provider; they are not determined by the vehicle.

For your convenience, you may also wish to have your authorized BMW center perform the work necessary to fulfill these state inspection requirements in your area concurrent with the maintenance services specified above when possible.

Should you request more frequent maintenance service than is indicated by the BMW Maintenance System during the coverage period, the cost of these services will not be covered by the BMW Maintenance Program.

# SERVICE DATA — REMOTE CONTROL KEY

Maintenance service task status information for your BMW vehicle is continually updated and stored in your remote control key.

Your authorized BMW center can access this data and consult with you about applicable service procedures and tasks for your vehicle.

Therefore, always provide your service consultant with the most recent remote control key that was used to operate the vehicle when servicing your vehicle at a BMW center.

# VEHICLE STORAGE

Disconnecting the battery during periods of long-term vehicle storage will interrupt the calculation of time-dependent maintenance services.

In this situation, BMW recommends that you have all your time-based maintenance services, such as brake fluid, engine oil and cabin microfilter, brought up to the correct date by an authorized BMW center.

# ENGINE OIL

2025 model year vehicles with internal-combustion engines are factory-filled with:

Z BMW-approved fully synthetic oil for gasoline engines

Engine oil should be changed when the vehicle’s engine is at operating temperature.

If an engine oil service is being performed or you need to add engine oil between changes, please refer to the Owner’s Manual for the recommended engine oil for your BMW vehicle.

# LONG-TERM RATED FLUIDS AND OILS

The following systems and assemblies are factory-filled with long-term rated fluid and oil; fluid replacement is only necessary when repairs are being performed (unless otherwise noted):

$\\triangleright$ Engine cooling system (antifreeze/coolant) $\\triangleright$ Automatic (except for X1 and X2) and manual transmissions $\\triangleright$ All-wheel drive transfer cases (except when indicated by the vehicle)

# REGULAR CHECKS — VEHICLE OPERATOR

In addition to the maintenance service procedure information contained in this booklet, BMW recommends that you regularly check (when refueling, for example), and address when necessary, the following items:

$\\triangleright$ Washer fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Coolant level

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Tires — pressure, condition and wear

Please refer to the Owner’s Manual for additional information.

Your [brakes](https://vw.oempartsonline.com/brakes) stop your [Volkswagen](https://vw.oempartsonline.com/v-volkswagen) vehicle. They do it by clamping their calipers and brake rotors together. This is what creates the friction, or resistance, that slows your vehicle's wheels and tires. However, calipers can't press rotors without brake pads, or else they'd get damaged. Your VW has one of four types of pads, depending on its model. Organic brake pads are for everyday driving. They're reliable, they don't wear rotors down as badly, and they don't create much dust. Best of all, they're inexpensive. Ceramic brake pads work better in bad weather, they don't make much noise, and their dust isn't as sticky. Metallic brake pads, however, stand up to higher heat, feel firmer, and resist brake fade. Carbon fiber brake pads are the strongest and best performers, tolerant of high temperatures and providing the most stopping power. Most cars and SUVs use either metallic or organic pads. However, many sports cars and performance vehicles use ceramic or carbon fiber pads because they do the best job of expelling heat.

## How Long Do Volkswagen Brake Pads Last?

However, no brake pad lasts forever, not even those Volkswagen makes. You should change yours every 40,000 to 50,000 miles or so. Otherwise, figure out when to replace them by looking for the signs your brakes are going bad. They include warning lights, worn pad surfaces, pad damage, whiny brakes, and taking longer to stop. The worst are vibration and grinding, as they indicate your rotors are warped and getting damaged because your brake pads have degraded.

## VW Atlas Service Schedule

## 10,000 Miles or One Year

The base of your VW Atlas service schedule will consist of the following maintenance tasks:

- Inspect the Brake Pads
- VW Atlas Oil Change
- New Oil Filter
- Service Interval Display Rest (if needed)

## 20,000 Miles or Two Years

Two-year maintenance should also include a VW Atlas oil change and oil filter replacement. The following must also be checked so you can stay safe on Vienna roads:

- Horn
- Tire Repair Kit
- Engine and Engine Compartment Components
- Brake Fluid
- Tire Pressure
- Service Interval Display
- Exterior Lighting
- Battery
- Tires
- Windshield Wiper/Washer System
- Automatic headlight control
- Headlight Washing System
- Wiper Blades
- Coolant Level and Frost Protection
- Brake Pads
- Transmission
- Second Battery
- Tire Pressure Monitoring System

## 30,000 Miles or Three Years

The following VW Atlas routine maintenance tasks will be required every three years or 30,000 miles:

- Oil Change
- New Oil Filter
- Inspect Brake Pads
- Service Interval Display Rest (if needed)

## 40,000 Miles or Four Years

At 40,000 miles, you’ll get a VW Atlas oil change and a new oil filter, plus everything from the 20,000 service interval. These things will also be checked as part of your VW Atlas maintenance schedule:

- Tie Rod Ends
- Stabilizer Bushings
- New Dust and Pollen Filter
- Front and Rear Coil Springs and Shock Absorbers
- Sunroof and Panoramic Sunroof
- Ball Joints
- Wheel Bearings
- Axles
- Coupling Rods

## 50,000 Miles or Five Years

The 50,000 VW Atlas service interval includes:

- Engine Oil Change
- New Oil Filter
- Check Your Brake Pads
- Service Interval Display Rest (if needed)

## 60,000 Miles or 6 Years

Your safety is paramount as you drive around Fairfax, so along with new engine oil, oil filter, air filter, and snow filter, these components will be inspected:

- Fuel filter Replacement
- Dust and Pollen Filter Replacement
- Battery inspection
- Check the Tires
- Brake System Inspection
- Check the Tire fFller Bottle Expiration Date

## 70,000 Miles or 7 Years

The 70,000-mile mark of the VW Atlas maintenance schedule includes the following tasks:

- Engine Oil Filter Change
- Motor Oil Change
- Brake Pad Check
- Service Interval Display Rest (if needed)

## 80,000 Miles or 8 Years

All the same components from the 20,000-mile inspection are inspected, as well as:

- Ball Joints
- Transmission
- Wheel Bearings
- Axles
- Interior Lighting
- Ribbed V-belt
- Front and Rear Coil Springs
- Shock Absorbers
- Sunroof and Panoramic Sunroof
- Underbody

## 90,000 Miles or 9 Years

- Brake Discs
- Clutch Unit
- Engine Oil Change
- Engine Oil Filter Change
- Brake Pad Inspection
- Service Interval Display Rest (if needed)

## 100,000 Miles or 10 Years

At 100,000 miles, you’ll get a VW Atlas oil change and new oil filter, and the same things as the 20,000-mile inspection will be inspected.

## 110,000 Miles or 11 Years

- Brake Pad Check
- Engine Oil Change
- New Oil Filter
- Service Interval Display Rest (if needed)

## 120,000 Miles or 12 Years

Our certified VW Technicians will replace your engine oil, oil filter, and snow and air filter and check all the same components from the 20,000-mile inspection, plus:

- Underbody
- Wheel Bearings
- Axles
- Tie Rod Ends,
- Stabilizer Bushings
- Front and Rear Coil Springs
- Shock Absorbers
- Ball Joints
- Interior Lighting
- Coupling Rods
- Ribbed V-Belt
- Sunroof and Panoramic Sunroof

## What is the Volkswagen Atlas Maintenance Schedule?

Your [new VW Atlas](https://www.carolinavw.com/new-vehicles/atlas/) service intervals occur every 10,000 miles. Older Volkswagen models might have different maintenance requirements, so check your owner’s manual for the correct VW Atlas maintenance schedule. However, world-class engineering means longer VW Atlas service intervals when you have a late-model vehicle.

Every 10,000 miles represents the VW Atlas oil change interval, so expect to get a full synthetic oil change every 10,000 miles of driving unless you drive in less-than-ideal conditions regularly in Concord.

Below is the general VW Atlas maintenance schedule you should follow.

### **VW Atlas Maintenance Schedule: 10,000 Miles or One Year**

Your first Volkswagen Atlas service in Charlotte will get this:

- Inspect the Brake Pads
- Oil Change
- New Oil Filter
- Fluid Level Check
- Service Interval Display Reset (if needed)

### **VW Atlas Maintenance Schedule: 20,000 Miles or Two Years**

For this VW Atlas service interval, we will do everything from the first service at 10,000 miles, plus some extras:

- Automatic headlight control
- Headlight Washing System
- Wiper Blades
- Coolant Level and Frost Protection
- Brake Pads
- Transmission
- Second Battery
- Engine Air Filter Check
- Tire Pressure Monitoring System
- Horn
- Tire Repair Kit
- Engine and Engine Compartment Components
- Brake Fluid
- Tire Pressure
- Service Interval Display
- Exterior Lighting
- Battery
- Tires
- Windshield Wiper/Washer System

### **VW Atlas Maintenance Schedule: 30,000 Miles or Three Years**

Here’s what our team will do for your three-year Volkswagen Atlas service near Indian Trail:

- Oil Change
- New Oil Filter
- Inspect Brake Pads
- Service Interval Display Reset (if needed)

### **VW Atlas Maintenance Schedule: 40,000 Miles or Four Years**

At 40,000 miles, we’ll take care of the VW Atlas oil change interval, just like the other one-year maintenance. We’ll also check everything from the 20,000-mile VW Atlas service interval. Our team will also look over these things for your Atlas for four years:

- Sunroof and Panoramic Sunroof
- Ball Joints
- Wheel Bearings
- Axles
- Coupling Rods
- Tie Rod Ends
- Stabilizer Bushings
- New Dust and Pollen Filter for the Cabin
- Front and Rear Coil Springs and Shock Absorbers

### **VW Atlas Maintenance Schedule: 50,000 Miles or Five Years**

At the 50,000-mile mark, this service interval includes everything from the initial service interval:

- VW Atlas Oil Change Interval
- New Oil Filter
- Check Your Brake Pads
- Fluid Levels
- Service Interval Display Reset (if needed)

At this point in your SUV ownership, you might need a new battery, new tires, or new brake parts, depending on the condition of your Volkswagen Atlas. We’ll discuss your options with you if we see anything that needs service at this interval.

Moving forward, we’ll also inspect the drive belts, the condition of the transmission, and the radiator, as these parts might show more signs of wear. If our service technicians detect any looming issues that need to be resolved soon, we’ll suggest a way to remedy the situation.

# Ford F-250 Maintenance Schedule

![2020 Ford F-250 Super Duty](https://dealerinspire-image-library-prod.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/images/VYRTx8e8gKaHBWHGBdt0AFRQTd4eLZM3BjXEZt6Z.jpg)

* * *

As a truck owner, you need a vehicle that can continue to work as hard as you do. In order to achieve long-term performance, keeping pace with your Ford F-250 maintenance schedule is crucial. While it can seem confusing to follow the recommended service intervals properly, Sid Dillon Ford Crete is here with a range of [tips and tricks](https://www.siddillonfordcrete.com/service/service-and-parts-tips/) to help you care for your truck. Below, our team will walk you through the various stages of your Ford Super Duty maintenance schedule to ensure you can continue to take on tough tasks in Lincoln for years to come.

[Service Center](https://www.siddillonfordcrete.com/service/) [Contact Us](https://www.siddillonfordcrete.com/contact-us/)

## Ford F-250 Maintenance: 7,500 Mile Service

Once you log 7,500 miles on the Seward streets, you’ll want to make your way to our certified service center for maintenance. At this interval, and every 7,500-mile interval after, your vehicle will need the following care:

- Replace oil and oil filter
- [Rotate tires](https://www.siddillonfordcrete.com/service/service-and-parts-tips/how-often-should-you-rotate-your-tires/), inspect the tire tread
- Check wheels and a range of components for abnormalities
- Multi-point inspection

## Ford F-250 Maintenance: 15,000 Mile Service

At 15,000 miles, you’ll reach your next service interval on the Ford Super Duty maintenance schedule. Once you hit this service stop, our team will perform the following tasks:

- Check the automatic transmission fluid
- Check front axle and U-joints
- Check brake pads, shoes, rotors, drums, brake linings, hoses, and parking brake
- Check exhaust system and heat shields
- Check engine coolant concentration, freeze-point protection, hoses
- Check steering linkage, ball joints, suspension, tie-rod ends, driveshaft, and U-joints
- Change engine air filter and cabin air filter

## Ford F-250 Maintenance: 100,000 Mile Service

The well-built Ford F-250 doesn’t demand much care. By keeping up with your 7,500-mileage services, you can expect to break the 100,000-mile barrier with ease. Once you get there, the following services need to be performed:

- Change [spark plugs](https://www.siddillonfordcrete.com/service/service-and-parts-tips/signs-of-bad-spark-plugs/)
- Replace engine coolant if the color of the coolant is orange
- Check accessory drive belts

## Ford F-250 Maintenance: 150,000 Mile Service

When you reach 150,000 miles, our team is here to give your truck the TLC it deserves. After that many miles, it’s no doubt that your vehicle has put in a tremendous amount of work. That said, if you’ve kept pace with recommended maintenance, you’ll have many more miles ahead once the following service tasks are completed:

- Replace the automatic transmission fluid and filter on transmission
- Change the accessory drive belt
- Change the front wheel bearings and seals
- Replace axle fluid
- Replace transfer case

## Follow Your Ford Super Duty Maintenance Schedule in Crete

Whether you own a fleet of Super Duty trucks or one F-250 for personal use, keeping up with your recommended truck care is easy when you rely on Sid Dillon Ford Crete. We are here to help you stay in line with your Ford Super Duty maintenance schedule to ensure your work companion stays on the Omaha streets for years to come. [Get in touch](https://www.siddillonfordcrete.com/service/contact-service/) with our service team if you have any lingering questions about your Ford F-250 maintenance schedule.

# 6.7 Power Stroke Oil Capacity

### **How Much Oil Does a Powerstroke 6.7 Hold?**

The oil capacity of a [6.7 Powerstroke engine varies by year of manufacture](https://www.hotshotsecret.com/top-powerstroke-engines/) and the specific vehicle model.  If you own a Ford F-250 to F-650 manufactured after 2022, its Powerstroke 6.7L will hold 15 quarts (14.2 liters) of oil. Those manufactured between 2011 and 2022 hold approximately 13 quarts (12.3 liters).

A Ford F-650 and F-750 produced between 2015 and 2022 can hold a maximum of 15 quarts (14.2 liters) of oil. For newer models released in 2023 and later, the oil capacity increases slightly to 17 quarts (16 liters).

When performing an oil change, it is crucial to use the correct type of oil and adhere to the recommended capacity. Ford recommends using oils that meet its WSS-M2C17-F1 specification for the 6.7 Powerstroke. # 2024 Volkswagen Tiguan Maintenance Schedule

![hero image](https://dealerimages.dealereprocess.com/image/upload/3483350)

# 2024 Volkswagen Tiguan Maintenance Schedule

The 2024 Volkswagen Tiguan is crafted for long-term reliability, but to keep it performing at its
best, regular maintenance is essential. Routine service tasks not only extend your Tiguan’s lifespan
but also ensure your peace of mind. By bringing your SUV in for scheduled check-ups, our skilled
technicians can identify and resolve potential issues early, preventing them from escalating into
more significant problems and saving you time and money.

![](https://dealerimages.dealereprocess.com/image/upload/3483347)

[Schedule Service](https://www.pohankavw.com/online-service-scheduler/)

## 10,000-Mile Maintenance

According to the Volkswagen maintenance schedule, your 2024 Tiguan recommends minor maintenance every
10,000 miles. If you drive in severe weather, tow a trail often, or otherwise operate the vehicle under
more rigorous than average conditions, more frequent maintenance may be advisable (when in doubt, ask
your service advisor). This visit is straightforward, consisting of a tire rotation and oil (and oil
filter) change.

## 20,000-Mile Maintenance

This will be a repeat of the 10,000-mile service (tire rotation and oil change). If your Tiguan has a
sunroof, the drains need to be cleaned and inspected for blockage at this service interval (every 20,000
miles or 2 years, whichever occurs first).

## 30,000-Mile Maintenance

For this appointment, technicians repeat the 10,000-mile minor maintenance schedule, consisting of an
engine oil/filter change and tire rotation.

## 40,000-Mile Maintenance

This service combines the 10,000- and 20,000-mile visits, with a couple of additional tasks:

- change engine oil/filter
- rotate tires
- clean sunroof drains and lubricate panoramic sliding sunroof
- replace in-cabin air filter replacement (every 40,000 miles or two years, whichever comes first)


## 50,000-Mile Maintenance

This visit calls for a repeat of the 10,000-mile service, consisting of an engine oil and filter change
plus a tire rotation.

## 60,000-Mile Maintenance

This visit repeats the 10,000- and 20,000-mile services, with one additional task: replacing the engine
air filter replaced and cleaning its screen.

## 70,000-Mile Maintenance

As another 10,000-mile interval, this visit calls for just a tire rotation and oil change.

## 80,000-Mile Maintenance

Along with the 10,000-, 20,000-, and 40,000-mile services, a couple more tasks are added in at this time.
Altogether, now is the time to perform the following:

- change engine oil/filter
- rotate tire
- clean sunroof drains
- replace in-cabin air filter
- clean and grease panoramic sliding sunroof
- change spark plugs
- drain and replace automatic transmission fluid

## 90,000-Mile Maintenance

The 90,000-mile service is simple, consisting of a tire rotation and engine oil/filter change.

## 100,000-Mile Maintenance

You’ve reached your first 100K miles with your Tiguan: congratulations! The 10,000- and 20,000-mile
intervals will be repeated at this time. Our technicians will change the oil and perform a tire
rotation. If your Tiguan has a sunroof, its drains will also be cleaned.

## 110,000-Mile Maintenance

Minor servicing occurs at this point, with a straightforward oil and filter change and tire rotation.

## 120,000-Mile Maintenance

This more extensive service interval combines the 40,000- and 60,000-mile tasks:

- rotate tires
- clean sunroof drains
- change engine oil and filter
- replace engine air filter and clean the screen
- clean and grease panorama sliding sunroof
- replace in-cabin dust/pollen filter

## Post-120K Miles & Time-Based Services

Your Tiguan has been built for longevity, and continued maintenance will keep it running well through
more significant milestones. After 120,000 miles, the same task intervals apply, with a few additional
requirements recommended, as well as time-based services. For example:

- Replace coolant pump toothed belt every 180,000 miles.
- Change AWD clutch fluid (if equipped) every 3 years.
- Replace tire filler bottle in mobility kit every 4 years.
- Change brake fluid every 2 years (after the first 3 years).

## Regular Inspections (Every Visit)

During every maintenance appointment, our factory-trained Volkswagen technicians will perform a complete
inspection of your Tiguan’s major components. They will check that the vehicle is operating as intended
and make sure that any issues they detect are corrected before they become more serious. Here are some
of the components and systems that are routinely inspected:

- brake system (pad thickness, rotor wear, brake lines, fluid levels, etc.)
- interior lights and electronics
- tire tread/wear
- battery
- windshield, wipers, and washer fluid
- exterior lighting
- horn
- suspension system (ball joints, control arms, stabilizer bar, struts, springs, bearings, etc.)
- cooling system
- air conditioning/heater
- exhaust system
- transmission fluid
- chassis
- steering system

# BMW SERVICE

BMW recommends you have your maintenance and repair work performed by an authorized BMW center.

# MAINTAINING YOUR BMW VEHICLE

A well-maintained vehicle will help safeguard its operational performance, road-safety and its reliability. This is why it is important to follow and perform BMW’s recommended periodic vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks as indicated by your vehicle’s Maintenance Service Display, along with the other maintenance work described in this booklet.

A improper maintenance is not covered under the BMW New Vehicle Damage, including consequential damage, which results from lack of or Limited Warranty for Passenger Cars and Light Trucks.

# MAINTENANCE INTERVALS

Maintenance intervals on motor vehicles were conventionally based solely on a fixed time period or a specified amount of accumulated driving mileage.

However, operational and driving conditions have a major influence on your vehicle’s routine maintenance requirements; the distance traveled is only one of these significant factors. A vehicle used for short trips in the city with numerous cold starts, prolonged periods of idling, stop-and-go driving, and high engine speeds during acceleration may require more frequent maintenance intervals than a vehicle that is driven long distances at moderate engine speeds.

Your BMW vehicle uses sensors and algorithms together with the elapsed time and the driving distance/profile to monitor and evaluate your vehicle’s maintenance service needs. This information is then used to adapt dynamically the parameters used to forecast the applicable maintenance service task intervals.

# THE BMW MAINTENANCE SYSTEM

All BMW vehicles are equipped with an integrated BMW Maintenance System. This maintenance “reminder” system helps ensure that the vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks are performed at the forecasted intervals that apply to your vehicle.

The BMW Maintenance System display provides the vehicle operator access to the current status information for the following maintenance service tasks:

$\\triangleright$ Engine oil (date and miles)\*

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle check (date and miles)

$\\triangleright$ Front brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Rear brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid (date)

$\\triangleright$ 1200 Mile running-in service (date and miles) (Applicable to BMW M vehicles only)\*

For each specific maintenance service task, either the future date (month/ year), remaining miles or both are provided as noted above. The system monitors variable inputs to forecast the intervals and alert the driver when one or more specific maintenance tasks should be performed.

NOTE: For certain vehicles, the status of the front and rear brake pads will only be observable in the maintenance system’s display when there are approximately 2,000 miles or less remaining before a brake service will be required to be performed.

For information about the vehicle’s maintenance system displays, please refer to the Maintenance Service Display Overview section beginning on page 5.

The following “combine with Engine oil”\* maintenance service tasks may be identified as needing to be performed with a specific occurrence of the “Engine oil” service task (service counter number):

$\\triangleright$ Cabin Microfilter(s)

$\\triangleright$ Engine air filter(s)\*

$\\triangleright$ Spark plugs\*

$\\triangleright$ Final drive oil (Applicable M vehicles only)

\\* Does not apply to BEV

Although these items do not appear in the BMW Maintenance System’s display in the vehicle, these services should be performed when your vehicle’s engine oil is changed in accordance with the interval identified by your vehicle’s BMW Maintenance System.

For more information on your vehicle’s maintenance services requirements, procedures and intervals, please refer the Maintenance Service Summary section beginning on page 10.

The BMW Maintenance System also includes an option to set service reminders for the following state-specific mandatory vehicle inspections, including:

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle safety inspection; and/or $\\triangleright$ Emissions test

The corresponding interval data for these inspections can be inputted into the BMW Maintenance System by a service provider; they are not determined by the vehicle.

For your convenience, you may also wish to have your authorized BMW center perform the work necessary to fulfill these state inspection requirements in your area concurrent with the maintenance services specified above when possible.

Should you request more frequent maintenance service than is indicated by the BMW Maintenance System during the coverage period, the cost of these services will not be covered by the BMW Maintenance Program.

# SERVICE DATA — REMOTE CONTROL KEY

Maintenance service task status information for your BMW vehicle is continually updated and stored in your remote control key.

Your authorized BMW center can access this data and consult with you about applicable service procedures and tasks for your vehicle.

Therefore, always provide your service consultant with the most recent remote control key that was used to operate the vehicle when servicing your vehicle at a BMW center.

# VEHICLE STORAGE

Disconnecting the battery during periods of long-term vehicle storage will interrupt the calculation of time-dependent maintenance services.

In this situation, BMW recommends that you have all your time-based maintenance services, such as brake fluid, engine oil and cabin microfilter, brought up to the correct date by an authorized BMW center.

# ENGINE OIL

2025 model year vehicles with internal-combustion engines are factory-filled with:

Z BMW-approved fully synthetic oil for gasoline engines

Engine oil should be changed when the vehicle’s engine is at operating temperature.

If an engine oil service is being performed or you need to add engine oil between changes, please refer to the Owner’s Manual for the recommended engine oil for your BMW vehicle.

# LONG-TERM RATED FLUIDS AND OILS

The following systems and assemblies are factory-filled with long-term rated fluid and oil; fluid replacement is only necessary when repairs are being performed (unless otherwise noted):

$\\triangleright$ Engine cooling system (antifreeze/coolant) $\\triangleright$ Automatic (except for X1 and X2) and manual transmissions $\\triangleright$ All-wheel drive transfer cases (except when indicated by the vehicle)

# REGULAR CHECKS — VEHICLE OPERATOR

In addition to the maintenance service procedure information contained in this booklet, BMW recommends that you regularly check (when refueling, for example), and address when necessary, the following items:

$\\triangleright$ Washer fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Coolant level

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Tires — pressure, condition and wear

Please refer to the Owner’s Manual for additional information.

The **BMW i5 maintenance schedule** looks very different from a gas-powered 5 Series. There’s no engine oil, spark plugs, or timing chain to worry about, but you still have brakes, tires, coolant, software, and a sophisticated high-voltage system that all need attention. If you’re driving or shopping for a BMW i5, understanding the real service intervals and long‑term maintenance picture can save you time, money, and stress.

### Quick take

Compared with a gasoline 5 Series, a BMW i5 typically needs fewer scheduled services and less routine maintenance. Most owners will visit a service center about once a year for inspections, fluids, and software, plus wear items like tires and brakes as they age.

## BMW i5 maintenance overview

The BMW i5 is built on the same platform as the current 5 Series, but its **electric powertrain dramatically changes the maintenance profile**. You still follow a factory schedule, but the high‑value items are:

\- Safety inspections (suspension, steering, brakes)
\- Brake fluid changes
\- Cabin air filter and other filters
\- Coolant for the battery and power electronics
\- High‑voltage system checks
\- Software and firmware updates

For most U.S. drivers, you’re looking at **annual visits** rather than old‑school 5,000–7,500‑mile oil changes.

### How BMW i5 maintenance compares to gas cars
