# BMW SERVICE

BMW recommends you have your maintenance and repair work performed by an authorized BMW center.

# MAINTAINING YOUR BMW VEHICLE

A well-maintained vehicle will help safeguard its operational performance, road-safety and its reliability. This is why it is important to follow and perform BMW’s recommended periodic vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks as indicated by your vehicle’s Maintenance Service Display, along with the other maintenance work described in this booklet.

A improper maintenance is not covered under the BMW New Vehicle Damage, including consequential damage, which results from lack of or Limited Warranty for Passenger Cars and Light Trucks.

# MAINTENANCE INTERVALS

Maintenance intervals on motor vehicles were conventionally based solely on a fixed time period or a specified amount of accumulated driving mileage.

However, operational and driving conditions have a major influence on your vehicle’s routine maintenance requirements; the distance traveled is only one of these significant factors. A vehicle used for short trips in the city with numerous cold starts, prolonged periods of idling, stop-and-go driving, and high engine speeds during acceleration may require more frequent maintenance intervals than a vehicle that is driven long distances at moderate engine speeds.

Your BMW vehicle uses sensors and algorithms together with the elapsed time and the driving distance/profile to monitor and evaluate your vehicle’s maintenance service needs. This information is then used to adapt dynamically the parameters used to forecast the applicable maintenance service task intervals.

# THE BMW MAINTENANCE SYSTEM

All BMW vehicles are equipped with an integrated BMW Maintenance System. This maintenance “reminder” system helps ensure that the vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks are performed at the forecasted intervals that apply to your vehicle.

The BMW Maintenance System display provides the vehicle operator access to the current status information for the following maintenance service tasks:

$\\triangleright$ Engine oil (date and miles)\*

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle check (date and miles)

$\\triangleright$ Front brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Rear brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid (date)

$\\triangleright$ 1200 Mile running-in service (date and miles) (Applicable to BMW M vehicles only)\*

For each specific maintenance service task, either the future date (month/ year), remaining miles or both are provided as noted above. The system monitors variable inputs to forecast the intervals and alert the driver when one or more specific maintenance tasks should be performed.

NOTE: For certain vehicles, the status of the front and rear brake pads will only be observable in the maintenance system’s display when there are approximately 2,000 miles or less remaining before a brake service will be required to be performed.

For information about the vehicle’s maintenance system displays, please refer to the Maintenance Service Display Overview section beginning on page 5.

The following “combine with Engine oil”\* maintenance service tasks may be identified as needing to be performed with a specific occurrence of the “Engine oil” service task (service counter number):

$\\triangleright$ Cabin Microfilter(s)

$\\triangleright$ Engine air filter(s)\*

$\\triangleright$ Spark plugs\*

$\\triangleright$ Final drive oil (Applicable M vehicles only)

\\* Does not apply to BEV

Although these items do not appear in the BMW Maintenance System’s display in the vehicle, these services should be performed when your vehicle’s engine oil is changed in accordance with the interval identified by your vehicle’s BMW Maintenance System.

For more information on your vehicle’s maintenance services requirements, procedures and intervals, please refer the Maintenance Service Summary section beginning on page 10.

The BMW Maintenance System also includes an option to set service reminders for the following state-specific mandatory vehicle inspections, including:

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle safety inspection; and/or $\\triangleright$ Emissions test

The corresponding interval data for these inspections can be inputted into the BMW Maintenance System by a service provider; they are not determined by the vehicle.

For your convenience, you may also wish to have your authorized BMW center perform the work necessary to fulfill these state inspection requirements in your area concurrent with the maintenance services specified above when possible.

Should you request more frequent maintenance service than is indicated by the BMW Maintenance System during the coverage period, the cost of these services will not be covered by the BMW Maintenance Program.

# SERVICE DATA — REMOTE CONTROL KEY

Maintenance service task status information for your BMW vehicle is continually updated and stored in your remote control key.

Your authorized BMW center can access this data and consult with you about applicable service procedures and tasks for your vehicle.

Therefore, always provide your service consultant with the most recent remote control key that was used to operate the vehicle when servicing your vehicle at a BMW center.

# VEHICLE STORAGE

Disconnecting the battery during periods of long-term vehicle storage will interrupt the calculation of time-dependent maintenance services.

In this situation, BMW recommends that you have all your time-based maintenance services, such as brake fluid, engine oil and cabin microfilter, brought up to the correct date by an authorized BMW center.

# ENGINE OIL

2025 model year vehicles with internal-combustion engines are factory-filled with:

Z BMW-approved fully synthetic oil for gasoline engines

Engine oil should be changed when the vehicle’s engine is at operating temperature.

If an engine oil service is being performed or you need to add engine oil between changes, please refer to the Owner’s Manual for the recommended engine oil for your BMW vehicle.

# LONG-TERM RATED FLUIDS AND OILS

The following systems and assemblies are factory-filled with long-term rated fluid and oil; fluid replacement is only necessary when repairs are being performed (unless otherwise noted):

$\\triangleright$ Engine cooling system (antifreeze/coolant) $\\triangleright$ Automatic (except for X1 and X2) and manual transmissions $\\triangleright$ All-wheel drive transfer cases (except when indicated by the vehicle)

# REGULAR CHECKS — VEHICLE OPERATOR

In addition to the maintenance service procedure information contained in this booklet, BMW recommends that you regularly check (when refueling, for example), and address when necessary, the following items:

$\\triangleright$ Washer fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Coolant level

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Tires — pressure, condition and wear

Please refer to the Owner’s Manual for additional information.

## Keep Your BMW 2 Series Performing at it's Best

**Basic BMW 2-Series Preventative Maintenance: Every 5,000 Miles**

BMW’s maintenance schedule is built around a standard 5,000-mile interval, guided by your vehicle’s pre-installed Condition-Based Service (CBS) monitor. This intelligent system tracks critical areas of your car and alerts you when additional services are needed.

The regular BMW recommended maintenance schedule includes the following:

- Vehicle check and inspection
- Engine oil check
- Coolant check
- Tire rotation
- Brake fluid check
- Front and rear brake inspection
- Inspection of the engine and cabin air filters
- Wiper blade inspection
- Standard scope

Not every part inspected will need replacement during your visit. Our BMW-certified maintenance experts use the CBS monitor to identify exactly what requires attention, ensuring precise and efficient service.

**BMW 2-Series Recommended Maintenance Services**

Maintenance needs can vary depending on your model and driving habits. For tailored recommendations, consult your owner’s manual or speak with one of our knowledgeable service advisors. Below is a general guideline for BMW 2 Series maintenance milestones:

**BMW 2-Series 10,000-Mile Maintenance**

- Replace the engine oil, oil filter and coolant
- Repeat every 10,000 miles

**BMW 2-Series 20,000-Mile Maintenance**

- Inspect and replace the oil filters
- Repeat every 20,000 miles

**BMW 2-Series 30,000-Mile Maintenance**

- Replace brake fluid. After the first service, schedule brake fluid replacement every 60,000 miles.
- If equipped with a manual transmission, replace transmission fluid every 30,000 miles.

**BMW 2-Series 60,000-mile maintenance**

- Replace the engine air filter and spark plugs
- Inspect and replace brake pads and rotors as needed
- For automatic transmissions, replace the transmission fluid every 60,000 miles.

**BMW 2-Series 90,000-Mile Maintenance**

- Replace the timing belt and hoses
- Repeat every 90,000 miles

**BMW 2-Series Maintenance after 90,000 Miles**

Continue following the BMW 2 Series maintenance schedule with 5,000-mile intervals and adhere to service milestones as listed above to ensure optimal performance.

# What is the Recommended BMW Maintenance Schedule?

![Mechanic fixing BMW](https://dealerinspire-image-library-prod.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/images/qOCqBJVRI2dmLPMZp2H4nX2vvpahYMjkkgG6QC7e.jpg)

* * *

At BMW of Tigard, we often get questions from customers about their BMW maintenance schedule. And when you buy a [quality new BMW](https://www.bmwtigard.com/new-vehicles/), it’s important to stick to its BMW service schedule. That’s why we’ve provided the recommended maintenance schedule for general BMW vehicles for Portland and Tigard drivers. With this handy guide, it’ll be easy to stay on track and have your vehicle serviced. We’ll ensure that your vehicle will always be running at its best! As always, before you schedule maintenance on your vehicle, be sure to read your owner’s manual for any specific maintenance information that applies to your BMW vehicle. That way, you’ll better understand your specific model and trim’s future maintenance and repair needs.

[BMW X3 SERVICE SCHEDULE](https://www.bmwtigard.com/service/service-and-parts-tips/bmw-x3-service-schedule/) [Service & Parts Specials](https://www.bmwtigard.com/service-parts-specials/)

## BMW Preventative Maintenance: Every 5,000 Miles / 6 Months

It’s important to bring in your BMW two or three times a year (or every 5,000 miles) for these preventative maintenance services:

- Front and rear brake inspection
- Brake fluid check
- Coolant check
- Engine oil check
- Cabin air filter inspection
- Engine inspection
- Vehicle inspection
- Wiper blade inspection
- Any necessary tire rotations

Your BMW also comes with something called the Condition-Based Service Monitor (CBS). Your CBS tracks the condition of important systems in your BMW, letting you know if service is required. Our technicians will also use your CBS to determine what needs to be replaced, repaired, or serviced when you schedule service. Keep in mind that just because your CBS may say that service may not be necessary at 5,000 miles doesn’t mean that you shouldn’t come in for preventative maintenance and checks. Sometimes human eyes are necessary to determine a problem or to nip any potential issues in the bud.

## Recommended BMW Maintenance Schedule

Your BMW service schedule needs will vary based on how often you drive, where you drive, and your driving conditions. Your owner’s manual can give you detailed information on common service tasks for your specific model and trim, but here’s what BMW owners can generally expect:

- **Every 10,000 miles** (or yearly): replace your vehicle’s engine oil, oil filter, and coolant.
- **Every 20,000 miles** (or every two years): inspect and replace your vehicle’s fuel filters.
- **Every 30,000 miles** (or every three years): replace your vehicle’s brake fluid (after the first replacement, **every 60,000 miles**) and replace your vehicle’s transmission fluid on manual-transmission BMWs.
- **Every 60,000 miles** (or every six years): replace your vehicle’s engine air filter and spark plugs, inspect and replace any brake pads and brake rotors, and replace transmission fluid on automatic-transmission BMWs.
- **Every 90,000 miles** (or every nine years): replace your vehicle’s timing belts and hoses.

You’ll want to repeat the cycle above after 90,000 miles and always follow the 5,000-mile maintenance schedule. Your BMW’s New Vehicle Limited Warranty will also expire at 50,000 miles, so we recommend getting in any repairs or service before this warranty expires! We also recommend replacing your BMW battery around 50,000 miles.

# BMW SERVICE

BMW recommends you have your maintenance and repair work performed by an authorized BMW center.

# MAINTAINING YOUR BMW VEHICLE

A well-maintained vehicle will help safeguard its operational performance, road-safety and its reliability. This is why it is important to follow and perform BMW’s recommended periodic vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks as indicated by your vehicle’s Maintenance Service Display, along with the other maintenance work described in this booklet.

A improper maintenance is not covered under the BMW New Vehicle Damage, including consequential damage, which results from lack of or Limited Warranty for Passenger Cars and Light Trucks.

# MAINTENANCE INTERVALS

Maintenance intervals on motor vehicles were conventionally based solely on a fixed time period or a specified amount of accumulated driving mileage.

However, operational and driving conditions have a major influence on your vehicle’s routine maintenance requirements; the distance traveled is only one of these significant factors. A vehicle used for short trips in the city with numerous cold starts, prolonged periods of idling, stop-and-go driving, and high engine speeds during acceleration may require more frequent maintenance intervals than a vehicle that is driven long distances at moderate engine speeds.

Your BMW vehicle uses sensors and algorithms together with the elapsed time and the driving distance/profile to monitor and evaluate your vehicle’s maintenance service needs. This information is then used to adapt dynamically the parameters used to forecast the applicable maintenance service task intervals.

# THE BMW MAINTENANCE SYSTEM

All BMW vehicles are equipped with an integrated BMW Maintenance System. This maintenance “reminder” system helps ensure that the vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks are performed at the forecasted intervals that apply to your vehicle.

The BMW Maintenance System display provides the vehicle operator access to the current status information for the following maintenance service tasks:

$\\triangleright$ Engine oil (date and miles)\*

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle check (date and miles)

$\\triangleright$ Front brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Rear brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid (date)

$\\triangleright$ 1200 Mile running-in service (date and miles) (Applicable to BMW M vehicles only)\*

For each specific maintenance service task, either the future date (month/ year), remaining miles or both are provided as noted above. The system monitors variable inputs to forecast the intervals and alert the driver when one or more specific maintenance tasks should be performed.

NOTE: For certain vehicles, the status of the front and rear brake pads will only be observable in the maintenance system’s display when there are approximately 2,000 miles or less remaining before a brake service will be required to be performed.

For information about the vehicle’s maintenance system displays, please refer to the Maintenance Service Display Overview section beginning on page 5.

The following “combine with Engine oil”\* maintenance service tasks may be identified as needing to be performed with a specific occurrence of the “Engine oil” service task (service counter number):

$\\triangleright$ Cabin Microfilter(s)

$\\triangleright$ Engine air filter(s)\*

$\\triangleright$ Spark plugs\*

$\\triangleright$ Final drive oil (Applicable M vehicles only)

\\* Does not apply to BEV

Although these items do not appear in the BMW Maintenance System’s display in the vehicle, these services should be performed when your vehicle’s engine oil is changed in accordance with the interval identified by your vehicle’s BMW Maintenance System.

For more information on your vehicle’s maintenance services requirements, procedures and intervals, please refer the Maintenance Service Summary section beginning on page 10.

The BMW Maintenance System also includes an option to set service reminders for the following state-specific mandatory vehicle inspections, including:

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle safety inspection; and/or $\\triangleright$ Emissions test

The corresponding interval data for these inspections can be inputted into the BMW Maintenance System by a service provider; they are not determined by the vehicle.

For your convenience, you may also wish to have your authorized BMW center perform the work necessary to fulfill these state inspection requirements in your area concurrent with the maintenance services specified above when possible.

Should you request more frequent maintenance service than is indicated by the BMW Maintenance System during the coverage period, the cost of these services will not be covered by the BMW Maintenance Program.

# SERVICE DATA — REMOTE CONTROL KEY

Maintenance service task status information for your BMW vehicle is continually updated and stored in your remote control key.

Your authorized BMW center can access this data and consult with you about applicable service procedures and tasks for your vehicle.

Therefore, always provide your service consultant with the most recent remote control key that was used to operate the vehicle when servicing your vehicle at a BMW center.

# VEHICLE STORAGE

Disconnecting the battery during periods of long-term vehicle storage will interrupt the calculation of time-dependent maintenance services.

In this situation, BMW recommends that you have all your time-based maintenance services, such as brake fluid, engine oil and cabin microfilter, brought up to the correct date by an authorized BMW center.

# ENGINE OIL

2025 model year vehicles with internal-combustion engines are factory-filled with:

Z BMW-approved fully synthetic oil for gasoline engines

Engine oil should be changed when the vehicle’s engine is at operating temperature.

If an engine oil service is being performed or you need to add engine oil between changes, please refer to the Owner’s Manual for the recommended engine oil for your BMW vehicle.

# LONG-TERM RATED FLUIDS AND OILS

The following systems and assemblies are factory-filled with long-term rated fluid and oil; fluid replacement is only necessary when repairs are being performed (unless otherwise noted):

$\\triangleright$ Engine cooling system (antifreeze/coolant) $\\triangleright$ Automatic (except for X1 and X2) and manual transmissions $\\triangleright$ All-wheel drive transfer cases (except when indicated by the vehicle)

# REGULAR CHECKS — VEHICLE OPERATOR

In addition to the maintenance service procedure information contained in this booklet, BMW recommends that you regularly check (when refueling, for example), and address when necessary, the following items:

$\\triangleright$ Washer fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Coolant level

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Tires — pressure, condition and wear

Please refer to the Owner’s Manual for additional information.

# MAINTENANCE SERVICE DISPLAY OVERVIEW

**Basic BMW 2-Series Preventative Maintenance: Every 5,000 Miles**

BMW’s maintenance schedule is built around a standard 5,000-mile interval, guided by your vehicle’s pre-installed Condition-Based Service (CBS) monitor. This intelligent system tracks critical areas of your car and alerts you when additional services are needed.

The regular BMW recommended maintenance schedule includes the following:

- Vehicle check and inspection
- Engine oil check
- Coolant check
- Tire rotation
- Brake fluid check
- Front and rear brake inspection
- Inspection of the engine and cabin air filters
- Wiper blade inspection
- Standard scope

Not every part inspected will need replacement during your visit. Our BMW-certified maintenance experts use the CBS monitor to identify exactly what requires attention, ensuring precise and efficient service.

**BMW 2-Series Recommended Maintenance Services**

Maintenance needs can vary depending on your model and driving habits. For tailored recommendations, consult your owner’s manual or speak with one of our knowledgeable service advisors. Below is a general guideline for BMW 2 Series maintenance milestones:

**BMW 2-Series 10,000-Mile Maintenance**

- Replace the engine oil, oil filter and coolant
- Repeat every 10,000 miles

**BMW 2-Series 20,000-Mile Maintenance**

- Inspect and replace the oil filters
- Repeat every 20,000 miles

**BMW 2-Series 30,000-Mile Maintenance**

- Replace brake fluid. After the first service, schedule brake fluid replacement every 60,000 miles.
- If equipped with a manual transmission, replace transmission fluid every 30,000 miles.

**BMW 2-Series 60,000-mile maintenance**

- Replace the engine air filter and spark plugs
- Inspect and replace brake pads and rotors as needed
- For automatic transmissions, replace the transmission fluid every 60,000 miles.

**BMW 2-Series 90,000-Mile Maintenance**

- Replace the timing belt and hoses
- Repeat every 90,000 miles

**BMW 2-Series Maintenance after 90,000 Miles**

Continue following the BMW 2 Series maintenance schedule with 5,000-mile intervals and adhere to service milestones as listed above to ensure optimal performance.

# 2024 Volkswagen Atlas Maintenance Schedule

# 2024 Volkswagen Atlas Maintenance Schedule

Regular maintenance is vital to ensuring the longevity and efficiency of your 2024 Atlas. By adhering to the manufacturer's recommended maintenance schedule, you can prevent costly repairs down the road and prolong its resale value. Scheduled maintenance also increases overall safety by addressing potential issues before they escalate. The VW-certified technicians at Pohanka Volkswagen of Capitol Heights always prioritize your safety and satisfaction. Here, we summarize the maintenance schedule recommended by Volkswagen to keep the 2024 Atlas running its best.

![](https://dealerimages.dealereprocess.com/image/upload/3382164)

[Schedule Service](https://www.pohankavw.com/online-service-scheduler/)

## 10,000 Miles

At the 10,000-mile mark, your 2024 Atlas will require its first maintenance visit. During this service, our technicians will look over the vehicle's systems to ensure that everything is functioning properly. They will also take care of the scheduled oil and filter change, along with a tire rotation to promote even tread wear.

## 20,000 Miles

When your Atlas reaches 20,000 miles, it will be time for another round of essential maintenance. Our service technicians will conduct a more thorough examination, this time including elements such as the battery’s well-being (including how well it is charging), the coolant level, transmission function, and operation of all lights. Once again, your Atlas will receive an oil and filter change, as well as a tire rotation, brake inspection, and comprehensive check of all fluid levels and components.

## 40,000 Miles

When the odometer on your Atlas reads 40,000 miles, it will be time once again for our certified technicians to perform all the services included in the previous intervals (oil change, tire rotation, and multipoint inspection). They will also replace the dust and pollen filters.

## 60,000 Miles

The 60,000-mile service interval for the 2024 Atlas will cover everything performed at the 20,000-mile mark, in addition to replacing the cabin air filter to make sure you and your passengers are breathing clean air.

## 80,000 Miles

The 80,000-mile mark means it’s time for a more comprehensive maintenance service, as well as a complete mechanical check to monitor the vehicle’s continued reliability and performance. Besides repeating all of the services mentioned for the previous intervals, they will put in a fresh set of spark plugs and drain and replace the transmission fluid.

## What is the Volkswagen Atlas Maintenance Schedule?

Your [new VW Atlas](https://www.carolinavw.com/new-vehicles/atlas/) service intervals occur every 10,000 miles. Older Volkswagen models might have different maintenance requirements, so check your owner’s manual for the correct VW Atlas maintenance schedule. However, world-class engineering means longer VW Atlas service intervals when you have a late-model vehicle.

Every 10,000 miles represents the VW Atlas oil change interval, so expect to get a full synthetic oil change every 10,000 miles of driving unless you drive in less-than-ideal conditions regularly in Concord.

Below is the general VW Atlas maintenance schedule you should follow.

### **VW Atlas Maintenance Schedule: 10,000 Miles or One Year**

Your first Volkswagen Atlas service in Charlotte will get this:

- Inspect the Brake Pads
- Oil Change
- New Oil Filter
- Fluid Level Check
- Service Interval Display Reset (if needed)

### **VW Atlas Maintenance Schedule: 20,000 Miles or Two Years**

For this VW Atlas service interval, we will do everything from the first service at 10,000 miles, plus some extras:

- Automatic headlight control
- Headlight Washing System

- Brake Fluid
- Tire Pressure
- Service Interval Display
- Exterior Lighting
- Battery
- Tires
- Windshield Wiper/Washer System

### **VW Atlas Maintenance Schedule: 30,000 Miles or Three Years**

Here’s what our team will do for your three-year Volkswagen Atlas service near Indian Trail:

- Oil Change
- New Oil Filter
- Inspect Brake Pads
- Service Interval Display Reset (if needed)

### **VW Atlas Maintenance Schedule: 40,000 Miles or Four Years**

At 40,000 miles, we’ll take care of the VW Atlas oil change interval, just like the other one-year maintenance. We’ll also check everything from the 20,000-mile VW Atlas service interval. Our team will also look over these things for your Atlas for four years:

- Sunroof and Panoramic Sunroof
- Ball Joints
- Wheel Bearings
- Axles
- Coupling Rods
- Tie Rod Ends
- Stabilizer Bushings
- New Dust and Pollen Filter for the Cabin
- Front and Rear Coil Springs and Shock Absorbers

### **VW Atlas Maintenance Schedule: 50,000 Miles or Five Years**

At the 50,000-mile mark, this service interval includes everything from the initial service interval:

- VW Atlas Oil Change Interval
- New Oil Filter
- Check Your Brake Pads
- Fluid Levels
- Service Interval Display Reset (if needed)

At this point in your SUV ownership, you might need a new battery, new tires, or new brake parts, depending on the condition of your Volkswagen Atlas. We’ll discuss your options with you if we see anything that needs service at this interval.

Moving forward, we’ll also inspect the drive belts, the condition of the transmission, and the radiator, as these parts might show more signs of wear. If our service technicians detect any looming issues that need to be resolved soon, we’ll suggest a way to remedy the situation.

In this video, we walk you through every step of changing the oil on a 2024 VW Atlas equipped with the 2.0L 4-cylinder EA888 engine. Whether you're a seasoned DIY mechanic or a beginner, our detailed guide is designed to help you maintain your vehicle with confidence and precision to keep your vehicle running and healthy.

** What You'll Learn **
 ✅ Essential Tools & Supplies: Get a rundown of all the tools needed for the job, from rhino ramps to the oil filter socket

 ✅ Tips from a seasoned veteran of the automotive industry

** Please take this into account when selecting your oil and your oil change intervals. **

Volkswagen calls for VW 508 00 Spec Oil. It's suggested that if you want to run the 10,000 Mile drain intervals that you run oil that meets this specification. If you run 3,000 to 5,000 Mile oil change intervals, you can use alternative high quality synthetic oil with anti-wear, anti-friction additives like Liqui Moly or others.

Oil filter cap torque spec: 18.8 Ft/Lbs

# WARRANTY & MAINTENANCE GUIDE

RAV4 HYBRID

# SAFETY PRECAUTIONS

Your RAV4 Hybrid has both high-voltage DC and AC systems as well as a 12-volt system. Both DC and AC high voltage are very dangerous and can cause personal injury, severe burns, electric shock and even fatal injury.

To avoid personal injury, please follow all caution labels attached to high-voltage parts. Do not touch or attempt to remove or replace any high-voltage (orange-colored) wiring and connectors. Do not touch the service plug, which is located under the rear seat.

If an accident occurs, do not touch any high-voltage wiring, connectors or parts such as the inverter unit or hybrid vehicle battery assembly.

Do not touch the potassium hydroxide electrolyte that might spill or leak from the hybrid vehicle battery as the result of an accident. - Exhaust pipes and mountings

When you hit 55,000 miles, it’s time to check all of the fluids, get a tire rotation, and a visual examination of your brakes.

This consists of all of the standard 30,000-mile checks, refills, and replacements.

# How Often Should You Change Your Transmission Fluid?

There's no one-size-fits-all answer when it comes to how often you should change your vehicle's transmission fluid. In general, adhere to the manufacturer guidelines to ensure that your ride's transmission fluid and filter maintenance is on point and that your car, truck, SUV, or van operates and performs at its peak.

## What is a Transmission Fluid Change?

A transmission fluid change involves draining the old transmission fluid from the transmission pan, replacing 30 to 40 percent of the fluid, and installing a new transmission filter. It's recommended for routine maintenance to keep the transmission functioning smoothly.

A transmission fluid change is not the same thing as a transmission fluid flush, which is more time-consuming and typically pricier. A flush, as the name suggests, involves completely flushing out all the old transmission fluid from the system. Special transmission flush fluid is circulated into the transmission system, cleaning out any residue or contaminants. A flush replaces nearly 100 percent of the old fluid. Both procedures can help maintain the health of your transmission, preserve its performance, and prolong its lifespan.

It's always best to consult your vehicle's manual or reach out to the auto techs at your local Toyota dealership for specific recommendations for your car.

## How Often Should Transmission Fluid Be Changed?

When it comes to changing transmission fluid, it's essential to follow the manufacturer's recommendations outlined in your vehicle's owner's manual. Some newer vehicles with "lifetime" transmission fluid require less-frequent transmission fluid changes unless a problem with the transmission crops up, necessitating it.

However, some conditions may warrant shorter transmission fluid change intervals such as: towing or hauling, frequent exposure to severe weather conditions, stop-and-go traffic, or at the first sign of transmission problems, such as gear slippage, grinding noises, delayed shifting, and excessive vibration.

Manual transmissions typically require less frequent fluid changes compared to automatic transmissions. Defer to the recommendations of your owner's manual or the service technician at your local Toyota dealership.

## How to Check Transmission Fluid?

It's essential to consult your vehicle's owner's manual for specific instructions and recommendations regarding transmission fluid type and level-checking procedures, as they can vary between different vehicles. If you're unsure or uncomfortable performing this task yourself, it's always best to seek assistance from a skilled technician.

In general, to check your transmission fluid, park your car on a level surface and start the engine. Locate the transmission dipstick under the hood, pull it out, and wipe it clean. Fully reinsert the dipstick, then pull it out again to check the fluid level to see where it falls between the markings on the dipstick.

Next, check the color of the transmission fluid: pinkish-red transmission fluid typically indicates that the fluid is clean and healthy with the chemical composition to effectively lubricate and cool the transmission components. If the fluid appears significantly darker or has a burnt smell, it may indicate contamination or degradation, suggesting it's time for a fluid change or closer inspection by a technician.

Most newer model vehicles have sealed transmission systems which may not have a dipstick for checking transmission fluid levels. Instead, the vehicle's internal mechanisms may automatically check and adjust fluid levels. Sealed transmission systems are designed to be maintenance-free. However, if you suspect a problem with a sealed transmission, it's best to consult an auto technician at your local Toyota dealership.

## How to Change Transmission Fluid

Changing transmission fluid involves locating the transmission fluid drain plug, draining the old fluid into a container, and removing the transmission pan to access the filter. Final steps include cleaning the pan, reinstalling it, and refilling the transmission with the appropriate type and amount of new fluid, following manufacturer recommendations, and then checking for leaks.

Ultimately, regular maintenance and staying attentive to your vehicle's performance are helpful in determining when transmission fluid changes may be needed. If in doubt, consult the professionals at your local Toyota dealership for personalized advice based on your vehicle's specific needs and usage.

- Drive shaft boots

- Exhaust pipes and mountings
- Fuel lines and connections

If our team sees anything that might need repairs soon, we will let you know.

### Toyota RAV4 Maintenance Required At 35,000 Miles Or 42 Months

The 35,000-mile service interval includes what you get during the 5,000-mile maintenance period.

### Toyota RAV4 Maintenance Schedule At 40,000 Miles Or 48 Months

This is when the engine oil and oil filter are changed, as well as the other standard tasks.

### Toyota RAV4 Maintenance Schedule At 45,000 Miles Or 54 Months

During your 45,000-mile Toyota RAV4 service appointment, you can expect the following:

- Ball joints and dust covers
- Brake lines and hoses
- Cabin air filter
- Drive shaft boots
- Engine coolant
- Exhaust pipes and mountings
- Radiator and condenser
- Steering gear
- Steering linkage and boots

### Toyota RAV4 Maintenance Schedule At 50,000 Miles Or 60 Months

The 50,000-mile appointment requires another oil change and replacement of the oil and cabin air filter. At this point, your SUV may need new tires, new brake pads, or a battery, depending on your Long Branch driving habits and the amount of wear and tear on your vehicle.

### Toyota RAV4 Service Schedule At 55,000 Miles Or 66 Months

When you hit 55,000 miles, it’s time to check all of the fluids, get a tire rotation, and a visual examination of your brakes.

### Toyota RAV4 Service Schedule At 60,000 Miles Or 72 Months

This consists of all of the standard 30,000-mile checks, refills, and replacements.

Your [brakes](https://vw.oempartsonline.com/brakes) stop your [Volkswagen](https://vw.oempartsonline.com/v-volkswagen) vehicle. They do it by clamping their calipers and brake rotors together. This is what creates the friction, or resistance, that slows your vehicle's wheels and tires. However, calipers can't press rotors without brake pads, or else they'd get damaged. Your VW has one of four types of pads, depending on its model. Organic brake pads are for everyday driving. They're reliable, they don't wear rotors down as badly, and they don't create much dust. Best of all, they're inexpensive. Ceramic brake pads work better in bad weather, they don't make much noise, and their dust isn't as sticky. Metallic brake pads, however, stand up to higher heat, feel firmer, and resist brake fade. Carbon fiber brake pads are the strongest and best performers, tolerant of high temperatures and providing the most stopping power. Most cars and SUVs use either metallic or organic pads. However, many sports cars and performance vehicles use ceramic or carbon fiber pads because they do the best job of expelling heat.

## How Long Do Volkswagen Brake Pads Last?

However, no brake pad lasts forever, not even those Volkswagen makes. You should change yours every 40,000 to 50,000 miles or so. Otherwise, figure out when to replace them by looking for the signs your brakes are going bad. They include warning lights, worn pad surfaces, pad damage, whiny brakes, and taking longer to stop. The worst are vibration and grinding, as they indicate your rotors are warped and getting damaged because your brake pads have degraded.

This OEM Audi engine oil filter element, part number 06L-115-562-B, is a filtration medium, one that captures impurities and contaminants before they get into an Audi vehicle's engine, build up, and wear out parts like the oil pump and its bearings. # BMW SERVICE

BMW recommends you have your maintenance and repair work performed by an authorized BMW center.

# MAINTAINING YOUR BMW VEHICLE

A well-maintained vehicle will help safeguard its operational performance, road-safety and its reliability. This is why it is important to follow and perform BMW’s recommended periodic vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks as indicated by your vehicle’s Maintenance Service Display, along with the other maintenance work described in this booklet.

A improper maintenance is not covered under the BMW New Vehicle Damage, including consequential damage, which results from lack of or Limited Warranty for Passenger Cars and Light Trucks.

# MAINTENANCE INTERVALS

Maintenance intervals on motor vehicles were conventionally based solely on a fixed time period or a specified amount of accumulated driving mileage.

However, operational and driving conditions have a major influence on your vehicle’s routine maintenance requirements; the distance traveled is only one of these significant factors. A vehicle used for short trips in the city with numerous cold starts, prolonged periods of idling, stop-and-go driving, and high engine speeds during acceleration may require more frequent maintenance intervals than a vehicle that is driven long distances at moderate engine speeds.

Your BMW vehicle uses sensors and algorithms together with the elapsed time and the driving distance/profile to monitor and evaluate your vehicle’s maintenance service needs. This information is then used to adapt dynamically the parameters used to forecast the applicable maintenance service task intervals.

# THE BMW MAINTENANCE SYSTEM

All BMW vehicles are equipped with an integrated BMW Maintenance System. This maintenance “reminder” system helps ensure that the vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks are performed at the forecasted intervals that apply to your vehicle.

The BMW Maintenance System display provides the vehicle operator access to the current status information for the following maintenance service tasks:

$\\triangleright$ Engine oil (date and miles)\*

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle check (date and miles)

$\\triangleright$ Front brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Rear brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid (date)

$\\triangleright$ 1200 Mile running-in service (date and miles) (Applicable to BMW M vehicles only)\*

For each specific maintenance service task, either the future date (month/ year), remaining miles or both are provided as noted above. The system monitors variable inputs to forecast the intervals and alert the driver when one or more specific maintenance tasks should be performed.

NOTE: For certain vehicles, the status of the front and rear brake pads will only be observable in the maintenance system’s display when there are approximately 2,000 miles or less remaining before a brake service will be required to be performed.

For information about the vehicle’s maintenance system displays, please refer to the Maintenance Service Display Overview section beginning on page 5.

The following “combine with Engine oil”\* maintenance service tasks may be identified as needing to be performed with a specific occurrence of the “Engine oil” service task (service counter number):

$\\triangleright$ Cabin Microfilter(s)

$\\triangleright$ Engine air filter(s)\*

$\\triangleright$ Spark plugs\*

$\\triangleright$ Final drive oil (Applicable M vehicles only)

\\* Does not apply to BEV

Although these items do not appear in the BMW Maintenance System’s display in the vehicle, these services should be performed when your vehicle’s engine oil is changed in accordance with the interval identified by your vehicle’s BMW Maintenance System.

For more information on your vehicle’s maintenance services requirements, procedures and intervals, please refer the Maintenance Service Summary section beginning on page 10.

The BMW Maintenance System also includes an option to set service reminders for the following state-specific mandatory vehicle inspections, including:

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle safety inspection; and/or $\\triangleright$ Emissions test

The corresponding interval data for these inspections can be inputted into the BMW Maintenance System by a service provider; they are not determined by the vehicle.

For your convenience, you may also wish to have your authorized BMW center perform the work necessary to fulfill these state inspection requirements in your area concurrent with the maintenance services specified above when possible.

Should you request more frequent maintenance service than is indicated by the BMW Maintenance System during the coverage period, the cost of these services will not be covered by the BMW Maintenance Program.

# SERVICE DATA — REMOTE CONTROL KEY

Maintenance service task status information for your BMW vehicle is continually updated and stored in your remote control key.

Your authorized BMW center can access this data and consult with you about applicable service procedures and tasks for your vehicle.

Therefore, always provide your service consultant with the most recent remote control key that was used to operate the vehicle when servicing your vehicle at a BMW center.

# VEHICLE STORAGE

Disconnecting the battery during periods of long-term vehicle storage will interrupt the calculation of time-dependent maintenance services.

In this situation, BMW recommends that you have all your time-based maintenance services, such as brake fluid, engine oil and cabin microfilter, brought up to the correct date by an authorized BMW center.

# ENGINE OIL

2025 model year vehicles with internal-combustion engines are factory-filled with:

Z BMW-approved fully synthetic oil for gasoline engines

Engine oil should be changed when the vehicle’s engine is at operating temperature.

If an engine oil service is being performed or you need to add engine oil between changes, please refer to the Owner’s Manual for the recommended engine oil for your BMW vehicle.

# LONG-TERM RATED FLUIDS AND OILS

The following systems and assemblies are factory-filled with long-term rated fluid and oil; fluid replacement is only necessary when repairs are being performed (unless otherwise noted):

$\\triangleright$ Engine cooling system (antifreeze/coolant) $\\triangleright$ Automatic (except for X1 and X2) and manual transmissions $\\triangleright$ All-wheel drive transfer cases (except when indicated by the vehicle)

# REGULAR CHECKS — VEHICLE OPERATOR

In addition to the maintenance service procedure information contained in this booklet, BMW recommends that you regularly check (when refueling, for example), and address when necessary, the following items:

$\\triangleright$ Washer fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Coolant level

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Tires — pressure, condition and wear

Please refer to the Owner’s Manual for additional information.

The **BMW i5 maintenance schedule** looks very different from a gas-powered 5 Series. There’s no engine oil, spark plugs, or timing chain to worry about, but you still have brakes, tires, coolant, software, and a sophisticated high-voltage system that all need attention. If you’re driving or shopping for a BMW i5, understanding the real service intervals and long‑term maintenance picture can save you time, money, and stress.

### Quick take

Compared with a gasoline 5 Series, a BMW i5 typically needs fewer scheduled services and less routine maintenance. Most owners will visit a service center about once a year for inspections, fluids, and software, plus wear items like tires and brakes as they age.

## BMW i5 maintenance overview

The BMW i5 is built on the same platform as the current 5 Series, but its **electric powertrain dramatically changes the maintenance profile**. You still follow a factory schedule, but the high‑value items are:

\- Safety inspections (suspension, steering, brakes)
\- Brake fluid changes
\- Cabin air filter and other filters
\- Coolant for the battery and power electronics
\- High‑voltage system checks
\- Software and firmware updates

For most U.S. drivers, you’re looking at **annual visits** rather than old‑school 5,000–7,500‑mile oil changes.

## BMW i5 service intervals by mileage and time

BMW doesn’t publish a simple one‑page chart for every market; instead, the i5 uses **Condition Based Service (CBS)**. The car monitors mileage, time, and driving style, then tells you when service is due. That said, most i5s in the U.S. will follow patterns that look roughly like this:

- Every 10,000–12,000 miles or 12 months: General inspection and basic service
- Every 2 years: Brake fluid replacement and broader safety checks
- Every 3–4 years: Cabin air filter, key coolant checks, 12‑volt battery health review
- Around 5–6 years: Deeper coolant service and more detailed high‑voltage inspections

### Always defer to your i5’s on‑screen reminders

Use this guide as a planning tool, not a substitute for the factory schedule. Your i5’s digital service reminders and your BMW service advisor have the final word on what’s actually due.

## BMW i5 maintenance schedule at a glance

Here’s a simplified BMW i5 maintenance schedule to help you visualize what’s coming. Actual mileage can vary a bit by model year, driving style, and market, but this table gives you a realistic roadmap.

### Typical BMW i5 maintenance schedule (planning guide)

Approximate intervals for common BMW i5 service items. Always confirm with your vehicle’s on‑board service menu and owner’s manual.

| Mileage / Time | Main Service Items | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 10,000–12,000 miles or 12 months | Multi‑point inspection, tire rotation (if applicable), brake check, fluid level check | First full check‑in; some owners may see this closer to 8,000–10,000 miles |
| 20,000–24,000 miles or 2 years | Inspection, brake fluid change, cabin filter (if needed), software updates | Brake fluid interval is usually time‑based (about every 2 years) |
| 30,000–36,000 miles or 3 years | Inspection, alignment check if needed, coolant checks, 12‑volt battery test | May coincide with tire replacement depending on driving style |
| 40,000–48,000 miles or 4 years | Inspection, brake fluid change, cabin filter, more detailed suspension/brake check | Good time to evaluate brake pad/rotor wear |
| 60,000–72,000 miles or 6 years | Inspection, brake fluid, coolant service as recommended, high‑voltage system check | Heavier service visit; budget extra for any wear items |
| \> 75,000 miles | Ongoing annual inspections, fluids as due, tires/brakes as needed | Battery and drive units typically inspected, not routinely replaced |

High‑voltage battery and drive units are generally inspected, not replaced, during normal ownership.

### Use the BMW app to stay ahead

The BMW app can show upcoming service items and help you schedule visits. Syncing your car and app makes it easier to plan maintenance around your life instead of the other way around.

![BMW i5 on a service lift with a technician inspecting the suspension and underbody components](https://recharged.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fd365moeqy2c2l.cloudfront.net%2Fimages%2Fcontent%2Fc9aa6f4589738f1f554a084598e79a63-content.png&w=3840&q=75)

Even with fewer moving parts than a gas car, a BMW i5 still needs regular inspections for brakes, suspension, and tires.

## Key BMW i5 EV maintenance items explained

The BMW i5 eliminates many traditional services, but a few EV‑specific items matter more. Understanding them helps you read your maintenance schedule with confidence, and avoid approving work you don’t need.

### Core BMW i5 maintenance items

What they are, why they matter, and when to expect them

#### Brake fluid

EVs still use hydraulic brakes. Over time, brake fluid absorbs moisture, which can corrode components and reduce performance.

**Typical pattern:** Every ~2 years, regardless of mileage.

#### Cabin air filter

Keeps dust and pollutants out of the cabin and HVAC system.

**Typical pattern:** About every 2–3 years, or sooner in dusty or urban environments.

#### Coolant for battery & power electronics

Liquid coolant manages temperatures for the high‑voltage battery, inverter, and other components.

**Typical pattern:** Inspected regularly; partial or full replacement tends to show up around the 5–6 year mark.

#### High‑voltage battery checks

Technicians monitor battery health, seal integrity, and software diagnostics rather than swapping major components.

**Typical pattern:** Inspected during scheduled services or when the car flags an issue.

#### Suspension & steering

i5s are heavy, powerful sedans. Bushings, tie rods, and other hardware still wear over time.

**Typical pattern:** Inspected annually; replacement is mileage and road‑condition dependent.

#### Software & firmware updates

Updates can improve efficiency, charging behavior, and even add features.

**Typical pattern:** Applied over‑the‑air or during dealer visits as they become available.

### Don’t ignore brake warnings

Because EVs use regenerative braking, physical brake pads can last a long time, but when your i5 flags a brake issue, it’s critical. Delaying brake service risks rotor damage and safety problems that are far more expensive than a timely repair.

## BMW i5 maintenance costs and what actually wears out

With no oil changes or exhaust system, a BMW i5’s **routine maintenance costs** often undercut a gas 5 Series over the first several years. Where EVs catch up, or even surpass, traditional cars is in **wear items** like tires, brakes, and out‑of‑warranty electronics.

### Lower‑frequency, lower‑cost items

- Annual inspections and fluid checks
- Brake fluid every ~2 years
- Cabin air filter every few years
- Basic software updates during visits

These visits are predictable and usually modest in cost compared with major ICE services like spark plug replacement or timing components.

### Big‑ticket wear items to budget for

- **Tires:** Instant torque and weight can wear them faster, especially on performance trims.

# BMW SERVICE

BMW recommends you have your maintenance and repair work performed by an authorized BMW center.

# MAINTAINING YOUR BMW VEHICLE

A well-maintained vehicle will help safeguard its operational performance, road-safety and its reliability. This is why it is important to follow and perform BMW’s recommended periodic vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks as indicated by your vehicle’s Maintenance Service Display, along with the other maintenance work described in this booklet.

A improper maintenance is not covered under the BMW New Vehicle Damage, including consequential damage, which results from lack of or Limited Warranty for Passenger Cars and Light Trucks.

# MAINTENANCE INTERVALS

Maintenance intervals on motor vehicles were conventionally based solely on a fixed time period or a specified amount of accumulated driving mileage.

However, operational and driving conditions have a major influence on your vehicle’s routine maintenance requirements; the distance traveled is only one of these significant factors. A vehicle used for short trips in the city with numerous cold starts, prolonged periods of idling, stop-and-go driving, and high engine speeds during acceleration may require more frequent maintenance intervals than a vehicle that is driven long distances at moderate engine speeds.

Your BMW vehicle uses sensors and algorithms together with the elapsed time and the driving distance/profile to monitor and evaluate your vehicle’s maintenance service needs. This information is then used to adapt dynamically the parameters used to forecast the applicable maintenance service task intervals.

# THE BMW MAINTENANCE SYSTEM

All BMW vehicles are equipped with an integrated BMW Maintenance System. This maintenance “reminder” system helps ensure that the vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks are performed at the forecasted intervals that apply to your vehicle.

The BMW Maintenance System display provides the vehicle operator access to the current status information for the following maintenance service tasks:

$\\triangleright$ Engine oil (date and miles)\*

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle check (date and miles)

$\\triangleright$ Front brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Rear brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid (date)

$\\triangleright$ 1200 Mile running-in service (date and miles) (Applicable to BMW M vehicles only)\*

For each specific maintenance service task, either the future date (month/ year), remaining miles or both are provided as noted above. The system monitors variable inputs to forecast the intervals and alert the driver when one or more specific maintenance tasks should be performed.

NOTE: For certain vehicles, the status of the front and rear brake pads will only be observable in the maintenance system’s display when there are approximately 2,000 miles or less remaining before a brake service will be required to be performed.

For information about the vehicle’s maintenance system displays, please refer to the Maintenance Service Display Overview section beginning on page 5.

The following “combine with Engine oil”\* maintenance service tasks may be identified as needing to be performed with a specific occurrence of the “Engine oil” service task (service counter number):

$\\triangleright$ Cabin Microfilter(s)

$\\triangleright$ Engine air filter(s)\*

$\\triangleright$ Spark plugs\*

$\\triangleright$ Final drive oil (Applicable M vehicles only)

\\* Does not apply to BEV

Although these items do not appear in the BMW Maintenance System’s display in the vehicle, these services should be performed when your vehicle’s engine oil is changed in accordance with the interval identified by your vehicle’s BMW Maintenance System.

For more information on your vehicle’s maintenance services requirements, procedures and intervals, please refer the Maintenance Service Summary section beginning on page 10.

The BMW Maintenance System also includes an option to set service reminders for the following state-specific mandatory vehicle inspections, including:

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle safety inspection; and/or $\\triangleright$ Emissions test

The corresponding interval data for these inspections can be inputted into the BMW Maintenance System by a service provider; they are not determined by the vehicle.

For your convenience, you may also wish to have your authorized BMW center perform the work necessary to fulfill these state inspection requirements in your area concurrent with the maintenance services specified above when possible.

Should you request more frequent maintenance service than is indicated by the BMW Maintenance System during the coverage period, the cost of these services will not be covered by the BMW Maintenance Program.

# SERVICE DATA — REMOTE CONTROL KEY

Maintenance service task status information for your BMW vehicle is continually updated and stored in your remote control key.

Your authorized BMW center can access this data and consult with you about applicable service procedures and tasks for your vehicle.

Therefore, always provide your service consultant with the most recent remote control key that was used to operate the vehicle when servicing your vehicle at a BMW center.

# VEHICLE STORAGE

Disconnecting the battery during periods of long-term vehicle storage will interrupt the calculation of time-dependent maintenance services.

In this situation, BMW recommends that you have all your time-based maintenance services, such as brake fluid, engine oil and cabin microfilter, brought up to the correct date by an authorized BMW center.

# ENGINE OIL

2025 model year vehicles with internal-combustion engines are factory-filled with:

Z BMW-approved fully synthetic oil for gasoline engines

Engine oil should be changed when the vehicle’s engine is at operating temperature.

If an engine oil service is being performed or you need to add engine oil between changes, please refer to the Owner’s Manual for the recommended engine oil for your BMW vehicle.

# LONG-TERM RATED FLUIDS AND OILS

The following systems and assemblies are factory-filled with long-term rated fluid and oil; fluid replacement is only necessary when repairs are being performed (unless otherwise noted):

$\\triangleright$ Engine cooling system (antifreeze/coolant) $\\triangleright$ Automatic (except for X1 and X2) and manual transmissions $\\triangleright$ All-wheel drive transfer cases (except when indicated by the vehicle)

# REGULAR CHECKS — VEHICLE OPERATOR

In addition to the maintenance service procedure information contained in this booklet, BMW recommends that you regularly check (when refueling, for example), and address when necessary, the following items:

$\\triangleright$ Washer fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Coolant level

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Tires — pressure, condition and wear

Please refer to the Owner’s Manual for additional information.

# BMW X3 Maintenance Schedule

* * *

Owning a BMW X3 means enjoying top-tier performance and luxury, but regular maintenance is key to keeping your vehicle running smoothly. Staying on top of your X3’s maintenance schedule will not only enhance its performance but also extend its lifespan on the roads of Norwood, Westwood, and Dedham, MA.

Here's a breakdown of what [BMW services](https://www.bmwnorwood.com/service/schedule-service/) are needed at various mileage intervals.

## Every 5,000-10,000 Miles

At the first interval after you start driving your BMW X3, typically around 5,000 to 10,000 miles, you’ll need to perform several basic yet essential maintenance tasks.

First and foremost is an oil change. Your vehicle’s oil should be changed every 10,000 miles or 12 months, depending on which comes first. However, a more regular oil check, say every 5,000 miles or so, can help ensure your X3 is always equipped with clean and healthy oil.

Some other services you may see at this interval include a quick inspection of your brakes as well as a tire rotation.

![Brake Service](https://di-uploads-pod40.dealerinspire.com/bmwnorwood/uploads/2024/10/Brake-2.jpg)

## Every 10,000-15,000 Miles

Around this mileage, you should include additional checks on essential [vehicle parts](https://www.bmwnorwood.com/parts/) like your brakes, battery, engine, and more. Additionally, you’ll see a handful of routine services such as:

- **Replace Wiper Blades**
- **Replace Key Fob Battery**
- **Inspect/Replace Coolant**
- **Inspect Brake Pads and Rotors**

## Every 60,000 Miles

The 60,000-mile mark is a fairly significant one in the lifespan of your BMW X3. At this interval, you’ll have several key components replaced.

You can expect your vehicle’s spark plugs, transmission fluid, and tires to all be replaced around this time. Be sure to keep an eye on the condition of your tires, however, as they may need to be replaced sooner.

## Every 75,000 Miles

At the 75,000-mile interval, you can expect many of the standard services like an oil change or a tire rotation. Though, there are several other components you’ll want to have inspected at this point, including:

- **Brake Pads, Calipers, and Rotors**
- **Cooling System and Hoses**
- **Suspension System**

## Every 90,000-100,000 Miles

As you near 90,000 to 100,000 miles in your BMW X3, another important set of services awaits. Here, you’ll see a complete flush and replacement of your transmission fluid. The driveshaft must also be lubricated to ensure your engine parts are moving without any issues.

The service team will also inspect a number of parts once again like the driveshaft boots, fuel injector, any belts and hoses, as well as the water pump.

# MAINTAINING YOUR BMW VEHICLE

A well-maintained vehicle will help safeguard its operational performance, road-safety and its reliability. This is why it is important to follow and perform BMW’s recommended periodic vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks as indicated by your vehicle’s Maintenance Service Display, along with the other maintenance work described in this booklet.

A improper maintenance is not covered under the BMW New Vehicle Damage, including consequential damage, which results from lack of or Limited Warranty for Passenger Cars and Light Trucks.

# MAINTENANCE INTERVALS

Maintenance intervals on motor vehicles were conventionally based solely on a fixed time period or a specified amount of accumulated driving mileage.

However, operational and driving conditions have a major influence on your vehicle’s routine maintenance requirements; the distance traveled is only one of these significant factors. A vehicle used for short trips in the city with numerous cold starts, prolonged periods of idling, stop-and-go driving, and high engine speeds during acceleration may require more frequent maintenance intervals than a vehicle that is driven long distances at moderate engine speeds.

Your BMW vehicle uses sensors and algorithms together with the elapsed time and the driving distance/profile to monitor and evaluate your vehicle’s maintenance service needs. This information is then used to adapt dynamically the parameters used to forecast the applicable maintenance service task intervals.

# THE BMW MAINTENANCE SYSTEM

All BMW vehicles are equipped with an integrated BMW Maintenance System. This maintenance “reminder” system helps ensure that the vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks are performed at the forecasted intervals that apply to your vehicle.

The BMW Maintenance System display provides the vehicle operator access to the current status information for the following maintenance service tasks:

$\\triangleright$ Engine oil (date and miles)\*

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle check (date and miles)

$\\triangleright$ Front brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Rear brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid (date)

$\\triangleright$ 1200 Mile running-in service (date and miles) (Applicable to BMW M vehicles only)\*

For each specific maintenance service task, either the future date (month/ year), remaining miles or both are provided as noted above. The system monitors variable inputs to forecast the intervals and alert the driver when one or more specific maintenance tasks should be performed.

NOTE: For certain vehicles, the status of the front and rear brake pads will only be observable in the maintenance system’s display when there are approximately 2,000 miles or less remaining before a brake service will be required to be performed.

For information about the vehicle’s maintenance system displays, please refer to the Maintenance Service Display Overview section beginning on page 5.

The following “combine with Engine oil”\* maintenance service tasks may be identified as needing to be performed with a specific occurrence of the “Engine oil” service task (service counter number):

$\\triangleright$ Cabin Microfilter(s)

$\\triangleright$ Engine air filter(s)\*

$\\triangleright$ Spark plugs\*

$\\triangleright$ Final drive oil (Applicable M vehicles only)

\\* Does not apply to BEV

Although these items do not appear in the BMW Maintenance System’s display in the vehicle, these services should be performed when your vehicle’s engine oil is changed in accordance with the interval identified by your vehicle’s BMW Maintenance System.

For more information on your vehicle’s maintenance services requirements, procedures and intervals, please refer the Maintenance Service Summary section beginning on page 10.

The BMW Maintenance System also includes an option to set service reminders for the following state-specific mandatory vehicle inspections, including:

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle safety inspection; and/or $\\triangleright$ Emissions test

The corresponding interval data for these inspections can be inputted into the BMW Maintenance System by a service provider; they are not determined by the vehicle.

For your convenience, you may also wish to have your authorized BMW center perform the work necessary to fulfill these state inspection requirements in your area concurrent with the maintenance services specified above when possible.

Should you request more frequent maintenance service than is indicated by the BMW Maintenance System during the coverage period, the cost of these services will not be covered by the BMW Maintenance Program.

# SERVICE DATA — REMOTE CONTROL KEY

Maintenance service task status information for your BMW vehicle is continually updated and stored in your remote control key.

Your authorized BMW center can access this data and consult with you about applicable service procedures and tasks for your vehicle.

Therefore, always provide your service consultant with the most recent remote control key that was used to operate the vehicle when servicing your vehicle at a BMW center.

# VEHICLE STORAGE

Disconnecting the battery during periods of long-term vehicle storage will interrupt the calculation of time-dependent maintenance services.

In this situation, BMW recommends that you have all your time-based maintenance services, such as brake fluid, engine oil and cabin microfilter, brought up to the correct date by an authorized BMW center.

# ENGINE OIL

2025 model year vehicles with internal-combustion engines are factory-filled with:

Z BMW-approved fully synthetic oil for gasoline engines

Engine oil should be changed when the vehicle’s engine is at operating temperature.

If an engine oil service is being performed or you need to add engine oil between changes, please refer to the Owner’s Manual for the recommended engine oil for your BMW vehicle.

# LONG-TERM RATED FLUIDS AND OILS

The following systems and assemblies are factory-filled with long-term rated fluid and oil; fluid replacement is only necessary when repairs are being performed (unless otherwise noted):

$\\triangleright$ Engine cooling system (antifreeze/coolant) $\\triangleright$ Automatic (except for X1 and X2) and manual transmissions $\\triangleright$ All-wheel drive transfer cases (except when indicated by the vehicle)

# REGULAR CHECKS — VEHICLE OPERATOR

In addition to the maintenance service procedure information contained in this booklet, BMW recommends that you regularly check (when refueling, for example), and address when necessary, the following items:

$\\triangleright$ Washer fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Coolant level

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Tires — pressure, condition and wear

Please refer to the Owner’s Manual for additional information.

- Inspect Suspension System

- Inspect/Replace Calipers/Rotors
- Inspect/Replace Your Brake Pads

**Every 90,000-100,000 Miles:**

- Inspect Fuel Injector
- Lubricate the Driveshaft
- Inspect Driveshaft Boots
- Inspect/Replace Belts, Hoses, and Water Pump
- Flush and Replace All the Transmission Fluid

- Regular service visits keep your vehicle running as efficiently as possible on the roads of Fort Lauderdale and Hollywood.
- Drive with confidence behind the wheel of a well-maintained vehicle.
- If you plan to sell your vehicle in the future, one that is up to date on the BMW X3 service schedule will be more appealing to potential buyers.

# BMW X3 Maintenance Schedule

* * *

Owning a BMW X3 means enjoying top-tier performance and luxury, but regular maintenance is key to keeping your vehicle running smoothly. Staying on top of your X3’s maintenance schedule will not only enhance its performance but also extend its lifespan on the roads of Norwood, Westwood, and Dedham, MA.

Here's a breakdown of what [BMW services](https://www.bmwnorwood.com/service/schedule-service/) are needed at various mileage intervals.

## Every 5,000-10,000 Miles

At the first interval after you start driving your BMW X3, typically around 5,000 to 10,000 miles, you’ll need to perform several basic yet essential maintenance tasks.

First and foremost is an oil change. Your vehicle’s oil should be changed every 10,000 miles or 12 months, depending on which comes first. However, a more regular oil check, say every 5,000 miles or so, can help ensure your X3 is always equipped with clean and healthy oil.

Some other services you may see at this interval include a quick inspection of your brakes as well as a tire rotation.

![Brake Service](https://di-uploads-pod40.dealerinspire.com/bmwnorwood/uploads/2024/10/Brake-2.jpg)

## Every 10,000-15,000 Miles

Around this mileage, you should include additional checks on essential [vehicle parts](https://www.bmwnorwood.com/parts/) like your brakes, battery, engine, and more. Additionally, you’ll see a handful of routine services such as:

- **Replace Wiper Blades**
- **Replace Key Fob Battery**
- **Inspect/Replace Coolant**
- **Inspect Brake Pads and Rotors**

## Every 60,000 Miles

The 60,000-mile mark is a fairly significant one in the lifespan of your BMW X3. At this interval, you’ll have several key components replaced.

You can expect your vehicle’s spark plugs, transmission fluid, and tires to all be replaced around this time. Be sure to keep an eye on the condition of your tires, however, as they may need to be replaced sooner.

## Every 75,000 Miles

At the 75,000-mile interval, you can expect many of the standard services like an oil change or a tire rotation. Though, there are several other components you’ll want to have inspected at this point, including:

- **Brake Pads, Calipers, and Rotors**
- **Cooling System and Hoses**
- **Suspension System**

## Every 90,000-100,000 Miles

As you near 90,000 to 100,000 miles in your BMW X3, another important set of services awaits. Here, you’ll see a complete flush and replacement of your transmission fluid. The driveshaft must also be lubricated to ensure your engine parts are moving without any issues.

The service team will also inspect a number of parts once again like the driveshaft boots, fuel injector, any belts and hoses, as well as the water pump.

## Schedule BMW X3 Service Today!

* * *

Keeping up with your BMW X3’s maintenance schedule is essential for long-term performance and safety. If you're near Norwood, Westwood, or Dedham, MA, [schedule service](https://www.bmwnorwood.com/service/schedule-service/) at BMW of Norwood to show your vehicle the expert care it deserves.

# BMW SERVICE

BMW recommends you have your maintenance and repair work performed by an authorized BMW center.

# MAINTAINING YOUR BMW VEHICLE

A well-maintained vehicle will help safeguard its operational performance, road-safety and its reliability. This is why it is important to follow and perform BMW’s recommended periodic vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks as indicated by your vehicle’s Maintenance Service Display, along with the other maintenance work described in this booklet.

A improper maintenance is not covered under the BMW New Vehicle Damage, including consequential damage, which results from lack of or Limited Warranty for Passenger Cars and Light Trucks.

# MAINTENANCE INTERVALS

Maintenance intervals on motor vehicles were conventionally based solely on a fixed time period or a specified amount of accumulated driving mileage.

However, operational and driving conditions have a major influence on your vehicle’s routine maintenance requirements; the distance traveled is only one of these significant factors. A vehicle used for short trips in the city with numerous cold starts, prolonged periods of idling, stop-and-go driving, and high engine speeds during acceleration may require more frequent maintenance intervals than a vehicle that is driven long distances at moderate engine speeds.

Your BMW vehicle uses sensors and algorithms together with the elapsed time and the driving distance/profile to monitor and evaluate your vehicle’s maintenance service needs. This information is then used to adapt dynamically the parameters used to forecast the applicable maintenance service task intervals.

# THE BMW MAINTENANCE SYSTEM

All BMW vehicles are equipped with an integrated BMW Maintenance System. This maintenance “reminder” system helps ensure that the vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks are performed at the forecasted intervals that apply to your vehicle.

The BMW Maintenance System display provides the vehicle operator access to the current status information for the following maintenance service tasks:

$\\triangleright$ Engine oil (date and miles)\*

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle check (date and miles)

$\\triangleright$ Front brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Rear brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid (date)

$\\triangleright$ 1200 Mile running-in service (date and miles) (Applicable to BMW M vehicles only)\*

For each specific maintenance service task, either the future date (month/ year), remaining miles or both are provided as noted above. The system monitors variable inputs to forecast the intervals and alert the driver when one or more specific maintenance tasks should be performed.

NOTE: For certain vehicles, the status of the front and rear brake pads will only be observable in the maintenance system’s display when there are approximately 2,000 miles or less remaining before a brake service will be required to be performed.

For information about the vehicle’s maintenance system displays, please refer to the Maintenance Service Display Overview section beginning on page 5.

The following “combine with Engine oil”\* maintenance service tasks may be identified as needing to be performed with a specific occurrence of the “Engine oil” service task (service counter number):

$\\triangleright$ Cabin Microfilter(s)

$\\triangleright$ Engine air filter(s)\*

$\\triangleright$ Spark plugs\*

$\\triangleright$ Final drive oil (Applicable M vehicles only)

\\* Does not apply to BEV

Although these items do not appear in the BMW Maintenance System’s display in the vehicle, these services should be performed when your vehicle’s engine oil is changed in accordance with the interval identified by your vehicle’s BMW Maintenance System.

For more information on your vehicle’s maintenance services requirements, procedures and intervals, please refer the Maintenance Service Summary section beginning on page 10.

The BMW Maintenance System also includes an option to set service reminders for the following state-specific mandatory vehicle inspections, including:

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle safety inspection; and/or $\\triangleright$ Emissions test

The corresponding interval data for these inspections can be inputted into the BMW Maintenance System by a service provider; they are not determined by the vehicle.

For your convenience, you may also wish to have your authorized BMW center perform the work necessary to fulfill these state inspection requirements in your area concurrent with the maintenance services specified above when possible.

Should you request more frequent maintenance service than is indicated by the BMW Maintenance System during the coverage period, the cost of these services will not be covered by the BMW Maintenance Program.

# SERVICE DATA — REMOTE CONTROL KEY

Maintenance service task status information for your BMW vehicle is continually updated and stored in your remote control key.

Your authorized BMW center can access this data and consult with you about applicable service procedures and tasks for your vehicle.

Therefore, always provide your service consultant with the most recent remote control key that was used to operate the vehicle when servicing your vehicle at a BMW center.

# VEHICLE STORAGE

Disconnecting the battery during periods of long-term vehicle storage will interrupt the calculation of time-dependent maintenance services.

In this situation, BMW recommends that you have all your time-based maintenance services, such as brake fluid, engine oil and cabin microfilter, brought up to the correct date by an authorized BMW center.

# ENGINE OIL

2025 model year vehicles with internal-combustion engines are factory-filled with:

Z BMW-approved fully synthetic oil for gasoline engines

Engine oil should be changed when the vehicle’s engine is at operating temperature.

If an engine oil service is being performed or you need to add engine oil between changes, please refer to the Owner’s Manual for the recommended engine oil for your BMW vehicle.

# LONG-TERM RATED FLUIDS AND OILS

The following systems and assemblies are factory-filled with long-term rated fluid and oil; fluid replacement is only necessary when repairs are being performed (unless otherwise noted):

$\\triangleright$ Engine cooling system (antifreeze/coolant) $\\triangleright$ Automatic (except for X1 and X2) and manual transmissions $\\triangleright$ All-wheel drive transfer cases (except when indicated by the vehicle)

# REGULAR CHECKS — VEHICLE OPERATOR

In addition to the maintenance service procedure information contained in this booklet, BMW recommends that you regularly check (when refueling, for example), and address when necessary, the following items:

$\\triangleright$ Washer fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Coolant level

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Tires — pressure, condition and wear

Please refer to the Owner’s Manual for additional information.
