## What Does the BMW Maintenance Schedule Include?

BMW maintenance is broken down into intervals, based on time or mileage. Below are general service milestones for most BMW models:

### BMW 10,000-Mile Maintenance

- At 10,000 miles or 12 months, schedule an oil change, brake inspection, and tire rotation.

### BMW 20,000-Mile Maintenance

- At 20,000 miles, replace the cabin air filter and perform a more comprehensive inspection.

### BMW 30,000-Mile Maintenance

- At 30,000-40,000 miles, inspect suspension, steering components, coolant, and belts.
- If manual transmission: replace [transmission fluid](https://www.bmwofturnersville.com/service/service-tips/check-your-transmission-fluid/) every 30,000 miles

### BMW 60,000-Mile Maintenance

- At 60,000 miles, flush and replace brake fluid, inspect spark plugs, and change the engine air filter.

### Additional BMW Maintenance

Every two years, replace the cabin microfilter and test battery performance.

Additional services like coolant flushes, differential fluid replacement, or transmission service may vary depending on your BMW model and driving habits.

We recommend checking your BMW iDrive system or owner’s manual, or speaking with a certified technician at our Turnersville location, for a custom plan.

# BMW SERVICE

BMW recommends you have your maintenance and repair work performed by an authorized BMW center.

# MAINTAINING YOUR BMW VEHICLE

A well-maintained vehicle will help safeguard its operational performance, road-safety and its reliability. This is why it is important to follow and perform BMW’s recommended periodic vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks as indicated by your vehicle’s Maintenance Service Display, along with the other maintenance work described in this booklet.

A improper maintenance is not covered under the BMW New Vehicle Damage, including consequential damage, which results from lack of or Limited Warranty for Passenger Cars and Light Trucks.

# MAINTENANCE INTERVALS

Maintenance intervals on motor vehicles were conventionally based solely on a fixed time period or a specified amount of accumulated driving mileage.

However, operational and driving conditions have a major influence on your vehicle’s routine maintenance requirements; the distance traveled is only one of these significant factors. A vehicle used for short trips in the city with numerous cold starts, prolonged periods of idling, stop-and-go driving, and high engine speeds during acceleration may require more frequent maintenance intervals than a vehicle that is driven long distances at moderate engine speeds.

Your BMW vehicle uses sensors and algorithms together with the elapsed time and the driving distance/profile to monitor and evaluate your vehicle’s maintenance service needs. This information is then used to adapt dynamically the parameters used to forecast the applicable maintenance service task intervals.

# THE BMW MAINTENANCE SYSTEM

All BMW vehicles are equipped with an integrated BMW Maintenance System. This maintenance “reminder” system helps ensure that the vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks are performed at the forecasted intervals that apply to your vehicle.

The BMW Maintenance System display provides the vehicle operator access to the current status information for the following maintenance service tasks:

$\\triangleright$ Engine oil (date and miles)\*

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle check (date and miles)

$\\triangleright$ Front brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Rear brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid (date)

$\\triangleright$ 1200 Mile running-in service (date and miles) (Applicable to BMW M vehicles only)\*

For each specific maintenance service task, either the future date (month/ year), remaining miles or both are provided as noted above. The system monitors variable inputs to forecast the intervals and alert the driver when one or more specific maintenance tasks should be performed.

NOTE: For certain vehicles, the status of the front and rear brake pads will only be observable in the maintenance system’s display when there are approximately 2,000 miles or less remaining before a brake service will be required to be performed.

For information about the vehicle’s maintenance system displays, please refer to the Maintenance Service Display Overview section beginning on page 5.

The following “combine with Engine oil”\* maintenance service tasks may be identified as needing to be performed with a specific occurrence of the “Engine oil” service task (service counter number):

$\\triangleright$ Cabin Microfilter(s)

$\\triangleright$ Engine air filter(s)\*

$\\triangleright$ Spark plugs\*

$\\triangleright$ Final drive oil (Applicable M vehicles only)

\\* Does not apply to BEV

Although these items do not appear in the BMW Maintenance System’s display in the vehicle, these services should be performed when your vehicle’s engine oil is changed in accordance with the interval identified by your vehicle’s BMW Maintenance System.

For more information on your vehicle’s maintenance services requirements, procedures and intervals, please refer the Maintenance Service Summary section beginning on page 10.

The BMW Maintenance System also includes an option to set service reminders for the following state-specific mandatory vehicle inspections, including:

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle safety inspection; and/or $\\triangleright$ Emissions test

The corresponding interval data for these inspections can be inputted into the BMW Maintenance System by a service provider; they are not determined by the vehicle.

For your convenience, you may also wish to have your authorized BMW center perform the work necessary to fulfill these state inspection requirements in your area concurrent with the maintenance services specified above when possible.

Should you request more frequent maintenance service than is indicated by the BMW Maintenance System during the coverage period, the cost of these services will not be covered by the BMW Maintenance Program.

# SERVICE DATA — REMOTE CONTROL KEY

Maintenance service task status information for your BMW vehicle is continually updated and stored in your remote control key.

Your authorized BMW center can access this data and consult with you about applicable service procedures and tasks for your vehicle.

Therefore, always provide your service consultant with the most recent remote control key that was used to operate the vehicle when servicing your vehicle at a BMW center.

# VEHICLE STORAGE

Disconnecting the battery during periods of long-term vehicle storage will interrupt the calculation of time-dependent maintenance services.

In this situation, BMW recommends that you have all your time-based maintenance services, such as brake fluid, engine oil and cabin microfilter, brought up to the correct date by an authorized BMW center.

# ENGINE OIL

2025 model year vehicles with internal-combustion engines are factory-filled with:

Z BMW-approved fully synthetic oil for gasoline engines

Engine oil should be changed when the vehicle’s engine is at operating temperature.

If an engine oil service is being performed or you need to add engine oil between changes, please refer to the Owner’s Manual for the recommended engine oil for your BMW vehicle.

# LONG-TERM RATED FLUIDS AND OILS

The following systems and assemblies are factory-filled with long-term rated fluid and oil; fluid replacement is only necessary when repairs are being performed (unless otherwise noted):

$\\triangleright$ Engine cooling system (antifreeze/coolant) $\\triangleright$ Automatic (except for X1 and X2) and manual transmissions $\\triangleright$ All-wheel drive transfer cases (except when indicated by the vehicle)

# REGULAR CHECKS — VEHICLE OPERATOR

In addition to the maintenance service procedure information contained in this booklet, BMW recommends that you regularly check (when refueling, for example), and address when necessary, the following items:

$\\triangleright$ Washer fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Coolant level

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Tires — pressure, condition and wear

Please refer to the Owner’s Manual for additional information.

# 2024 Volkswagen Golf GTI Maintenance Schedule

![hero image](https://dealerimages.dealereprocess.com/image/upload/3441624)

# 2024 Volkswagen Golf GTI Maintenance Schedule

Get ahead of the curve with our comprehensive guide to maintaining your 2024 VW Golf GTI. Our meticulously crafted maintenance schedule ensures your vehicle stays in peak condition, maximizing its performance and longevity. From routine oil changes to intricate inspections, our expert technicians are dedicated to keeping your GTI running smoothly mile after mile.

![](https://dealerimages.dealereprocess.com/image/upload/3441621)

[Schedule Schedule](https://www.pohankavw.com/online-service-scheduler/)

## 10,000-Mile Maintenance

Volkswagen recommends a minor maintenance visit every 10,000 miles for your 2024 Golf GTI. More frequent service is recommended if the car is used routinely in severe temperatures or under other extreme conditions (ask your service advisor for guidance). The technicians will change the engine oil and filter, rotate the tires, and perform a general look-over during each of these appointments.

## 20,000-Mile Maintenance

The tasks from the 10,000-mile service will be repeated at this visit. The sunroof drains will also be cleaned and checked for any blockage (recommended every 20,000 miles or two years, whichever comes first).

## 30,000-Mile Maintenance

Our team will repeat the 10,000-mile maintenance tasks.

## 40,000-Mile Maintenance

While this service is going to repeat the measures from the 10,000- and 20,000-mile intervals (engine oil/filter change, tire rotation, and sunroof drain cleaning), they will also replace the dust and pollen filter.

## 50,000-Mile Maintenance

This point on your 2024 Golf GTI’s odometer calls for our service team to simply change the engine oil and filter, rotate the tires, and keep their eyes open for any developing issues.

## 60,000-Mile Maintenance

Along with the standard service (engine oil/filter change and tire rotation), VW recommends replacing the engine air filter and cleaning the screen (every 60,000 miles or six years). As this is an interval of 20K miles, it’s time once again to have the sunroof drains cleaned and checked for blockage, along with installing a new dust and pollen filter.

## 70,000-Mile Maintenance

This is another simplified visit calling for engine oil/filter change and tire rotation.

## 80,000-Mile Maintenance

Along with the engine oil/filter change and tire rotation at this interval, our technicians will also replace the spark plugs (recommended every 80,000 miles or six years, whichever comes first). They will also repeat the sunroof drain cleaning and replace the cabin air filter.

## 90,000-Mile Maintenance

The expected minor maintenance is performed at this visit (tire rotation and the engine oil/filter change).

## 100,000-Mile Maintenance

Although 100K miles is a major interval, this will be a relatively simple service visit consisting of an engine oil/filter change, tire rotation, mechanical inspection, and sunroof drains cleaning.

## 110,000-Mile Maintenance

This appointment only requires the engine oil and filter change along with tire rotation.

## 120,000-Mile Maintenance

This visit is one of the more extensive ones, combining these tasks from the 40,000- and 60,000-mile services:

- Change engine oil/filter
- Rotate tires
- Clean sunroof drains/check for blockage
- Replace dust and pollen filter
- Replace engine air filter and clean the screen

## After 120,000 Miles & Time-Based Services

It’s important to get your 2024 Golf GTI in to Pohanka VW’s service department so that our service team can repeat the tasks at the appropriate mileage intervals, based on the schedule given above. They will also address the following important maintenance:

- Check coolant pump belt – Every 180,000 miles
- Change brake fluid – Every three years
- Change front axle differential lock fluid – Every three years
- Replace tire filler bottle in tire mobility set – Every four years

## Regular Inspections (Every Visit)

Volkswagen is committed to prioritizing safety and reliability. That’s why our technicians are sure to inspect the vehicle every time it’s here for service. This allows them to monitor the major systems and components and address anything that requires attention. Here are a few of the critical items that will be looked at during these inspections:

- Brake pad thickness
- Tire tread/wear
- Battery
- Exterior lighting
- Brake fluid levels
- Cooling system
- Wiper blades
- Suspension check (ball joints, stabilizer bar, coupling rod, axle bearings, springs, etc.)
- Exhaust system
- Underbody
- Transmission fluid
- Steering system

# Volkswagen Tiguan Recommended Maintenance Schedule

The Volkswagen Tiguan stands out as one of Volkswagen's most popular vehicles, and for good reason. It offers a smooth ride, responsive handling, and a practical design, all of which have made it the go-to model for those who want a compact crossover.

The best way to protect your investment and keep your Tiguan running at its best? Keeping up with routine maintenance. We recommend following this VW Tiguan maintenance schedule to protect performance and extend your vehicle's lifespan.

![](https://pictures.dealer.com/h/hoovervolkswagenlithiaspringvw/1234/f5c328b76bb0498498c2e1ecd26148b9.jpeg?impolicy=downsize_bkpt&w=2500)

## Volkswagen Tiguan Maintenance Schedule

* * *

Most new Volkswagen Tiguan models follow a recommended service interval of every 10,000 miles or 12 months, whichever comes first, with the first scheduled service at 10,000 miles.

Older models may have different maintenance needs, so it's always a good idea to check your owner's manual to confirm the correct VW Tiguan maintenance schedule for your specific vehicle.

For Tiguans using synthetic oil, oil changes are typically recommended every 10,000 miles or once a year, though this can vary depending on your driving habits, commute length, and overall usage.

Here is a general VW Tiguan maintenance schedule to help you stay on track:

### Every 10,000 Miles (or 12 Months)

This is your most frequent service visit and focuses on routine upkeep.

- Engine oil and filter change (synthetic oil)
- Tire rotation
- Brake inspection
- Multi-point vehicle inspection
- Check fluid levels and top off as needed
- Inspect lights, wipers, and battery condition

### Every 20,000 Miles

In addition to the 10,000-mile services:

- Replace the cabin air filter
- Inspect the engine air filter
- Inspect suspension and steering components
- Check the cooling system and hoses

### Every 30,000-40,000 Miles

Along with previous maintenance items:

- Replace engine air filter (if needed)
- Brake service inspection
- Wheel alignment check
- Battery and charging system test
- Inspect the exhaust system

### Every 50,000 Miles

In addition to routine oil changes and tire rotations, this service interval typically includes:

- Brake system inspection
- Battery and charging system test
- Suspension and steering evaluation
- Engine air filter replacement (if needed)
- Cooling system inspection
- Wheel alignment check

### Every 60,000 Miles

This is a larger service interval that may include:

- Spark plug replacement (varies by model year)
- Transmission service (model-dependent)
- Coolant system inspection or service
- More in-depth brake and suspension evaluation

### Beyond 60,000 Miles

As mileage increases, your Tiguan may also need:

- Additional drivetrain inspections
- Timing-related component checks (model dependent)
- Continued fluid services
- Suspension and steering repairs as needed

**Important note:** Older Volkswagen Tiguan models and certain driving habits (frequent short trips, stop-and-go traffic, towing, or extreme weather) may require more frequent service. Always refer to your owner's manual for the exact maintenance requirements for your specific vehicle. If you still have questions, don't hesitate to contact us!

# Volkswagen Tiguan Service Schedule

The Volkswagen Tiguan is a great addition to your family trips around Vienna. However, to maintain your smooth family adventures, it’s necessary to stay on top of your VW Tiguan maintenance plans. Let’s take a look at the Tiguan service intervals with the team at Stohlman Volkswagen service, and trust your service to the certified technicians in our [service center](https://www.stohlman-vw.com/department-fod33-1906).

## VW Tiguan Maintenance Plan

The specifics to your Tiguan service intervals vary depending on your driving habits around Fairfax, but here are the recommended service you should schedule each year or mileage:

### 10,000 Miles/1 Year

**Oil change­­**: Oil is essential to your smooth engine performance, so it’s likely that whenever you [schedule service](https://www.stohlman-vw.com/online-service-scheduler/), it’s also time for an oil change.

**Brake pad inspection:** Our individual driving style affects the wear of your brake pads, and it makes sense that the more you use them, the sooner they’ll need to be replaced. The technicians will inspect the brake pad to see if a replacement is needed.

**Safety inspection**: You and your family should feel safe on your daily commute. Each year, your airbags, seatbelts, and driver-assisting features are inspected to ensure your safety on the road.

**Rotate your tires**: As your tires wear over time, regular tire rotations will help them wear evenly, and lengthen the lifespan of your tires.

**Check light bulbs**: Your VW Tiguan maintenance schedule helps you maintain visibility on your trips, too. Technicians will check your interior and exterior lights to ensure you’re not left in the dark when you really need them.

### 20,000 Miles/2 Year

Service for your VW Tiguan is recommended every 10,000 miles. On top of the previous inspections, the 20,000-mile mark includes a more complete brake system inspection that includes examining brake pads, brake discs, and brake-fluid levels. This Tiguan service interval also includes:

- **Battery inspection:** From your TV remote to your car battery, every battery needs to be replaced eventually. At this point in the Volkswagen Tiguan service schedule, your battery will be checked for any sign of leaks, cracks, or corrosion.
- **Tire inspection:** As mentioned above, rotating tires helps extend the lifespan of your tires, but eventually they will take on too much wear. They’ll be inspected for signs of holes, tearing, and bulging along the sidewall, as well as a tire pressure check for each wheel, including the spare.
- **Coolant replacement:** Coolant is essential in removing heat from the vital components of your engine, so it’s important to check coolant levels and replace as needed.

### 30,000 Miles/3 Year

When you’ve reached 30,000 miles, you’ll receive the same checks found in the 20,000-mile Tiguan service interval. A service technician will also replace your oil, replace the engine oil filter, and perform a brake pad inspection to get you back on Alexandria roads without a problem.

### 40,000 Miles/4 Year

- **Check and replace spark plugs:** A properly functioning spark plug means you can fire up the engine quickly and get on the road.
- **Inspect the electrical system:** On top of a spark plug and battery check, technicians will check to make sure your other electrical components are performing as they should.
- **Inspect for signs of body corrosion:** Vienna weather and accidents may have left their mark on your vehicle. A check to your interior exterior, and parts under the hood will allow your car to like new again.
- **Check the exhaust system:** The cycle from your spark plugs to the exhaust system completes the ignition sequence. This inspection makes sure your engine is firing on all cylinders.

### 50,000 Miles/5 Year

At the five-year or 50,000-mile mark in your Volkswagen Tiguan service schedule, it’s recommended you perform all the service mentioned above, along with extra attention to your brake pads, battery, and engine. As your vehicle puts on more mileage, our technicians will continue to thoroughly check to make sure you’re heading out in the best possible condition.

### 60,000 Miles/6 Year

At this point in the VW Tiguan maintenance plan, service should continue to be performed as mentioned as you progress to the 100k-mile mark. However, it is recommended that you replace your air filter. Not only will it bring a refresh to your cabin air quality, but replacing the air filter helps the spark plugs draw clean air into the engine, and help the ignition sequence run smoothly.

Your first Mercedes-Benz GLE SUV Service A will be needed at 10,000 miles or 1 year. After that, your vehicle will require Service A every 20,000 miles or 2 years.

# BMW SERVICE

BMW recommends you have your maintenance and repair work performed by an authorized BMW center.

# MAINTAINING YOUR BMW VEHICLE

A well-maintained vehicle will help safeguard its operational performance, road-safety and its reliability. This is why it is important to follow and perform BMW’s recommended periodic vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks as indicated by your vehicle’s Maintenance Service Display, along with the other maintenance work described in this booklet.

A improper maintenance is not covered under the BMW New Vehicle Damage, including consequential damage, which results from lack of or Limited Warranty for Passenger Cars and Light Trucks.

# MAINTENANCE INTERVALS

Maintenance intervals on motor vehicles were conventionally based solely on a fixed time period or a specified amount of accumulated driving mileage.

However, operational and driving conditions have a major influence on your vehicle’s routine maintenance requirements; the distance traveled is only one of these significant factors. A vehicle used for short trips in the city with numerous cold starts, prolonged periods of idling, stop-and-go driving, and high engine speeds during acceleration may require more frequent maintenance intervals than a vehicle that is driven long distances at moderate engine speeds.

Your BMW vehicle uses sensors and algorithms together with the elapsed time and the driving distance/profile to monitor and evaluate your vehicle’s maintenance service needs. This information is then used to adapt dynamically the parameters used to forecast the applicable maintenance service task intervals.

# THE BMW MAINTENANCE SYSTEM

All BMW vehicles are equipped with an integrated BMW Maintenance System. This maintenance “reminder” system helps ensure that the vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks are performed at the forecasted intervals that apply to your vehicle.

The BMW Maintenance System display provides the vehicle operator access to the current status information for the following maintenance service tasks:

$\\triangleright$ Engine oil (date and miles)\*

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle check (date and miles)

$\\triangleright$ Front brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Rear brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid (date)

$\\triangleright$ 1200 Mile running-in service (date and miles) (Applicable to BMW M vehicles only)\*

For each specific maintenance service task, either the future date (month/ year), remaining miles or both are provided as noted above. The system monitors variable inputs to forecast the intervals and alert the driver when one or more specific maintenance tasks should be performed.

NOTE: For certain vehicles, the status of the front and rear brake pads will only be observable in the maintenance system’s display when there are approximately 2,000 miles or less remaining before a brake service will be required to be performed.

For information about the vehicle’s maintenance system displays, please refer to the Maintenance Service Display Overview section beginning on page 5.

The following “combine with Engine oil”\* maintenance service tasks may be identified as needing to be performed with a specific occurrence of the “Engine oil” service task (service counter number):

$\\triangleright$ Cabin Microfilter(s)

$\\triangleright$ Engine air filter(s)\*

$\\triangleright$ Spark plugs\*

$\\triangleright$ Final drive oil (Applicable M vehicles only)

\\* Does not apply to BEV

Although these items do not appear in the BMW Maintenance System’s display in the vehicle, these services should be performed when your vehicle’s engine oil is changed in accordance with the interval identified by your vehicle’s BMW Maintenance System.

For more information on your vehicle’s maintenance services requirements, procedures and intervals, please refer the Maintenance Service Summary section beginning on page 10.

The BMW Maintenance System also includes an option to set service reminders for the following state-specific mandatory vehicle inspections, including:

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle safety inspection; and/or $\\triangleright$ Emissions test

The corresponding interval data for these inspections can be inputted into the BMW Maintenance System by a service provider; they are not determined by the vehicle.

For your convenience, you may also wish to have your authorized BMW center perform the work necessary to fulfill these state inspection requirements in your area concurrent with the maintenance services specified above when possible.

Should you request more frequent maintenance service than is indicated by the BMW Maintenance System during the coverage period, the cost of these services will not be covered by the BMW Maintenance Program.

# SERVICE DATA — REMOTE CONTROL KEY

Maintenance service task status information for your BMW vehicle is continually updated and stored in your remote control key.

Your authorized BMW center can access this data and consult with you about applicable service procedures and tasks for your vehicle.

Therefore, always provide your service consultant with the most recent remote control key that was used to operate the vehicle when servicing your vehicle at a BMW center.

# VEHICLE STORAGE

Disconnecting the battery during periods of long-term vehicle storage will interrupt the calculation of time-dependent maintenance services.

In this situation, BMW recommends that you have all your time-based maintenance services, such as brake fluid, engine oil and cabin microfilter, brought up to the correct date by an authorized BMW center.

# ENGINE OIL

2025 model year vehicles with internal-combustion engines are factory-filled with:

Z BMW-approved fully synthetic oil for gasoline engines

Engine oil should be changed when the vehicle’s engine is at operating temperature.

If an engine oil service is being performed or you need to add engine oil between changes, please refer to the Owner’s Manual for the recommended engine oil for your BMW vehicle.

# LONG-TERM RATED FLUIDS AND OILS

The following systems and assemblies are factory-filled with long-term rated fluid and oil; fluid replacement is only necessary when repairs are being performed (unless otherwise noted):

$\\triangleright$ Engine cooling system (antifreeze/coolant) $\\triangleright$ Automatic (except for X1 and X2) and manual transmissions $\\triangleright$ All-wheel drive transfer cases (except when indicated by the vehicle)

# REGULAR CHECKS — VEHICLE OPERATOR

In addition to the maintenance service procedure information contained in this booklet, BMW recommends that you regularly check (when refueling, for example), and address when necessary, the following items:

$\\triangleright$ Washer fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Coolant level

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Tires — pressure, condition and wear

Please refer to the Owner’s Manual for additional information.

## Keep Your BMW 2 Series Performing at it's Best

**Basic BMW 2-Series Preventative Maintenance: Every 5,000 Miles**

BMW’s maintenance schedule is built around a standard 5,000-mile interval, guided by your vehicle’s pre-installed Condition-Based Service (CBS) monitor. This intelligent system tracks critical areas of your car and alerts you when additional services are needed.

The regular BMW recommended maintenance schedule includes the following:

- Vehicle check and inspection
- Engine oil check
- Coolant check
- Tire rotation
- Brake fluid check
- Front and rear brake inspection
- Inspection of the engine and cabin air filters
- Wiper blade inspection
- Standard scope

Not every part inspected will need replacement during your visit. Our BMW-certified maintenance experts use the CBS monitor to identify exactly what requires attention, ensuring precise and efficient service.

**BMW 2-Series Recommended Maintenance Services**

Maintenance needs can vary depending on your model and driving habits. For tailored recommendations, consult your owner’s manual or speak with one of our knowledgeable service advisors. Below is a general guideline for BMW 2 Series maintenance milestones:

**BMW 2-Series 10,000-Mile Maintenance**

- Replace the engine oil, oil filter and coolant
- Repeat every 10,000 miles

**BMW 2-Series 20,000-Mile Maintenance**

- Inspect and replace the oil filters
- Repeat every 20,000 miles

**BMW 2-Series 30,000-Mile Maintenance**

- Replace brake fluid. After the first service, schedule brake fluid replacement every 60,000 miles.
- If equipped with a manual transmission, replace transmission fluid every 30,000 miles.

**BMW 2-Series 60,000-mile maintenance**

- Replace the engine air filter and spark plugs
- Inspect and replace brake pads and rotors as needed
- For automatic transmissions, replace the transmission fluid every 60,000 miles.

**BMW 2-Series 90,000-Mile Maintenance**

- Replace the timing belt and hoses
- Repeat every 90,000 miles

**BMW 2-Series Maintenance after 90,000 Miles**

Continue following the BMW 2 Series maintenance schedule with 5,000-mile intervals and adhere to service milestones as listed above to ensure optimal performance.

BMW recommends you have your maintenance and repair work performed by an authorized BMW center.

# MAINTAINING YOUR BMW VEHICLE

A well-maintained vehicle will help safeguard its operational performance, road-safety and its reliability. This is why it is important to follow and perform BMW’s recommended periodic vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks as indicated by your vehicle’s Maintenance Service Display, along with the other maintenance work described in this booklet.

A improper maintenance is not covered under the BMW New Vehicle Damage, including consequential damage, which results from lack of or Limited Warranty for Passenger Cars and Light Trucks.

# MAINTENANCE INTERVALS

Maintenance intervals on motor vehicles were conventionally based solely on a fixed time period or a specified amount of accumulated driving mileage.

However, operational and driving conditions have a major influence on your vehicle’s routine maintenance requirements; the distance traveled is only one of these significant factors. A vehicle used for short trips in the city with numerous cold starts, prolonged periods of idling, stop-and-go driving, and high engine speeds during acceleration may require more frequent maintenance intervals than a vehicle that is driven long distances at moderate engine speeds.

Your BMW vehicle uses sensors and algorithms together with the elapsed time and the driving distance/profile to monitor and evaluate your vehicle’s maintenance service needs. This information is then used to adapt dynamically the parameters used to forecast the applicable maintenance service task intervals.

# THE BMW MAINTENANCE SYSTEM

All BMW vehicles are equipped with an integrated BMW Maintenance System. This maintenance “reminder” system helps ensure that the vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks are performed at the forecasted intervals that apply to your vehicle.

The BMW Maintenance System display provides the vehicle operator access to the current status information for the following maintenance service tasks:

$\\triangleright$ Engine oil (date and miles)\*

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle check (date and miles)

$\\triangleright$ Front brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Rear brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid (date)

$\\triangleright$ 1200 Mile running-in service (date and miles) (Applicable to BMW M vehicles only)\*

For each specific maintenance service task, either the future date (month/ year), remaining miles or both are provided as noted above. The system monitors variable inputs to forecast the intervals and alert the driver when one or more specific maintenance tasks should be performed.

NOTE: For certain vehicles, the status of the front and rear brake pads will only be observable in the maintenance system’s display when there are approximately 2,000 miles or less remaining before a brake service will be required to be performed.

For information about the vehicle’s maintenance system displays, please refer to the Maintenance Service Display Overview section beginning on page 5.

The following “combine with Engine oil”\* maintenance service tasks may be identified as needing to be performed with a specific occurrence of the “Engine oil” service task (service counter number):

$\\triangleright$ Cabin Microfilter(s)

$\\triangleright$ Engine air filter(s)\*

$\\triangleright$ Spark plugs\*

$\\triangleright$ Final drive oil (Applicable M vehicles only)

\\* Does not apply to BEV

Although these items do not appear in the BMW Maintenance System’s display in the vehicle, these services should be performed when your vehicle’s engine oil is changed in accordance with the interval identified by your vehicle’s BMW Maintenance System.

For more information on your vehicle’s maintenance services requirements, procedures and intervals, please refer the Maintenance Service Summary section beginning on page 10.

The BMW Maintenance System also includes an option to set service reminders for the following state-specific mandatory vehicle inspections, including:

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle safety inspection; and/or $\\triangleright$ Emissions test

The corresponding interval data for these inspections can be inputted into the BMW Maintenance System by a service provider; they are not determined by the vehicle.

For your convenience, you may also wish to have your authorized BMW center perform the work necessary to fulfill these state inspection requirements in your area concurrent with the maintenance services specified above when possible.

Should you request more frequent maintenance service than is indicated by the BMW Maintenance System during the coverage period, the cost of these services will not be covered by the BMW Maintenance Program.

# SERVICE DATA — REMOTE CONTROL KEY

Maintenance service task status information for your BMW vehicle is continually updated and stored in your remote control key.

Your authorized BMW center can access this data and consult with you about applicable service procedures and tasks for your vehicle.

Therefore, always provide your service consultant with the most recent remote control key that was used to operate the vehicle when servicing your vehicle at a BMW center.

# VEHICLE STORAGE

Disconnecting the battery during periods of long-term vehicle storage will interrupt the calculation of time-dependent maintenance services.

In this situation, BMW recommends that you have all your time-based maintenance services, such as brake fluid, engine oil and cabin microfilter, brought up to the correct date by an authorized BMW center.

# ENGINE OIL

2025 model year vehicles with internal-combustion engines are factory-filled with:

Z BMW-approved fully synthetic oil for gasoline engines

Engine oil should be changed when the vehicle’s engine is at operating temperature.

If an engine oil service is being performed or you need to add engine oil between changes, please refer to the Owner’s Manual for the recommended engine oil for your BMW vehicle.

# LONG-TERM RATED FLUIDS AND OILS

The following systems and assemblies are factory-filled with long-term rated fluid and oil; fluid replacement is only necessary when repairs are being performed (unless otherwise noted):

$\\triangleright$ Engine cooling system (antifreeze/coolant) $\\triangleright$ Automatic (except for X1 and X2) and manual transmissions $\\triangleright$ All-wheel drive transfer cases (except when indicated by the vehicle)

# REGULAR CHECKS — VEHICLE OPERATOR

In addition to the maintenance service procedure information contained in this booklet, BMW recommends that you regularly check (when refueling, for example), and address when necessary, the following items:

$\\triangleright$ Washer fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Coolant level

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Tires — pressure, condition and wear

Please refer to the Owner’s Manual for additional information.

## Keep Your BMW 2 Series Performing at it's Best

**Basic BMW 2-Series Preventative Maintenance: Every 5,000 Miles**

BMW’s maintenance schedule is built around a standard 5,000-mile interval, guided by your vehicle’s pre-installed Condition-Based Service (CBS) monitor. This intelligent system tracks critical areas of your car and alerts you when additional services are needed.

The regular BMW recommended maintenance schedule includes the following:

- Vehicle check and inspection
- Engine oil check
- Coolant check
- Tire rotation
- Brake fluid check
- Front and rear brake inspection
- Inspection of the engine and cabin air filters
- Wiper blade inspection
- Standard scope

Not every part inspected will need replacement during your visit. Our BMW-certified maintenance experts use the CBS monitor to identify exactly what requires attention, ensuring precise and efficient service.

**BMW 2-Series Recommended Maintenance Services**

Maintenance needs can vary depending on your model and driving habits. For tailored recommendations, consult your owner’s manual or speak with one of our knowledgeable service advisors. Below is a general guideline for BMW 2 Series maintenance milestones:

**BMW 2-Series 10,000-Mile Maintenance**

- Replace the engine oil, oil filter and coolant
- Repeat every 10,000 miles

**BMW 2-Series 20,000-Mile Maintenance**

- Inspect and replace the oil filters
- Repeat every 20,000 miles

**BMW 2-Series 30,000-Mile Maintenance**

- Replace brake fluid. After the first service, schedule brake fluid replacement every 60,000 miles.
- If equipped with a manual transmission, replace transmission fluid every 30,000 miles.

**BMW 2-Series 60,000-mile maintenance**

- Replace the engine air filter and spark plugs
- Inspect and replace brake pads and rotors as needed
- For automatic transmissions, replace the transmission fluid every 60,000 miles.

**BMW 2-Series 90,000-Mile Maintenance**

- Replace the timing belt and hoses
- Repeat every 90,000 miles

**BMW 2-Series Maintenance after 90,000 Miles**

Continue following the BMW 2 Series maintenance schedule with 5,000-mile intervals and adhere to service milestones as listed above to ensure optimal performance.

Tires, brakes, and suspension still matter just as much as any performance Audi. ## How Audi e-tron GT maintenance works The e-tron GT is built like a high‑performance Audi but maintained like a modern EV. Instead of the familiar A6 or S5 routine of **oil changes every 10,000 miles**, the electric GT leans on long inspection intervals and software‑driven checks. The car’s service reminder in the cockpit display is your referee, counting down to the next visit based on time and mileage. - There’s no engine oil, spark plugs, or exhaust system to service. - The big-ticket item, the high‑voltage battery, is monitored constantly by onboard software. - Most scheduled visits center around inspections, filters, fluids, tires, and brake components. - Audi typically structures service as flexible inspections rather than long lists of parts to replace. ### Tip for first-time EV owners On an e-tron GT, time matters as much as miles. Fluid ages with time and moisture and typically gets replaced about every 2 years. #### Cabin & 12‑V battery The high‑voltage pack powers the car, but the 12‑V battery runs control modules. Expect conventional 12‑V battery replacement every few years plus cabin air filter changes for clean HVAC performance. Beyond those basics, expect the usual wear items: tires, wiper blades, and, over time, brake pads and rotors. Because the e-tron GT is heavy and very quick, it can chew through tires faster than a regular sedan, especially on performance rubber. ### Don’t skip tire rotations With dual‑motor all‑wheel drive and instant torque, uneven tire wear can sneak up on you. Regular rotations (often every 5,000–10,000 miles) keep the car tracking straight and protect those expensive 20‑ or 21‑inch tires. ## Battery health checks for the e-tron GT The high‑voltage battery is the e-tron GT’s heart and its most expensive single component. That’s a big advantage over a generic used‑car inspection. ## Typical Audi e-tron GT maintenance costs You’re driving a flagship Audi, so service visits won’t be bargain‑basement. The good news is that **EVs shift more of your budget from maintenance to tires** rather than piling on fluid changes and engine work. EVs skip oil changes and timing belts, but that doesn’t mean they’re maintenance‑free, especially when you’re shopping used. ### Quick takeaway Audi recommends time‑ and mileage‑based service for the e-tron GT, with major inspections roughly every 2 years/20,000 miles, regular brake fluid changes, cabin filters, and detailed high‑voltage system checks. Tires, brakes, and suspension still matter just as much as any performance Audi. ## How Audi e-tron GT maintenance works The e-tron GT is built like a high‑performance Audi but maintained like a modern EV. Instead of the familiar A6 or S5 routine of **oil changes every 10,000 miles**, the electric GT leans on long inspection intervals and software‑driven checks. The car’s service reminder in the cockpit display is your referee, counting down to the next visit based on time and mileage. - There’s no engine oil, spark plugs, or exhaust system to service. - The big-ticket item, the high‑voltage battery, is monitored constantly by onboard software. - Most scheduled visits center around inspections, filters, fluids, tires, and brake components. - Audi typically structures service as flexible inspections rather than long lists of parts to replace. ### Tip for first-time EV owners On an e-tron GT, time matters as much as miles. Even if you only drive a few thousand miles a year, you’ll still want those 2‑year inspections for things like brake fluid, seals, and suspension wear. ## Audi e-tron GT maintenance schedule overview Exact intervals can vary slightly by model year and market, but most Audi e-tron GT schedules in the U.S. follow this general rhythm. Always confirm with the owner’s manual or Audi dealer for your specific VIN, but this overview will get you 95% of the way there. ![Audi e-tron GT on a lift in a service bay during a scheduled inspection](https://recharged.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fd365moeqy2c2l.cloudfront.net%2Fimages%2Fcontent%2Feebb01bf70db2e32ec581d22b03e813e-content.png&w=3840&q=75) Most e-tron GT scheduled services are inspections and fluid checks rather than big mechanical repairs. ### Audi e-tron GT service interval table Common U.S. market inspection and replacement intervals for key e-tron GT maintenance items. Fluid ages with time and moisture and typically gets replaced about every 2 years. #### Cabin & 12‑V battery The high‑voltage pack powers the car, but the 12‑V battery runs control modules. Expect conventional 12‑V battery replacement every few years plus cabin air filter changes for clean HVAC performance. Beyond those basics, expect the usual wear items: tires, wiper blades, and, over time, brake pads and rotors. Because the e-tron GT is heavy and very quick, it can chew through tires faster than a regular sedan, especially on performance rubber. ### Don’t skip tire rotations With dual‑motor all‑wheel drive and instant torque, uneven tire wear can sneak up on you. Regular rotations (often every 5,000–10,000 miles) keep the car tracking straight and protect those expensive 20‑ or 21‑inch tires. ## Battery health checks for the e-tron GT The high‑voltage battery is the e-tron GT’s heart and its most expensive single component. Day to day, you’ll see only a percentage and range estimate on the dash, but during scheduled service Audi technicians can pull detailed diagnostic data, including fault codes, temperature behavior, and any cell‑level issues. ### What Audi checks at service - Battery control module fault codes and thermal alerts. - Cooling system performance and coolant level/condition. - High‑voltage wiring and connectors for damage or corrosion. - Sealing and underbody protection around the pack. ### What you can watch at home - Sudden loss of range with the same driving pattern. - Charging behavior that’s much slower than usual on the same charger. - Warning lights related to the electrical system or drive system. - Unusual fan noise or frequent cooling activity when parked. ### How Recharged helps on used e-tron GTs Every EV sold through Recharged includes a **Recharged Score Report** with verified battery health, so you’re not guessing how the last owner treated the pack. That’s a big advantage over a generic used‑car inspection. ## Typical Audi e-tron GT maintenance costs You’re driving a flagship Audi, so service visits won’t be bargain‑basement. The good news is that **EVs shift more of your budget from maintenance to tires** rather than piling on fluid changes and engine work. Actual prices vary by dealer and region, but this is a realistic way to think about costs in the U.S. ### Typical U.S. e-tron GT maintenance and wear costs $200–$350 Minor visit Basic inspection with cabin filter and rotation at an Audi dealer. $400–$800 Major service 2‑year/20,000‑mile type visit with brake fluid and deeper checks. $1,200–$2,000+ Tire set High‑performance 20–21" tires, including mounting and alignment. # BMW SERVICE

BMW recommends you have your maintenance and repair work performed by an authorized BMW center.

# MAINTAINING YOUR BMW VEHICLE

A well-maintained vehicle will help safeguard its operational performance, road-safety and its reliability. This is why it is important to follow and perform BMW’s recommended periodic vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks as indicated by your vehicle’s Maintenance Service Display, along with the other maintenance work described in this booklet.

A improper maintenance is not covered under the BMW New Vehicle Damage, including consequential damage, which results from lack of or Limited Warranty for Passenger Cars and Light Trucks.

# MAINTENANCE INTERVALS

Maintenance intervals on motor vehicles were conventionally based solely on a fixed time period or a specified amount of accumulated driving mileage.

However, operational and driving conditions have a major influence on your vehicle’s routine maintenance requirements; the distance traveled is only one of these significant factors. A vehicle used for short trips in the city with numerous cold starts, prolonged periods of idling, stop-and-go driving, and high engine speeds during acceleration may require more frequent maintenance intervals than a vehicle that is driven long distances at moderate engine speeds.

Your BMW vehicle uses sensors and algorithms together with the elapsed time and the driving distance/profile to monitor and evaluate your vehicle’s maintenance service needs. This information is then used to adapt dynamically the parameters used to forecast the applicable maintenance service task intervals.

# THE BMW MAINTENANCE SYSTEM

All BMW vehicles are equipped with an integrated BMW Maintenance System. This maintenance “reminder” system helps ensure that the vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks are performed at the forecasted intervals that apply to your vehicle.

The BMW Maintenance System display provides the vehicle operator access to the current status information for the following maintenance service tasks:

$\\triangleright$ Engine oil (date and miles)\*

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle check (date and miles)

$\\triangleright$ Front brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Rear brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid (date)

$\\triangleright$ 1200 Mile running-in service (date and miles) (Applicable to BMW M vehicles only)\*

For each specific maintenance service task, either the future date (month/ year), remaining miles or both are provided as noted above. The system monitors variable inputs to forecast the intervals and alert the driver when one or more specific maintenance tasks should be performed.

NOTE: For certain vehicles, the status of the front and rear brake pads will only be observable in the maintenance system’s display when there are approximately 2,000 miles or less remaining before a brake service will be required to be performed.

For information about the vehicle’s maintenance system displays, please refer to the Maintenance Service Display Overview section beginning on page 5.

The following “combine with Engine oil”\* maintenance service tasks may be identified as needing to be performed with a specific occurrence of the “Engine oil” service task (service counter number):

$\\triangleright$ Cabin Microfilter(s)

$\\triangleright$ Engine air filter(s)\*

$\\triangleright$ Spark plugs\*

$\\triangleright$ Final drive oil (Applicable M vehicles only)

\\* Does not apply to BEV

Although these items do not appear in the BMW Maintenance System’s display in the vehicle, these services should be performed when your vehicle’s engine oil is changed in accordance with the interval identified by your vehicle’s BMW Maintenance System.

For more information on your vehicle’s maintenance services requirements, procedures and intervals, please refer the Maintenance Service Summary section beginning on page 10.

The BMW Maintenance System also includes an option to set service reminders for the following state-specific mandatory vehicle inspections, including:

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle safety inspection; and/or $\\triangleright$ Emissions test

The corresponding interval data for these inspections can be inputted into the BMW Maintenance System by a service provider; they are not determined by the vehicle.

For your convenience, you may also wish to have your authorized BMW center perform the work necessary to fulfill these state inspection requirements in your area concurrent with the maintenance services specified above when possible.

Should you request more frequent maintenance service than is indicated by the BMW Maintenance System during the coverage period, the cost of these services will not be covered by the BMW Maintenance Program.

# SERVICE DATA — REMOTE CONTROL KEY

Maintenance service task status information for your BMW vehicle is continually updated and stored in your remote control key.

Your authorized BMW center can access this data and consult with you about applicable service procedures and tasks for your vehicle.

Therefore, always provide your service consultant with the most recent remote control key that was used to operate the vehicle when servicing your vehicle at a BMW center.

# VEHICLE STORAGE

Disconnecting the battery during periods of long-term vehicle storage will interrupt the calculation of time-dependent maintenance services.

In this situation, BMW recommends that you have all your time-based maintenance services, such as brake fluid, engine oil and cabin microfilter, brought up to the correct date by an authorized BMW center.

# ENGINE OIL

2025 model year vehicles with internal-combustion engines are factory-filled with:

Z BMW-approved fully synthetic oil for gasoline engines

Engine oil should be changed when the vehicle’s engine is at operating temperature.

If an engine oil service is being performed or you need to add engine oil between changes, please refer to the Owner’s Manual for the recommended engine oil for your BMW vehicle.

# LONG-TERM RATED FLUIDS AND OILS

The following systems and assemblies are factory-filled with long-term rated fluid and oil; fluid replacement is only necessary when repairs are being performed (unless otherwise noted):

$\\triangleright$ Engine cooling system (antifreeze/coolant) $\\triangleright$ Automatic (except for X1 and X2) and manual transmissions $\\triangleright$ All-wheel drive transfer cases (except when indicated by the vehicle)

# REGULAR CHECKS — VEHICLE OPERATOR

In addition to the maintenance service procedure information contained in this booklet, BMW recommends that you regularly check (when refueling, for example), and address when necessary, the following items:

$\\triangleright$ Washer fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Coolant level

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Tires — pressure, condition and wear

Please refer to the Owner’s Manual for additional information.

# What is the Recommended BMW Maintenance Schedule?

At BMW of Tigard, we often get questions from customers about their BMW maintenance schedule. And when you buy a [quality new BMW](https://www.bmwtigard.com/new-vehicles/), it’s important to stick to its BMW service schedule. That’s why we’ve provided the recommended maintenance schedule for general BMW vehicles for Portland and Tigard drivers. ## BMW Preventative Maintenance: Every 5,000 Miles / 6 Months

It’s important to bring in your BMW two or three times a year (or every 5,000 miles) for these preventative maintenance services:

- Front and rear brake inspection
- Brake fluid check
- Coolant check
- Engine oil check
- Cabin air filter inspection
- Engine inspection
- Vehicle inspection
- Wiper blade inspection
- Any necessary tire rotations

Your BMW also comes with something called the Condition-Based Service Monitor (CBS). Your CBS tracks the condition of important systems in your BMW, letting you know if service is required. Our technicians will also use your CBS to determine what needs to be replaced, repaired, or serviced when you schedule service. Keep in mind that just because your CBS may say that service may not be necessary at 5,000 miles doesn’t mean that you shouldn’t come in for preventative maintenance and checks. Sometimes human eyes are necessary to determine a problem or to nip any potential issues in the bud.

## Recommended BMW Maintenance Schedule

Your BMW service schedule needs will vary based on how often you drive, where you drive, and your driving conditions. Your owner’s manual can give you detailed information on common service tasks for your specific model and trim, but here’s what BMW owners can generally expect:

- **Every 10,000 miles** (or yearly): replace your vehicle’s engine oil, oil filter, and coolant.
- **Every 20,000 miles** (or every two years): inspect and replace your vehicle’s fuel filters.
- **Every 30,000 miles** (or every three years): replace your vehicle’s brake fluid (after the first replacement, **every 60,000 miles**) and replace your vehicle’s transmission fluid on manual-transmission BMWs.
- **Every 60,000 miles** (or every six years): replace your vehicle’s engine air filter and spark plugs, inspect and replace any brake pads and brake rotors, and replace transmission fluid on automatic-transmission BMWs.
- **Every 90,000 miles** (or every nine years): replace your vehicle’s timing belts and hoses.

You’ll want to repeat the cycle above after 90,000 miles and always follow the 5,000-mile maintenance schedule. Your BMW’s New Vehicle Limited Warranty will also expire at 50,000 miles, so we recommend getting in any repairs or service before this warranty expires! We also recommend replacing your BMW battery around 50,000 miles.

# BMW SERVICE

BMW recommends you have your maintenance and repair work performed by an authorized BMW center.

# MAINTAINING YOUR BMW VEHICLE

A well-maintained vehicle will help safeguard its operational performance, road-safety and its reliability. This is why it is important to follow and perform BMW’s recommended periodic vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks as indicated by your vehicle’s Maintenance Service Display, along with the other maintenance work described in this booklet.

A improper maintenance is not covered under the BMW New Vehicle Damage, including consequential damage, which results from lack of or Limited Warranty for Passenger Cars and Light Trucks.

# MAINTENANCE INTERVALS

Maintenance intervals on motor vehicles were conventionally based solely on a fixed time period or a specified amount of accumulated driving mileage.

However, operational and driving conditions have a major influence on your vehicle’s routine maintenance requirements; the distance traveled is only one of these significant factors. A vehicle used for short trips in the city with numerous cold starts, prolonged periods of idling, stop-and-go driving, and high engine speeds during acceleration may require more frequent maintenance intervals than a vehicle that is driven long distances at moderate engine speeds.

Your BMW vehicle uses sensors and algorithms together with the elapsed time and the driving distance/profile to monitor and evaluate your vehicle’s maintenance service needs. This information is then used to adapt dynamically the parameters used to forecast the applicable maintenance service task intervals.

# THE BMW MAINTENANCE SYSTEM

All BMW vehicles are equipped with an integrated BMW Maintenance System. This maintenance “reminder” system helps ensure that the vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks are performed at the forecasted intervals that apply to your vehicle.

The BMW Maintenance System display provides the vehicle operator access to the current status information for the following maintenance service tasks:

$\\triangleright$ Engine oil (date and miles)\*

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle check (date and miles)

$\\triangleright$ Front brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Rear brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid (date)

$\\triangleright$ 1200 Mile running-in service (date and miles) (Applicable to BMW M vehicles only)\*

For each specific maintenance service task, either the future date (month/ year), remaining miles or both are provided as noted above. The system monitors variable inputs to forecast the intervals and alert the driver when one or more specific maintenance tasks should be performed.

NOTE: For certain vehicles, the status of the front and rear brake pads will only be observable in the maintenance system’s display when there are approximately 2,000 miles or less remaining before a brake service will be required to be performed.

For information about the vehicle’s maintenance system displays, please refer to the Maintenance Service Display Overview section beginning on page 5.

The following “combine with Engine oil”\* maintenance service tasks may be identified as needing to be performed with a specific occurrence of the “Engine oil” service task (service counter number):

$\\triangleright$ Cabin Microfilter(s)

$\\triangleright$ Engine air filter(s)\*

$\\triangleright$ Spark plugs\*

$\\triangleright$ Final drive oil (Applicable M vehicles only)

\\* Does not apply to BEV

Although these items do not appear in the BMW Maintenance System’s display in the vehicle, these services should be performed when your vehicle’s engine oil is changed in accordance with the interval identified by your vehicle’s BMW Maintenance System.

For more information on your vehicle’s maintenance services requirements, procedures and intervals, please refer the Maintenance Service Summary section beginning on page 10.

The BMW Maintenance System also includes an option to set service reminders for the following state-specific mandatory vehicle inspections, including:

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle safety inspection; and/or $\\triangleright$ Emissions test

The corresponding interval data for these inspections can be inputted into the BMW Maintenance System by a service provider; they are not determined by the vehicle.

For your convenience, you may also wish to have your authorized BMW center perform the work necessary to fulfill these state inspection requirements in your area concurrent with the maintenance services specified above when possible.

Should you request more frequent maintenance service than is indicated by the BMW Maintenance System during the coverage period, the cost of these services will not be covered by the BMW Maintenance Program.

# SERVICE DATA — REMOTE CONTROL KEY

Maintenance service task status information for your BMW vehicle is continually updated and stored in your remote control key.

Your authorized BMW center can access this data and consult with you about applicable service procedures and tasks for your vehicle.

Therefore, always provide your service consultant with the most recent remote control key that was used to operate the vehicle when servicing your vehicle at a BMW center.

# VEHICLE STORAGE

Disconnecting the battery during periods of long-term vehicle storage will interrupt the calculation of time-dependent maintenance services.

In this situation, BMW recommends that you have all your time-based maintenance services, such as brake fluid, engine oil and cabin microfilter, brought up to the correct date by an authorized BMW center.

# ENGINE OIL

2025 model year vehicles with internal-combustion engines are factory-filled with:

Z BMW-approved fully synthetic oil for gasoline engines

Engine oil should be changed when the vehicle’s engine is at operating temperature.

If an engine oil service is being performed or you need to add engine oil between changes, please refer to the Owner’s Manual for the recommended engine oil for your BMW vehicle.

# LONG-TERM RATED FLUIDS AND OILS

The following systems and assemblies are factory-filled with long-term rated fluid and oil; fluid replacement is only necessary when repairs are being performed (unless otherwise noted):

$\\triangleright$ Engine cooling system (antifreeze/coolant) $\\triangleright$ Automatic (except for X1 and X2) and manual transmissions $\\triangleright$ All-wheel drive transfer cases (except when indicated by the vehicle)

# REGULAR CHECKS — VEHICLE OPERATOR

In addition to the maintenance service procedure information contained in this booklet, BMW recommends that you regularly check (when refueling, for example), and address when necessary, the following items:

$\\triangleright$ Washer fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Coolant level

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Tires — pressure, condition and wear

Please refer to the Owner’s Manual for additional information.

EVs skip oil changes and timing belts, but that doesn’t mean they’re maintenance‑free, especially when you’re shopping used. ### Quick takeaway Audi recommends time‑ and mileage‑based service for the e-tron GT, with major inspections roughly every 2 years/20,000 miles, regular brake fluid changes, cabin filters, and detailed high‑voltage system checks. Tires, brakes, and suspension still matter just as much as any performance Audi. ## How Audi e-tron GT maintenance works The e-tron GT is built like a high‑performance Audi but maintained like a modern EV. Instead of the familiar A6 or S5 routine of **oil changes every 10,000 miles**, the electric GT leans on long inspection intervals and software‑driven checks. The car’s service reminder in the cockpit display is your referee, counting down to the next visit based on time and mileage. - There’s no engine oil, spark plugs, or exhaust system to service. - The big-ticket item, the high‑voltage battery, is monitored constantly by onboard software. - Most scheduled visits center around inspections, filters, fluids, tires, and brake components. - Audi typically structures service as flexible inspections rather than long lists of parts to replace. ### Tip for first-time EV owners On an e-tron GT, time matters as much as miles. Even if you only drive a few thousand miles a year, you’ll still want those 2‑year inspections for things like brake fluid, seals, and suspension wear. ## Audi e-tron GT maintenance schedule overview Exact intervals can vary slightly by model year and market, but most Audi e-tron GT schedules in the U.S. follow this general rhythm. Always confirm with the owner’s manual or Audi dealer for your specific VIN, but this overview will get you 95% of the way there. ![Audi e-tron GT on a lift in a service bay during a scheduled inspection](https://recharged.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fd365moeqy2c2l.cloudfront.net%2Fimages%2Fcontent%2Feebb01bf70db2e32ec581d22b03e813e-content.png&w=3840&q=75) Most e-tron GT scheduled services are inspections and fluid checks rather than big mechanical repairs. ### Audi e-tron GT service interval table Common U.S. market inspection and replacement intervals for key e-tron GT maintenance items. Always verify against the service booklet for your car. | Interval (time / miles) | What usually happens | EV‑specific notes | | --- | --- | --- | | Every 1 year / 10,000 miles | General inspection, tire rotation, visual brake check, fluids top‑off | High‑voltage cables and underbody shield visually checked. | | Every 2 years / 20,000 miles | Comprehensive inspection, brake fluid change, cabin filter replacement | High‑voltage system and battery cooling circuit checked with diagnostics. | | Every 3 years | Air conditioning service check, refrigerant leak inspection | Heat pump and battery thermal management performance evaluated. | | Every 4 years / ~40,000 miles | More detailed suspension/steering check, alignment check recommended | Extra attention to weight‑related wear on tires, bushings, and control arms. | | Every 6 years / 60,000+ miles | Possible coolant exchange depending on Audi guidance and climate | Battery coolant condition and thermal system capacity reviewed. | | As needed | Tires, brake pads/rotors, wiper blades, 12‑V battery | Tire wear can be quicker than on non‑performance EVs; regen doesn’t eliminate brake service. | Intervals shown are typical guidelines; local schedules and warranty plans may differ. ## Key maintenance items on the Audi e-tron GT, explained ### What your e-tron GT actually needs serviced Think inspections and wear items, not constant fluid changes. #### Annual inspections Audi techs scan for software faults, check steering and suspension, inspect axle boots and underbody panels, and look for leaks or physical damage to the high‑voltage system. #### Brake fluid & hydraulics Even with strong regenerative braking, the car still relies on a conventional hydraulic system. Fluid ages with time and moisture and typically gets replaced about every 2 years. #### Cabin & 12‑V battery The high‑voltage pack powers the car, but the 12‑V battery runs control modules. Expect conventional 12‑V battery replacement every few years plus cabin air filter changes for clean HVAC performance. Beyond those basics, expect the usual wear items: tires, wiper blades, and, over time, brake pads and rotors. Because the e-tron GT is heavy and very quick, it can chew through tires faster than a regular sedan, especially on performance rubber. ### Don’t skip tire rotations With dual‑motor all‑wheel drive and instant torque, uneven tire wear can sneak up on you. Regular rotations (often every 5,000–10,000 miles) keep the car tracking straight and protect those expensive 20‑ or 21‑inch tires. ## Battery health checks for the e-tron GT The high‑voltage battery is the e-tron GT’s heart and its most expensive single component. Day to day, you’ll see only a percentage and range estimate on the dash, but during scheduled service Audi technicians can pull detailed diagnostic data, including fault codes, temperature behavior, and any cell‑level issues. ### What Audi checks at service - Battery control module fault codes and thermal alerts. - Cooling system performance and coolant level/condition. - High‑voltage wiring and connectors for damage or corrosion. - Sealing and underbody protection around the pack. ### What you can watch at home - Sudden loss of range with the same driving pattern. - Charging behavior that’s much slower than usual on the same charger. - Warning lights related to the electrical system or drive system. - Unusual fan noise or frequent cooling activity when parked. ### How Recharged helps on used e-tron GTs Every EV sold through Recharged includes a **Recharged Score Report** with verified battery health, so you’re not guessing how the last owner treated the pack. That’s a big advantage over a generic used‑car inspection. ## Typical Audi e-tron GT maintenance costs You’re driving a flagship Audi, so service visits won’t be bargain‑basement. The good news is that **EVs shift more of your budget from maintenance to tires** rather than piling on fluid changes and engine work. Actual prices vary by dealer and region, but this is a realistic way to think about costs in the U.S. ### Typical U.S. e-tron GT maintenance and wear costs $200–$350 Minor visit Basic inspection with cabin filter and rotation at an Audi dealer. $400–$800 Major service 2‑year/20,000‑mile type visit with brake fluid and deeper checks. $1,200–$2,000+ Tire set High‑performance 20–21" tires, including mounting and alignment. Low Drivetrain upkeep No timing belt, spark plugs, or engine oil changes vs gas Audi. ### Budgeting tip If you’re planning long‑term ownership, set aside a tire fund and assume one major service every 2 years. Compared with a V6 or V8 Audi, you’re likely to come out ahead over 5–7 years of driving. ## Maintenance differences: e-tron GT vs gas Audi If you’re coming out of a gas‑powered S or RS model, the e-tron GT will feel strangely low‑maintenance. EVs skip oil changes and timing belts, but that doesn’t mean they’re maintenance‑free, especially when you’re shopping used. ### Quick takeaway Audi recommends time‑ and mileage‑based service for the e-tron GT, with major inspections roughly every 2 years/20,000 miles, regular brake fluid changes, cabin filters, and detailed high‑voltage system checks. Tires, brakes, and suspension still matter just as much as any performance Audi. ## How Audi e-tron GT maintenance works The e-tron GT is built like a high‑performance Audi but maintained like a modern EV. Instead of the familiar A6 or S5 routine of **oil changes every 10,000 miles**, the electric GT leans on long inspection intervals and software‑driven checks. The car’s service reminder in the cockpit display is your referee, counting down to the next visit based on time and mileage. - There’s no engine oil, spark plugs, or exhaust system to service. - The big-ticket item, the high‑voltage battery, is monitored constantly by onboard software. - Most scheduled visits center around inspections, filters, fluids, tires, and brake components. - Audi typically structures service as flexible inspections rather than long lists of parts to replace. ### Tip for first-time EV owners On an e-tron GT, time matters as much as miles. Even if you only drive a few thousand miles a year, you’ll still want those 2‑year inspections for things like brake fluid, seals, and suspension wear. ## Audi e-tron GT maintenance schedule overview Exact intervals can vary slightly by model year and market, but most Audi e-tron GT schedules in the U.S. follow this general rhythm. Always confirm with the owner’s manual or Audi dealer for your specific VIN, but this overview will get you 95% of the way there. ![Audi e-tron GT on a lift in a service bay during a scheduled inspection](https://recharged.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fd365moeqy2c2l.cloudfront.net%2Fimages%2Fcontent%2Feebb01bf70db2e32ec581d22b03e813e-content.png&w=3840&q=75) Most e-tron GT scheduled services are inspections and fluid checks rather than big mechanical repairs. ### Audi e-tron GT service interval table Common U.S. market inspection and replacement intervals for key e-tron GT maintenance items. Always verify against the service booklet for your car. | Interval (time / miles) | What usually happens | EV‑specific notes | | --- | --- | --- | | Every 1 year / 10,000 miles | General inspection, tire rotation, visual brake check, fluids top‑off | High‑voltage cables and underbody shield visually checked. | | Every 2 years / 20,000 miles | Comprehensive inspection, brake fluid change, cabin filter replacement | High‑voltage system and battery cooling circuit checked with diagnostics. | | Every 3 years | Air conditioning service check, refrigerant leak inspection | Heat pump and battery thermal management performance evaluated. | | Every 4 years / ~40,000 miles | More detailed suspension/steering check, alignment check recommended | Extra attention to weight‑related wear on tires, bushings, and control arms. | | Every 6 years / 60,000+ miles | Possible coolant exchange depending on Audi guidance and climate | Battery coolant condition and thermal system capacity reviewed. | | As needed | Tires, brake pads/rotors, wiper blades, 12‑V battery | Tire wear can be quicker than on non‑performance EVs; regen doesn’t eliminate brake service. | Intervals shown are typical guidelines; local schedules and warranty plans may differ. ## Key maintenance items on the Audi e-tron GT, explained ### What your e-tron GT actually needs serviced Think inspections and wear items, not constant fluid changes. #### Annual inspections Audi techs scan for software faults, check steering and suspension, inspect axle boots and underbody panels, and look for leaks or physical damage to the high‑voltage system. #### Brake fluid & hydraulics Even with strong regenerative braking, the car still relies on a conventional hydraulic system. Fluid ages with time and moisture and typically gets replaced about every 2 years. #### Cabin & 12‑V battery The high‑voltage pack powers the car, but the 12‑V battery runs control modules. Expect conventional 12‑V battery replacement every few years plus cabin air filter changes for clean HVAC performance. Beyond those basics, expect the usual wear items: tires, wiper blades, and, over time, brake pads and rotors. Because the e-tron GT is heavy and very quick, it can chew through tires faster than a regular sedan, especially on performance rubber. ### Don’t skip tire rotations With dual‑motor all‑wheel drive and instant torque, uneven tire wear can sneak up on you. Regular rotations (often every 5,000–10,000 miles) keep the car tracking straight and protect those expensive 20‑ or 21‑inch tires. ## Battery health checks for the e-tron GT The high‑voltage battery is the e-tron GT’s heart and its most expensive single component. Day to day, you’ll see only a percentage and range estimate on the dash, but during scheduled service Audi technicians can pull detailed diagnostic data, including fault codes, temperature behavior, and any cell‑level issues. ### What Audi checks at service - Battery control module fault codes and thermal alerts. - Cooling system performance and coolant level/condition. - High‑voltage wiring and connectors for damage or corrosion. - Sealing and underbody protection around the pack. ### What you can watch at home - Sudden loss of range with the same driving pattern. - Charging behavior that’s much slower than usual on the same charger. - Warning lights related to the electrical system or drive system. - Unusual fan noise or frequent cooling activity when parked. ### How Recharged helps on used e-tron GTs Every EV sold through Recharged includes a **Recharged Score Report** with verified battery health, so you’re not guessing how the last owner treated the pack. That’s a big advantage over a generic used‑car inspection. ## Typical Audi e-tron GT maintenance costs You’re driving a flagship Audi, so service visits won’t be bargain‑basement. The good news is that **EVs shift more of your budget from maintenance to tires** rather than piling on fluid changes and engine work. Actual prices vary by dealer and region, but this is a realistic way to think about costs in the U.S. ### Typical U.S. e-tron GT maintenance and wear costs $200–$350 Minor visit Basic inspection with cabin filter and rotation at an Audi dealer. $400–$800 Major service 2‑year/20,000‑mile type visit with brake fluid and deeper checks. $1,200–$2,000+ Tire set High‑performance 20–21" tires, including mounting and alignment. Low Drivetrain upkeep No timing belt, spark plugs, or engine oil changes vs gas Audi. ### Budgeting tip If you’re planning long‑term ownership, set aside a tire fund and assume one major service every 2 years. Compared with a V6 or V8 Audi, you’re likely to come out ahead over 5–7 years of driving. ## Maintenance differences: e-tron GT vs gas Audi If you’re coming out of a gas‑powered S or RS model, the e-tron GT will feel strangely low‑maintenance.
