# BMW iX Maintenance Schedule

### Your Local BMW iX Experts

The BMW iX maintenance schedule is a list of time-based and usage-based service items designed to keep your vehicle reliable and efficient over time. By following the BMW iX maintenance schedule at designated intervals, you can help improve the health and range of your EV, and help prevent small issues from becoming bigger service items down the road. Learn about these essential services below, and book your next service at BMW of Carlsbad

[Schedule Service](https://www.bmwcarlsbad.com/ServiceApptForm.htm)

## BMW iX Service Intervals (2022-Current)

Since the BMW iX is an electric vehicle, it benefits from having fewer required services as compared to a traditional gas-powered vehicle. That being said, servicing your BMW iX at least once every two years is crucial to help identify any issues and inspect wear items such as tires or brakes.

### Time-Based Services

#### Every Two Years (or sooner based on usage)

- **Cabin Air Filter** \- Replace the interior cabin air filter.
- **Brake Fluid** \- Flush and replace brake fluid.
- **Key Fob** \- Replace remote control key battery.
- **Vehicle Check** \- Test basic vehicle functions, inspect tires, top off fluid levels. inspect high-voltage charging port, inspect brakes and lines, and conduct a road test.

#### Every Four Years (or sooner based on usage)

- **Supplemental Vehicle Check** \- Inspect tie rod ends, steering boots and clamps, warning light functionality, and inspect the Mobility Kit components.
- **Cabin Air Filter** \- Replace the interior cabin air filter.
- **Brake Fluid** \- Flush and replace brake fluid.
- **Key Fob** \- Replace remote control key battery.
- **Vehicle Check** \- Test basic vehicle functions, inspect tires, top off fluid levels. inspect high-voltage charging port, inspect brakes and lines, and conduct a road test.

### Condition-Based Services

Based on your overall vehicle usage, which factors in mileage and driving hours, some services will be called out by your vehicle's onboard computer. In addition to the services listed above, the Condition-Based Service system (CBS) will suggest these brake services over time:

- **Front Brakes** \- Replace brake pads and wear sensors, grease mating surfaces, and check front brake disc condition.
- **Rear Brakes** \- Replace brake pads and wear sensors, grease mating surfaces, check front brake disc condition, and test parking brake functions.

The [Volkswagen ID.4](https://www.alexandriavw.com/new-id-4/) is an all-electric SUV known for its efficient performance, spaciousness, and comfort. As an ID.4 owner, it only makes sense that you’d want to take care of the vehicle you rely on for your Arlington and Washington D.C. drives. After all, when you take proper care of your vehicle, your vehicle will continue to take care of you. Learn all about the ID.4 maintenance schedule in this checklist from your friends at Alexandria Volkswagen.

## VW ID.4 Maintenance Schedule

Your ID.4 requires its first maintenance visit at 10,000 miles and every 10,000 miles thereafter. Let’s take a look at the services performed at each appointment.

### 10K, 30K, 50K, 70K, 90K, 110K\* Miles

- Check battery
- Inspect tires
- Obtain diagnostic system readings
- Reset service interval indicator/display

\*At 110,000 miles, a few additional services are included in the recommended ID.4 maintenance schedule:

- Check rear window
- Replace cabin air filter
- Rotate tires

### 20K, 40K, 60K, 80K, 100K, 120K Miles

At these intervals, your service technician will perform the above services, in addition to road-testing the vehicle, servicing its high-voltage parts, and inspecting the following components:

- Brake fluid
- Brake system
- Cooling system
- Headlight washer
- Horn function
- Lighting operation and alignment
- Motor parts
- Steering
- Suspension
- Underbody contact points and linkage
- Windshield wipers

## VW ID.4 Maintenance Cost

Now that you know the recommended ID.4 maintenance schedule, you may be wondering about the VW ID.4 maintenance cost. Some of the above services will likely be included in the VW Scheduled Carefree Maintenance plan, which comes standard on most new Volkswagen models–including the ID.4–for the first two years of manufacturer-suggested maintenance intervals. # SAFETY PRECAUTIONS

Your RAV4 Hybrid has both high-voltage DC and AC systems as well as a 12-volt system. Both DC and AC high voltage are very dangerous and can cause personal injury, severe burns, electric shock and even fatal injury.

To avoid personal injury, please follow all caution labels attached to high-voltage parts. Do not touch or attempt to remove or replace any high-voltage (orange-colored) wiring and connectors. Do not touch the service plug, which is located under the rear seat.

If an accident occurs, do not touch any high-voltage wiring, connectors or parts such as the inverter unit or hybrid vehicle battery assembly.

Do not touch the potassium hydroxide electrolyte that might spill or leak from the hybrid vehicle battery as the result of an accident. If potassium hydroxide electrolyte gets on your skin or in your eyes, neutralize it immediately with a saturated boric acid solution (ratio: 80 grams boric acid to two liters water). Seek immediate medical attention.

If a vehicle fire occurs, extinguish it with a Class D powder-type fire extinguisher.

## Toyota RAV4 Maintenance Schedule By Mileage

In general, the Toyota RAV4 maintenance schedule happens every 5,000 miles or six months, whichever comes first. As your vehicle ages, we’ll keep you updated on what parts or items are starting to show signs of wear and will need replacement. Expect a tire rotation and basic inspection every 5,000 miles, followed by a full synthetic [oil change](https://www.galaxytoyota.net/service/genuine-toyota-oil-change/) at 10,000 miles. As your SUV approaches 40,000 miles, our team might tell you that the tires and brake pads might need to be replaced, and you could need a new battery.

### Toyota RAV4 Service Schedule At 5,000 Miles Or 6 Months

We’ll take care of these items at 5,000 miles:

- An inspection of the [wiper blades](https://www.galaxytoyota.net/parts/toyota-wiper-blades/) for cracking
- Checking and refilling all fluid levels as needed
- [Tire](https://www.galaxytoyota.net/toyota-tire-center/) rotation
- A visual inspection of the [brakes](https://www.galaxytoyota.net/service/genuine-toyota-brakes/)

### Toyota RAV4 Service Schedule At 10,000 Miles Or 12 Months

At 10,000 miles, your Toyota RAV4 service includes all of the 5,000-mile maintenance tasks, as well as an oil change and filter replacement.

### Toyota RAV4 Service Schedule At 15,000 Miles Or 18 Months

Once your vehicle hits 15,000 miles, you will need a more intensive appointment. We will take care of these items:

- New cabin air filter
- Ball joints and dust covers
- Brake lines and hoses
- Drive shaft boots
- Engine coolant
- Exhaust pipes and mountings
- Radiator and condenser
- Steering gear
- Steering linkage and boots

### Toyota RAV4 Maintenance Required At 20,000 Miles Or 24 Months

The 20,000-mile mark is another oil change and filter replacement. Additional service includes the routine 5,000-mile service, as well as the wiper blade inspection, assessment of all fluid levels, and tire rotation.

### Toyota RAV4 Maintenance Required At 25,000 Miles Or 30 Months

During this Toyota RAV4 service interval, you’re getting all of the previous service tasks except the oil change and filter replacement. You can also expect a brake inspection during this time.

### Toyota RAV4 Maintenance Required At 30,000 Miles Or 36 Months

During the [30,000-mile service interval](https://www.galaxytoyota.net/service/service-tips/toyota-30000-mile-service/), you can expect standard tasks like an oil change, cabin filter replacement, engine air filter replacement, and tire rotation. There are also extensive maintenance service tasks and inspections:

- Automatic transmission (will be checked for signs of leakage)
- Ball joints and dust covers
- Brake components, lines, and hoses
- Drive shaft boots
- Engine coolant
- Exhaust pipes and mountings
- Fuel lines and connections
- Fuel tank band
- Fuel tank vapor vent system hoses
- Fuel tank cap gasket
- Radiator and condenser
- Steering gear
- Steering linkage and boots

If our team sees anything that might need repairs soon, we will let you know.

### Toyota RAV4 Maintenance Required At 35,000 Miles Or 42 Months

The 35,000-mile service interval includes what you get during the 5,000-mile maintenance period.

### Toyota RAV4 Maintenance Schedule At 40,000 Miles Or 48 Months

This is when the engine oil and oil filter are changed, as well as the other standard tasks.

### Toyota RAV4 Maintenance Schedule At 45,000 Miles Or 54 Months

During your 45,000-mile Toyota RAV4 service appointment, you can expect the following:

- Ball joints and dust covers
- Brake lines and hoses
- Cabin air filter
- Drive shaft boots
- Engine coolant
- Exhaust pipes and mountings
- Radiator and condenser
- Steering gear
- Steering linkage and boots

### Toyota RAV4 Maintenance Schedule At 50,000 Miles Or 60 Months

The 50,000-mile appointment requires another oil change and replacement of the oil and cabin air filter. At this point, your SUV may need new tires, new brake pads, or a battery, depending on your Long Branch driving habits and the amount of wear and tear on your vehicle.

### Toyota RAV4 Service Schedule At 55,000 Miles Or 66 Months

When you hit 55,000 miles, it’s time to check all of the fluids, get a tire rotation, and a visual examination of your brakes.

### Toyota RAV4 Service Schedule At 60,000 Miles Or 72 Months

This consists of all of the standard 30,000-mile checks, refills, and replacements.

Your Toyota RAV4 is engineered for longevity, and a thoughtful service rhythm is the simplest way to protect its performance, efficiency, and resale value. Our Toyota-trained technicians know each RAV4 generation inside and out — from gas to Hybrid — and we maintain your vehicle using Genuine Toyota parts, up-to-date diagnostics, and clear service records that help you plan ahead. Our service center in Shreveport, LA also offers Express Maintenance for quick oil changes, tire rotations, battery testing, and multipoint inspections, so you can stay on schedule without rearranging your day. Whether your RAV4 is a recent model with Toyota Safety Sense™ or a well-traveled companion, we check critical systems like brakes, steering, suspension, and cooling at each visit, and we can align wheels, balance tires, and replace filters the same day in most cases. If your RAV4 is equipped with AWD, we monitor differential and transfer case fluids; Hybrid models receive attention to inverter coolant and the battery cooling intake. Because driving conditions, mileage, and model year vary, your Owner’s Manual remains the ultimate guide, and we are happy to tailor a plan to your commute and climate. Use the following general cadence to map out the year, then check in with us to confirm the right interval for your specific vehicle.

- **Every 5,000-7,500 miles or 6 months**: Change engine oil and filter, rotate tires, inspect brakes, top off fluids, check lights and wipers.
- **Every 15,000 miles or annually**: Replace cabin air filter as needed, measure brake wear, test 12V battery, inspect steering and suspension.
- **Every 30,000 miles**: Replace engine air filter, inspect cooling system and hoses, service brake fluid as needed, clean throttle body if required.
- **Every 60,000 miles**: Inspect transmission or CVT fluid per manual, replace AWD differential and transfer case fluids if equipped, check spark plugs on applicable years.
- **At 90,000-100,000 miles**: Replace spark plugs on many gas models, refresh engine coolant, inspect drive belts and water pump, service PCV valve if applicable.
- **Hybrid models**: Clean battery cooling intake, replace inverter coolant at specified intervals, verify hybrid system health with a scan.
- **Seasonal or before trips**: Check alignment and tire pressure, measure tread depth, test A/C performance, inspect washer fluid and exterior lights.

Start by reviewing your Owner’s Manual and any ToyotaCare® coverage, then call or schedule online; we will pre-plan parts, verify any campaigns, and note concerns you want us to inspect. When service is complete, we return your RAV4 washed, document everything in your digital file, and remind you of upcoming items so you can budget time around work and family. If you’re preparing for a road trip, ask us for a quick alignment check and A/C performance test; if you’ve added accessories or drive on rough roads, we can tighten underbody shields and re-torque wheel fasteners. Intervals may differ by model year, engine, Hybrid system, towing use, and climate; always consult your Owner’s Manual or contact the manufacturer or our team for details. # How Often Should You Change Your Transmission Fluid?

There's no one-size-fits-all answer when it comes to how often you should change your vehicle's transmission fluid. In general, adhere to the manufacturer guidelines to ensure that your ride's transmission fluid and filter maintenance is on point and that your car, truck, SUV, or van operates and performs at its peak.

## What is a Transmission Fluid Change?

A transmission fluid change involves draining the old transmission fluid from the transmission pan, replacing 30 to 40 percent of the fluid, and installing a new transmission filter. It's recommended for routine maintenance to keep the transmission functioning smoothly.

A transmission fluid change is not the same thing as a transmission fluid flush, which is more time-consuming and typically pricier. A flush, as the name suggests, involves completely flushing out all the old transmission fluid from the system. Special transmission flush fluid is circulated into the transmission system, cleaning out any residue or contaminants. A flush replaces nearly 100 percent of the old fluid. Both procedures can help maintain the health of your transmission, preserve its performance, and prolong its lifespan.

It's always best to consult your vehicle's manual or reach out to the auto techs at your local Toyota dealership for specific recommendations for your car.

## How Often Should Transmission Fluid Be Changed?

When it comes to changing transmission fluid, it's essential to follow the manufacturer's recommendations outlined in your vehicle's owner's manual. Some newer vehicles with "lifetime" transmission fluid require less-frequent transmission fluid changes unless a problem with the transmission crops up, necessitating it.

However, some conditions may warrant shorter transmission fluid change intervals such as: towing or hauling, frequent exposure to severe weather conditions, stop-and-go traffic, or at the first sign of transmission problems, such as gear slippage, grinding noises, delayed shifting, and excessive vibration.

Manual transmissions typically require less frequent fluid changes compared to automatic transmissions. Defer to the recommendations of your owner's manual or the service technician at your local Toyota dealership.

## How to Check Transmission Fluid?

It's essential to consult your vehicle's owner's manual for specific instructions and recommendations regarding transmission fluid type and level-checking procedures, as they can vary between different vehicles. If you're unsure or uncomfortable performing this task yourself, it's always best to seek assistance from a skilled technician.

In general, to check your transmission fluid, park your car on a level surface and start the engine. Locate the transmission dipstick under the hood, pull it out, and wipe it clean. Fully reinsert the dipstick, then pull it out again to check the fluid level to see where it falls between the markings on the dipstick.

Next, check the color of the transmission fluid: pinkish-red transmission fluid typically indicates that the fluid is clean and healthy with the chemical composition to effectively lubricate and cool the transmission components. If the fluid appears significantly darker or has a burnt smell, it may indicate contamination or degradation, suggesting it's time for a fluid change or closer inspection by a technician.

Most newer model vehicles have sealed transmission systems which may not have a dipstick for checking transmission fluid levels. Instead, the vehicle's internal mechanisms may automatically check and adjust fluid levels. Sealed transmission systems are designed to be maintenance-free. However, if you suspect a problem with a sealed transmission, it's best to consult an auto technician at your local Toyota dealership.

## How to Change Transmission Fluid

Changing transmission fluid involves locating the transmission fluid drain plug, draining the old fluid into a container, and removing the transmission pan to access the filter. Final steps include cleaning the pan, reinstalling it, and refilling the transmission with the appropriate type and amount of new fluid, following manufacturer recommendations, and then checking for leaks.

Ultimately, regular maintenance and staying attentive to your vehicle's performance are helpful in determining when transmission fluid changes may be needed. If in doubt, consult the professionals at your local Toyota dealership for personalized advice based on your vehicle's specific needs and usage.

# What Is The Toyota RAV4 Maintenance Schedule?

![2022 Toyota RAV4 Driving Down City Street](https://dealerinspire-image-library-prod.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/images/ItyQQY8keT1prE6dJLNzGgrYvv4kcLmDChVxc8j6.jpg)

A [Toyota RAV4](https://www.galaxytoyota.net/new-vehicles/rav4/) is one of the most popular SUVs, and for good reason. From reliability and fuel efficiency to cargo space and family-friendly features, this [SUV](https://www.galaxytoyota.net/new-vehicles/crossovers-suvs/) is perfect for your Toms River lifestyle.

We highly recommend following the Toyota RAV4 maintenance schedule to keep your SUV in prime condition. You could have a quality vehicle that gives you many years of service going well past 200,000 miles! Keep reading to learn more about the Toyota RAV4 service schedule. When it’s time for your vehicle’s next maintenance, make an appointment with our factory-trained service team near Freehold.

[Service Tips](https://www.galaxytoyota.net/service/service-tips/) [Schedule Service](https://www.galaxytoyota.net/service/schedule-service/)

## Toyota RAV4 Maintenance Schedule By Mileage

In general, the Toyota RAV4 maintenance schedule happens every 5,000 miles or six months, whichever comes first. As your vehicle ages, we’ll keep you updated on what parts or items are starting to show signs of wear and will need replacement. Expect a tire rotation and basic inspection every 5,000 miles, followed by a full synthetic [oil change](https://www.galaxytoyota.net/service/genuine-toyota-oil-change/) at 10,000 miles. As your SUV approaches 40,000 miles, our team might tell you that the tires and brake pads might need to be replaced, and you could need a new battery.

### Toyota RAV4 Service Schedule At 5,000 Miles Or 6 Months

We’ll take care of these items at 5,000 miles:

- An inspection of the [wiper blades](https://www.galaxytoyota.net/parts/toyota-wiper-blades/) for cracking
- Checking and refilling all fluid levels as needed
- [Tire](https://www.galaxytoyota.net/toyota-tire-center/) rotation
- A visual inspection of the [brakes](https://www.galaxytoyota.net/service/genuine-toyota-brakes/)

### Toyota RAV4 Service Schedule At 10,000 Miles Or 12 Months

At 10,000 miles, your Toyota RAV4 service includes all of the 5,000-mile maintenance tasks, as well as an oil change and filter replacement.

### Toyota RAV4 Service Schedule At 15,000 Miles Or 18 Months

Once your vehicle hits 15,000 miles, you will need a more intensive appointment. We will take care of these items:

- New cabin air filter
- Ball joints and dust covers
- Brake lines and hoses
- Drive shaft boots
- Engine coolant
- Exhaust pipes and mountings
- Radiator and condenser
- Steering gear
- Steering linkage and boots

### Toyota RAV4 Maintenance Required At 20,000 Miles Or 24 Months

The 20,000-mile mark is another oil change and filter replacement. Additional service includes the routine 5,000-mile service, as well as the wiper blade inspection, assessment of all fluid levels, and tire rotation.

### Toyota RAV4 Maintenance Required At 25,000 Miles Or 30 Months

During this Toyota RAV4 service interval, you’re getting all of the previous service tasks except the oil change and filter replacement. You can also expect a brake inspection during this time.

### Toyota RAV4 Maintenance Required At 30,000 Miles Or 36 Months

During the [30,000-mile service interval](https://www.galaxytoyota.net/service/service-tips/toyota-30000-mile-service/), you can expect standard tasks like an oil change, cabin filter replacement, engine air filter replacement, and tire rotation. There are also extensive maintenance service tasks and inspections:

- Automatic transmission (will be checked for signs of leakage)
- Ball joints and dust covers
- Brake components, lines, and hoses
- Drive shaft boots
- Engine coolant
- Exhaust pipes and mountings
- Fuel lines and connections
- Fuel tank band
- Fuel tank vapor vent system hoses
- Fuel tank cap gasket
- Radiator and condenser
- Steering gear
- Steering linkage and boots

If our team sees anything that might need repairs soon, we will let you know.

### Toyota RAV4 Maintenance Required At 35,000 Miles Or 42 Months

The 35,000-mile service interval includes what you get during the 5,000-mile maintenance period.

### Toyota RAV4 Maintenance Schedule At 40,000 Miles Or 48 Months

This is when the engine oil and oil filter are changed, as well as the other standard tasks.

### Toyota RAV4 Maintenance Schedule At 45,000 Miles Or 54 Months

During your 45,000-mile Toyota RAV4 service appointment, you can expect the following:

- Ball joints and dust covers
- Brake lines and hoses
- Cabin air filter
- Drive shaft boots
- Engine coolant
- Exhaust pipes and mountings
- Radiator and condenser
- Steering gear
- Steering linkage and boots

### Toyota RAV4 Maintenance Schedule At 50,000 Miles Or 60 Months

The 50,000-mile appointment requires another oil change and replacement of the oil and cabin air filter. At this point, your SUV may need new tires, new brake pads, or a battery, depending on your Long Branch driving habits and the amount of wear and tear on your vehicle.

### Toyota RAV4 Service Schedule At 55,000 Miles Or 66 Months

When you hit 55,000 miles, it’s time to check all of the fluids, get a tire rotation, and a visual examination of your brakes.

### Toyota RAV4 Service Schedule At 60,000 Miles Or 72 Months

This consists of all of the standard 30,000-mile checks, refills, and replacements.

# 2024 Volkswagen Golf GTI Maintenance Schedule

![hero image](https://dealerimages.dealereprocess.com/image/upload/3441624)

# 2024 Volkswagen Golf GTI Maintenance Schedule

Get ahead of the curve with our comprehensive guide to maintaining your 2024 VW Golf GTI. Our meticulously crafted maintenance schedule ensures your vehicle stays in peak condition, maximizing its performance and longevity. From routine oil changes to intricate inspections, our expert technicians are dedicated to keeping your GTI running smoothly mile after mile.

![](https://dealerimages.dealereprocess.com/image/upload/3441621)

[Schedule Schedule](https://www.pohankavw.com/online-service-scheduler/)

## 10,000-Mile Maintenance

Volkswagen recommends a minor maintenance visit every 10,000 miles for your 2024 Golf GTI. More frequent service is recommended if the car is used routinely in severe temperatures or under other extreme conditions (ask your service advisor for guidance). The technicians will change the engine oil and filter, rotate the tires, and perform a general look-over during each of these appointments.

## 20,000-Mile Maintenance

The tasks from the 10,000-mile service will be repeated at this visit. The sunroof drains will also be cleaned and checked for any blockage (recommended every 20,000 miles or two years, whichever comes first).

## 30,000-Mile Maintenance

Our team will repeat the 10,000-mile maintenance tasks.

## 40,000-Mile Maintenance

While this service is going to repeat the measures from the 10,000- and 20,000-mile intervals (engine oil/filter change, tire rotation, and sunroof drain cleaning), they will also replace the dust and pollen filter.

## 50,000-Mile Maintenance

This point on your 2024 Golf GTI’s odometer calls for our service team to simply change the engine oil and filter, rotate the tires, and keep their eyes open for any developing issues.

## 60,000-Mile Maintenance

Along with the standard service (engine oil/filter change and tire rotation), VW recommends replacing the engine air filter and cleaning the screen (every 60,000 miles or six years). As this is an interval of 20K miles, it’s time once again to have the sunroof drains cleaned and checked for blockage, along with installing a new dust and pollen filter.

## 70,000-Mile Maintenance

This is another simplified visit calling for engine oil/filter change and tire rotation.

## 80,000-Mile Maintenance

Along with the engine oil/filter change and tire rotation at this interval, our technicians will also replace the spark plugs (recommended every 80,000 miles or six years, whichever comes first). They will also repeat the sunroof drain cleaning and replace the cabin air filter.

## 90,000-Mile Maintenance

The expected minor maintenance is performed at this visit (tire rotation and the engine oil/filter change).

## 100,000-Mile Maintenance

Although 100K miles is a major interval, this will be a relatively simple service visit consisting of an engine oil/filter change, tire rotation, mechanical inspection, and sunroof drains cleaning.

## 110,000-Mile Maintenance

This appointment only requires the engine oil and filter change along with tire rotation.

## 120,000-Mile Maintenance

This visit is one of the more extensive ones, combining these tasks from the 40,000- and 60,000-mile services:

- Change engine oil/filter
- Rotate tires
- Clean sunroof drains/check for blockage
- Replace dust and pollen filter
- Replace engine air filter and clean the screen

## After 120,000 Miles & Time-Based Services

It’s important to get your 2024 Golf GTI in to Pohanka VW’s service department so that our service team can repeat the tasks at the appropriate mileage intervals, based on the schedule given above. They will also address the following important maintenance:

- Check coolant pump belt – Every 180,000 miles
- Change brake fluid – Every three years
- Change front axle differential lock fluid – Every three years
- Replace tire filler bottle in tire mobility set – Every four years

## Regular Inspections (Every Visit)

Volkswagen is committed to prioritizing safety and reliability. That’s why our technicians are sure to inspect the vehicle every time it’s here for service. This allows them to monitor the major systems and components and address anything that requires attention. Here are a few of the critical items that will be looked at during these inspections:

- Brake pad thickness
- Tire tread/wear
- Battery
- Exterior lighting
- Brake fluid levels
- Cooling system
- Wiper blades
- Suspension check (ball joints, stabilizer bar, coupling rod, axle bearings, springs, etc.)
- Exhaust system
- Underbody
- Transmission fluid
- Steering system

[![Recommended service and maintenance schedule for Ford Super Duty F-250](https://scout.customerscout.net/Gallery/IMAGES/2025/Ford/Super-Duty-F-250/2025FordSuperDutyF-250-exterior-01.jpg)](https://www.alpineford.com/service.aspx)

## [Alpine Ford – Recommended service and maintenance schedule for Ford Super Duty F-250](https://www.alpineford.com/service.aspx)

At Alpine Ford, we know your Ford Super Duty F-250 is built to conquer demanding jobs, long towing days, and rugged miles. Keeping it performing at its best takes a plan—one that fits how you drive, what you tow, and the conditions you face. Our factory-trained technicians use genuine Motorcraft® parts, advanced diagnostics, and detailed multi-point inspections to help you stay ahead of wear and tear while protecting long-term value. Whether you drive gas or Power Stroke® diesel, we tailor maintenance to your duty cycle, climate, and payloads, and we can document service history to support warranty needs and future resale. From quick oil changes and rotations to diesel fuel filter service, axle and transfer case care, and brake and cooling system maintenance, we make it straightforward and transparent. We’re proud to be serving in Pueblo, CO, Colorado Springs, and Canon City, offering flexible scheduling, clear estimates, and maintenance reminders designed around real-world use. The general schedule below covers common needs across most model years; actual intervals can vary by engine, model year, and use case. Always consult your Owner’s Manual and contact the manufacturer or our service team for specifics, especially if you tow frequently, idle often, or operate in dust, cold, or mountainous conditions.

1. **Every month:** Check tire pressures, tire condition, exterior lights, wiper blades, and all fluids; top off Diesel Exhaust Fluid on diesel models.
2. **Every 5,000-7,500 miles or 6 months:** Change engine oil and filter, rotate tires, inspect brakes, steering, and suspension; check alignment if you notice pull or uneven wear.
3. **15,000-20,000 miles:** Replace Power Stroke® diesel fuel filters, inspect engine air filter, service front hubs if equipped, and clean battery terminals.
4. **30,000 miles or sooner for severe duty:** Replace engine air filter as needed, inspect transfer case and axle fluids, balance tires, and verify torque on lug nuts.
5. **Every 3 years:** Replace brake fluid, test coolant condition, and replace the cabin air filter if equipped.
6. **60,000 miles:** Inspect transmission fluid and service based on use and temperature load; inspect belts, hoses, and 4×4 components.
7. **100,000 miles:** Replace coolant, replace spark plugs on applicable gas engines, inspect water pump, and service front and rear axle fluids as needed.
8. **Before and after towing season:** Request a full multi-point inspection, verify trailer brake controller operation, and test 7-pin trailer wiring.

Our team makes maintenance easy with clear recommendations, photos and videos from your inspection, and parts designed to meet Ford® specs. We handle the details—DEF top-offs, diesel-specific tests, brake and rotor measurements, and alignment checks after tire rotations—so your F-250 tracks straight, tows confidently, and stops smoothly. If your truck sees heavy loads, frequent mountain drives, or jobsite dust, ask us to customize a severe-service plan and interval tracker. Disclaimers: schedules vary by model year, engine, and use; always follow the Owner’s Manual and contact the manufacturer or our service department for exact guidance. Ready to plan your next visit or customize a schedule for your truck? Request more information and we’ll build a maintenance roadmap that fits your mileage, towing profile, and budget, then get you on the books at a time that works for you.

# 6.7 Power Stroke Oil Capacity

### **How Much Oil Does a Powerstroke 6.7 Hold?**

The oil capacity of a [6.7 Powerstroke engine varies by year of manufacture](https://www.hotshotsecret.com/top-powerstroke-engines/) and the specific vehicle model.  If you own a Ford F-250 to F-650 manufactured after 2022, its Powerstroke 6.7L will hold 15 quarts (14.2 liters) of oil. Those manufactured between 2011 and 2022 hold approximately 13 quarts (12.3 liters).

A Ford F-650 and F-750 produced between 2015 and 2022 can hold a maximum of 15 quarts (14.2 liters) of oil. For newer models released in 2023 and later, the oil capacity increases slightly to 17 quarts (16 liters).

When performing an oil change, it is crucial to use the correct type of oil and adhere to the recommended capacity. Ford recommends using oils that meet its WSS-M2C17-F1 specification for the 6.7 Powerstroke. Always refer to your owner’s manual for exact information about the type and weight of oil that best suits your truck and application.

# BMW SERVICE

BMW recommends you have your maintenance and repair work performed by an authorized BMW center.

# MAINTAINING YOUR BMW VEHICLE

A well-maintained vehicle will help safeguard its operational performance, road-safety and its reliability. This is why it is important to follow and perform BMW’s recommended periodic vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks as indicated by your vehicle’s Maintenance Service Display, along with the other maintenance work described in this booklet.

A improper maintenance is not covered under the BMW New Vehicle Damage, including consequential damage, which results from lack of or Limited Warranty for Passenger Cars and Light Trucks.

# MAINTENANCE INTERVALS

Maintenance intervals on motor vehicles were conventionally based solely on a fixed time period or a specified amount of accumulated driving mileage.

However, operational and driving conditions have a major influence on your vehicle’s routine maintenance requirements; the distance traveled is only one of these significant factors. A vehicle used for short trips in the city with numerous cold starts, prolonged periods of idling, stop-and-go driving, and high engine speeds during acceleration may require more frequent maintenance intervals than a vehicle that is driven long distances at moderate engine speeds.

Your BMW vehicle uses sensors and algorithms together with the elapsed time and the driving distance/profile to monitor and evaluate your vehicle’s maintenance service needs. This information is then used to adapt dynamically the parameters used to forecast the applicable maintenance service task intervals.

# THE BMW MAINTENANCE SYSTEM

All BMW vehicles are equipped with an integrated BMW Maintenance System. This maintenance “reminder” system helps ensure that the vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks are performed at the forecasted intervals that apply to your vehicle.

The BMW Maintenance System display provides the vehicle operator access to the current status information for the following maintenance service tasks:

$\\triangleright$ Engine oil (date and miles)\*

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle check (date and miles)

$\\triangleright$ Front brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Rear brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid (date)

$\\triangleright$ 1200 Mile running-in service (date and miles) (Applicable to BMW M vehicles only)\*

For each specific maintenance service task, either the future date (month/ year), remaining miles or both are provided as noted above. The system monitors variable inputs to forecast the intervals and alert the driver when one or more specific maintenance tasks should be performed.

NOTE: For certain vehicles, the status of the front and rear brake pads will only be observable in the maintenance system’s display when there are approximately 2,000 miles or less remaining before a brake service will be required to be performed.

For information about the vehicle’s maintenance system displays, please refer to the Maintenance Service Display Overview section beginning on page 5.

The following “combine with Engine oil”\* maintenance service tasks may be identified as needing to be performed with a specific occurrence of the “Engine oil” service task (service counter number):

$\\triangleright$ Cabin Microfilter(s)

$\\triangleright$ Engine air filter(s)\*

$\\triangleright$ Spark plugs\*

$\\triangleright$ Final drive oil (Applicable M vehicles only)

\\* Does not apply to BEV

Although these items do not appear in the BMW Maintenance System’s display in the vehicle, these services should be performed when your vehicle’s engine oil is changed in accordance with the interval identified by your vehicle’s BMW Maintenance System.

For more information on your vehicle’s maintenance services requirements, procedures and intervals, please refer the Maintenance Service Summary section beginning on page 10.

The BMW Maintenance System also includes an option to set service reminders for the following state-specific mandatory vehicle inspections, including:

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle safety inspection; and/or $\\triangleright$ Emissions test

The corresponding interval data for these inspections can be inputted into the BMW Maintenance System by a service provider; they are not determined by the vehicle.

For your convenience, you may also wish to have your authorized BMW center perform the work necessary to fulfill these state inspection requirements in your area concurrent with the maintenance services specified above when possible.

Should you request more frequent maintenance service than is indicated by the BMW Maintenance System during the coverage period, the cost of these services will not be covered by the BMW Maintenance Program.

# SERVICE DATA — REMOTE CONTROL KEY

Maintenance service task status information for your BMW vehicle is continually updated and stored in your remote control key.

Your authorized BMW center can access this data and consult with you about applicable service procedures and tasks for your vehicle.

Therefore, always provide your service consultant with the most recent remote control key that was used to operate the vehicle when servicing your vehicle at a BMW center.

# VEHICLE STORAGE

Disconnecting the battery during periods of long-term vehicle storage will interrupt the calculation of time-dependent maintenance services.

In this situation, BMW recommends that you have all your time-based maintenance services, such as brake fluid, engine oil and cabin microfilter, brought up to the correct date by an authorized BMW center.

# ENGINE OIL

2025 model year vehicles with internal-combustion engines are factory-filled with:

Z BMW-approved fully synthetic oil for gasoline engines

Engine oil should be changed when the vehicle’s engine is at operating temperature.

If an engine oil service is being performed or you need to add engine oil between changes, please refer to the Owner’s Manual for the recommended engine oil for your BMW vehicle.

# LONG-TERM RATED FLUIDS AND OILS

The following systems and assemblies are factory-filled with long-term rated fluid and oil; fluid replacement is only necessary when repairs are being performed (unless otherwise noted):

$\\triangleright$ Engine cooling system (antifreeze/coolant) $\\triangleright$ Automatic (except for X1 and X2) and manual transmissions $\\triangleright$ All-wheel drive transfer cases (except when indicated by the vehicle)

# REGULAR CHECKS — VEHICLE OPERATOR

In addition to the maintenance service procedure information contained in this booklet, BMW recommends that you regularly check (when refueling, for example), and address when necessary, the following items:

$\\triangleright$ Washer fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Coolant level

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Tires — pressure, condition and wear

Please refer to the Owner’s Manual for additional information.

## BMW Preventative Maintenance: Every 5,000 Miles / 6 Months

It’s important to bring in your BMW two or three times a year (or every 5,000 miles) for these preventative maintenance services:

- Front and rear brake inspection
- Brake fluid check
- Coolant check
- Engine oil check
- Cabin air filter inspection
- Engine inspection
- Vehicle inspection
- Wiper blade inspection
- Any necessary tire rotations

Your BMW also comes with something called the Condition-Based Service Monitor (CBS). Your CBS tracks the condition of important systems in your BMW, letting you know if service is required. Our technicians will also use your CBS to determine what needs to be replaced, repaired, or serviced when you schedule service. Keep in mind that just because your CBS may say that service may not be necessary at 5,000 miles doesn’t mean that you shouldn’t come in for preventative maintenance and checks. Sometimes human eyes are necessary to determine a problem or to nip any potential issues in the bud.

## Recommended BMW Maintenance Schedule

Your BMW service schedule needs will vary based on how often you drive, where you drive, and your driving conditions. Your owner’s manual can give you detailed information on common service tasks for your specific model and trim, but here’s what BMW owners can generally expect:

- **Every 10,000 miles** (or yearly): replace your vehicle’s engine oil, oil filter, and coolant.
- **Every 20,000 miles** (or every two years): inspect and replace your vehicle’s fuel filters.
- **Every 30,000 miles** (or every three years): replace your vehicle’s brake fluid (after the first replacement, **every 60,000 miles**) and replace your vehicle’s transmission fluid on manual-transmission BMWs.
- **Every 60,000 miles** (or every six years): replace your vehicle’s engine air filter and spark plugs, inspect and replace any brake pads and brake rotors, and replace transmission fluid on automatic-transmission BMWs.
- **Every 90,000 miles** (or every nine years): replace your vehicle’s timing belts and hoses.

You’ll want to repeat the cycle above after 90,000 miles and always follow the 5,000-mile maintenance schedule. Your BMW’s New Vehicle Limited Warranty will also expire at 50,000 miles, so we recommend getting in any repairs or service before this warranty expires! We also recommend replacing your BMW battery around 50,000 miles.

# BMW SERVICE

BMW recommends you have your maintenance and repair work performed by an authorized BMW center.

# MAINTAINING YOUR BMW VEHICLE

A well-maintained vehicle will help safeguard its operational performance, road-safety and its reliability. This is why it is important to follow and perform BMW’s recommended periodic vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks as indicated by your vehicle’s Maintenance Service Display, along with the other maintenance work described in this booklet.

A improper maintenance is not covered under the BMW New Vehicle Damage, including consequential damage, which results from lack of or Limited Warranty for Passenger Cars and Light Trucks.

# MAINTENANCE INTERVALS

Maintenance intervals on motor vehicles were conventionally based solely on a fixed time period or a specified amount of accumulated driving mileage.

However, operational and driving conditions have a major influence on your vehicle’s routine maintenance requirements; the distance traveled is only one of these significant factors. A vehicle used for short trips in the city with numerous cold starts, prolonged periods of idling, stop-and-go driving, and high engine speeds during acceleration may require more frequent maintenance intervals than a vehicle that is driven long distances at moderate engine speeds.

Your BMW vehicle uses sensors and algorithms together with the elapsed time and the driving distance/profile to monitor and evaluate your vehicle’s maintenance service needs. This information is then used to adapt dynamically the parameters used to forecast the applicable maintenance service task intervals.

# THE BMW MAINTENANCE SYSTEM

All BMW vehicles are equipped with an integrated BMW Maintenance System. This maintenance “reminder” system helps ensure that the vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks are performed at the forecasted intervals that apply to your vehicle.

The BMW Maintenance System display provides the vehicle operator access to the current status information for the following maintenance service tasks:

$\\triangleright$ Engine oil (date and miles)\*

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle check (date and miles)

$\\triangleright$ Front brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Rear brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid (date)

$\\triangleright$ 1200 Mile running-in service (date and miles) (Applicable to BMW M vehicles only)\*

For each specific maintenance service task, either the future date (month/ year), remaining miles or both are provided as noted above. The system monitors variable inputs to forecast the intervals and alert the driver when one or more specific maintenance tasks should be performed.

NOTE: For certain vehicles, the status of the front and rear brake pads will only be observable in the maintenance system’s display when there are approximately 2,000 miles or less remaining before a brake service will be required to be performed.

For information about the vehicle’s maintenance system displays, please refer to the Maintenance Service Display Overview section beginning on page 5.

The following “combine with Engine oil”\* maintenance service tasks may be identified as needing to be performed with a specific occurrence of the “Engine oil” service task (service counter number):

$\\triangleright$ Cabin Microfilter(s)

$\\triangleright$ Engine air filter(s)\*

$\\triangleright$ Spark plugs\*

$\\triangleright$ Final drive oil (Applicable M vehicles only)

\\* Does not apply to BEV

Although these items do not appear in the BMW Maintenance System’s display in the vehicle, these services should be performed when your vehicle’s engine oil is changed in accordance with the interval identified by your vehicle’s BMW Maintenance System.

For more information on your vehicle’s maintenance services requirements, procedures and intervals, please refer the Maintenance Service Summary section beginning on page 10.

The BMW Maintenance System also includes an option to set service reminders for the following state-specific mandatory vehicle inspections, including:

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle safety inspection; and/or $\\triangleright$ Emissions test

The corresponding interval data for these inspections can be inputted into the BMW Maintenance System by a service provider; they are not determined by the vehicle.

For your convenience, you may also wish to have your authorized BMW center perform the work necessary to fulfill these state inspection requirements in your area concurrent with the maintenance services specified above when possible.

Should you request more frequent maintenance service than is indicated by the BMW Maintenance System during the coverage period, the cost of these services will not be covered by the BMW Maintenance Program.

# SERVICE DATA — REMOTE CONTROL KEY

Maintenance service task status information for your BMW vehicle is continually updated and stored in your remote control key.

Your authorized BMW center can access this data and consult with you about applicable service procedures and tasks for your vehicle.

Therefore, always provide your service consultant with the most recent remote control key that was used to operate the vehicle when servicing your vehicle at a BMW center.

# VEHICLE STORAGE

Disconnecting the battery during periods of long-term vehicle storage will interrupt the calculation of time-dependent maintenance services.

In this situation, BMW recommends that you have all your time-based maintenance services, such as brake fluid, engine oil and cabin microfilter, brought up to the correct date by an authorized BMW center.

# ENGINE OIL

2025 model year vehicles with internal-combustion engines are factory-filled with:

Z BMW-approved fully synthetic oil for gasoline engines

Engine oil should be changed when the vehicle’s engine is at operating temperature.

If an engine oil service is being performed or you need to add engine oil between changes, please refer to the Owner’s Manual for the recommended engine oil for your BMW vehicle.

# LONG-TERM RATED FLUIDS AND OILS

The following systems and assemblies are factory-filled with long-term rated fluid and oil; fluid replacement is only necessary when repairs are being performed (unless otherwise noted):

$\\triangleright$ Engine cooling system (antifreeze/coolant) $\\triangleright$ Automatic (except for X1 and X2) and manual transmissions $\\triangleright$ All-wheel drive transfer cases (except when indicated by the vehicle)

# REGULAR CHECKS — VEHICLE OPERATOR

In addition to the maintenance service procedure information contained in this booklet, BMW recommends that you regularly check (when refueling, for example), and address when necessary, the following items:

$\\triangleright$ Washer fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Coolant level

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Tires — pressure, condition and wear

Please refer to the Owner’s Manual for additional information.

# Volkswagen Tiguan Recommended Maintenance Schedule

The Volkswagen Tiguan stands out as one of Volkswagen's most popular vehicles, and for good reason. It offers a smooth ride, responsive handling, and a practical design, all of which have made it the go-to model for those who want a compact crossover.

The best way to protect your investment and keep your Tiguan running at its best? Keeping up with routine maintenance. We recommend following this VW Tiguan maintenance schedule to protect performance and extend your vehicle's lifespan.

![](https://pictures.dealer.com/h/hoovervolkswagenlithiaspringvw/1234/f5c328b76bb0498498c2e1ecd26148b9.jpeg?impolicy=downsize_bkpt&w=2500)

## Volkswagen Tiguan Maintenance Schedule

* * *

Most new Volkswagen Tiguan models follow a recommended service interval of every 10,000 miles or 12 months, whichever comes first, with the first scheduled service at 10,000 miles.

Older models may have different maintenance needs, so it's always a good idea to check your owner's manual to confirm the correct VW Tiguan maintenance schedule for your specific vehicle.

For Tiguans using synthetic oil, oil changes are typically recommended every 10,000 miles or once a year, though this can vary depending on your driving habits, commute length, and overall usage.

Here is a general VW Tiguan maintenance schedule to help you stay on track:

### Every 10,000 Miles (or 12 Months)

This is your most frequent service visit and focuses on routine upkeep.

- Engine oil and filter change (synthetic oil)
- Tire rotation
- Brake inspection
- Multi-point vehicle inspection
- Check fluid levels and top off as needed
- Inspect lights, wipers, and battery condition

### Every 20,000 Miles

In addition to the 10,000-mile services:

- Replace the cabin air filter
- Inspect the engine air filter
- Inspect suspension and steering components
- Check the cooling system and hoses

### Every 30,000-40,000 Miles

Along with previous maintenance items:

- Replace engine air filter (if needed)
- Brake service inspection
- Wheel alignment check
- Battery and charging system test
- Inspect the exhaust system

### Every 50,000 Miles

In addition to routine oil changes and tire rotations, this service interval typically includes:

- Brake system inspection
- Battery and charging system test
- Suspension and steering evaluation
- Engine air filter replacement (if needed)
- Cooling system inspection
- Wheel alignment check

### Every 60,000 Miles

This is a larger service interval that may include:

- Spark plug replacement (varies by model year)
- Transmission service (model-dependent)
- Coolant system inspection or service
- More in-depth brake and suspension evaluation

### Beyond 60,000 Miles

As mileage increases, your Tiguan may also need:

- Additional drivetrain inspections
- Timing-related component checks (model dependent)
- Continued fluid services
- Suspension and steering repairs as needed

**Important note:** Older Volkswagen Tiguan models and certain driving habits (frequent short trips, stop-and-go traffic, towing, or extreme weather) may require more frequent service. Always refer to your owner's manual for the exact maintenance requirements for your specific vehicle. If you still have questions, don't hesitate to contact us!

Your [brakes](https://vw.oempartsonline.com/brakes) stop your [Volkswagen](https://vw.oempartsonline.com/v-volkswagen) vehicle. They do it by clamping their calipers and brake rotors together. This is what creates the friction, or resistance, that slows your vehicle's wheels and tires. However, calipers can't press rotors without brake pads, or else they'd get damaged. Your VW has one of four types of pads, depending on its model. Organic brake pads are for everyday driving. They're reliable, they don't wear rotors down as badly, and they don't create much dust. Best of all, they're inexpensive. Ceramic brake pads work better in bad weather, they don't make much noise, and their dust isn't as sticky. Metallic brake pads, however, stand up to higher heat, feel firmer, and resist brake fade. Carbon fiber brake pads are the strongest and best performers, tolerant of high temperatures and providing the most stopping power. Most cars and SUVs use either metallic or organic pads. However, many sports cars and performance vehicles use ceramic or carbon fiber pads because they do the best job of expelling heat.

## How Long Do Volkswagen Brake Pads Last?

However, no brake pad lasts forever, not even those Volkswagen makes. You should change yours every 40,000 to 50,000 miles or so. Otherwise, figure out when to replace them by looking for the signs your brakes are going bad. They include warning lights, worn pad surfaces, pad damage, whiny brakes, and taking longer to stop. The worst are vibration and grinding, as they indicate your rotors are warped and getting damaged because your brake pads have degraded.

## VW ID.4 Maintenance Schedule

Your ID.4 requires its first maintenance visit at 10,000 miles and every 10,000 miles thereafter. Let’s take a look at the services performed at each appointment.

### 10K, 30K, 50K, 70K, 90K, 110K\* Miles

- Check battery
- Inspect tires
- Obtain diagnostic system readings
- Reset service interval indicator/display

\*At 110,000 miles, a few additional services are included in the recommended ID.4 maintenance schedule:

- Check rear window
- Replace cabin air filter
- Rotate tires

### 20K, 40K, 60K, 80K, 100K, 120K Miles

At these intervals, your service technician will perform the above services, in addition to road-testing the vehicle, servicing its high-voltage parts, and inspecting the following components:

- Brake fluid
- Brake system
- Cooling system
- Headlight washer
- Horn function
- Lighting operation and alignment
- Motor parts
- Steering
- Suspension
- Underbody contact points and linkage
- Windshield wipers

# Minor Maintenance

 Battery, 12 Volt: Checking with battery tester if necessary

 Service interval display: Reset

 Tires: Check condition and wear pattern. Record tread depth

 Guided Fault Finding: Use the Vehicle Diagnostic Tester to check for, resolve, and clear any Diagnostic Trouble Codes that may be present

# Standard Maintenance (Includes All Minor Maintenance Items)

 Battery, 12 Volt: Checking with battery tester if necessary

 Battery, High-voltage: Check charge level and charge as necessary

 Body Interior and Exterior: Check for corrosion

 Brake fluid: Check level depending on brake wear

 Brake Pads (Front and Rear): Check thickness and brake disc condition. Look for contact pattern and corrosion of brake discs

 Brake System and Shock Absorbers: Check for leaks and damage

 Charging cable: Check that the cable is present and check condition of the cable

Coil Springs and Rubber Stop Buffers: Inspect for damage

 Cooling System: Check frost protection and coolant level Exterior lighting: Check function of front and rear lights, headlights (adjust if necessary), automatic headlights (if equipped), turn signals, cornering lights, and hazard warning lights

 Guided Fault Finding: Use the Vehicle Diagnostic Tester to check for, resolve, and clear any Diagnostic Trouble Codes that may be present

 Headlight Washing System: Check function (if equipped)

 High-voltage Charging Sockets in Radiator Grille and Filler Cap: Inspect for dirt, debris, and damage

 High-voltage components and High-voltage Cables: Inspect for damage and correct routing and securing

 Horn: Check function

 Interior lighting: Check function of headliner, luggage compoartment and glove compartment

 Motor and Motor compartment components (from above): Check for leaks and damage

 Motor and Motor compartment components (from below): Check related components including transmission, final drive, and drive axle boots for leaks and damage

# Standard Maintenance (continued)

 Service interval display: Reset

 Suspension and Steering: Check ball joints, wheel bearings, drive axles, coupling rods, tie rod ends, and stabilizer bar rubber bushings for damage and excessive play.

 Test Drive: Check braking, steering, electrical, heating/ventilation systems, air conditioning, handling, and parking brake  Tire pressure: Check LF RF\_ LR RR Spare

 Tire Repair Kit: Check for damage and prior use

 Tires: Check condition and wear pattern. Record tread depth

 Tire Pressure Monitoring System: Calibrate to correct tire pressure settings

 Underbody: Check underbody protection, underbody trim panels, wire routing, and plugs for damage

 Warning Labels: Check that they are present

 Windshield: Check for damage

 Windshield Wiper/Washer System: Check for damage, function and adjust spray nozzle if necessary, fluid level, and freeze protection  Wiper Blades: Bring into service position, check for damage, and check park position

Your first Mercedes-Benz GLE SUV Service A will be needed at 10,000 miles or 1 year. After that, your vehicle will require Service A every 20,000 miles or 2 years.

## Mercedes-Benz GLE SUV Service B

# BMW SERVICE

BMW recommends you have your maintenance and repair work performed by an authorized BMW center.

# MAINTAINING YOUR BMW VEHICLE

A well-maintained vehicle will help safeguard its operational performance, road-safety and its reliability. This is why it is important to follow and perform BMW’s recommended periodic vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks as indicated by your vehicle’s Maintenance Service Display, along with the other maintenance work described in this booklet.

A improper maintenance is not covered under the BMW New Vehicle Damage, including consequential damage, which results from lack of or Limited Warranty for Passenger Cars and Light Trucks.

# MAINTENANCE INTERVALS

Maintenance intervals on motor vehicles were conventionally based solely on a fixed time period or a specified amount of accumulated driving mileage.

However, operational and driving conditions have a major influence on your vehicle’s routine maintenance requirements; the distance traveled is only one of these significant factors. A vehicle used for short trips in the city with numerous cold starts, prolonged periods of idling, stop-and-go driving, and high engine speeds during acceleration may require more frequent maintenance intervals than a vehicle that is driven long distances at moderate engine speeds.

Your BMW vehicle uses sensors and algorithms together with the elapsed time and the driving distance/profile to monitor and evaluate your vehicle’s maintenance service needs. This information is then used to adapt dynamically the parameters used to forecast the applicable maintenance service task intervals.

# THE BMW MAINTENANCE SYSTEM

All BMW vehicles are equipped with an integrated BMW Maintenance System. This maintenance “reminder” system helps ensure that the vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks are performed at the forecasted intervals that apply to your vehicle.

The BMW Maintenance System display provides the vehicle operator access to the current status information for the following maintenance service tasks:

$\\triangleright$ Engine oil (date and miles)\*

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle check (date and miles)

$\\triangleright$ Front brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Rear brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid (date)

$\\triangleright$ 1200 Mile running-in service (date and miles) (Applicable to BMW M vehicles only)\*

For each specific maintenance service task, either the future date (month/ year), remaining miles or both are provided as noted above. The system monitors variable inputs to forecast the intervals and alert the driver when one or more specific maintenance tasks should be performed.

NOTE: For certain vehicles, the status of the front and rear brake pads will only be observable in the maintenance system’s display when there are approximately 2,000 miles or less remaining before a brake service will be required to be performed.

For information about the vehicle’s maintenance system displays, please refer to the Maintenance Service Display Overview section beginning on page 5.

The following “combine with Engine oil”\* maintenance service tasks may be identified as needing to be performed with a specific occurrence of the “Engine oil” service task (service counter number):

$\\triangleright$ Cabin Microfilter(s)

$\\triangleright$ Engine air filter(s)\*

$\\triangleright$ Spark plugs\*

$\\triangleright$ Final drive oil (Applicable M vehicles only)

\\* Does not apply to BEV

Although these items do not appear in the BMW Maintenance System’s display in the vehicle, these services should be performed when your vehicle’s engine oil is changed in accordance with the interval identified by your vehicle’s BMW Maintenance System.

For more information on your vehicle’s maintenance services requirements, procedures and intervals, please refer the Maintenance Service Summary section beginning on page 10.

The BMW Maintenance System also includes an option to set service reminders for the following state-specific mandatory vehicle inspections, including:

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle safety inspection; and/or $\\triangleright$ Emissions test

The corresponding interval data for these inspections can be inputted into the BMW Maintenance System by a service provider; they are not determined by the vehicle.

For your convenience, you may also wish to have your authorized BMW center perform the work necessary to fulfill these state inspection requirements in your area concurrent with the maintenance services specified above when possible.

Should you request more frequent maintenance service than is indicated by the BMW Maintenance System during the coverage period, the cost of these services will not be covered by the BMW Maintenance Program.

# SERVICE DATA — REMOTE CONTROL KEY

Maintenance service task status information for your BMW vehicle is continually updated and stored in your remote control key.

Your authorized BMW center can access this data and consult with you about applicable service procedures and tasks for your vehicle.

Therefore, always provide your service consultant with the most recent remote control key that was used to operate the vehicle when servicing your vehicle at a BMW center.

# VEHICLE STORAGE

Disconnecting the battery during periods of long-term vehicle storage will interrupt the calculation of time-dependent maintenance services.

In this situation, BMW recommends that you have all your time-based maintenance services, such as brake fluid, engine oil and cabin microfilter, brought up to the correct date by an authorized BMW center.

# ENGINE OIL

2025 model year vehicles with internal-combustion engines are factory-filled with:

Z BMW-approved fully synthetic oil for gasoline engines

Engine oil should be changed when the vehicle’s engine is at operating temperature.

If an engine oil service is being performed or you need to add engine oil between changes, please refer to the Owner’s Manual for the recommended engine oil for your BMW vehicle.

# LONG-TERM RATED FLUIDS AND OILS

The following systems and assemblies are factory-filled with long-term rated fluid and oil; fluid replacement is only necessary when repairs are being performed (unless otherwise noted):

$\\triangleright$ Engine cooling system (antifreeze/coolant) $\\triangleright$ Automatic (except for X1 and X2) and manual transmissions $\\triangleright$ All-wheel drive transfer cases (except when indicated by the vehicle)

# REGULAR CHECKS — VEHICLE OPERATOR

In addition to the maintenance service procedure information contained in this booklet, BMW recommends that you regularly check (when refueling, for example), and address when necessary, the following items:

$\\triangleright$ Washer fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Coolant level

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Tires — pressure, condition and wear

Please refer to the Owner’s Manual for additional information.

## What Does the BMW Maintenance Schedule Include?

BMW maintenance is broken down into intervals, based on time or mileage. Below are general service milestones for most BMW models:

### BMW 10,000-Mile Maintenance

- At 10,000 miles or 12 months, schedule an oil change, brake inspection, and tire rotation.

### BMW 20,000-Mile Maintenance

- At 20,000 miles, replace the cabin air filter and perform a more comprehensive inspection.

### BMW 30,000-Mile Maintenance

- At 30,000-40,000 miles, inspect suspension, steering components, coolant, and belts.
- If manual transmission: replace [transmission fluid](https://www.bmwofturnersville.com/service/service-tips/check-your-transmission-fluid/) every 30,000 miles

### BMW 60,000-Mile Maintenance

- At 60,000 miles, flush and replace brake fluid, inspect spark plugs, and change the engine air filter.

### Additional BMW Maintenance

Every two years, replace the cabin microfilter and test battery performance.

Additional services like coolant flushes, differential fluid replacement, or transmission service may vary depending on your BMW model and driving habits.

We recommend checking your BMW iDrive system or owner’s manual, or speaking with a certified technician at our Turnersville location, for a custom plan.

# BMW SERVICE

BMW recommends you have your maintenance and repair work performed by an authorized BMW center.

# MAINTAINING YOUR BMW VEHICLE

A well-maintained vehicle will help safeguard its operational performance, road-safety and its reliability. This is why it is important to follow and perform BMW’s recommended periodic vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks as indicated by your vehicle’s Maintenance Service Display, along with the other maintenance work described in this booklet.

A improper maintenance is not covered under the BMW New Vehicle Damage, including consequential damage, which results from lack of or Limited Warranty for Passenger Cars and Light Trucks.

# MAINTENANCE INTERVALS

Maintenance intervals on motor vehicles were conventionally based solely on a fixed time period or a specified amount of accumulated driving mileage.

However, operational and driving conditions have a major influence on your vehicle’s routine maintenance requirements; the distance traveled is only one of these significant factors. A vehicle used for short trips in the city with numerous cold starts, prolonged periods of idling, stop-and-go driving, and high engine speeds during acceleration may require more frequent maintenance intervals than a vehicle that is driven long distances at moderate engine speeds.

Your BMW vehicle uses sensors and algorithms together with the elapsed time and the driving distance/profile to monitor and evaluate your vehicle’s maintenance service needs. This information is then used to adapt dynamically the parameters used to forecast the applicable maintenance service task intervals.

# THE BMW MAINTENANCE SYSTEM

All BMW vehicles are equipped with an integrated BMW Maintenance System. This maintenance “reminder” system helps ensure that the vehicle inspections and maintenance service tasks are performed at the forecasted intervals that apply to your vehicle.

The BMW Maintenance System display provides the vehicle operator access to the current status information for the following maintenance service tasks:

$\\triangleright$ Engine oil (date and miles)\*

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle check (date and miles)

$\\triangleright$ Front brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Rear brake pads (miles)

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid (date)

$\\triangleright$ 1200 Mile running-in service (date and miles) (Applicable to BMW M vehicles only)\*

For each specific maintenance service task, either the future date (month/ year), remaining miles or both are provided as noted above. The system monitors variable inputs to forecast the intervals and alert the driver when one or more specific maintenance tasks should be performed.

NOTE: For certain vehicles, the status of the front and rear brake pads will only be observable in the maintenance system’s display when there are approximately 2,000 miles or less remaining before a brake service will be required to be performed.

For information about the vehicle’s maintenance system displays, please refer to the Maintenance Service Display Overview section beginning on page 5.

The following “combine with Engine oil”\* maintenance service tasks may be identified as needing to be performed with a specific occurrence of the “Engine oil” service task (service counter number):

$\\triangleright$ Cabin Microfilter(s)

$\\triangleright$ Engine air filter(s)\*

$\\triangleright$ Spark plugs\*

$\\triangleright$ Final drive oil (Applicable M vehicles only)

\\* Does not apply to BEV

Although these items do not appear in the BMW Maintenance System’s display in the vehicle, these services should be performed when your vehicle’s engine oil is changed in accordance with the interval identified by your vehicle’s BMW Maintenance System.

For more information on your vehicle’s maintenance services requirements, procedures and intervals, please refer the Maintenance Service Summary section beginning on page 10.

The BMW Maintenance System also includes an option to set service reminders for the following state-specific mandatory vehicle inspections, including:

$\\triangleright$ Vehicle safety inspection; and/or $\\triangleright$ Emissions test

The corresponding interval data for these inspections can be inputted into the BMW Maintenance System by a service provider; they are not determined by the vehicle.

For your convenience, you may also wish to have your authorized BMW center perform the work necessary to fulfill these state inspection requirements in your area concurrent with the maintenance services specified above when possible.

Should you request more frequent maintenance service than is indicated by the BMW Maintenance System during the coverage period, the cost of these services will not be covered by the BMW Maintenance Program.

# SERVICE DATA — REMOTE CONTROL KEY

Maintenance service task status information for your BMW vehicle is continually updated and stored in your remote control key.

Your authorized BMW center can access this data and consult with you about applicable service procedures and tasks for your vehicle.

Therefore, always provide your service consultant with the most recent remote control key that was used to operate the vehicle when servicing your vehicle at a BMW center.

# VEHICLE STORAGE

Disconnecting the battery during periods of long-term vehicle storage will interrupt the calculation of time-dependent maintenance services.

In this situation, BMW recommends that you have all your time-based maintenance services, such as brake fluid, engine oil and cabin microfilter, brought up to the correct date by an authorized BMW center.

# ENGINE OIL

2025 model year vehicles with internal-combustion engines are factory-filled with:

Z BMW-approved fully synthetic oil for gasoline engines

Engine oil should be changed when the vehicle’s engine is at operating temperature.

If an engine oil service is being performed or you need to add engine oil between changes, please refer to the Owner’s Manual for the recommended engine oil for your BMW vehicle.

# LONG-TERM RATED FLUIDS AND OILS

The following systems and assemblies are factory-filled with long-term rated fluid and oil; fluid replacement is only necessary when repairs are being performed (unless otherwise noted):

$\\triangleright$ Engine cooling system (antifreeze/coolant) $\\triangleright$ Automatic (except for X1 and X2) and manual transmissions $\\triangleright$ All-wheel drive transfer cases (except when indicated by the vehicle)

# REGULAR CHECKS — VEHICLE OPERATOR

In addition to the maintenance service procedure information contained in this booklet, BMW recommends that you regularly check (when refueling, for example), and address when necessary, the following items:

$\\triangleright$ Washer fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Coolant level

$\\triangleright$ Brake fluid level

$\\triangleright$ Tires — pressure, condition and wear

Please refer to the Owner’s Manual for additional information.

## 2024 Ford Mustang Maintenance Schedule

If you own a 2024 Ford Mustang, you appreciate the incredible performance that’s become synonymous
with this iconic car. Now in its seventh generation, the Mustang’s reputation has been solidified
over nearly 60 years. While the Mustang is built with quality in mind, routine maintenance at
Winslow Ford, the Star Valley Ford dealer, is essential to ensure it continues to run in peak
condition.

Adhering to Ford’s recommended maintenance schedule is crucial for the longevity of your Mustang.
Turn to the skilled team at the Star Valley Ford dealership for all your maintenance needs. Your
Mustang will receive the best possible care. Here’s a brief overview of your 2024 Ford Mustang’s
maintenance schedule.

### Every 5,000 Miles

During every service visit, the service technicians at the Winslow Ford Service Center will change your
Mustang’s engine oil and install a new oil filter. Motor oil plays a pivotal role in ensuring the engine
components are properly lubricated, and it helps dissipate heat. Old engine oil breaks down and picks up
contaminants over time, so replacing it with fresh oil is important to ensure the engine runs efficiently.

Your Mustang’s tires will be rotated and checked for signs of wear and tear. Rotating the tires promotes even
wear and increases their longevity. Other services performed during this visit include a safety inspection
and a visual inspection of the brakes, belts, and hoses.

Every 15,000 Miles

At 15,000 miles, our service technicians will repeat the services of the 5,000-mile maintenance visit.
Additionally, they’ll replace the engine air filter. They’ll also change the cabin air filter, which
prevents airborne particles such as dust, pollen, and pollutants from entering the vehicle’s interior,
ensuring passengers breathe cleaner air. This visit also includes an inspection of the suspension, steering
linkage, driveshaft, ball joints, wheel ends, cooling system and hoses, brake pads, rotors, hoses, brake
lines, and the parking brake. Your Mustang’s brake pads may need to be replaced at this juncture.

### Every 30,000 Miles

At the 30,000-mile mark, the service checklist expands to include an inspection of the exhaust system, the heat shields, and the drive belts. If your Mustang has an automatic transmission, the service technicians will replace the transmission and power steering fluids. They’ll also check the spark plugs and replace them if needed.

### At 45,000 Miles

Once your Mustang reaches 45,000 miles, our service technicians will perform all the procedures listed in the 15,000-mile service and replace the engine coolant.

### At 60,000 Miles

Besides the maintenance tasks of the 30,000-mile maintenance visit, at 60,000 miles, the service technicians will replace your 2024 Ford Mustang’s fuel filter.

### At 100,000 Miles

Today’s Ford vehicles are built to be reliable. If you’ve kept up with the recommended maintenance schedule, your Mustang will provide you with many years of exhilarating driving. When your 2024 Mustang reaches 100,000 miles, the technicians will change the PCV valve.

If you drive under special operating conditions, including off-roading, towing, and in dusty terrains, your 2024 Mustang may need more frequent maintenance visits. Contact the experts at the Winslow Ford Service Center if you have any questions about your vehicle’s maintenance requirements or to schedule your next appointment.

###### Source: Ford

* * *

#### **Oil Viscosity Explained**

Why do I see a “W” on my engine and gear oil? Simply explained, this means the oil being used is a multi-viscosity application. The ‘W” in motor and gear oil stands for winter. The first number you see is the classification of cold weather viscosity. The smaller the number is on this first number means the oil being used will be less viscous at lower temps. The second number after the “W” is the high temp viscosity, or how the oil is at operating temps. Once again, the higher the number, the thicker the oil would be. Thicker oil is not always better, depending on the age and wear of the engine, thicker viscosity oil can benefit you. On a brand new engine, this could actually hurt you. Ford and other manufacturers have specifications normally listed on the oil cap or in the factory owner’s manual.

# BMW X5 Maintenance Schedule

![2024 BMW X5 driving down the highway](https://dealerinspire-image-library-prod.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/images/ABGtY2AGIHPv5VlGWpvFvkB0hDl0IB7xvLJJbJAe.jpg)

The BMW X5 has everything you love about driving a luxury SUV in Orland Park, from the quality materials in the cabin to a stout engine. We highly recommend following the BMW X5 maintenance schedule for the best results, whether you own your SUV in Frankfort or lease it from a dealership.

Our service team will happily help you follow the BMW X5 service intervals so your Ultimate Driving Machine® lives up to the hype. Keep reading to learn more from BMW of Orland Park.
